### T4 deferred swaps (2026-08-22, title-screen stretch)

Known-BE data left unswapped because nothing on the boot/title path reads
it yet. Each will surface as a crash or wrong values when its reader runs;
swap at the load choke point per the convention in
docs/decisions/native-boot.md:

- **Render vertex arrays** (DisplayList/DLPrimary/Op05/07 `Vertices`) —
  RSP-consumed; the T2 interpreter will read them native, so swap at model
  load when T2 lands. CPU readers (glass2.c tc[] writes, explosions) crash
  before that if reached.
- **PointUsage tables** (DLCollision) — s16 entries, count unconfirmed.
- **bg.c / propobj.c / bgapply.c byte-positional DL parsers** (bytes[0] ==
  G_SETTIMG etc.) — need SL_DLOP guards when level geometry loads (stage
  paths, not title).
- **chrprop.c raw-byte g_Textures access** (`((u8*)g_Textures)[i*8] & 0xf`)
  — assumes BE bitfield packing; use field access natively (hit-sound
  lookup, gameplay path).
- **fontdl segment** (lv.c:268 romCopy → ptr_font_DL) — Gfx data, swap
  wholesale if/when parsed natively.
- **Flaky uninit crash**: one raw run segfaulted at addr=nil where repeats
  survive — ASLR-sensitive uninitialized read somewhere on the title path.
  Will need valgrind when it resurfaces.
- **Menu progression**: current_menu stays at MENU_EYE_INTRO through 10k
  frames; frames tick and it renders, but the intro doesn't advance to the
  GE logo. Likely timer/counter semantics in the intro sequence (or wants
  controller input) — first thing to look at next.

### Post-attract-loop items (2026-08-22)

- ~~Anim bit descriptors swapped at wrong granularity~~ RESOLVED
  2026-08-22: the wire header is 0x14 bytes (only address/frames/widths/
  bitDescriptors/bitStream are wire fields); descriptors are read
  byte-positionally at their single consumer. See commits 7956d63d and
  48f76fcc.
- **Unknown propdef types get header-only swap** (LINK, SWITCH,
  SAFE_ITEM, GUARD_ATTRIBUTE, DEBRIS, remaining OBJECTIVE_* payloads):
  their readers will surface them.
- **N64 Makefile lacks header dependency tracking**: header edits leave
  stale objects; MATCH can pass on lies (the setupCctv case). Before
  any MATCH gate after header changes, delete affected objects or
  clean-rebuild. Consider adding gcc -MMD-style deps to the Makefile.
- **The sightline/session-0-bootstrap branch** carries all of this;
  Phase 1 tracks T2 (fast3d oracle) and the native state reader are the
  next big rocks toward trace-verify --backend native.

### Native replay: the 1-ULP frontier (2026-08-22, late)

archives-sweep-agent replays byte-identically through tick 53 (input,
intro-skip taps, RNG chain, spawn), and props hold through tick 112.
Everything that remains is a single class: **float values 1-244 ULPs
off in the bond head/body matrix chain**, first visible as standheight
0x4320507d native vs 0x4320507c emulator at level init, later as
1-ULP position drift and one prop ONSCREEN-flag flip at a cull
boundary (tick 113).

Evidence assembled so far, all bit-level:
- All inputs compared equal: swirl records, theta, anchors, timers,
  RNG seeds, anim frame numbers (95.0400/95.3599... match exactly).
- The sinf/cosf ports are bit-exact: native output == a Python mirror
  of the IDO algorithm in exact IEEE double, for the 9 live rotation
  angles observed. The rotation angle u16->radian conversion is exact
  arithmetic.
- The matching build contains zero madd.s (no fused ops to mimic).
- parallel-n64's interpreter/dynarec use host float/double IEEE ops.
- modelInitRwData zeroes all rwdata; no read-before-write found.

The divergent op is somewhere in the anim-blend/quaternion/matrix
chain with inputs that LOOK equal at every probe point sampled.
Resolving it needs instruction-level tracing of the emulator (mupen
gdb stub or a step-compare harness) - the deferred divergence-tooling
item. Until then trace-verify --backend native will report player
divergence from tick 54 on archives with everything else clean.

**Drift characterization (SL_TRACE_DETAIL=-2 vs an emu field log),
2026-08-22 late:** the ULP class is BOUNDED, not chaotic.  Player
position is bit-exact through tick 53, then pinned within 4 ULPs for
the whole remaining hour of gameplay (frames 106-3629 without
exception; three self-healing excursions of at most 128 ULPs during
the post-intro settling, frames 91-105).  The init perturbation acts
as a constant forcing term through a contractive sim - it never
amplifies.  Practical consequences: (1) fixing the single init-time
standheight/head-matrix computation would likely lock the whole trace
to near-bit-exact; (2) an interim ULP-tolerant comparison would pass
94% of frames today.  The tail past frame 3630 is the recording
ending (the emulator's run hits its mission outro and teardown while
the native build keeps simulating on exhausted input) - the native
comparison window should clamp at the recording's end-of-run, worth a
small nativediff change.

A follow-up experiment overrode standheight and standbodyoffset with
the recorded bits at init: NO effect on the tick-54 hash.  The
divergent op therefore runs PER FRAME in the live subcalcmatrices/
bondhead chain - replaying frozen outputs cannot help; only finding
the op can.

**Three-way vote (2026-08-22, late): THE NATIVE BUILD IS THE DEVIANT.**
parallel-n64's pure interpreter computes the same standheight bits as
its dynarec (4320507c), and mupen64plus - an independent lineage, LLE
config, via the old sltrace/emu.py driver - ALSO computes 4320507c.
Two emulator families agree; native alone says 4320507d.  No emulator
tracer is needed: the bug is in the native build's execution of the
init/per-frame head-matrix chain and can be found with native gdb plus
the exact-IEEE Python mirror (sinf/cosf mirrors already verified
bit-exact against the native objects).  Suspect classes: an
N64-frame-dependent behavior the emulators reproduce and the native
canary fixes prevent (OOB stack spill read back), a subtle
GCC-vs-source semantics gap, or a remaining unswapped input read only
this chain performs.

Also queued: tools/trace should recover SL_RNG_SEED automatically per
trace (invert the LFSR from early seed samples - see commit 9409813b)
instead of the hand-derived env value.

### Native replay: the render-path frontier (2026-08-22, latest)

The 1-ULP frontier is RESOLVED: the game's own single-precision
sinf/cosf (math_sincos.s, hand-written assembly) never built natively,
and libultra's gu weak aliases silently substituted double-precision
trig into every game call site.  Ported bit-exactly in
sl_ported_asm.c.  Player hash now byte-identical through tick 292
(was 53).

What remains on archives-sweep-agent, fully characterized:
1. Tick 113 (fc 678): object id 50's PROPFLAG_ONSCREEN reads 06
   natively, 04 on the emulator - one borderline posIsOnScreen call
   (room-visibility walk + camIsPosInScreen frustum math from
   UNHASHED camera state).  Sole props divergence at that point.
2. From ~fc 727 the native build draws ONE FEWER randomGetNext per
   frame than the emulator - a render-path consumer (muzzle-flash
   class, e.g. gunfire.c:780 draws per rendered flash) runs on the
   emulator but not natively, most likely gated on stubbed gfx state
   in the native render walk.  The RNG chains stay value-identical
   but slip one draw per frame.
3. At fc 1052 (tick 293) the accumulated RNG offset flips a guard
   shot: Bond's health drops to 0.99375 on the emulator, stays 1.0
   natively.  First hashed player divergence.

CORRECTED (same session, after bisecting): the render-path framing
above was wrong.  The chain starts with PLAYER MOVEMENT, ten frames
before the RNG slip:

  fc 717  g_CurrentPlayer->speedforwards (player+372) is -0.2314 then
          -0.3395 natively for four frames; the emulator holds 0.0
          across the whole window (707-725, settled samples).
  ->      percent_speed = speedforwards / maxspeed reaches bheadUpdate
          nonzero, and `m[3][2] *= percent_speed` (the only z-specific
          term - x uses `+= speedsideways`) gives the head matrix a
          nonzero z ONLY natively.  Confirmed field-by-field: head
          matrix m[3][0] and m[3][1] match the emulator BIT-EXACTLY
          frame for frame; only m[3][2] differs, and only while
          speedforwards is nonzero.
  ->      headpos.z feeds the horizontal move terms in the MoveBond /
          FrozenMoveBond offset calculation, so collision_position
          drifts in x and z with y still exact (first seen fc 717).
  ->      Bond stands somewhere slightly different; visibility and AI
          inputs shift; by ~fc 727 the native build makes one fewer
          randomGetNext call per frame (the RNG VALUES still chain
          correctly - it is a draw-count slip, not a broken RNG).
  ->      fc 1052 (tick 293): the accumulated RNG offset flips a guard
          shot - emu health 0.99375, native 1.0.  First hashed player
          divergence.

The tick-113 ONSCREEN flip on object id 50 sits between the movement
divergence and the RNG slip and is very likely the same cause (a
borderline posIsOnScreen from a slightly different camera position),
not an independent bug.

LOCALIZED FURTHER (same session): speedforwards is written directly
from the analog stick in bondviewProcessInput (bondview2.c:5656), and
the stick value the game consumes is samples[curlast] of the joy ring.
Both backends' RING CONTENTS agree exactly - at fc 715 each holds
input record 696 = (x=64, y=-20) as the newest sample.  What differs
is the POINTERS:

    emulator   curstart=2  curlast=0   nextlast=2   -> game reads rec 694
    native     curstart=9  curlast=11  nextlast=11  -> game reads rec 696

On hardware the scheduler polls throughout the frame, so some of a
frame's VIs land AFTER the game's joyConsumeSamples and curlast trails
the newest polled sample by ~2 records.  The pump does the entire
batch at the frame boundary, before the consume, so native's curlast
IS the newest and the game runs one frame ahead on analog values.
Buttons are unaffected because joyConsumeSamples ORs edges across the
whole window.

A uniform hold-back does NOT fix it - SL_VIS_LAG (new env knob,
default 0, no behaviour change) was measured:

    lag=0   player 293   props 113     <- current default
    lag=1   player 107   props 107
    lag=2   player  53   props  53     <- intro-skip breaks again

So the offset is not a constant phase: the frame->VI mapping is right
early (the intro is exact) and drifts later.  Two candidate causes,
both testable: (a) .vis targets are derived from the tick at which the
frame counter is first OBSERVED to change, which can lag the true
boundary by a sample and accumulate; (b) the split of a frame's VIs
around the consume point genuinely varies with frame length (2 vs 3
VIs) and must be modelled rather than approximated.

Next experiment: log, per frame, the record identity that each backend
consumes (match the ring's (x,y,button) triple back to the input
stream during a motion window), and plot native-vs-emulator record
index against frame index.  A constant offset means (a) and a
re-extraction fixes it; a growing or frame-length-correlated offset
means (b) and the poll batch must be split around a hook at
joyConsumeSamplesWrapper.

### Native replay: the save-settings fix (2026-08-22, latest)

The input-phase theory in the section above is RETRACTED.  Logging the
controller sample the game actually consumes (SL_TRACE_DETAIL=-4,
samples[curlast] of the joy ring) and comparing it frame for frame
shows the two backends consume the IDENTICAL sample for all 3750
frames of archives-sweep-agent.  Input replay is faithful; the earlier
"curlast trails by two records" reading compared a mid-frame emulator
VI sample against a native frame boundary.

The real cause was the SAVE FILE.  EEPROM images are cartridge
(big-endian) byte dumps, and save_data has three fields the game reads
as VALUES: s32 chksum1, s32 chksum2, u16 options.  Unswapped, every
folder failed its checksum, fileResetSave() overwrote it, and the game
ran on DEFAULT_OPTIONS (0x3A).  The recorded session had inverted look
saved (options 0x3B, and control type 1), so from the first stick
movement the same input produced different speedforwards, a different
head-matrix z, and the horizontal drift.  It hid for 292 frames purely
because the trace has no stick input until record 694.

Fixed in file2.c: checksums promoted right after each read (they sit
outside the CRC's byte range), options promoted only for saves that
survive validation.  The CRC is byte-wise and uses the already-exact
LFSR, so it needs nothing.  Native now reads the same eight options
and the same control type as the emulator.  MATCH verified.

**RESOLVED 2026-08-24** (see the resolution note at the end of this entry).

**Was: current blocker - collision-DL rwdata.**  With settings correct,
native follows the emulator through the first guard shot at tick 293
and SIGSEGVs in the weapon hit test:

    bgTestHitOnObj (propobj.c)      <- vertices is a float, not a pointer
    propobjFindHit
    sub_GAME_7F04E720 / 7F04E9BC
    chraiDefaultWeaponFireHandler   <- a guard fires at Bond
    chraiCheckUseHeldItem(s)
    lvlRender

Half of it is fixed: bgTestHitOnObj also read WORDS out of the
(wire-order) display list as values - the G_VTX offset and the G_TRI2
indices - now handled by SL_DLW/SL_DLH.  What remains is the vertex
base itself, taken from `rwdata->Vertices` on the
MODELNODE_OPCODE_DLCOLLISION path (propobj.c ~8785).  That is runtime
data, a different union variant from the ModelRwData_HeaderRecord we
already fixed, and it is holding a float bit pattern (~482.5f).  Next:
find who fills that rwdata variant at model load and whether the
native path writes it at all - the sibling MODELNODE_OPCODE_DL branch
uses rodata->BaseAddr, which is promoted correctly, so the DLCOLLISION
writer is the suspect.

*2026-08-24 - suspects narrowed, all the static ones are dead.*
`rwdata->DisplayListCollisions.Vertices` has exactly two writers in the
whole tree: `propobj.c:7045`, which is the MONITOR path (it sits among
screen->colfrac/red/green state and cannot apply to a general model),
and `propobj.c:11130`, which is a RESTORE - it frees the current
pointer and puts rodata's value back, and only runs when the two
already differ. `modelInitRwData`'s DLCOLLISION case (`model.c:411`)
computes an rwdata INDEX and never touches Vertices.

So for an ordinary model nothing writes it, and the observed ~482.5f is
not a stale pointer - it is a float that was already sitting there.
That points at the rwdata SLOT, not the value: a wrong RwDataIndex
would land the read inside a vertex array and produce exactly this.
But `DisplayListCollisions.RwDataIndex` IS byte-swapped natively
(`sl_swap_model.c:204`), so that explanation is dead too.

*2026-08-24, later - reproduced and symbolised. TWO root-cause claims
made here were WRONG; both were killed by measurement, and the notes
are kept because each rules something out.*

Reproduced (this command was never written down, which is most of why
this sat):

    .venv/bin/python3 tools/trace/nativediff.py /dev/null \
        tools/trace/traces/archives-sweep-agent.sltrace \
        --extract-ticks /tmp/arch.ticks

    SL_ROM=build/u/direct/ge007.u.archives-sweep-agent.z64 \
    SL_BOOT_LEVEL=24 \
    SL_INPUT=tools/trace/inputs/archives-sweep-agent.input \
    SL_EEPROM=tools/trace/inputs/archives-sweep-agent.eeprom \
    SL_TICKS=/tmp/arch.ticks SL_VIS=/tmp/arch.ticks.vis \
    SL_FRAMES=1500 build/native/skeleton

SL_FRAMES counts PUMPED FRAMES, not game ticks: 320 survives, 1500
faults. Do not read a short clean run as a fix.

    SIGSEGV addr=0x43f1459f      (IEEE bits for ~482.54f)
    bgTestHitOnObj   propobj.c:8648   v->coord.x, v = vtxbase + idx
    propobjFindHit   propobj.c:8855   passes `vertices`

**Wrong claim 1: "rodata->Vertices is an unpromoted file offset."**
Measured in the promote pass: base=0xf6d86930, vertices=0xf6d86aa8 -
already a native pointer 0x178 above the base. Promoting it would have
produced 0xf7b0d3d8 and broken a working path. `sl_swap_model.c:428`
passing it straight to sl_model_vertices_swap is CORRECT.

**Wrong claim 2: "rwdata->gdl is unpromoted and that is the bug."**
It is unpromoted - measured gdl=0x50012f0, a segment address, copied
raw from rodata->Primary by modelInitRwData - but that is BY DESIGN.
propobj.c:8769 uses `rwdata->gdl == rodata->Primary` as a sentinel
meaning "nobody has replaced this", and promotes via BaseAddr at use
(8773). Promoting at init would silently defeat that comparison.

**What is actually established.** A probe at the DLCOLLISION read site,
firing only when `vertices` has a different high byte from BaseAddr,
never fired across a full run to the fault. So the vertex base handed
to bgTestHitOnObj is VALID every time, and:

    vtxbase = (Vertex *)(((s32) vertices) + padC - (op << 4));   :8507

is where the address goes wild - from `op` (and padC), which come from
walking the display list, not from `vertices`. The DL bytes or the walk
are the remaining suspects, which fits the file-header note in
sl_swap_model.c that the Gfx display lists "get their own pass".

*2026-08-24, resolved to root cause. The fix is NOT in - see the
warning at the end.*

**The opcode is read from the wrong byte.** `sl_gfx_dl_swap` rewrites
every DL command to NATIVE word order in place, so the opcode is the
top byte of a native u32 - byte 3 on x86. `bgTestHitOnObj` reads
`op = *((s8 *) gdl)`, byte 0. Measured on the walked list:

    bytes: 01 10 00 ba   byte0=01  byte3=ba   G_SETOTHERMODE_H
    bytes: 01 28 00 bb   byte0=01  byte3=bb   G_TEXTURE
    bytes: 00 00 00 e7   byte0=00  byte3=e7   G_RDPPIPESYNC

Byte 3 is real opcodes; byte 0 is low bytes. `SL_DLOP` extracts it
correctly. `ucode05.txt` in the docs confirms 04 = rsp_uc05_vertex and
warns that Rare's Tri4 diverges from F3DEX.

So `op` never equals G_VTX (0x04), the vertex branch never runs, and
`vtxbase` - assigned ONLY in that branch - is used uninitialised. That
accounts for every symptom that misled two earlier attempts: the fault
address is always a float bit pattern (stack leftovers), it MOVES when
instrumentation is added (stack layout shifts), and probes on
`vertices` and `vtxbase` stay silent because the assignment never
happens. rwdata->Vertices and rwdata->gdl were fine throughout.

Proof: with `op = (s8) SL_DLOP(gdl)` on native, the no-G_VTX probe goes
silent and the replay survives 1500 frames, exit 0.

**WARNING - do not land that one-liner alone.** With the opcode fixed
the walk starts entering branches it never reached before, including
G_DL at propobj.c:8493, and computes jump targets with `SL_DLW`, which
on native is `sl_be32r` - a BIG-ENDIAN read against native-order data.
Result: it stops crashing and starts spinning. Measured 67 minutes of
CPU on a run that takes two, no completion. A hang is worse than a
crash, so this was reverted rather than committed.

**The actual defect is that the accessors disagree:**

    SL_DLOP(p)     top byte of a native word   -> assumes NATIVE order
    SL_DLW(p,i)    sl_be32r(p + i*4)           -> assumes WIRE order
    sl_gfx_dl_swap rewrites commands           -> MAKES them native

Two of the three agree; the macros do not. The whole collision-DL
parser has to be converted in one go: opcode via SL_DLOP, word reads as
plain native `((u32 *) p)[i]`, and the byte/nibble reads (the G_VTX
count and the G_TRI2 indices around propobj.c:8505-8640) re-derived
from the native word rather than read positionally. Half-converting is
what produced the hang - and note the earlier SL_DLW/SL_DLH work,
described above as "half of it is fixed", is itself on the wrong side
of this and needs revisiting.

Also stale and worth fixing while in here: sl_swap_model.c's header
comment says the Gfx display lists are "deliberately not swapped yet".
The code swaps them.

- **data_compress.sh emits `printf: 0x: invalid hex number`** on every
  direct-boot build. Pre-existing and cosmetic - its grep for the
  `load address 0x0000000000c00000` line finds nothing, so `0x` is
  printf'd with no digits. The script's own header calls itself hacky and
  warns it breaks if the data vaddr moves. Harmless today; worth fixing
  before it hides a real failure.


### Resolution - collision-DL crash (2026-08-24)

`sl_gfx_dl_swap` rewrites every model DL command to NATIVE word order, so on a
little-endian host the opcode is byte 3, not byte 0. `bgTestHitOnObj` read
`op = *((s8 *) gdl)`. `op` therefore never matched G_VTX (04), the vertex
branch never ran, and `vtxbase` - assigned only in that branch - was used
uninitialised. Hence a fault address that was always a float bit pattern and
that MOVED when instrumentation shifted the stack, which sent two
investigations chasing `rwdata->Vertices` and `rwdata->gdl`. Both were fine.

The convention was already in the same file: `SL_OP()` reads the opcode from
the top byte of the native word, commented "room DLs are native word order
after the decompress swap", and is used four times inside this very function.
The parser was half-converted.

Fixed by converting it whole: `SL_DLB(p, word, byte)` extracts bytes
ARITHMETICALLY from the native word, `SL_DLW`/`SL_DLH` no longer read
big-endian natively, and all 11 positional byte reads now go through it. The
`__sgi` expansions are textually identical to the originals, so MATCH is
unaffected by construction - and verified.

Authority: `ucode05.txt` (04 vertex, B1 GE_TRI4 - Rare's four-triangle command
in F3DEX's G_TRI2 slot and explicitly NOT F3DEX format, BF tri1, B8 enddl;
indices are nibbles 0-F; triangles REQUIRE a vertex offset set by the vertex
command - the precondition the crash violated). `Absolute Basic Rendering
Models.txt` supplied the worked G_VTX encoding: byte 1 is `((n-1) << 4) | v0`,
word 1 is the source offset, which confirms `vtxbase = vertices + padC -
(v0 << 4)` operates on the right values.

Verified: archives-sweep-agent replays all 3750 frames, exit 0, no crash and no
spin (the earlier half-fix hung for 67 minutes). MATCH byte-identical.

Do not re-add a "DLs stay in cartridge byte order" comment. They do not.

### B-012 — a depth-1 `G_DL` resolves into 22,610 words of zeroed memory

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, measuring why the DL interpreter called 97.6% of commands unknown
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`, `seg_resolve` / the `OP_DL` arm
- **Blocks:** textures, and any confidence that what is drawn is what the game asked for

An opcode histogram splits the 26,903 "unknown" commands per frame cleanly in two.

Most of it is benign: `F5` settile, `F2` settilesize, `E7` pipesync, `BA`
setothermode_h, `E6` loadsync, `F3` loadblock, `FD` settextureimage, `BB`
texture, `ED` setscissor, `B9` setothermode_l — textbook texture-setup
sequences in sane proportion. That is the implement-next list for texturing,
not a defect.

Underneath it is a real bug. Opcode `00` accounts for **22,736 — 84.5% of all
unknowns — and `zero-words=22610`**: the walker is grinding through zero-filled
memory. Depth localises it exactly: `d0=752`, `d1=3717`, **`d2=23092`**. A
depth-1 `G_DL` is resolving its target to an unpopulated region, and
`off-command-set=1534` is byte-identical every frame, so it is the same fixed
region each time rather than drifting garbage.

Bounding the walk by the `end` pointer was tried and is NOT the fix:
`end-stops=0`, `guard-stops=0`, and the top-level list terminates correctly on
its own `B8`. The bound was kept as a cheap correctness win (depth 0 only —
`G_DL` targets legitimately live outside `[first,end)`), but the overrun is not
a top-level overrun. Suspect the depth-1 segment base.

### B-013 — `textWrap` faults in the objectives menu, but only under `SL_TRACE_OUT`

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, replaying the recorded Facility playthrough natively
- **Owner:**  Phase 1 (trace harness)
- **Where:** `src/game/textrelated.c:777` via `print_objectives_and_status_to_menu` (`src/game/front.c:6645`) via `lvlRender`
- **Blocks:** native trace capture of any run that opens the objectives menu. NOT the demo.

`SIGSEGV addr=(nil)` at `textWrap+0xa4`, reached from `lvlRender`.

Bisected, and the result is the interesting part: **the crash requires trace
capture.** The identical run without `SL_TRACE_OUT` completes all 45,000 frames,
exit 0 — twice, once under gdb and once not. So this is the harness perturbing
the run, not a gameplay defect, and the demo path is unaffected.

One inference was made and disproved, recorded so it is not made again: the
obvious suspect is `src`, since `langGet` returns NULL natively for an unloaded
bank by design (`language.c:423`, guarded and commented) and the caller does not
check it. A conditional breakpoint on `src == 0` **never fired**. `src` is not
the null pointer; `chars`, `font` or something reached through them is the place
to look. `textMeasure` is called immediately before with the same font pointers
and survives, which is suggestive but was the reasoning that produced the wrong
guess in the first place — measure it.

### B-014 — six campaign levels do not boot natively

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, first sweep of all twenty campaign levels on the native build
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (native bring-up)
- **Where:** varies; see the table
- **Blocks:** the full game as shipping scope. Facility and thirteen others were fine, so this was invisible from the vertical slice.
- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-08-25. All 6 fixed; bootsweep is 20/20 OK.

`make bootsweep` boots each campaign level natively for 400 frames. **14 of 20
reach a running sim; 6 do not.** Run 2026-08-25 against `ac34de10`:

| level | stage | result | fault site | now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| surface | 36 | SEGV | `modelLoad+0x26` | **OK** — `e24c9d9e` |
| surface2 | 43 | SEGV | `modelLoad+0x26` | **OK** — `e24c9d9e` |
| bunker2 | 27 | SEGV | `modelLoad+0x26` | **OK** — `e24c9d9e` |
| bunker1 | 9 | HANG | `sub_GAME_7F0B37EC+0x77` | **OK** — `0756ba2d` |
| streets | 29 | SEGV | `bgBuildRoomVtxBounds+0x204` | **OK** — `0756ba2d` |
| egypt | 32 | SEGV | `chrIsNotDeadOrShot+0x13` | **OK** — [[B-016]] |

Re-swept 2026-08-25 after the fixes: **20 of 20 boot.**

The three `modelLoad` failures are one bug. Measured on surface: `setupDoor`
calls `modelLoad(25127)`. The DoorRecord's first two words are `0x01000500`
and `0x01006227` — header correct (`type=1`, PROPDEF_DOOR), but `obj=25127` and
`pad=256` are **transposed**, and per-field swapping would give `obj=256`
(a plausible model) and `pad=25127` (a tag, matching the range other records
use).

**RESOLVED 2026-08-25** in commit `e24c9d9e`, and the hypothesis recorded here
first was WRONG in an instructive way — left in place because the wrong guess
is the useful part.

The guess was that a preceding record's `sizepropdef` overruns, citing the
decomp's own comments calling `SAFE`, `GAS_RELEASING` and `GLASS` wrong. It is
not that. **`sizepropdef` is correct**: it reproduces the word-count table in
`Action Block Types.txt` exactly for all 47 types, including those three. The
decomp's comments are the author's speculation and the notes contradict them —
rule 7 settling an argument the source had already lost.

The actual cause was a per-type *swapper* writing past its record.
`sizeof(CCTVRecord)/4` is 63 words; the file record is `0x3b` = 59
("06 3B Camera"). `unkEC/unkF0/unkF4/unkF8` are a four-word overhang: the
struct describes what the game READS — Rare reads past the record — but the
swapper WROTE there. On surface the camera at `0xf5d2c568` plus `0x3b` words
ends exactly at `0xf5d2c654`, whose wire header `01 00 00 05` is a type-5
ALARM; `SW32` of `unkEC` lands `05 00 00 01`, making byte 3 `0x01` =
PROPDEF_DOOR. The stride was never wrong — the advance re-reads the camera's
own type and lands correctly, then dispatches the victim on its corrupted type.

Every camera did this on every level; only the victim's first wire byte decided
whether it crashed, which is why it looked level-specific (facility and dam have
no cameras).

The invariant that came out of it: **a per-type swapper may only write inside
`[p, p + sizepropdef(p))`.** 25 compile-time stride assertions now enforce it.

`sub_GAME_7F0B37EC` also appeared in an unrelated hang on another stage, so it
may be a shared chokepoint rather than bunker1-specific.

### B-015 — live input samples state rather than latching events, so a very short press can be missed

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, verifying that firing works in the native demo
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (platform)
- **Where:** `src/platform/sl_input.c`, sampled once per presented frame from `sdl_poll`
- **Blocks:** nothing today. A human click is ~80-100ms and samples fine.

`sl_input_live_poll()` reads current key/button state once per presented frame
(~16ms at 60Hz). A press shorter than the sampling interval falls between polls
and never reaches the game.

Found by accident and worth writing down because it looks exactly like a broken
input path: `xdotool click` (press+release in ~12ms) produced **zero** `Z`
presses across two separate runs, which reads as "fire is not wired". Holding
the same button for 2s produced `button=2000` on 241 consecutive polls. The
input path was correct the whole time; the measurement was too fast for it.

Not urgent — no human presses a button for 12ms. It matters if anything ever
drives this programmatically (an automated demo, a scripted test, a replay
harness that pushes live input rather than the recorded stream), where it would
silently drop commands. The fix, if wanted, is to latch button-down events in
the SDL event loop and OR them into the frame's pad state, so a press that
begins and ends between two samples still registers once.

### B-016 — egypt: the propdef walk strides on a type byte its own swapper destroyed — RESOLVED

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, native boot sweep (B-014); root cause proven the same day
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (native bring-up)
- **Where:** `src/native/sl_swap_setup.c`, the `sl_propdefs_swap` walk
- **Blocks:** nothing. Fixed 2026-08-25; all 20 campaign levels boot.

`SIGSEGV addr=0x7` at `chrIsNotDeadOrShot+0x13`.

**Root cause, measured.** The walk takes its stride with `sizepropdef(p)` *after*
the per-type swapper has run. Word 0 carries the type byte, and several records
legitimately overlap a `u32` field onto it — `objective_entry.id` and
`setup_objective_text.unk00` both sit at offset 0. Their swappers `SW32` that
word, which is correct for the game (it reads `id` as a whole `u32`) but
destroys the type byte on the way:

```
BEFORE-SWAP off=0  type=35  sizepropdef=4   w0bytes=00 00 00 23
AFTER-SWAP  off=0  type=0   sizepropdef=1   w0bytes=23 00 00 00   <-- stride used
```

A 4-word record strides by 1. The list desynchronises, and debris inside the
OBJECTIVE_START record reads back as type `0x28` = PROPDEF_AIRCRAFT. `prop.c`
builds a phantom aircraft; its `ailist` is 0, `isGlobalAIListID(0)` is true and
`GAILIST_AIM_AT_BOND == 0`, so it resolves to `m_AimAtBond`, whose first command
dereferences `ChrEntityp` unconditionally — NULL, because `ai()` was entered as
`PROP_TYPE_OBJ`. Hence reading `actiontype` at offset 7.

The differential that rules out "egypt's data is simply like this": cradle's
real aircraft dumps pre-swap byte-for-byte as the helicopter example in
`object block types.txt`, with `03 e8` at 0x74. Egypt's "aircraft" has
extrascale 0, obj 0, and no `0x3E8`. It is not an aircraft.

**A fix was tried and REVERTED — record this before trying it again.** Taking
the stride *before* the switch (`s32 stride = sizepropdef(p);` at the top of the
loop, advancing by the saved value) is the obvious repair and it is not
sufficient: it did **not** fix egypt, and it **regressed cradle** from OK to
SIGSEGV at `0x812d9af`. So the diagnosis above is sound but incomplete — some
record's handling depends on the current post-swap stride in a way that is not
yet understood, and the walk cannot simply be switched over wholesale.

**RESOLVED 2026-08-25.** The diagnosis above was right about the mechanism and
wrong about the blast radius, which is exactly why the stride-first repair
failed.

**The measurement that explains both levels.** Instrumenting the walk to log
offset / pre- and post-swap type / pre- and post-swap `sizepropdef` / words 0-1
for every record, on every campaign level:

```
egypt   off=20  pre_t=23 pre_sz=4  post_t=0 post_sz=1   pre_w=17000000 -> post_w=00000017
cradle  off=20  pre_t=23 pre_sz=4  post_t=0 post_sz=1   pre_w=17000000 -> post_w=00000017
```

egypt and cradle desynchronise **identically** - same offsets, same six records
(five type-35, one type-23). Every campaign level does; they all have objective
text. The walk then drifts one word at a time through the mostly-zero objective
payload and re-reads word 2 of the OBJECTIVE_START record as a header. Word 2 of
an `objective_entry` is `reserved:u16, text:u16` - the briefing string ID - so
the type byte the walk picks up is the high byte of a text ID:

| level | word 2 of OBJECTIVE_START | phantom type | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| egypt | text=`0x280c` | `0x28` PROPDEF_AIRCRAFT (45 words) | fatal |
| cradle | text=`0x241f` | `0x24` PROPDEF_GAS_RELEASING (32 words) | survivable |

So "egypt's data is different" was never the difference. **Every level builds a
phantom object out of its own briefing-text ID**; only egypt's string ID happens
to begin `0x28`, and only an aircraft reaches `m_AimAtBond` with a NULL
`ChrEntityp`. The differential in the original entry (cradle's real aircraft vs.
egypt's fake one) was measuring the symptom, not the cause.

**Why stride-first did not fix egypt, and broke cradle.** The swap walk is not
the only consumer of that buffer. `prop.c:68`, `prop.c:2004`,
`loadobjectmodel.c:267/296/324/539` and `cleanup_objects.c:81` all re-walk it
with `sizepropdef()`. Saving the stride before the switch fixes the *walk* but
leaves the type byte destroyed *in memory*, so every later consumer desyncs at
the same six records and rebuilds the same phantom - egypt crashes unchanged.
Cradle regressed because the corrected walk stops visiting `off=22` as a
32-word GAS_RELEASING, so those words are no longer swapped, and prop.c's own
desynced walk then hands `domakedefaultobj` an unswapped record instead of a
swapped one.

**The fix** (commit below, `src/native/sl_swap_setup.c`): stop the five
swappers writing word 0. `objective_entry.id`, `setup_objective_text.unk00` and
`criteria_roomentered/deposit/picture.unk00` are `u32` **aliases of the
PropDefHeaderRecord**, not fields. The game says so itself -
`objective_status.c:179` does

```c
for (objective = &objective_ptrs[n]->id; objective->type != PROPDEF_OBJECTIVE_END;
     objective = sizepropdef(objective) + (PropDefHeaderRecord *) objective)
```

taking the *address* of `id` and reading `->type` through it.
`grep -rn -- '->id\b' src/game/ src/*.c` returns exactly two hits, both in
`objective_status.c`, **both address-of** - `id` is never read as a value
anywhere in the tree, so leaving it unswapped costs nothing.

**THE WORD-0 INVARIANT** (now stated in the file, sibling of THE INVARIANT):
*word 0 of every propdef record is the PropDefHeaderRecord, and
`sl_swap_PropDefHeaderRecord` is its only permitted writer.* THE INVARIANT
bounds a swapper's writes to `[p, p + sizepropdef(p))`; this one carves out
bytes 2-3 of word 0 *inside* that range, because the walk and five other
consumers still need them.

**The open question is closed: no record's stride is knowable only post-swap.**
Across 5731 records on all 20 campaign levels, every stride equals the
`Action Block Types.txt` word-count table, and no type ever showed two different
strides. Stride is a pure function of the pre-swap type byte.

**Verified:** `tools/native/build.sh` clean; **bootsweep 20/20 OK** (egypt
stage 32 now exit 0, cradle stage 41 still OK); `make matching` MATCH!;
`make trace-verify LEVEL=facility` IDENTICAL, 15869 ticks, schema v13.

**Latent hazard found while measuring, not fixed here.** The walk dispatches
`PROPDEF_UNK41` (type `0x29`) to `sl_swap_ObjectRecord`, which writes 32 words
and zeroes the runtime slots - but `Action Block Types.txt` gives `29  1  N/A`
and `sizepropdef` returns 1 (it has no case for it, so it falls to `default`).
That is a 31-word overrun and a straight THE INVARIANT violation. It has never
fired because **type `0x29` does not occur in any campaign level**: zero records
across all 20 levels' walks. The `SL_STRIDE(ObjectRecord, 0x20)` comment listing
`29` among its types is wrong for the same reason. Types `0x0f`, `0x10`, `0x1f`
and `0x30` are likewise absent. Worth correcting before any multiplayer or
custom setup is loaded natively, where the assumption does not hold.

### B-017 — the render is wrong: black spiky shards, near-black scene

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, the first time anyone actually saw this renderer (`SL_SHOT`)
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`, vertex decode and/or colour path
- **Blocks:** the demo looking like GoldenEye. It runs, it does not look right.

Every software-side metric says the renderer is healthy: unknown opcodes 0,
916/916 triangles textured, 46 textures decoded with zero failures, matrices
resolving with `unresolved=0`, 76% of vertices inside the clip volume, zero GL
errors. **All of that was true while the picture was wrong**, which is the
lesson worth keeping — the telemetry measured that commands were consumed, not
that they were interpreted correctly.

What the capture actually shows at 640x480, Facility, ~frame 80-120:

- Correct letterbox bars top and bottom.
- Real 3D structure with depth and shading — this is not noise.
- **Dominated by tall, thin, black spiky shards** radiating upward, which is
  not level geometry.
- **Near-black overall** (frame mean 0.079 and 0.115) despite every triangle
  reporting as textured.
- Exactly one small blue/teal patch that does look like a correctly applied
  texture.

Two independent hypotheses, neither confirmed:

1. **Vertex field transposition.** A vertex is 16 bytes = four words
   `{s16 x,y,z; u16 flag; s16 s,t; u8 r,g,b,a}`. The interpreter now sniffs each
   list's word order and vertex data inherits the order of the list that names
   it. If a wire-order list's vertices are word-swapped, the `s16` pairs inside
   each word TRANSPOSE — x↔y, z↔flag, s↔t. Structurally-present-but-distorted
   geometry is exactly what that produces, and this is the same transposition
   family behind B-014, the gas-tank fix and the door corruption. Swapping a
   4-byte region that holds two 16-bit fields has now caused three separate bugs
   in this codebase.
2. **Colour/combiner.** `texenv=prim-replace` with `rgb-const=PRIM`: if the
   primitive colour is dark or the modulation is wrong, textured surfaces go
   black while still counting as textured.

`SL_SHOT=<prefix> SL_SHOT_EVERY=<n>` now makes this directly observable — check
against the picture, not only the counters.
**RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — and neither hypothesis was right.** The cause was the
**GE_TRI4 (B1) index decode**, a third possibility nobody listed. Both
hypotheses above were tested and cleared by measurement:

- *Vertex transposition:* the per-field `SL_SW16` in `OP_VTX` is already the
  correct operation (not a word swap), and the 04 command's two redundant
  length fields agree in 3360 of 3360 Facility commands and 3900 of 3900 dam
  ones, which they could not do under a transposition.
- *Colour/combiner:* forcing a flat white vertex colour changed the image not
  at all. The colour path is not what darkens the scene.

The actual bug: `ucode05.txt` and "Absolute Basic Rendering Models.txt" both
document B1 as `B100zzzz yxyxyxyx` — four z indices in nibbles 0-3 of the
UPPER word, four x/y pairs in nibbles 0-7 of the LOWER word. The interpreter
instead read all eight indices as one run of nibbles straddling both words,
starting at w0 bit 19. Since bits 16-23 of w0 are structurally zero — measured
8340/8340 on Facility, 9000/9000 on dam — **one triangle in every four was
pinned to vertex 0 of the batch**. That fan of degenerate slivers anchored on a
single point is precisely the "tall thin black spiky shards"; the other three
triangles per command were permutations of real-but-wrong indices, which is why
surfaces half-formed instead of vanishing. The note's "if all the points are
set to 0, that triangle is not drawn" rule was also missing, so zero-filled
unused slots were being drawn as real triangles on vertex 0.

BF (`G_TRI1`) was wrong the same way — it read its indices from w0, which is
`0xBF000000` in every such command, so every one drew the degenerate {0,0,0}.
Corrected from the note (indices are in w1, each divided by 0xA); not exercised
by either level measured (`tri1=0`), so corrected-by-note, not by measurement.

After the fix, Facility resolves into two recognisable cylindrical tanks, a
shaded pillar, a wall slab and the teal console; dam gains a visible door and
detail on its structure and regresses nowhere.

### B-018 — textures decode to rainbow swirls — FIXED 2026-08-25

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, while fixing B-017; a genuinely separate defect
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Fixed:**  2026-08-25 — the palette address, not its contents or order
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` texture path and/or `sl_gfx_tex.c`, CI/TLUT
- **Blocks:** the demo looking like GoldenEye. Geometry is right; surfaces are not.

With B-017 fixed, geometry is coherent and the remaining defect is isolated:
character models and level surfaces are covered in smooth magenta/cyan/orange
rainbow swirls (severe on Facility, milder speckling on dam's roof). What has
been ruled out by measurement:

- **Not the colour/combiner path.** Forcing `glColor4ub(255,255,255,255)` for
  every vertex produced a byte-comparable image. The rainbow is in the texel
  data.
- **Not the odd-row swizzle alone.** Decoding with `SL_TEX_FLAG_ROWSWAPPED`
  cleared still produces rainbow, only a slightly different one.
- **Not format misclassification.** The (fmt,siz) histogram of tiles at draw
  time pairs *exactly* with the TLUT mode: fmt 3 and 4 (IA/I) account for
  precisely the G_TT_NONE draws and fmt 2 (CI4/CI8) for precisely the
  RGBA16+IA16 ones — 21120+3360+120 = 24600 = mode-0 count in one frame, and
  (2,1)=5280 = 1920+3360 in another. Format and palette-mode tracking agree.

That leaves the CI/TLUT *contents* as the prime suspect: right indices, wrong
palette. `g_tlut_addr` is set to "whatever the current FD image points at" at
F0 loadtlut time and is a single global, so a stale or mis-resolved palette
would give exactly this — spatially structured output in nonsense colours.
Byte order or stride within the RGBA16 palette entries is the other candidate.
Next step is to dump a decoded texture to a PPM and look at it beside its
palette, the same way B-017 was settled.

**Resolution.** The suspicion was right about *which* palette and wrong about
*why*: the address was wrong, not the byte order or the stride. `g_tlut_addr`
was set to the current `FD settextureimage` address, so every CI texture was
"decoded" against the first 32/512 bytes of its own pixel data.

GoldenEye emits exactly ONE `settextureimage` for a paletted texture — at
`tex->data` — then `loadblock`, then `loadtlut` against that same still-current
image (src/game/tex.c:522-552, repeated at tex.c:632-670 and
othermodemicrocode.c:455-479, :595-616). Tree-wide, `grep -rn "gDPLoadTLUT"
src/` returns those four sites plus textrelated.c's two `gDPLoadTLUT_pal16`
(Japanese font — which does set its own FD, so uls=0) and front.c's one
`gDPLoadTLUTCmd2`; no GE path re-points the image between the block load and
the palette load. The palette therefore lives INSIDE the texture buffer, `uls`
texels past its start — tex.c:533 sets `uls = len`, the byte length of the
texel data itself — and the uls/ult split below it is only the 10-bit field
limit, so the offset is the SUM.

Authority for the packing: ucode05.txt's `F0 rdp_loadtlut` entry ("upper word
00FFF000 x0, lower 07000000 tile / 00FFF000 count / 00000FFF palette start"),
confirmed exactly by this tree's own emitter, `gDPLoadTLUT07(a,b,c,d)` at
include/gbi_extension.h:162, which writes `w0 = a<<14 | b<<2` — i.e. uls =
a<<2 in 10.2 fixed, the standard tile-load encoding. Entry count is
`lrs - uls + 1 = tex->unk0a + 1 = numcolours` (image.c:202, :215).

**Measured, not argued.** A new `SL_TEX_DUMP=<prefix>` writes each decoded CI
image beside both candidate palettes — the one the F0 names and the one the FD
base would have given. On dam the second is confetti of saturated cyan/magenta/
green; the first is a coherent GoldenEye ramp, and the images decode to a green
wall panel, a grey concrete band and a brown slatted wall. The computed offsets
land exactly on each image's full mipmap-chain size — 760 bytes for a 32x32 CI4
(512+128+64+32+16+8) and 1400 for a 32x32 CI8 (1024+256+64+32+16+8) — which is
an independent arithmetic confirmation that the palette begins immediately
after the texel data. `fd-w=1` in the new `sl_tex: tlut` telemetry confirms the
FD width the offset formula divides by.

Two things fell out of it. The F0's entry count is now honoured instead of the
format's 16/256, so a short palette no longer reads whatever follows it in the
texpool (counts observed on dam: 11, 13, 16, 19, 29, 36, 42, 47, 71, 80, 127,
183). And the texture cache now keys on the palette pointer as well as the
source, which it did not before.

### B-019 — room geometry has never rendered natively — RESOLVED 2026-08-25

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, looking for a *rendering* cause and not finding one
- **Owner:**  Phase 2, but the defect is upstream of `src/gfx/`
- **Where:** `OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL` (`include/PR/os.h`) and the `G_DL`/`G_VTX`
  operand resolution in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`. See the resolution note at the
  end of this entry — the title above is the corrected one; the original was
  "the pause/watch screen submits a display list with no geometry", and both
  the screen it named and the frame range it blamed were wrong.

Boot Facility and wait. Around DL frame ~600 the screen settles into a flat
field with correct letterbox and nothing else, and stays byte-identical.

This was filed as a 2D/texrect problem — "225 texrects per frame, all drawn,
all textured, zero rejects", with coordinate space, primitive alpha and draw
order as the candidates. **All three are ruled out, and so is the premise.**
The 225-texrect frame is a DIFFERENT frame: it is the level-title card, and it
renders its text correctly (`m-00003`, 1780 distinct colours, "Chemical Warfare
Facility #2" legible at the right size and position). The blank frame reports
`texrect cmds=0`.

What the blank frame actually reports, from DL frame 601 onward:

```
sl_dl:  frame 601 cmds=489 vtx=0(rej=0) tris=0 unknown=0
sl_walk: lists=2/2(native/swapped)  per-depth: d0=455 d1=34
sl_mtx: cmds=20 ... unresolved=0
sl_2d:  texrect cmds=0   fillrect cmds=7 drawn=6 coverage=100.0%
sl_tex: loadblocks=4  tris textured=0  distinct textures drawn=0
```

489 commands, 20 matrices, 4 texture block-loads, 6 fill rects — and **zero
vertices, zero triangles, zero texrects**. There is nothing to mis-place,
mis-tint or cover. On a live frame `d1` carries ~1100 commands; here it carries
34, so the branch structure is present but the branches that should hold the
screen's content are empty or not taken. The walk itself is healthy:
`unknown=0`, `zero-words=0`, `end-stops=0`, `guard-stops=0`, `unresolved=0`.

Two experiments, both negative, recorded so they are not repeated:

- **Nothing is covering it.** Suppressing every fill rect leaves the frame a
  single flat colour — the GL clear — with one distinct colour in the capture.
  With fills on, the capture has exactly two: the fill and the letterbox. No
  geometry pixels exist in either case.
- **It is not rasterisation.** `sl_tri` (new, see below) reports
  `covering=0 degenerate=0 clipped=0` — the renderer is not dropping
  triangles, it is never given any.

Likely a segment or menu-DL pointer the native shim never populates, or menu
state that never advances because nothing presses a button. Start in the game
code that builds that list, not in `src/gfx/`.

**New guard.** `sl_tri: window-area px covering/degenerate/clipped` measures
the window-space area of every triangle emitted. This bug wore the most
dangerous disguise there is — every counter healthy, nothing on screen — and
cost this investigation a wrong intermediate conclusion ("732 triangles produce
zero pixels", read off a stale telemetry block). A vertex inside the NDC cube
says nothing about whether the triangle covers a pixel; `sl_tri` says it
directly.


**Narrowed further 2026-08-25 (owner session), two hypotheses killed by measurement:**

- **Not missing text banks.** `langGet` was the obvious suspect: it returns NULL
  natively for an unloaded bank by design and B-013 already involved it. Broke on
  it across 1400 frames: **4 calls total, all bank 3, none returning NULL.** A
  menu drawing text would call it constantly, so nothing is being starved of
  strings.
- **Not a menu render path at all.** `lvlRender` is called **699 times** across
  the same run. The game is running the LEVEL render path on the blank frames,
  not a front-end one. (`frontRender` does not exist as a symbol — a first
  attempt to break on it failed, and because gdb rebinds a bare `commands` block
  to the previous breakpoint, the failure initially read as 699 `frontRender`
  hits. The number belongs to `lvlRender`. Noted because the misreading is easy
  and the corrected run is the one to trust.)

So on the blank frames the game is in-level, rendering, and emitting zero
vertices and zero triangles. The leading hypothesis is now **room/portal
visibility culling**: `bgRenderRoomPrimary`/`bgRenderRoomSecondary` draw rooms
selected by the camera's current room and portal visibility, and a camera that
resolves to no valid room draws nothing at all. That would also explain why
pressing Enter/E restores geometry — it re-enters the level and puts the camera
back in a room.

Worth noting the adjacency: bunker1's HANG (fixed in `0756ba2d`) was a
special-portal table walked past its end, and streets' SIGSEGV was room DL
opcodes read from the wrong byte. Room and portal handling has already produced
two native-only defects, so a third is plausible rather than surprising.

Next step: instrument the room selection — how many rooms are visible per frame,
and what room the camera resolves to — across the transition at frame ~601.


**RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — and the premise was wrong twice over.**

The room/portal hypothesis is dead, and so is the framing. Instrumenting
`bgDetermineVisibleRooms` and `bgRenderRoomPrimary` across the transition
(native-only, `SL_ROOM_LOG`, since removed) showed the visibility pipeline
working perfectly the whole time: `g_BgNumberOfRoomsDrawn` is never 0 — it is
2 on every blank frame — the camera resolves to a real room (13, then 14),
`bgRenderRoomPrimary` reaches its emit branch for **both** rooms every frame
(`calls=2 noload=0 emit=2`), and walking each room's expanded mapping-info DL
from the game side found well-formed lists of 118 and 92 commands opening
`E7 BA B9 FC BA BB` and ending at a real `G_ENDDL`.

What actually changed at frame ~601 is the camera mode: `CAMERAMODE_SWIRL` →
`CAMERAMODE_FP` (measured, `cam=3` → `cam=4` at visibility call n=561). And
what it changed was `chrpropsRenderPass`, whose per-frame contribution drops
from 219 commands to 6 — Bond's own body leaves the on-screen prop list when
the first-person camera takes over. **That was the only thing on screen.**

The captures settle it. `f-00002` before the fix is the bottling-room tanks
floating in a flat dark-green void — no floor, no walls, no ceiling. `f-00012`
is Bond's model alone in the same void. Room geometry had **never** rendered
natively; every world pixel ever seen came from props and characters, and the
screen went fully blank at the moment the last character stopped being drawn.
The "empty frame from 601" was the symptom of a bug that had been total since
the first native frame.

Root cause, in two halves, both measured:

1. `OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL` (`include/PR/os.h:848`) is `(u32)((char *)(x) -
   0x80000000)`. On N64 that relabels a KSEG0 address as the physical address
   behind it; natively there is one flat address space, which is exactly why
   the shim already makes `osVirtualToPhysical` the identity
   (`src/platform/sl_ultra_shim.c:387`). The macro was never given the same
   treatment, so every DL operand built through it came out 0x80000000 below
   the real pointer. Measured: `bgRenderRoomPrimary` emitted the room list
   living at `0xc8354890` as `0x48354890`, and the vertex segment base for
   `0xc8352210` as `0x48352210`. `OS_PHYSICAL_TO_K0` is the mirror of the same
   mistake (`options.c` hands it pointers that are already host pointers).

2. `seg_resolve()` (`src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c:297`) reads bits 24-27 as a segment
   index unconditionally, and `G_DL` and `G_VTX` were the only two operands
   still going through it bare. Both `0x48354890` and the corrected
   `0xc8354890` land on "segment 8" — a segment nothing in the tree ever sets
   (`grep -rn gSPSegment src/ --include=*.c` sets only 0,1,2,3,4,5,14,15, and
   `SPSEGMENT` has no 8 at all) — so `g_seg[8] == 0`, the target became NULL,
   and `if (t) walk(...)` dropped the entire room display list in silence.
   The two sibling resolvers in the same file already had the right ladder:
   `mtx_resolve` (line 313) and `tex_operand` (line 336) try the segment form
   **only** when the top nibble is clear and that segment has actually been
   set, then fall back to the raw host pointer and to the K0 form. Its own
   comment names the trap — "keeps a raw `0xc8xxxxxx` pointer from being
   mistaken for segment 8" — and `G_DL`/`G_VTX` simply never got it.

Fix: `#ifdef __sgi`-guard the four address-translation macros so the native
build gets the identity (the matching build's text is untouched, and it still
MATCHes), and give `G_DL` and `G_VTX` the same resolution ladder via a new
`dl_operand()` next to its two siblings.

Effect, same run, same frames:

```
                  before                         after
frame   1   cmds=1842 vtx=1084 tris=648    cmds=3228 vtx=3949 tris=2218
frame 241   cmds=1425 vtx=814  tris=498    cmds=2548 vtx=3362 tris=1889
frame 601   cmds=489  vtx=0    tris=0      cmds=734  vtx=661  tris=358
```

`f-00002` after the fix is the bottling room as a room: tiled floor, grated
ceiling with skylight panels, wall pillars, a mezzanine with railing and a
staircase, the tanks now standing on a floor instead of in a void. `f-00013`
is the intro camera on Bond's head with the cross-braced airlock door and its
rivets rendered behind him. The formerly blank FP frames show the door filling
the view at point-blank range — Bond spawns facing it and nothing is pressed;
consecutive captures have different MD5s, so the surface is live, not stale.

Two notes for whoever is next in this area:

- **The frame range in the original entry was a red herring, and so was the
  screen name.** There is no pause/watch screen involved; `lvlRender` was
  right, and the 699 calls were real. Frames 1-600 looked "live" only because
  props and characters were drawn, and that is precisely the "green counter
  beside a wrong image" trap this file keeps warning about — every renderer
  counter was healthy because the renderer was faithfully drawing everything
  it was given.
- **Look at the picture before trusting the delta.** The decisive evidence was
  not a counter at all; it was noticing that the "correct geometry" in the
  early frames had no floor under it.

### B-020 — font glyphs decode corrupted; text layout is correct — FIXED 2026-08-25

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, first playtest after room geometry started rendering
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Fixed:**  2026-08-25 — the odd-row swizzle, applied where it does not belong
- **Where:** font glyph decode / sampling — `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` call site, or the font asset path
- **Blocks:** reading any menu. The player cannot navigate what they cannot read.

Opening the watch (Start) renders correctly in every respect except the glyphs:
the watch face, its coloured ring segments and hands are clean and correctly
placed, and the 2D path reports healthy.

**Text layout is right; the glyph bitmaps are wrong.** Word count, word lengths,
spacing, baseline and colour all match the controller-options screen — the
default control style the boot path selects. Enlarged 3x, each character is a
blocky, partially-formed shape rather than a letter. So the text pipeline is
placing the right glyphs in the right places and drawing corrupted pixels.

That narrows it to the glyph source rather than the text engine:
- Font characters are intensity/alpha formats (I4/I8/IA4/IA8). A wrong format
  code, bit depth, or row stride at the call site corrupts glyphs while leaving
  placement untouched — which is exactly this signature.
- The odd-row swizzle is the other candidate, and note the corpus is **silent**
  on it (recorded `not_covered`); authority is Rare's own `texSwapAltRowBytes`
  (`image.c:2168`).
- The font DL lives in the segment that arrives in WIRE order — the interpreter
  sniffs per-list word order and reports `lists=18/2`. Font glyph DATA may need
  the same treatment as the list that names it, or may need none.

Worth checking against the assets the Makefile already knows about
(`font_chardatae`, `font_chardataj`, `jfont_chardata`) for the declared format.
The decoder itself is well tested and is the exact inverse of Rare's swizzle
routine; as with B-018, the likely fault is the call site handing it the wrong
format or dimensions, which its unit tests structurally cannot see.

**Resolution.** The third candidate was the right one, and — as with B-018 —
the decoder was correct and the CALL SITE handed it the wrong thing. Format,
depth, stride and word order were all already right: the ASCII glyphs are I8
with a `(width + 7) & 0xF8` stride, which `textrelated.c:243` states outright
and the notes' font microcode generator (`7F0AD0F8`, "settile.u: i 8bit",
`line = ceil(width)/8`) independently confirms. `tex_acquire` was passing
`SL_TEX_FLAG_ROWSWAPPED` **unconditionally**, so the glyphs were unswizzled
when they were never swizzled to begin with.

Measured before changing anything, which is what settled it in one step: the
0x5E small-font glyphs read straight out of the ROM table at 0x2E63F0 (entry
layout from `images text and font/Fonts/ASCII Font table entries.txt`: +0x8
height, +0xC width, +0x14 image offset) and decoded as I8 are legible letters
with the swizzle OFF, and are exactly the blocky half-formed shapes above with
it ON.

The discriminator is one field of the F3 loadblock, its **dxt**, and both sides
are source-cited rather than inferred:

- World textures — `src/game/tex.c:514` and `:530`,
  `gDPLoadBlock(gdl++, 7, 0, 0, len - 1, 0)`: dxt is the literal 0, so the load
  never advances a row and swaps nothing, while the fetch still swaps odd rows.
  Net odd-row swap, which Rare pre-compensates for in the asset itself
  (`texSwapAltRowBytes`, image.c:2168, from :237, :277, :289, :293, :987,
  :1036, :1047, :1051).
- Font glyphs — `src/game/textrelated.c:243` goes through
  `gDPLoadTextureBlock`, which `include/gbi_extension.h:252` expands to
  `gDPLoadBlock(..., CALC_DXT(width, siz##_BYTES))`: never 0, so load and fetch
  cancel and the data is plain. Glyph data also never passes through image.c at
  all — it is `romCopy`'d raw out of the font table — so there is nothing to
  pre-compensate for.

So the fix is one condition at the call site: pass `SL_TEX_FLAG_ROWSWAPPED`
only when the loadblock's dxt was zero. Per-frame telemetry
(`sl_tex: loadblock dxt=0 N dxt!=0 M`) reports 76-97 dxt=0 loads against 1
otherwise in gameplay, rising to 26 with the watch open — the glyphs, and
nothing else, take the new path.

Verified by looking: the watch reads `Q WATCH V2.01 BETA` /
`MISSION STATUS: INCOMPLETE` / `ABORT: CANCEL CONFIRM` / `Mine (Remote)`, and
the dam intro caption reads `Byelomorye Dam, Arkangelsk, USSR`, so both the
small and the large font tables are fixed. Dam and Facility world textures are
unchanged. `make matching` MATCHes, `trace-verify LEVEL=facility` is IDENTICAL
across 15869 ticks, headless emits no renderer telemetry, and bootsweep is
still 20/20.

### B-021 — character models deform: limbs scatter, the matrix stack is never used

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, visual survey; re-diagnosed the same day after looking closely
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` — matrix flag decode and the `BD popmatrix` filter
- **Blocks:** every character in the game looking right. Guards are the most visible thing in a level after the level itself.

**This entry was filed wrong the first time** ("guards may sit slightly below the
floor"). That was one frame judged by eye at full-frame scale. Enlarged 2.5x it
is not a placement problem at all:

- The guard's **head and torso are correct** — face, green uniform, red shoulder
  epaulettes, all cleanly textured.
- The **lower body is fragmented** — legs scattered into loose polygons.
- **Hands are detached** and floating away from the arms.

That is skeletal deformation, not floor height. Recorded as a correction rather
than a silent edit, because "trust the enlargement, not the thumbnail" is the
same lesson as "trust the image, not the counter".

**The measurement that fits it is already in hand.** Every windowed run reports:

    sl_mtx: ... load=51 mul=0 push=0 pop=0 ...

**`push=0 pop=0` in every frame of every run — the matrix stack is never used.**
GoldenEye composes character bone transforms hierarchically with matrix
push/pop; with no stack, each limb receives an absolute transform instead of one
composed through its parent, and the limbs fly apart. That is exactly the
observed signature: the root (torso/head) is right and everything downstream of
a joint is wrong.

Two specific suspects, both introduced with the matrix work in `b6a6910b`:

1. **The `BD popmatrix` filter may be too aggressive.** That commit notes a
   `gImmp1` check (all low 24 bits clear) which "removed 8 phantom popmatrixes
   per frame". There were 8 `BD` commands a frame and ALL were rejected. If any
   were real, the stack can never pop.
2. **The push bit may be misread.** The same commit established from
   `ucode05.txt` that bit0 = projection, bit1 = load, bit2 = push — overruling a
   brief that used gbi.h's `F3DEX_GBI_2` values. If push is still being read
   from the wrong bit, no command ever looks like a push.

`mul` is 0 or 2 depending on the frame, which is also low for a scene with
articulated characters.

Next step: log every `01` and `BD` command with its raw words and decoded flags
across a frame containing a guard, and check the rejected `BD`s against the
notes rather than against the filter that rejected them.

**RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — and the matrix stack was a red herring.**

Both guards in the reference captures now render intact: complete legs, boots on
the ground, hands attached and gripping the barrier. Looked at, at 2.5x, on the
same two crops the diagnosis was written from.

`push=0 pop=0` is **correct for this game**, not a symptom. GoldenEye composes
bone hierarchy on the CPU — each node's local transform is multiplied by its
parent's into `model->render_pos` via `matrix_4x4_multiply_homogeneous`
(`model.c:1783`, with the parent resolved by `modelFindNodeMtx` above it) — and
issues the result as absolute `G_MTX_LOAD | G_MTX_NOPUSH` matrices. Tree-wide,
`grep -rn "G_MTX_PUSH" src/ include/` and
`grep -rn "gSPPopMatrix\|gsSPPopMatrix\|G_POPMTX" src/ include/` return nothing
outside `gbi.h` and the interpreter's own comments. There is no stack to use, so
neither suspect (the `BD` filter, the push-bit decode) was load-bearing. Both
were left alone. The notes do carry a `BD` operand layout after all
(`ucode05.txt` l.629), which the interpreter's comment said they did not — but
every field in it is annotated "Perfect Dark:", so it changes nothing here.

The actual cause was two faults in the **vertex** path, both in
`src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`:

1. **`v0` was hardcoded to 0 and its bits folded into the length check.**
   `ucode05.txt`'s Rare vertex table reads bits 16-19 as the top nibble of a
   20-bit byte count; they are really the destination slot. Measured on a
   streets guard frame: 513 of 513 commands had `(w0 & 0xffff) == n*16`, only
   476 matched on 20 bits, and the 37 that differed were exactly the 37 with a
   non-zero `v0` — and exactly the 37 the length check was rejecting. Facility
   and dam measure 0, which is why this hid for so long. The 37 come from one
   call site: `dotube` (`model.c:4686`), the tube renderer that draws character
   limbs, which loads a tube's proximal ring at `v0 = 0` and the rest at
   `v0 = 2`. Dropping that second load is the scattered legs and floating hands.

2. **Vertices were transformed at draw time, not at load time.** The RSP
   transforms a vertex when the `04` loads it, using the modelview then in
   effect; a later `01` does not reach back. That is exactly how a limb deforms
   with no matrix stack — `dotube` loads the two ends of a tube under two
   different bone matrices. Applying the current matrix at draw time gave both
   ends the second bone's transform, so with fault 1 fixed the limbs stretched
   and a spike came out of one shoulder. The modelview is now applied at load
   (`g_veye`) and GL's own modelview is held at identity.

Verified: `make matching` MATCHes; `trace-verify LEVEL=facility` IDENTICAL over
15869 ticks; headless emits zero renderer telemetry; `bootsweep` 20/20; Facility
and dam captures unchanged in character against the survey below.

### B-022 — native audio: the mixer is RSP microcode, and nothing executes an ACMD list

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, wiring the SDL audio seam and un-excluding `src/audi.c`
- **Owner:**  the T6 "port the synthesis library" work the `#ifndef __sgi`
  guards in `src/snd.c` and `src/music.c` already name
- **Where:**  `src/audi.c:522` (the seam), `src/libultra/audio/synthesizer.c:143`
  (`alAudioFrame`), `src/music.c:652`, `src/snd.c:118`
- **Blocks:** all native sound. Not the vertical slice's renderer work.

The seam itself is now closed and inert. `osAiSetFrequency`/`osAiGetLength`/
`osAiSetNextBuffer` are implemented in `src/platform/sl_ultra_shim.c` on top of
`src/platform/sl_audio.c` (one SDL2 queue-driven device). A tree-wide
`grep -rn "osAi" src/ tools/ include/` finds four call sites outside libultra,
all in `audi.c`, and `grep -rn "AI_DRAM_ADDR|AI_LEN_REG|AI_STATUS" src/` outside
libultra is EMPTY — so that is the whole boundary. Measured: a Facility run
submits ZERO buffers.

Three walls sit behind it, in the order they must fall:

1. **Nothing executes the command list.** `alAudioFrame` does not mix; it builds
   an ACMD list (16 opcodes, `include/PR/abi.h`) for the `aspMain` RSP
   microcode, and hands the RSP a DRAM pointer to write PCM into. The CPU never
   touches a sample. `aspMainTextStart`/`aspMainDataStart` are stubs. Producing
   PCM natively means an ACMD interpreter, roughly 700+ lines: ADPCM decode with
   predictor codebook, polyphase resample with 16-tap state, envelope mixing,
   aux bus, interleave.

   **Whether that is in scope is the owner's call, not this entry's.** The project
   rules list "RCP emulation or static recompilation" under *Explicitly out of scope*,
   and an ACMD interpreter is RSP microcode work by any plain reading. The
   argument on the other side is that `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` already interprets
   display lists, and an ACMD interpreter is its exact audio counterpart — so
   either the rule already has an unstated carve-out for "interpret the command
   list rather than emulate the processor", or the display-list interpreter is
   itself a departure that happened to be useful. That distinction has never
   been written down, and it should be settled deliberately rather than by
   precedent accumulated in a backlog entry. **Do not start this work without
   the owner deciding.**
2. **The banks are big-endian and nothing swaps them.** `alBnkfNew`
   (`src/music.c:676`) relocates ROM offsets but does not byte-swap;
   `grep -rn "ALBankFile|ALWaveTable" src/ --include=*.c` outside libultra finds
   only declarations. A `sl_swap_bank.c` is needed alongside the existing
   `sl_swap_model.c`/`sl_swap_setup.c`.
3. **The sound-off switch is sim-visible.** `g_sndBootswitchSound` is forced to 1
   natively (`src/snd.c:118`) and is read by ~50 sites in `src/game/` via
   `sndGetPlayingState` — `chrai.c`, `chraction.c`, `propobj.c`, `gunfire.c`,
   `bondview2.c`. Turning it off changes AI branching, so enabling audio must be
   gated to live play or it will diverge traces.

One trap is recorded because it cost a boot: the whole `al*` library compiles
`-m32` clean (37 + 3 files) and linking it drops the native stub count 59 → 33,
but it must NOT be linked before init runs. `musicSeqPlayerInit` early-returns
natively, so `g_musicXTrack1SeqPlayer` stays NULL, and `musicTrack1ApplySeqpVol`
— which has no bootswitch guard — reaches real `alCSPSetVol`/`alEvtqPostEvent`
and faults on `&seqp->evtq` at offset 0x48, via `lvlStageLoad`. The `return 0`
stubs are what currently absorb that. `tools/native/build.sh` carries the same
note.

The docs are silent here and that is now recorded: `docs/doc-routing.json`
gained a `not_covered` entry for the audio microcode / ACMD command set — a
content grep of all 465 notes for `acmd|aspMain|ADPCM|envmixer|aResample` matches
zero files. `include/PR/abi.h` is the authority instead.

**The oracle now exists — 2026-08-28.** Before any mixer is written, the
yardstick it will be judged against is in place, because "it sounds right" is
not a standard this project accepts.

```
tools/native/audiopair.py --input facility --frames 900 --out /tmp/pair
```

drives the SAME recorded input stream through the cartridge and the native
build and prints both sides through one shared metric implementation
(`tools/native/audiocap.py`), so a difference is attributable to the mixer
rather than to the measurement. `romshot.py` gained `--audio-out`/`--no-video`;
it needed no new plumbing, because `emu_libretro.py` already routed
`retro_set_audio_sample_batch` to an `_on_audio_capture` hook that only the
recorder was using. No new dependency: stdlib only, and `audioop` was
deliberately avoided as a deprecated-and-slated-for-removal landmine.

Measured on 900 frames of the facility stream — cartridge side: 320312 stereo
frames, peak 14540, rms 1804.66, 72.96% non-zero, onset at frame 82064
(3.842s), 83/313 blocks silent, PCM sha1 `0e104db06b5e68…` reproducible across
runs. Native side: **zero bytes**, and the game's own accounting agrees ("no
buffers were ever submitted"). The mechanism behind that zero is now pinned
rather than assumed: `musicSeqPlayerInit` spans `music.c:627-786` and its
native early return at line 652 sits *before* `amStartAudioThread()` at line
784, so the audio thread never starts and `amHandleFrameMessage` — the only
caller of the three `osAi*` entry points — is never reached.

Three controls, because a tool that can report "none" has to first prove it ran:

1. **The cartridge is the positive control.** If the ROM side comes back
   silent the harness is broken, and `audiopair` exits non-zero rather than
   reporting a comparison.
2. **The native READER is self-tested** on synthetic PCM with known peak,
   frame count and channel asymmetry — the ROM path arrives through `wave`, the
   native path through raw bytes, so the ROM control does not exercise it.
   Verified non-vacuous against two deliberate breaks (forcing `silent`,
   swapping the channel de-interleave); it caught both. It cannot catch an
   endianness misconfiguration by construction, and says so — the
   `rms_byteswapped` figure is the diagnostic a human reads for that.
3. **The native build's execution is evidenced** by "survived N pumped frames",
   so a boot crash cannot be mistaken for a silent mixer.

Two rate facts, both measured, both counter-intuitive, and the first CORRECTS a
comment standing in this tree:

- parallel_n64 declares **32040Hz through frame 33 and revises itself to
  22047Hz at frame 34**, the point GoldenEye configures the AI. So the declared
  rate is a stock N64 default early and essentially CORRECT later (`audi.c`
  `OUTPUT_RATE` is 22050). `record_libretro.py` samples it before the run and
  therefore sees 32040; its conclusion — measure, do not trust the declared
  rate — still holds, but the premise "the core reports 32040" is only true
  early.
- The rate measured from samples-per-video-frame is **~21360Hz, about 3% under
  both declarations, and that gap is NOT explained.** It is recorded here
  precisely so nobody later reports it as a mixer defect. Do not treat the
  wav's rate as settled.

Captures are ROM-derived and live under `/tmp`; nothing audio is committed.
Verified alongside: `make matching` MATCH!, `trace-verify LEVEL=facility`
IDENTICAL over 15869 ticks. Nothing under `src/` was touched.

**ACMD census and stages 1-3 — 2026-08-28.** `tools/native/acmd_census.py`
decodes the command stream the real game generates, read out of cartridge RDRAM
between `alAudioFrame` (`audi.c:537`) and `osSendMesg` (`audi.c:561`). The
native build has no stream to census: `alAudioFrame` is a stub and
`musicSeqPlayerInit` returns at `music.c:652` before `amStartAudioThread` at
`:784`. Two runs produced byte-identical output, so it is reproducible.

Measured over 900 facility frames: 435 audio frames, 555-1036 commands each,
5 sub-frames per audio frame. **15 of 16 opcodes are exercised; only `SPNOOP`
is never used.** Continuous in 435/435 frames: `SEGMENT` (exactly 5), `MIXER`
(exactly 95), `POLEF` (exactly 25), `INTERLEAVE` (exactly 5), plus `SETBUFF`,
`LOADBUFF`, `SAVEBUFF`, `CLEARBUFF`, `DMEMMOVE`, `RESAMPLE`, `LOADADPCM`.
Voice-specific: `ADPCM` 304/435, `ENVMIXER` 317/435, `SETVOL` 122/435,
`SETLOOP` 17/435.

Two measurements that overturned assumptions. All 25 idle `LOADADPCM` are
immediately followed by `POLEF` (25/25), so in a zero-voice frame they load
**pole-filter coefficients, not voice codebooks**. And `RESAMPLE` is
**output-chain, not voice**: the 5 per frame share one state address, run at
`UNITY_PITCH` (`abi.h:262`) with +-1 for drift, and are the rate correction
`audi.c:529` negotiates. An earlier plan of mine put `RESAMPLE` in the voice
stage, contradicting the census that measured it in 435/435 frames; that was
wrong and the 118 zero-voice frames cannot execute without it.

Every one of 107657 `addr` fields is PHYSICAL (below 8MB, zero in KSEG0), and
every `SEGMENT` carries base 0. So a native interpreter needs a subtraction,
**not** segment machinery. DMEM operands stay inside 0x0000-0x0800.

`src/platform/sl_acmd.c` (~260 lines) implements stages 1-3 only and refuses
any other opcode loudly rather than skipping it. `tools/native/acmdreplay.sh`
replays each captured zero-voice frame against the DRAM the cartridge had
before it, comparing only the bytes the list itself writes.

compared 1.33M bytes of which **zero were nonzero** - they prove cadence,
lengths and addressing, and prove nothing about arithmetic, because silence
cannot exercise it. All 86812 nonzero compared bytes fall in the 9 late
reverb-tail frames, and 75450 of them differ. **The custom FX is therefore NOT
numerically reproduced**, which is expected: `POLEF` is left as identity rather
than guessed at, since `abi.h` gives only `POLEF_STATE` as `short[4]` and the
filter lives inside the microcode the corpus does not document.
