### B6/B7 culling is decoded and correct, and still off — 2026-08-25

`SL_CULL=1` applies the geometry-mode cull bits with the sense the window
settled (`sl_gfx_dl.c`, the block above `cull_apply`). It stays off by default
and this is the reason, so nobody re-derives it:

The bits are live. `g_geom_seen` is `001f3205` on streets, dam, archives and
Facility; cull-back is set at triangle 0 and toggles all frame; 91–98% of
triangles are emitted under it, including 127 of 128 wall-sized ones on streets
and 394 of 412 on dam. The world is backface-culled, not just props and glass.

The sense is settled by looking. Sense 2 (GL winding opposite the RSP's) loses
the road, the building fronts and the guards' faces on streets — the level
becomes a hollow shell seen from inside. Sense 1 leaves the scene intact.

Sense 1 is still not purely a fix, which is why it is not the default:

- it *removes* back faces that were bleeding through — on archives a flat grey
  slab that occluded the left third of the roof truss goes away and the trusses
  become continuous;
- it *opens* holes where this renderer has nothing behind the face it drops —
  a wedge of far wall on archives, a wedge of hillside on dam, both showing
  through to black or sky.

0.4% of pixels change on streets, dam and Facility; 6% on archives; in both
directions.

The holes are not a winding bug in the B1 decode, which was the cheapest thing
to rule out and was ruled out: winding agreement measured on the *indices*,
over every pair of triangles in a vertex batch sharing an edge, is 2402:5,
1690:0, 2077:2 and 1137:0 across the four levels. Rare's data is consistently
wound and the decode preserves it. So the RSP would have dropped those surfaces
too, and whether a console shows the same holes is a question this repository
cannot answer without a reference frame.

To re-open it: `SL_CULL=3` culls nothing and draws only what sense 1 would have
dropped, which is the picture that makes the argument. What would settle it is
a hardware or emulator reference frame for the two spots above — until then
rule 5 decides, and the default is Rare's behaviour.

#### DMEM coordinates were wrong, and a cancelling error hid it (2026-08-29)

Every handler that takes a RAW DMEM address operand adds `0x5c0` to it before
use. Measured in the microcode, not assumed:

```
SETBUFF    blob 0x26c  addi at,k0,1472 / addi v0,v0,1472 / addi v1,t9,1472
CLEARBUFF  blob 0x164  addi a0,zero,1472 ; add v0,v0,a0
DMEMMOVE   blob 0x398  addi v0,v0,1472 / addi v1,v1,1472
INTERLEAVE blob 0x31c  addi v1,v1,1472 / addi v0,v0,1472
MIXER      blob 0xd5c  addi s3,s3,1472 / blob 0xd64 addi s4,s4,1472
```

The count field is NOT shifted (`sh t9,4(t8)`, blob 0x294). LOADADPCM's
destination is an ABSOLUTE `0x4C0` (blob 0x22c `addi at,zero,1216`), as is
ADPCM's codebook base (blob 0x490).

The interpreter had been using raw operands everywhere. That was invisible
because the error CANCELLED: MIXER's operands were unshifted too, so every
address lived in one consistently-relabelled space. Adding `0x5c0` to
SETBUFF/CLEARBUFF/DMEMMOVE/INTERLEAVE while leaving MIXER raw broke the
validated result — 118/118 byte-exact fell to 109/118 with 71414 differing
bytes, RMS 92.86 — and shifting MIXER too restored it to 118/118, 0 differing,
RMS 0.0000.

This mattered only once ADPCM arrived, because `0x4C0` is BELOW `0x5c0`: an
absolute codebook cannot coexist with relative buffers. Measured: with buffers
at raw offsets, landing the LOADADPCM payload at `0x4C0` clobbers a live buffer
and all 118 frames go wrong (8314 bytes differing). At `0x5c0` it is disjoint
and the numbers are identical with the book DMA on or off.

Isolation, all four configurations measured:

```
BUFBASE=0     book DMA off  118/118 exact  0 differing  RMS 0.00   (prior result reproduced)
BUFBASE=0     book DMA on     0/118 exact  8314         RMS 300.17 (codebook lands in a buffer)
BUFBASE=0x5c0 book DMA off  109/118 exact  71414        RMS 92.86  (MIXER left raw)
BUFBASE=0x5c0 book DMA on   118/118 exact  0 differing  RMS 0.0000 (MIXER shifted - accepted)
```

The first line is the control that proves nothing ELSE regressed.

Note the 118 figure is 109 frames that write nothing observable plus **9
non-vacuous frames**; the bracket-validity guard reports the 9 separately, and
those 9 are what the 71414 differing bytes were concentrated in. "118/118"
should always be read with that denominator in mind.

#### ADPCM and SETLOOP, derived from the microcode with every constant measured

SETLOOP (blob 0x3cc, nine instructions): resolve the segmented `w1` via the
table at DMEM 800, store to the audio state block at `+0x10`, return. It
touches nothing else.

ADPCM (blob 0x3f0..0x688). Frame = 9 bytes -> 16 samples -> 32 bytes.
Header low nibble = predictor (x32 from `0x4C0`), high nibble = scale.

Constants read out of `bin/aspboot.data.bin`, not chosen:

```
DMEM 0x30   four masks isolating successive nibbles of a halfword
              (v25 low half, v24 high half)
DMEM 0x38   four scalers renormalising each nibble to the top four bits
              (v23, both halves)
DMEM 0x00   the shared constant vector: one element is the VSAR
              recombine multiplier (32), another the current-residual
              tap (2048)
```

Mask x scaler is IDENTICAL in all four lanes, so an unpacked residual is
`signed4 << 12` and the sign extension is free — there is no sign logic in the
handler because none is needed. That the two independently-read tables multiply
out to the same single value in every lane is the check that the pairing
was read correctly.
Recurrence, per 8-lane half, with `b1 = book[0..7]`, `b2 = book[8..15]`:

```
acc[j] = b1[j]*prev2 + b2[j]*prev1 + SUM(i<j) b2[j-1-i]*r[i] + r[j]*0x800
out[j] = clamp_s16( wrap_int32(acc) >> 11 )
```

`b1` multiplies `v27[14]` and `b2` multiplies `v27[15]` — broadcast elements 6
and 7, so the OLDER sample takes the first table. The seven shifted operand
vectors `v19..v13` are LRV loads from `t5+30, +28, ... +18`, which fill only the
right-hand lanes and leave the rest at the `VXOR` zero from the preamble; that
is the lower-triangular convolution matrix, built by addressing rather than by
arithmetic.

`wrap_int32` is not a convenience. `VSAR` reads the 48-bit accumulator as
HIGH:MID and the recombine is `32*MID + (32*HIGH << 16)`, then `>> 16` — which
reconstructs exactly the low 32 bits of the sum taken as signed. Nine products
of two s16 can exceed 32 bits, so the wrap is reachable and is reproduced.

Scale: `a0 = 0x8000 >> (11 - scale)` and `VMUDM` takes the top 16 of the
product, giving `r << scale`. **Guarded by `blez` on `12 - scale` (blob 0x554):
at scale >= 12 the multiply is SKIPPED**, leaving the residual at `<< 12`
instead of `<< scale`. Reproduced, not corrected — rule 5.

Layout, which is easy to get wrong: the 32-byte incoming state is DMA'd to
`dmemout` and decoded frames start at **`dmemout + 32`** (blob 0x4a8 advances
`s3` before the loop). The prefix is deliberate — it is the history a following
RESAMPLE reads. Writeback is 32 bytes from `s3 - 32` to the resolved `w1`,
**always**: `A_LOOP` redirects the INPUT only (blob 0x460's delay slot sets the
source to `s1` unconditionally). Zero count branches straight to the writeback
with `s3` already advanced, so it still writes 32 bytes — `A_INIT`+0 writes
zeros, plain+0 copies the state back, `A_LOOP`+0 copies the LOOP state into the
normal address.

#### Grounded input model: three numbers, and they are equal

The previous predictor statistics were withdrawn as unsafe because the walking
tool zero-initialised DMEM and executed only byte movers, so an unmodelled
arithmetic writer left stale bytes and the walk INVENTED headers. Rebuilt with
provenance: every DMEM and DRAM byte carries a value and a grounded flag; exact
byte movers copy both; DMEM starts wholly UNGROUNDED; and every arithmetic
writer INVALIDATES its exact output range rather than leaving a stale value
live. ADPCM's own output is tainted too — the evaluator under test may never
ground a later frame's input. ENVMIXER's write range is not yet derived, so it
taints ALL of DMEM.

```
executed frames                      : 21857
  header grounded                    : 21857
  all nine compressed bytes grounded : 21857
  + coefficient bytes grounded       : 21857
```

**"Fully evaluable = 21857" is WITHDRAWN pending incoming-state provenance.**
The figure above establishes only that the compressed bytes and the codebook
entry are grounded. A frame is not fully evaluable until the 32-byte INCOMING
STATE it mathematically depends on is also grounded, tracked chronologically:
`A_INIT` gives grounded zero by handler semantics, a plain continuation depends
on the current 32 bytes at `s1` whose last writer may be an earlier ADPCM or
captured task-start DRAM, and `A_LOOP` depends on the bytes at the last SETLOOP
source AT THE MOMENT ADPCM READS THEM. Until that is per-command, the honest
denominators are two, not three.

Predictor histogram, over grounded headers only, maximum predictor 3:

```
pred 0 : 20405     pred 1 : 528     pred 2 : 616     pred 3 : 308
```

3732 multi-frame commands: 3456 hold the predictor constant, **276 change it**,
maximum 4 distinct predictors within one command. 34 commands carry a
non-multiple-of-32 count (smallest 4), contributing 144 frames; all 34 final
partial frames are fully grounded, and they decode a full 9-byte frame to a
full 32 bytes.

The taints are not vacuous — they destroy 4059128 (MIXER/POLEF/RESAMPLE),
268800 (ADPCM output) and 1639932 (ENVMIXER) grounded bytes. They simply never
destroy a byte a later ADPCM consumes.

Controls, seven, the last five non-discriminating and reported as such:

```
C1 baseline strict                        21857 / 21857 / 21857
C2 DRAM confers no grounding              21857 /     0 /     0   <- collapses
C3 ADPCM output taint removed             unchanged   -> ADPCM never feeds itself
C4 POLEF/RESAMPLE taint removed           unchanged
C5 ENVMIXER ignored entirely              unchanged   -> its unknown range reaches no ADPCM input
C6 LOADADPCM disabled                     21857 / 21857 /     0   <- discriminates on coefficients
C7 MIXER taint removed                    unchanged
```

C2 and C6 are the ones that bite, and they bite on exactly the axis they
target.

#### ENVMIXER's DRAM footprint, derived - which settles the question properly

The withdrawal below stands, and it was right: ENVMIXER **does** reach DRAM.
Its handler carries the SAME two DMA calls as ADPCM (`jal 0x184` read at blob
0xb04, `jal 0x1b0` write at 0xd2c), against a control disassembly of ADPCM
showing the identical pair. So "it cannot contaminate DRAM" was never available.

What IS available is the footprint, and it is bounded without deriving any of
ENVMIXER's arithmetic - the DMA address and length are three instructions:

```
0ac0  and v0,t9,a0 / 0acc lw a2,800(a1) / 0ad0 add v0,v0,a2   -> segaddr(w1)
0ad4  addi at,s7,0                                            -> DMEM 0xF90
0ad8  addi v1,zero,79                                         -> 80 bytes
0af4  beq t2,zero  (t2 = flags & A_INIT)                      -> read SKIPPED on A_INIT
0d30  addi v1,zero,79                                         -> 80 bytes written back
```

**ENVMIXER's entire DRAM footprint is 80 bytes at `segaddr(w1)`** - its own
state block, read at entry unless A_INIT and written back at exit. Nothing else
reaches DRAM. That converts the contamination question from "derive ENVMIXER"
into a pure ADDRESS census, which is the localisation asked for.

Result: modelling that exact 80-byte taint changes **nothing** - all 4427 ADPCM
commands stay fully evaluable. ENVMIXER's state blocks are measurably DISJOINT
from every DRAM range ADPCM depends on.

That is only worth anything with a non-vacuity control, because an inert taint
and a disjoint one look identical. Widening ENVMIXER's DRAM taint to ALL of
DRAM collapses the population:

```
                              derived 80-byte    all-DRAM control
ADPCM commands                     4427               4427
compressed+codebook grounded       4427                294
incoming state grounded/determined 4427                344
FULLY EVALUABLE                    4427                255
frames in those commands          21857               1940
```

The control's 255 is independently corroborated: a separate command-ordering
census counts 4427 ADPCM commands of which 4172 are preceded in the same task
by an ENVMIXER, leaving exactly **255** that are not. Two unrelated
measurements agreeing on 255 is what makes the DRAM grounding path credible
rather than merely permissive.

Note each task re-anchors from the captured before-image, so only WITHIN-task
ordering can contaminate; cross-task contamination is measured away by the
capture itself.

#### Incoming-state provenance, per command and chronological

`A_INIT` gives grounded zero by handler semantics. A plain continuation depends
on the 32 bytes at `s1` at the moment ADPCM reads them; `A_LOOP` on the bytes at
the last SETLOOP source. ADPCM's writeback is never marked GROUNDED - it is the
evaluator under test - but it is marked DETERMINED when every input to that
command was grounded, so a continuation chain stays evaluable without laundering
unknown data into it.

```
ADPCM commands                      : 4427
compressed+codebook grounded        : 4427
incoming state grounded/determined  : 4427
FULLY EVALUABLE commands            : 4427
frames in fully evaluable commands  : 21857
state kind: A_INIT 105  A_LOOP 19  continuation 4303
            ungrounded 0, of which chain-determined 3448
```

Three distinct denominators, as required: executed **21857**;
byte/codebook-grounded **21857**; grounded-incoming-state **4427 commands /
21857 frames**. 3448 commands take their state from an earlier ADPCM writeback,
which is why the chain distinction had to exist at all.

**WITHDRAWN: "ENVMIXER's underivedness is not currently blocking."** C5 shows
only that ignoring ENVMIXER's DMEM writes changes nothing. Tainting all of DMEM
is conservative for unknown **DMEM** outputs and says NOTHING about a possible
DRAM DMA or writeback, which is the path that would actually contaminate an
ADPCM input: LOADBUFF re-grounds a DMEM byte FROM DRAM, so a DRAM byte an
earlier unmodelled ENVMIXER wrote would be laundered into "grounded" by exactly
the mechanism C2 shows is load-bearing. The claim is withdrawn until ENVMIXER's
DRAM writes are known. Until then, any compressed byte or incoming state whose
DRAM source could have been written by a preceding unmodelled ENVMIXER is
**unresolved unless writer chronology proves otherwise**. ENVMIXER is not to be
derived as a side quest; the population affected is to be localised instead.

Scope, stated because it limits everything above: 435 tasks, one capture. The
21857 is the microcode-derived executed-frame count on THAT capture.

#### Dual-evaluator cross-check - ADPCM ACCEPTED and enabled (2026-08-29)

`tools/native/acmdvoicex.c`. Three evaluators, sharing only measured INPUTS
(command words, the grounded 9-byte frames, the grounded 32-byte codebook
entry, the grounded incoming state, the resolved loop address):

- **A** - literal transcription of the vector sequence: 8 lanes, products
  accumulated as `(a*b)<<16` into a 48-bit accumulator, VSAR HIGH and MID
  extracted as separate 16-bit slices and recombined by `x0x20` then `>>16`.
  Residual scaling goes through the VMUDM emulation.
- **B** - scalar, derived separately. History is a FLAT sample-indexed array,
  not per-half vector elements. Residual scaling is written directly as
  `signed4 << scale`, never through VMUDM. The shift is a plain `>>11` on a
  32-bit sum, never through VSAR.
- **P** - the SHIPPED interpreter, `src/platform/sl_acmd.c`. Added because A
  and B are both harness code, and two harnesses agreeing says nothing about
  what the production decoder does.

B therefore disagrees with A if the VMUDM reasoning, the VSAR recombine, or the
per-half history mapping is wrong. They share no residual, no accumulator, no
decoded sample, no history and no final state; each carries its own frame-N
output into frame N+1 and its own writeback into the next command continuing
the chain, from its own state image.

```
ADPCM commands total                      : 4427
commands fully grounded                   : 4427
frames executed / fully evaluable         : 21857 / 21857
  positive non-multiple-of-32 counts       : 34  (smallest 4, 144 frames)
samples compared                          : 349712
SAMPLE MISMATCHES                         : 0
FINAL-STATE MISMATCHES                    : 0
P (shipped interpreter) sample mismatches : 0
P command exec failures                   : 0
```

Seven controls, every one firing, so none of the zeros above is vacuous:

```
Q11 -> Q10                          349156 sample, 4387 state
Q11 -> Q12                          349303 sample, 4387 state
coefficient b2[0] += 1              239903 sample, 4291 state
A_LOOP reads normal s1                1138 sample,   15 state
A_LOOP writes loop addr               1086 sample,    5 state
history reset each frame            337065 sample, 4368 state
VACUITY: corrupt P's state only     211737 P-sample, A-vs-B still 0
```

The `A_LOOP writes loop addr` control is scored where it matters: within the
command the two evaluators still agree, so its 1086 sample mismatches come
entirely from LATER commands continuing the chain and reading the address that
was not updated - a dependent consumer, not changed destination metadata. The
final control proves P actually executes; without it, `P mismatches: 0` would
be indistinguishable from P never running.

The 34 commands carrying a **positive non-multiple-of-32 count** are inside
the accepted population, so full-final-frame behaviour is exercised rather than
assumed. To be exact about what that population is: 34 commands, **smallest
count 4**, **144 decoded frames** between them. It is NOT the case that all 34
counts are below 32 - most are larger counts with a non-zero residue, and only
the residue exercises the partial-frame path.

**ADPCM is now enabled by default** (`SL_ACMD_ADPCM` flipped to 1). Zero-voice
oracle re-run with it on: 118/118, all 9 non-vacuous frames byte-exact.

#### SETVOL derived, and an aliasing hazard it exposes in SETLOOP (2026-08-29)

Handler blob 0x2a8..0x308. **Pure state writer: no arithmetic, no DMA, no DMEM
access.** Five disjoint field groups in the audio state block at `t8` (0x360),
selected by two flag bits, every store a 16-bit `sh`:

```
flags & A_AUX (0x08)        t8+0x1C = w0 low,  t8+0x1E = w1 low
A_VOL|A_LEFT  (0x04|0x02)   t8+0x06 = w0 low
A_VOL|A_RIGHT (0x04)        t8+0x08 = w0 low
A_RATE|A_LEFT (0x02)        t8+0x10 = w0 low,  t8+0x12 = w1 high, t8+0x14 = w1 low
A_RATE|A_RIGHT (0x00)       t8+0x16 = w0 low,  t8+0x18 = w1 high, t8+0x1A = w1 low
```

Flag names from `include/PR/abi.h:56-67` (`A_VOL` 0x04, `A_RATE` 0x00, `A_LEFT`
0x02, `A_RIGHT` 0x00, `A_AUX` 0x08). Volumes are a single halfword per side;
rates carry three halfwords per side. Width is 16 bits by the store;
SIGNEDNESS is not determined here - `sh` says nothing about it - and must come
from the consumer, so it stays open until ENVMIXER is read.

The capture emits SETVOL in complete sets: exactly **206 of each** of the five
flag combinations, 1030 commands total. That uniformity is a structural fact
about the emitter, not an assumption.

**The hazard.** `A_RATE|A_LEFT` writes `t8+0x10` and `t8+0x12`. SETLOOP writes
a 32-bit `sw` at `t8+0x10` (blob 0x3e4), covering `t8+0x10..0x13`. **They are
the same storage.** A SETVOL(A_RATE|A_LEFT) between a SETLOOP and an A_LOOP
ADPCM would therefore destroy the loop address on hardware, and a SETLOOP would
equally destroy the left rate that a later ENVMIXER reads.

Measured on this capture: **0 hazards.** No A_LOOP ADPCM (19 of them) has a
SETVOL as the last writer of `t8+0x10`. So the ADPCM acceptance above is not
affected here.

**But the interpreter is not faithful to it.** `loop_addr` is a separate C
field, so SETLOOP and SETVOL cannot alias no matter what a command list does.
That is a latent divergence, currently unobservable. The correct fix is to
model the state block as actual overlapping storage rather than as named
fields, and that is the right thing to do WHEN SETVOL is implemented - doing it
now would be an unverifiable change to an accepted path. Recorded here so it is
not rediscovered.

#### SETVOL implemented, and the state block made real storage (2026-08-29)

The five field groups derived above are implemented exactly as the handler
branches, in its own test order. Two things that would each have been a quiet
bug:

**`flags == 0` is a real combination.** `A_RATE` is 0x00 and `A_RIGHT` is 0x00,
so a right-channel rate SETVOL carries flags of exactly zero and selects
`t8+0x16..0x1A`. It is not "no flags", not a default, and not a skip. The
emitter emits one of these per segment start, so treating zero as absent would
have silently dropped every right-channel rate.

**The state block is now REAL DMEM** at `SL_ACMD_STATE` (0x360), not named C
fields. `in`, `out`, `count`, the aux trio and the loop pointer were removed
from `sl_acmd_state` and are read and written through `sl_acmd_sget/sset`. This
is what makes the SETLOOP/SETVOL aliasing reproducible at all: with named
fields the clobber was structurally impossible, which is a worse failure than
getting it wrong, because no test could ever detect it.

Second control in `tools/native/acmdauxctl.c`, scored on the storage itself:

```
after SETLOOP 0x123456           t8+0x10 = 0x00123456
after SETVOL A_RATE|A_RIGHT (0)  t8+0x10 = 0x00123456   rate R at 0x16 = 0xbeef
after SETVOL A_RATE|A_LEFT  (2)  t8+0x10 = 0x11112222   loop address destroyed
after SETLOOP 0xABCDEF           t8+0x10 = 0x00abcdef   0x14 = 0x3333 survives
```

The surviving `0x14` is the detail worth keeping: SETLOOP's `sw` covers
`0x10..0x13` only, so it destroys two of the left rate's three halfwords and
leaves the third. A control that only checked "the loop address changed" would
have passed against a wrong overlap width.

Effect on coverage: SETVOL has disappeared from the blocker list. First-failure
counts on the 435-task capture go from 301 ENVMIXER + 16 SETVOL to **317
ENVMIXER and nothing else**. Still first-failure counts, not execution coverage.

#### Reconnaissance corroborations (independent of the microcode derivation)

- `ENVMIX_STATE[40]` at `abi.h:266` is **80 bytes**, independently matching the
  80-byte DRAM footprint derived from the DMA length at blob 0xad8. Two
  unrelated routes to the same number.
- The five SETVOL combinations are a fixed complete set emitted behind a single
  condition at segment start, which is why the census found exactly 206 of each.
- The corpus is a **clean negative** on the audio microcode, reproduced
  independently rather than taken from the existing `not_covered` entry.
- The three relevant files are byte-identical with upstream - nothing to rebase.

Three cautions recorded for the ENVMIXER work, none acted on yet:

1. The emitter's flag field is **16 bits wide**, not 8, and masks before
   shifting - a flags value >= 0x100 would spill into the opcode byte. All call
   sites pass <= 0x0C so it is harmless here, but the encoding is not a clean
   8-bit field. The C struct declares 8 bits, so **struct and emitter disagree**;
   the struct is decorative and is not an encoding authority.
2. Producer-side signedness is **asymmetric** - rate mantissas signed, rate low
   words unsigned, volumes and targets signed. This is a prior for reading
   ENVMIXER, not a settlement: the consumer decides, and if the microcode treats
   the low words as signed that is a divergence to flag, not to smooth over.
3. `alEnvmixerNew` assigns the **left** rate mantissa and low word twice and
   never assigns the right pair, leaving them uninitialised. That copy/paste
   bug is a fact and, under rule 5, gets reproduced rather than corrected.
   **Narrowed:** it does NOT follow that emitted first-segment rate commands are
   contaminated - `_pullSubFrame` recomputes both immediately before the
   first-segment SETVOL emission, so the uninitialised pair is overwritten
   before any emission reads it. No claim of contamination is made unless a
   concrete earlier consumer is found.

Still underived: ENVMIXER's ARITHMETIC and consumer-side signedness. Its
STRUCTURE is now mapped, below.

#### ENVMIXER structure - what it consumes and where it writes (2026-08-29)

Structure only. No arithmetic is derived here and none is implemented; the
opcode still fails loudly. This is the map needed to stop tainting all of DMEM.

Reads of the audio state block (blob 0xb30..0xbe0), all measured:

```
lh  t5, 0(t8)    dmemin            lh  s2, 10(t8)   A_AUX SETBUFF +0xA
lh  s3, 2(t8)    dmemout           lh  s1, 12(t8)   A_AUX SETBUFF +0xC
lh  t6, 4(t8)    count             lh  s0, 14(t8)   A_AUX SETBUFF +0xE
LSV v20[14], 3(t8)   -> t8+0x06 = SETVOL volume LEFT   (LSV offset scales by 2)
LSV v18[14], 4(t8)   -> t8+0x08 = SETVOL volume RIGHT
LQV v24[0],  1(t8)   -> t8+0x10..0x1F, the whole rate/target block, on A_INIT
```

**This answers what the auxiliary SETBUFF's three addresses mean.** They are
three additional DMEM OUTPUT buffers. ENVMIXER's `SQV` stores go to exactly
four destinations - `s3` (the normal dmemout) and `s2`/`s1`/`s0` (the three aux
addresses) - plus `s7` = 0xF90, the 80-byte ENVMIX state scratch that is DMA'd
back to DRAM at exit. So the opcode mixes one input into four output buffers.
The reconnaissance reached a wall here and declined to guess; the handler
settles it, and the earlier decision to keep the aux trio positional rather than
named was the right one to hold until now.

That makes the DMEM write range derivable: `count` bytes at each of the four
buffers, plus 80 bytes at 0xF90. The grounding model's conservative "taint ALL
of DMEM" can be replaced with that once it is confirmed against the store
addressing, which is the next bounded step.

**The LQV at 0xaf8 raises the aliasing stakes.** On A_INIT, ENVMIXER loads 16
bytes from `t8+0x10..0x1F` as a vector - the entire rate and target block. That
is the same storage SETLOOP's 32-bit store lands in. So SETLOOP does not merely
collide with a SETVOL field in the abstract: it corrupts the exact block
ENVMIXER's initialisation path reads. The hazard census found 0 occurrences of
the ADPCM-facing direction on this capture, but the ENVMIXER-facing direction
has not been censused and must be before ENVMIXER is trusted.

#### Task-state writer chronology, and the deferred measurement finally taken

**A disassembler bug found first, before it could mislead.** `/tmp/rsp/dis.py`
computes `j`/`jal` targets 0x80 too high (branch targets, being PC-relative,
are correct). ENVMIXER's `j 0x0bb0` is really file offset 0xb30. Consequence:
A_INIT skips ONLY the 80-byte state DMA and then rejoins at `lh t5,0(t8)`,
reading in/out/count/aux exactly as CONTINUE does - rather than skipping those
reads entirely, which is what the uncorrected target implied. Nothing already
derived is affected: ADPCM, SETLOOP, SETVOL and CLEARBUFF were all derived from
BRANCH targets, and the only `j` in each is the dispatcher return.

**WITHDRAWN - the first chronology census was SYNTACTIC, not control-flow
sensitive, and its headline numbers were wrong.** It counted every `(t8)` load
in the handler as if all of them execute on both paths. They do not:

- `beq t2,zero,0xc48` at blob 0xb6c means CONTINUE **skips blob 0xb70..0xc44**,
  and both volume loads live inside that block (`LSV v20[14],3(t8)` at 0xb84 and
  `LSV v18[14],4(t8)` at 0xbe0). They are **A_INIT-only consumers**.
- The delay-slot `LQV v24,1(t8)` at 0xaf8 does execute on CONTINUE, but v24 is
  **redefined at 0xb2c** by `LQV v24,4(s7)` from the 80-byte state, before its
  first use at 0xb4c (`mfc2 s5,v24[2]`). On CONTINUE that read is **DEAD**.

Withdrawn specifically: the 4283 CONTINUE volume consumers, the 4283 CONTINUE
rate/target consumers, the 12849 aggregate, and every conclusion resting on
them.

Rebuilt with control-flow and reaching-definition semantics - a read counts
only if it executes and its value reaches a use:

```
  field         A_INIT: live/task-start/dead   CONTINUE: live/task-start/dead
  in               206 /    0 /    0             5528 /    0 /    0
  out              206 /    0 /    0             5528 /    0 /    0
  count            206 /    0 /    0             5528 /    0 /    0
  aux+A            206 /    0 /    0             5528 /    0 /    0
  aux+C            206 /    0 /    0             5528 /    0 /    0
  aux+E            206 /    0 /    0             5528 /    0 /    0
  vol L            206 /    0 /    0                0 /    0 / 5528
  vol R            206 /    0 /    0                0 /    0 / 5528
  +0x10..0x1F      206 /    0 /    0                0 /    0 / 5528

  LIVE task-start reads, all fields, both paths : 0
```

**There is no live task-start dependency on either path.** A_INIT's live
consumers are all preceded in-task by the complete SETVOL set; CONTINUE's live
consumers are the SETBUFF fields plus the five vectors reloaded from the
80-byte DRAM state.

**So the bytes were measured rather than assumed.** A targeted capture over
0x5d000..0x5d800, 185 frames:

```
distinct 32-byte task-start state blocks at 0x5d380 : 1
value                                               : all 32 bytes zero
```

With a known-positive control, because an all-zero read is exactly what a dead
buffer also looks like:

```
window liveness       41.7% of bytes nonzero; 164 of 184 frames differ
aspMainData region    595/704 nonzero   <- the microcode data, where expected
rmonThread +0x00..9f   14/160 nonzero   <- thread struct, partly live
rmonThread +0xa0..bf    0/32  nonzero   <- the state block
```

The zero sits between two regions of live nonzero data, so it is a real
measured value.

**DEMOTED.** The exact claim this supports is only: *at the capture snapshot
point, those 32 source bytes read zero across 185 frames, with a non-vacuous
live-window control.* It is **not** "the exact bytes the task DMA delivers into
DMEM at task start" - the snapshot precedes execution and the source is live
thread storage, so timing equivalence was never proven. After the control-flow
correction above there is **no live task-start consumer at all**, so this is not
load-bearing and no further timing instrumentation is warranted.

#### ENVMIXER write spans, derived from the complete output loop

Initial pointers, all from the state block: `t5`=in(+0x00), `s3`=out(+0x02),
`s2`=aux(+0x0A), `s1`=aux(+0x0C), `s0`=aux(+0x0E), `t6`=count(+0x04), `t7`=16.

**The `t7` branch matters.** If ENVMIXER's own A_AUX is CLEAR (blob 0xb58
`bgtz t1`), then `s1 = s7+80`, `s0 = s1`, and `t7 = 0` - the two aux
destinations are redirected to a 16-byte scratch and never advance, so those
writes are discarded. With A_AUX set they are real buffers advancing by 16.

Per group, in the steady-state loop (blob 0xc50..0xd18):

```
loads    LQV v17,0(t5)  and the four destinations LQV from s3,s2,s1,s0
stores   SQV 16 bytes to each of s3, s1, s2, s0
         plus envelope scratch SQV v20@s7+0, v21@s7+16
advance  s3 += 16, s2 += 16, t5 += 16 ;  s1 += t7, s0 += t7
count    t6 -= 16   (blob 0xce4)
branch   blez t6 -> exit   (blob 0xd10) - decrement FIRST, no pre-test
```

**WITHDRAWN: "A_INIT writes one group more than CONTINUE for the same count."**
The peeled block decrements the counter, so it IS the first counted group, not
an extra one. Traced from the control flow:

```
  count   A_INIT   CONTINUE   count/16
    320       20         20         20
    224       14         14         14
    192       12         12         12
    160       10         10         10
     96        6          6          6
     64        4          4          4
     32        2          2          2
```

**For the entire measured population (counts 32..320, all divisible by 16) both
paths execute exactly `count/16` groups and each active output receives exactly
`count` bytes.**

The paths DO diverge below the measured range, and that asymmetry is derived
from control flow rather than from a rounding formula: A_INIT peels a group and
then enters the loop body, which stores before testing, so

```
  count 16 :  A_INIT 2 groups,  CONTINUE 1 group
  count  0 :  A_INIT 2 groups,  CONTINUE 1 group
```

A single rounding expression cannot describe both paths, so none is used. No
measured count reaches this region, which is why the current grounding survives.

Census of what the capture actually exercises, which is where the honesty is:

```
ENVMIXER commands                 5734
  A_INIT=0 A_AUX=1                5528
  A_INIT=1 A_AUX=1                 206
count residues mod 16             ALL ZERO (5734/5734)
zero counts                       0
count range                       32 .. 320  (mode 320, 4340 commands)
```

**Every command has A_AUX set and every count is a multiple of 16.** So:

- the `!A_AUX` scratch-redirect path is **unexercised** - 0 commands;
- the rounded-tail rule is **unexercised** - no non-multiple count exists;
- the zero-count path is **unexercised** - no zero count exists.

Item 3 asked for a control showing that changing the rounded-tail rule changes
the predicted written-byte set "if one exists". **It does not exist.** There is
no non-vacuous population, so no such control can be built from this capture,
and the tail rule is implemented from the handler while remaining
**underdetermined by observation**. Saying so is the point; manufacturing a
control on an empty population would assert validation that was not performed.

The grounding model's conservative all-DMEM taint was replaced with these four
derived spans plus the 80-byte scratch. Result is unchanged - 4427 commands and
21857 frames fully evaluable - so the ADPCM acceptance does not rest on the
coarser model.

#### ENVMIXER arithmetic, partially derived

Not yet implemented and not accepted; recorded so it is not re-derived.

The four outputs are a 2x2 matrix of {left, right} envelope against two gains:

```
s3 (out)      VMULF v29,v29,v10[14] ; VMACF v29,v17, VMULF(v20, v24[14])
s1 (aux 0x0C) VMULF v27,v27,v10[14] ; VMACF v27,v17, VMULF(v20, v24[15])
s2 (aux 0x0A) VMULF v28,v28,v10[14] ; VMACF v28,v17, VMULF(v18, v24[14])
s0 (aux 0x0E) VMULF v26,v26,v10[14] ; VMACF v26,v17, VMULF(v18, v24[15])
```

So **v20 is the LEFT envelope and v18 the RIGHT**, and `v24[14]`/`v24[15]` are
the two gains applied to both - the dry/wet association, pending confirmation
of which is which.

**Replace vs accumulate is settled: it accumulates.** `v10` is `LQV v10,0(zero)`
= DMEM 0..15, the same constant vector ADPCM uses, whose element 6 is `0x7FFF`.
So the existing destination passes through `VMULF(dest, 0x7FFF)` - the identical
near-unity pass-through MIXER uses - and the new contribution is added by
`VMACF`. Outputs are NOT replaced.

**WITHDRAWN: "cadence is per 8-sample group, not per sample."** The loop
position of the adds proves only that the envelope *state vectors* advance once
per 16-byte group. It does NOT prove a single scalar gain is held across those
eight samples: `v20`/`v18` are eight-lane and feed a **lane-wise** `VMULF`/
`VMACF` (element field 0 = element-wise, not broadcast), so each lane can carry
its own envelope value.

Corrected statement, and then settled by measurement: ENVMIXER advances its
left/right envelope vectors once per eight-sample group, and **the progression
inside each vector is a per-lane ramp**. The A_INIT lane construction multiplies
the rate by `v30 = LQV 7(t3)` with `t3`=64, i.e. DMEM 0xB0, whose eight
halfwords are

whose eight lanes carry **monotonically increasing fractional positions
corresponding to successive eighths of the group step**, with the final
lane at the maximum representable fraction.

- (k+1)/8 in unsigned Q16, saturated in the last lane. So lane k receives
`(k+1)/8` of the group step: the effective envelope is **per sample**, not
constant per eight. `v21`/`v19` are the low halves and `v20`/`v18` the high
halves of a 32-bit fixed-point value. Read out of the shipped data segment,
not fitted to the C producer's 16.16 appearance.

The ramp is clamped against a target each group by `VGE` or `VCL` (`v24[8]`
left, `v24[11]` right), selected by `s5`/`s4`, which come from `mfc2` of
`v24[2]` and `v24[8]` - i.e. the ramp direction picks max-clamp or min-clamp.

Still open: the A_INIT initialisation arithmetic that builds `v20`/`v18` from
the SETVOL fields; the 80-byte state layout by dataflow; consumer-side
signedness; and which of `v24[14]`/`v24[15]` is dry and which wet.

#### J/JAL coordinate systems normalised, and the blast radius audited

Not merely an arithmetic slip. The blob is DMA'd to IMEM `0x080`, so an
absolute jump operand encodes an **IMEM address** while every printed
instruction address is a **blob offset**: `blob = IMEM_target - 0x80`. The
disassembler masked the operand to 12 bits and printed it unlabelled, which is
exactly how the two systems mixed. It now prints both, so they cannot be
confused again:

```
0afc:  j imem:0x0bb0 blob:0x0b30
```

Bounded audit of every jump in every accepted handler - 43 jumps total:

```
handler      jumps present
CLEARBUFF, SEGMENT, SETBUFF, SETVOL, INTERLEAVE,
DMEMMOVE, SETLOOP, LOADBUFF, SAVEBUFF, LOADADPCM,
MIXER, POLEF, ADPCM                dispatcher return + DMA helpers ONLY
RESAMPLE                           + 2 intra-handler (0x854->0x868, 0xa50->0x958)
ENVMIXER                           + 6 intra-handler
```

Only three targets appear outside the handlers: blob 0x098 (dispatcher return),
0x104 (DMA read helper) and 0x130 (DMA wait helper).

**Conclusions that change: none outside ENVMIXER.** Every handler whose
semantics are accepted - ADPCM, SETLOOP, SETVOL, CLEARBUFF, SETBUFF,
INTERLEAVE, DMEMMOVE, LOADADPCM, MIXER, POLEF - has no intra-handler jump at
all, so no derivation of theirs could have depended on a mis-normalised target.
RESAMPLE has two, but its semantics are validated empirically byte-exact
against the cartridge in the zero-voice oracle, so its correctness does not rest
on how those targets were read. ENVMIXER's six are the ones that mattered, and
they were corrected before any ENVMIXER semantics were accepted - nothing built
on the wrong reading survived.

#### The persistent 80-byte state layout

Established first, as five consecutive 16-byte vectors, because entry and exit
agree exactly. CONTINUE entry loads (blob 0xb1c..0xb2c) and the exit stores
(0xc8c, 0xc94, 0xd20, 0xd24, 0xd28) touch the same five positions:

```
  +0x00  v20   left  envelope, HIGH half
  +0x10  v21   left  envelope, LOW half
  +0x20  v18   right envelope, HIGH half
  +0x30  v19   right envelope, LOW half
  +0x40  v24   the parameter vector (targets, rates, direction, gains)
```

80 bytes, matching both the DMA length (`addi v1,zero,79` at 0xad8 and 0xd30)
and `ENVMIX_STATE[40]` at `abi.h:266` - three independent routes to the same
number.

`v24` is the vector still to be decomposed lane by lane: `v24[8]` and `v24[11]`
are the left and right target clamps, `v24[9]`/`v24[10]` and
`v24[12]`/`v24[13]` the left and right rate high/low increments, `v24[14]` and
`v24[15]` the two output gains, and `mfc2` of `v24[2]` and `v24[8]` supplies the
ramp-direction flags selecting `VGE` versus `VCL`. Which gain is dry and which
wet is NOT settled and will be settled from the SETVOL aux dataflow, not from
naming.

**The A_INIT/CONTINUE ordering difference is load-bearing and is not to be
simplified away:** A_INIT emits its peeled output group BEFORE the vector
advance at 0xc48, while CONTINUE reaches that advance BEFORE its first steady
group. Both then run the same loop.

#### Vector element selection, derived - two index spaces that share notation

`v24[8]` is an ELEMENT SELECTOR, not a C array index, and `mfc2 v24[8]` means
something different again. Both appear in this handler and both were about to
be read as array subscripts.

RSP vector-op element field, from the encoding rather than from emulator
shorthand. ENVMIXER uses only `e=0` and `e=8..15`, so the quarter and half
forms never arise here and are listed only to show they were considered:

```
  e = 0,1      element-wise      destination lane i <- source lane i
  e = 2,3      quarter           (unused by ENVMIXER)
  e = 4..7     half              (unused by ENVMIXER)
  e = 8..15    broadcast         EVERY destination lane <- source halfword e-8
```

`mfc2 rt, vs[e]` is different: **`e` is a BYTE index**, and the instruction
reads the halfword at bytes `e..e+1`, so the halfword read is `e/2`. The two
`mfc2` reads therefore do NOT select what a vector selector of the same number
would:

```
  mfc2 s5, v24[2]   -> bytes 2..3  -> halfword 1   (NOT halfword 2)
  mfc2 s4, v24[8]   -> bytes 8..9  -> halfword 4   (NOT halfword 0)
```

#### The parameter vector, four index spaces separated

```
 hw   PERSISTENT   raw   canonical   selected    role
 idx  80B-state +   e    assembler   halfword     (80-byte ENVMIX state slot, +0x40)
   0   +0x40        8   v24[0]         0        left  target  (clamp operand, v20)
   1   +0x42        9   v24[1]         1        left  rate HIGH  (VADD  v20)
   2   +0x44       10   v24[2]         2        left  rate LOW   (VADDC v21)
   3   +0x46       11   v24[3]         3        right target  (clamp operand, v18)
   4   +0x48       12   v24[4]         4        right rate HIGH (VADD  v18)
   5   +0x4A       13   v24[5]         5        right rate LOW  (VADDC v19)
   6   +0x4C       14   v24[6]         6        gain A
   7   +0x4E       15   v24[7]         7        gain B
```

**The separation immediately pays off.** `mfc2 s5,v24[2]` reads halfword 1,
which is the SAME halfword the vector selector `v24[9]` broadcasts - the left
rate primary. Likewise `mfc2 s4,v24[8]` reads halfword 4, the right rate
primary. So the ramp-direction flags are **not separate fields at all**: `s5`
and `s4` ARE the two rate primaries, and `bgtz` tests their sign.

Two consequences:

1. **The rate primary is consumed as SIGNED**, because `bgtz` is a signed test.
   That is consumer-side evidence, and it agrees with the producer's signed rate
   mantissa - the first signedness question settled from the microcode rather
   than from the emitter.
2. Direction selects the clamp: `bgtz s5` taken (rate > 0, rising) selects
   `VCL`; not taken (rate <= 0, falling) selects `VGE`. `VGE` is max(vs,vt), so
   a falling envelope is floored at its target - coherent. `VCL`'s exact
   behaviour depends on the VCC/VCO flag state and is **not yet derived**; it is
   recorded as "the rising-ramp clamp" rather than assumed to be a plain min.

Names in the table above are provisional to that extent, and the paired
accumulators are still called primary/companion rather than high/low until the
carry relationship between `VADDC` and `VADD` is shown.

#### ENVMIXER vector-flag provenance - traced to an in-task writer, not task state

Structure only; the exact flag SEMANTICS (what `VADD` leaves, what `VGE` and
`VCL` read and write) are not derived here and are pending an authoritative RSP
source. What is established is where the state reaching each clamp comes from.

**Which instructions can touch flags.** Of everything ENVMIXER executes, only
`VADD`, `VADDC`, `VGE` and `VCL` are flag-relevant; `VMULF`, `VMACF`, `VMUDL`,
`VMADN`, `VMADM`, `VMADH` and `VXOR` are inert. Across the whole microcode only
**two handlers** write vector flags at all:

```
  RESAMPLE    VADD x8, VSUB x2
  ENVMIXER    VADD x5, VADDC x5, VCL x4, VGE x4
  every other handler                          - none -
```

**The asymmetry that matters.** On the CONTINUE path the first clamp is preceded
in-handler by `VADDC` (blob 0xc48) then `VADD` (0xc4c), so a flag writer runs
first. On the **A_INIT** path the peeled block reaches its first left clamp
(0xba4/0xbb0) and first right clamp (0xc00/0xc0c) through nothing but loads,
`VXOR`, `VMUDL`, `VMADN`, `VMADM` and `VMADH` - **all inert.** So on A_INIT the
clamps read flag state that no ENVMIXER instruction has written, and it must be
accounted for rather than assumed zero.

**Traced, not assumed.** The immediate predecessor is uniform and unhelpful -
all 206 A_INIT ENVMIXERs follow a SETVOL and all 5528 CONTINUE ones follow a
SETBUFF, and both are pure scalar state writers executing no vector instruction
at all. Walking back to the last command whose handler can write flags:

```
  A_INIT   ENVMIXER : RESAMPLE 206   task entry 0
  CONTINUE ENVMIXER : RESAMPLE 5528  task entry 0
```

**Every one of the 5734 ENVMIXER commands has a RESAMPLE as the last
flag-writing command before it, inside the same task.** None reaches task entry,
and none inherits from a preceding ENVMIXER. That part stands.

**WITHDRAWN: "therefore the ENVMIXER input flag state is grounded."** That
sentence treated VCO, VCC and VCE as ONE state object. They are three separate
control registers with different writers and different clearing rules, and a
last-writer census over "flag-writing instructions" cannot ground them jointly.
An add or subtract does not mean all three were freshly written. Redone per
register below.

Scoped to this 435-task capture. The general hazard - flags surviving across
commands because no handler clears them at entry - remains real, and the A_INIT
path is where it would bite.

#### Per-register control-flow state - VCO closed, VCC/VCE open

Authority for the documented behaviours is the SGI Nintendo 64 RSP
Programmer's Guide, Revision 1.0; the local trees are silent, which the
reconnaissance established as a documentation gap rather than a blocker.

**Element selection, corrected.** The documented rule is
`e=0 -> j=i`; quarter `j=(e&1)+(i&6)`; half `j=(e&3)+(i&4)`; whole/scalar
`j=e&7`. **The earlier note that "e=0,1 are both element-wise" is WITHDRAWN -
the vector operand is `e=0` only.** ENVMIXER uses `e=0` and `e=8..15`, so its
decoding is unaffected, but the table was wrong as written.

**Notation, normalised permanently - and the first attempt at this was itself
wrong.** Canonical assembler operands SUBTRACT the scalar offset, so raw `e=9`
is written `v24[1]` and selects source halfword 1; raw `e=14` is written
`v24[6]` and selects halfword 6. The earlier note that gave `v24[9]` as the
assembler form confused raw-e with assembler syntax - exactly the error the
normalisation existed to prevent.

Three separate columns everywhere from here: **raw e -> canonical assembler
operand -> physical source halfword.** The local throwaway disassembler prints
RAW e in its brackets, so any listing quoted from it is *local raw-e notation*,
not assembler syntax, and is labelled as such. MFC2 keeps its own byte-index
space and its actual byte indices.

**MFC2 is closed.** The element field is a BYTE index; the instruction reads a
16-bit value beginning at that byte; the VU register is big-endian; and the
result is **SIGN-EXTENDED** into the GPR. For the two aligned cases ENVMIXER
uses, that is physical halfword 1 (`mfc2 s5,v24[2]`) and physical halfword 4
(`mfc2 s4,v24[8]`), both sign-extended. The `e=15` wrap case is not reached and
was not pursued. **Consumer-side claim accepted:** the two rate-primary
quantities are interpreted as signed scalars by the `bgtz` tests. Producer
identity stays pending the SETVOL lineage.

**VCO provenance - complete executed path, not just handler bodies.** Auditing
the whole blob rather than the sixteen handler bodies:

```
boot + dispatcher        no flag-writing vector instruction
DMA read helper  0x104   no flag-writing vector instruction
DMA wait helper  0x130   no flag-writing vector instruction
anywhere outside RESAMPLE and ENVMIXER   NONE
```

So within the EXTRACTED region 0x000..0xdbf the only code that can mutate VCO
is RESAMPLE and ENVMIXER; nothing is claimed about 0xdc0..0xf7f, and nothing
below depends on it. Between a RESAMPLE and the ENVMIXER that follows it, the intervening
commands measured are SETVOL and SETBUFF, both flag-inert, and the dispatcher
and DMA helpers they pass through are flag-inert too. **Nothing between can
modify VCO.**

RESAMPLE's tail contains no VCO mutator after blob 0x0a14, so its final
VCO-mutating instruction is the `VADD` at 0x0a14 when the resample loop runs, or
a `VSUB` at 0x8bc/0x8d4 otherwise. Both forms are documented to consume VCO
carry and CLEAR VCO, so either way **VCO = 0 on exit**. All 206 RESAMPLE
commands preceding an A_INIT ENVMIXER carry a nonzero count (32..320, none
zero).

**One gap stated rather than papered over:** that every path through RESAMPLE
executes at least one `VADD` or `VSUB` is not formally derived - it rests on the
nonzero counts, not on a loop-entry proof. RESAMPLE's control flow would have to
be derived to close it, and that is only worth doing if VCO turns out to be
load-bearing in a way the clamps expose.

**VCC and VCE are NOT closed, and are not being guessed.** Establishing whether
stale VCC/VCE bits can reach a scored value requires the guide's exact
pseudocode for the greater-equal compare and the clip operation - specifically
which bits each consumes under VCO=0, and what each writes. That text is not in
hand, and writing plausible pseudocode from memory is precisely the failure mode
that produced the withdrawn claim above. Recorded as the next thing to obtain.

Until then: no claim that the ENVMIXER clamp inputs are grounded, and no
reduction of either clamp to "max" or "min" shorthand.

#### Item 7 - the carry pair, and high/low now justified

`VADDC` operates on v21 (left) and v19 (right); `VADD` on v20 (left) and v18
(right). The operands settle which is which, rather than the naming being
assumed:

- field 10, written `v24[10]`, selects source halfword 2, which the producer
  supplies as the rate's LOW word - and it is the `VADDC` operand on v21.
- field 9, written `v24[9]`, selects source halfword 1, the rate's MANTISSA -
  and it is the `VADD` operand on v20.

Three further consumer uses corroborate independently: v20/v18 are the vectors
that feed the gain multiply, the vectors the clamp instruction takes, and the
vectors stored at state +0x00/+0x20 with their partners at +0x10/+0x30.

**So primary/companion is promoted to LOW/HIGH:** v21/v19 are the low
fractional halves, v20/v18 the high integer halves of a per-lane
**two-word saturating fixed-point envelope state**. That phrasing is deliberate
and is itself the finding - it is NOT a 32-bit accumulator, because the low word
wraps while the high word saturates. Recurrence per group, with VCO closed at this point:

```
low[i]  = (low[i] + rate_low) mod 2^16          unsigned; the wrap IS the carry
carry[i]= that addition's carry-out             -> VCO
high[i] = sat_s16(high[i] + rate_mant + carry[i])   signed, saturating
VCO cleared by the plain add
```

The low half wraps; the high half **saturates** rather than wrapping. That
asymmetry is a real behavioural detail and is not a 32-bit wraparound counter.

#### Item 9 - SETVOL producer lineage, all four index spaces

`v24` is loaded by `LQV v24[0],1(t8)`, whose field 1 is a 16-byte offset, so
`v24` is the 16 bytes at state +0x10. **Physical halfword k maps directly to
state offset 0x10+2k - there is no rearrangement.**

The apparent producer/consumer conflict resolved: `abi.h`'s macro parameters are
GENERIC SLOTS, and the caller repurposes them per flag combination. Under
`A_RATE` the first slot carries a target, not a volume. Call sites are
`src/libultrare/audio/env.c:405-409`.

```
 hw  TASK-BLK  raw  canonical  SETVOL (flags)      slot  producer  consumer role
 idx  +off     e    assembler   (task state block at DMEM 0x360; NOT the 80-byte state)
  0  +0x10    8  v24[0]     A_RATE|A_LEFT  (2)   1st   ltgt     left  clamp target
  1  +0x12    9  v24[1]     A_RATE|A_LEFT        2nd   lratm    left  rate, HIGH
  2  +0x14   10  v24[2]     A_RATE|A_LEFT        3rd   lratl    left  rate, LOW
  3  +0x16   11  v24[3]     A_RATE|A_RIGHT (0)   1st   rtgt     right clamp target
  4  +0x18   12  v24[4]     A_RATE|A_RIGHT       2nd   rratm    right rate, HIGH
  5  +0x1A   13  v24[5]     A_RATE|A_RIGHT       3rd   rratl    right rate, LOW
  6  +0x1C   14  v24[6]     A_AUX          (8)   1st   dryamt   gain A
  7  +0x1E   15  v24[7]     A_AUX                3rd   wetamt   gain B
```

Volumes sit outside `v24`: +0x06 from `A_VOL|A_LEFT`, +0x08 from
`A_VOL|A_RIGHT`.

**A corroboration, narrowly scoped.** The handler's A_AUX branch stores only
the first and third operands, never the second, and the emitter passes a literal
zero in that second slot. That independently corroborates **the auxiliary slot
mapping only** - it says nothing about the target or rate rows, which rest on
their own evidence. The earlier claim that it "validates the whole mapping" is
withdrawn.

**Dry versus wet, settled by dataflow rather than ordering.** Gain A is
`dryamt` and gain B is `wetamt`. Substituting into the four output equations:

```
  s3 = dmemout +0x02   left  envelope x DRY
  s2 = aux     +0x0A   right envelope x DRY
  s1 = aux     +0x0C   left  envelope x WET
  s0 = aux     +0x0E   right envelope x WET
```

So the four destinations are a 2x2 of {left,right} x {dry,wet}, and the three
A_AUX SETBUFF addresses are, in order, dry-right, wet-left, wet-right.

**Signedness: producer and consumer AGREE, cited from declarations rather than
from a call site.** The call site proves identity, not type. The declarations
are `static s16 _getRate(f32 vol, f32 tgt, s32 count, u16 *ratel)`
(`src/libultrare/audio/env.c:62,474`) and, in
`src/libultra/audio/synthInternals.h:272-278`, `s16 lratm`, `u16 lratl`,
`s16 ltgt`, `s16 cvolL`, `s16 dryamt`. So the mantissa is **signed 16-bit** and
the rate low word is **unsigned 16-bit** at the producer.

The consumer matches both: it sign-extends halfwords 1 and 4 through MFC2 and
tests them with a signed branch (mantissa signed), and it feeds halfwords 2 and
5 into an unsigned carry-generating add (low word unsigned). The earlier note that a
disagreement would have to be surfaced rather than smoothed still stands as
policy - it simply does not arise here.

Consumer roles are now promoted to producer identities for these quantities.
The clamp SEMANTICS remain open: "clamp target" names which operand the clamp
instruction takes, established by the instruction's operand, and says nothing
about what the clamp computes - that still waits on the compare and clip
pseudocode.

```
  CTC2  (write a VU control register)   0 occurrences
```

**VCO at A_INIT entry: 206/206, proven structurally rather than inferred.**
The earlier argument leaned on nonzero counts, which was an inference. Walking
RESAMPLE's actual CFG instead:

```
  838  bgtz -> 85c        both arms converge at 868
  86c  beq  -> 888        both arms converge at 888
  8bc  VSUB   8d4  VSUB
  9dc..a14   VADD x8
  a48  blez -> a58 (exit)     a50  j -> 958 (loop back-edge)
```

**There is no control transfer at all between 0x86c and 0xa48.** The region
containing both VSUBs and all eight VADDs is therefore straight-line and
executes in full on every path that reaches 0x888 - and every path reaches it,
since both earlier branches converge there. The loop back-edge re-enters at

re-execute it. The exit region 0xa58..0xab0 contains no flag instruction.

`VADD` at blob 0x0a14, on every path, with no dependence on count or loop
entry.** That add consumes the carry and clears VCO, so RESAMPLE always exits
with **VCO = 0**. The count census is no longer load-bearing.

That CFG result was re-derived with a decoder covering **every** scalar control

```
  distinct opcodes ever appearing in that gap:  SETVOL 1030, SETBUFF 412
  MIXER in any gap?    NO

```

#### Clamp non-interference - VCC and VCE closed without tracing stale bits

With VCO = 0 established at every clamp, the documented semantics make the old
control-register contents unable to reach a numerical result:

- **Compare.** It clears its result register first, and its equality decision
  rests on the complement of the carry-low bits OR'd with the extension
  register. With VCO = 0 that condition holds whatever the old extension held,
  so neither old register affects the value selected. Under this reachable
  state it reduces numerically to a signed maximum.
- **Clip.** With VCO = 0 the sign bit is zero and the equality bit is one, so
  the non-sign branch runs and the comparison is recomputed from the current
  operands. The selected value is therefore independent of both old registers.
  It clears the carry and extension registers afterwards, but may preserve or
  re-emit a stale bit in the compare-result register.

  **WITHDRAWN: "the clip under VCO=0 is signed minimum."** The literal
  reachable-state rule is: compute the **wrapped 16-bit difference** of the
  operands, then select the second operand if that difference read as signed is
  non-negative, otherwise the first. That is not signed minimum whenever the
  subtraction overflows 16 bits. `tools/native/acmdauxctl.c` carries a
  **CONSTRUCTED** boundary control - explicitly not cartridge-measured - built
  from opposite-sign extremes; the literal rule and a naive minimum disagree on
  four of its six cases and agree on the two in-range pairs. Evaluator B must
  implement the exact wrapped-subtraction rule, or first prove an
  operand-domain invariant excluding signed overflow. The exact rule is
  preferred because it assumes nothing.

**So the remaining question is only whether that preserved bit has a live
consumer.** Audited: ENVMIXER's entire flag-relevant instruction set is `VADD`,
`VADDC`, `VGE` and `VCL`. There is no `VMRG` - the one instruction that would
consume the compare-result register numerically - and no `CFC2` inside ENVMIXER
to read it out. That is sufficient and needs no global claim: **ENVMIXER lies
wholly inside the extracted region**, so its own instruction set is fully known,
and the question is path-local - whether a live consumer exists after the clamp
on the grounded path. The only readers of that register are
the clip instances themselves, whose selected values are already shown
independent of it under VCO = 0. Each clamp also clears VCO and the extension
register, so VCO = 0 still holds at the next clamp, and the argument repeats.

**VCC and VCE are therefore closed by non-interference: no stale bit can reach
a scored value or a live flag dependency.** No backward tracing was needed, and
no task-start or cross-command flag state re-enters the derivation.

Two things this does NOT license. Evaluator A must still model the literal
operations including their control-register side effects. And **only the compare
simplifies**: under VCO = 0, with the result register cleared before the
comparison and the old extension unable to change equality selection, evaluator
B may use signed maximum for it - precondition documented at the use site. The
clip does **not** get a scalar reduction; see the withdrawal above. Neither
simplification is general semantics for those instructions.

#### RESAMPLE termination scan, and the alignment census

**No execution termination in RESAMPLE.** Scanned by encoding for SPECIAL
funct forms that halt the scalar core: none inside 0x7fc..0xab4. The two in the
extracted region sit at 0x094 and 0x0c0, in the boot/dispatcher area. So no
reachable path terminates before the final carry-mutating add, the final
mutator remains the already-derived site, and delay slots were accounted for.
Flags are now left alone.

**Alignment census, before treating any access as an ordinary 16-byte
operation.** Effective DMEM addresses computed from the modelled state block
across every command, not inferred from SETBUFF conventions:

```
  commands 5734    groups 101952
  buffer-instances aligned (addr % 16 == 0) : 509760
  buffer-instances UNALIGNED                :      0
  commands taking the no-aux redirect path  :      0
  distinct low nibble, each of the five roles: {0}
```

Every group address is base + 16*g, so alignment is invariant in g and the base
nibble settles it. Scoped: **all measured ENVMIXER vector-buffer accesses are
16-byte aligned on this capture**, and no partial-vector behaviour needs
deriving for it.

#### Lane-to-sample mapping - identity, and channel identity is not from naming

Three coordinate systems kept visible: DMEM byte offset, VU lane, PCM sample.

A 16-byte aligned `LQV` moves DMEM bytes A+2k and A+2k+1 into VU bytes 2k and
2k+1, which is lane k; DMEM holds big-endian s16 PCM, and the VU register is
big-endian, so **lane k carries PCM sample k**. `SQV` is the inverse. The
multiply-accumulate that joins them uses raw element field 0 - verified by
decoding the instruction word's bits 24..21 rather than by reading the
disassembler's bracket - which is element-wise, so lane k of the input meets
lane k of the envelope and lands in lane k of the destination.

**Input sample k -> VU lane k -> envelope lane k -> output sample k. Identity
throughout, on all four buses.**

Channel identity is established by lineage, not by buffer naming. The left
envelope vector is the one whose rate and target come from the halfwords written
by the `A_LEFT` SETVOL commands, and the right envelope vector from the
`A_RIGHT` ones; tracing those two vectors into the four output equations is what
assigns left and right to the destinations. A left output and a right output
were traced separately for exactly this reason.

#### A_INIT ramp construction, lane by lane

`LSV` loads the current volume into the vector's **byte** 14, i.e. lane 7, and
the following multiply-accumulate broadcasts that lane to all eight against an
all-ones vector - which is how one scalar current volume becomes the base of all
eight lanes. The fractional ramp vector supplies lane k with (k+1)/8 of the
group step. The accumulate chain is therefore

```
  env32[k] = (current_volume << 16) + ramp[k] * rate32
  rate32   = (rate_mantissa << 16) | rate_low     mantissa signed, low unsigned
  high[k]  = env32[k] >> 16     low[k] = env32[k] & 0xFFFF
```

then the target clamp. The C rate helper corroborates the shape and was not used
to derive it.

**WITHDRAWN: "measured ramp witness."** The command INPUTS are measured; the
eight envelope values below were generated by the proposed scalar recurrence
itself, so they are not measured envelope values and are not independent
evidence for that recurrence. Presenting them as a witness was circular.

Correct status: **104 measured A_INIT commands are non-vacuous candidate inputs
on which the proposed recurrence predicts multiple distinct lane values**, with
task 111 command 447 preferred. It becomes a real witness only when evaluators A
and B independently agree on all eight lanes and the grounded input PCM is
active on at least two lanes whose envelope values differ. The per-sample ramp
is NOT accepted from calculated values:

```
  sample/lane k :  0     1     2     3     4     5     6     7
  envelope high : 6214  6014  5813  5613  5412  5212  5011  4811
```

Those are PREDICTED values, not measured ones. Whether the measured population
actually exercises a per-sample ramp is settled by the flatten-to-one-gain
control changing scored destination samples, which belongs to the validator and
is not claimed here.

**Memory-operation lane proof, decoded by encoding.** Alignment alone does not
establish element zero, so every vector memory operation in ENVMIXER was decoded
from its instruction word - opcode, vector register, base register, the
element/byte field at bits 10..7, and the 7-bit offset. Result: **35 quadword
loads and stores on the input and all four destinations, every one with element
field 0.** The only nonzero-element vector memory operations in the handler are
the two short loads placing the current volume at vector byte 14, i.e. lane 7,
for the broadcast - they are not on the sample data path. With element 0, the
measured 16-byte alignment and the big-endian representation, sample k -> lane k
-> stored sample k is accepted for the measured path.

#### A RESIDUAL SHARED ASSUMPTION, found by the new instrumentation

Instrumenting the low-form extraction boundary reports **374 baseline hits** -
occasions where the accumulator's high field lies outside signed 16-bit range,
which is exactly where the documented low-form rule may clamp rather than take
the raw slice.

**A and B both take the raw low slice.** They therefore agree at those 374
points whether or not the raw slice is correct, so the zero-mismatch result does
**not** validate the low-form extraction rule. This is the same failure mode as
the shared lane-fraction helper: agreement on a rule neither side derived
independently.

The rule is unsettled and **exercised**, so it cannot be dismissed as
unreachable. Settling it needs the documented pseudocode or the cartridge
oracle; until then the low-form extraction is an explicit open assumption, and
the acceptance below is scoped around it.

#### The 374 classified, then resolved on the cartridge

**Classification.** All 374 boundary events land on LIVE destinations - 182 at
blob 0xba0 and 192 at blob 0xbfc, the two instructions producing the scored
envelope LOW word for left and right. Zero dead scratch. That withdrew the
earlier exactness claim outright: no acceptance around a known-wrong rule.

**The discriminator coordinate.** The signed clamp on the low-form result is
keyed on the accumulator's bits **47..31** - whether the value fits signed
32-bit - **not** the bits immediately above the 16-bit result window. That is
why ordinary envelope highs like 6214 do not trigger it. Verified that the
existing detector is exactly this predicate: 400000 random 48-bit values plus an
explicit boundary sweep, zero disagreements. The 374 census therefore stands
unchanged.

**Three candidates, kept apart until the cartridge chose.** raw low 16 bits;
sat32, the low half of a saturated signed 32-bit pair; and s16, a naive
signed-16 clamp. They genuinely diverge on this population - raw vs sat32 on 204
events, raw vs s16 on 170, and **sat32 vs s16 on all 374**.

**Resolved against the captured task oracle, not by preference.** The 80-byte
persistent state holds the envelope low words directly, left at +0x10 and right
at +0x30, so a candidate that changes a low word is observable in the bracketed
after-image with no output arithmetic needed. Restricting to A_INIT commands
that are the LAST ENVMIXER writer to their state address and whose clamp
actually fires:

```

  of those, with a clamp event firing    :  6
  lane low words differing sat32 vs s16  : 11

  cartridge match, final left high+low vs after-image:
    raw    0 / 6
    sat32  6 / 6
    s16    0 / 6
```

**sat32 reproduces the cartridge; raw and s16 both fail.** Two of three
candidates rejected on a nonempty population is what makes this a real
discrimination rather than an oracle satisfied by anything.

**Both evaluators repaired independently.** A adopts the selected rule inside
its literal instruction result extraction; B derives its own low recurrence in
