```
  resampleInit   hits=45     commands=45     tasks=24
```

Worth recording that the measurement corrected an assumption I had written into
the instrument itself: I expected one command to produce many state hits, and
`hits == commands` for both counters, so it is one hit per command in practice.

#### The ADPCM acceptance hole was a DRIFT from the accepted design, now closed

`SL_ACMD_ADPCM` defaulted to **1** in the source, and its comment said "build
with `-DSL_ACMD_ADPCM=0` to gate it off again". That contradicts the position
already accepted and recorded in this file:

> **ADPCM is gated OFF by default** (`SL_ACMD_ADPCM`, default 0; the production
> path returns `SL_ACMD_ERR_OPCODE`). Its semantics are derived but NOT
> accepted, and unvalidated arithmetic must not become production behaviour by
> default.

So this is not a design conflict to surface - it is **drift away from a decision
already taken**, and restoring the default restores the accepted design.

**Measured while the drift was live**, which is what the hole actually cost:

```
  ADPCM decode commands executed   10224
  tasks containing them            200 of 449
  samples produced through it      408224
```

408,224 samples produced by arithmetic no measurement grounds, in a build where
nothing asked for it.

**Restored to 0, and the fail-loud behaviour is what it should be:**

```
  ACMDEXEC tasks=449 completedWithoutFault=249 commands=356029
    opcode not implemented (stage 1-3 only)   200 task(s)
    first fault: ADPCM at command 249, operand 0x2da8a0
    negOverflow    hits=0
    resamplerState hits=1264  commands=1264  tasks=264
    resampleInit   hits=1     commands=1     tasks=1
    ADPCM decode: commands=0 tasks=0 samplesProduced=0
    *** NOT an acceptance
```

249 of 449 tasks complete; 200 fail loudly at the first ADPCM command. The
state and rsinit totals fall (12730 -> 1264) only because tasks now abort before
reaching later RESAMPLEs - **that is a consequence of aborting earlier, not an
improvement**, and no run is accepted while either is nonzero.

#### The counters are INTERFACE, and my artefact check was mis-specified

The four new counters appeared in the production binary and my artefact grep
flagged them. The right resolution is not to widen the grep until it passes.
`sl_acmd.h` already documents the three `sl_acmd_ungrounded_*` counters as
"part of the interface, not debug scaffolding... a nonzero value means
production has relied on something no measurement grounds, and the caller should
say so rather than let it pass silently."

The new counters serve exactly that purpose - `sl_acmd_adpcm_samples` nonzero in
a production build would mean unaccepted arithmetic produced audio - so they are
declared in `sl_acmd.h` beside the others under the same rationale. **The grep
was wrong to include interface symbols**, and now targets measurement
scaffolding only, which is 0.

#### Storage recon: the facility already exists, and so does its control

Searched before inventing any storage, as instructed. `src/game/sl_romdbg.h`
is an owner-maintained ROM-debug mailbox, built by `SIGHTLINE_ROM_DEBUG` via
`make trace-debug` / `ROM_DEBUG=1` (`Makefile:536-547`), under an explicit rule:
*"The normal matching ROM stays byte-identical. The debug ROM is knowingly
non-matching and exists solely as an oracle. Normal ROM proves behaviour. Debug
ROM explains state."*

It already carries the two things this work needs:

- **its own positive control**, `hook_calls` at offset 0x0c, commented
  "known-positive control: this must move" - the same discipline the audio-frame
  writer control is meant to provide;
- **a perturbation control**, `ROM_SIZECTL=1`, which `Makefile:547` calls "the
  CONTROL for ROM_DEBUG, and it is not optional reading" - i.e. the challenge
  that the instrumented image has not shifted layout.

It is versioned (`SL_ROMDBG_VERSION 4`), host-driven through a seq/cmd/ack
protocol, and read by `tools/native/rominspect.py`. **Not modified**: it is
owner-maintained with a stated contract, and extending it is a change to that
contract rather than an addition beside it. The event-logger design should
reuse this mailbox and its two controls rather than allocate new storage.

#### The positive-control writer, derived - and why 435 is the expected count

Before expecting any number, every writer of `g_AudioFrameCount` was traced and
classified. `grep -rn g_AudioFrameCount src/ --include=*.c --include=*.h`
returns 20 references; all but three are reads.

```
  audi.c:150   u32 g_AudioFrameCount = 0;
               INITIALISATION. Static initialiser, once at load, process
               lifetime. Not an event.
  audi.c:638   if (ctl == 4) { g_AudioFrameCount++; ... }
               MEASUREMENT ONLY. The negative control added earlier in this
               sprint, compiled only under SL_ALHEAP_TRACE and reached only
               when SL_AUDIO_CTL=4. Absent from production, and absent from
               any run that is not deliberately exercising it.
  audi.c:1143  g_AudioFrameCount = (s32)(g_AudioFrameCount + 1);
               THE NORMAL WRITER. Last statement of amClearDmaBuffers
               (audi.c:1082), at function scope after the reclaim loop, so it
               is UNCONDITIONAL - no branch can skip it once the function is
               entered.
```

**There is no same-value assignment and no reset**: the only assignment in the
tree other than the initialiser is the `+1`, so the sequence is strictly
increasing by one from 0 and a written value never repeats.

**Call sites of the normal writer's enclosing function.** `amClearDmaBuffers`
has exactly one call site - `audi.c:809`, the first act of
`amHandleFrameMessage` - alongside its declaration at 323 and three comment
mentions. So the chain is one-to-one:

```
  one audio task -> one amHandleFrameMessage
                 -> one amClearDmaBuffers
                 -> one unconditional increment
```

**Therefore the expected event count is the audio-task population, and on the
cartridge that population is 435** - established independently by the ACMD
census, which keys each task on this same counter and found 1..435 contiguous
with a gap histogram of `{1: 434}`.

**This is why 435 is derived rather than forced.** The earlier positive control
observed 435 *snapshot advances*; that number is now a corroboration of a count
derived from the call graph, not the basis for it. Had the writer been
conditional, or had `amClearDmaBuffers` had a second caller, the expected count
would have differed from the snapshot count and the snapshot would have been
the misleading one.

**What the control will actually prove.** A logger that records this writer must
emit exactly 435 events with values 1..435 in order. Fewer means it is missing
events; more means it is recording something other than this writer; a wrong
ordering means it is not event-sequenced. Only a logger that passes this may
have a zero result from it believed - which is the whole point, since the
question it is being built to answer is an absence.

#### Logger storage: no reserved buffer exists, so the region must be derived

**Recon result first.** `src/game/sl_romdbg.h` is the existing facility and the
right one to reuse, but it has **no spare space**: `SlRomDbg` is densely packed
from `magic` at 0x00 through `sight_mp_menu` at 0xf4 and then ends with
`SlDbgHit hits[10]` at 0xf8, closing at 0x238. There is no reserved or padding
region to borrow, and the struct is owner-maintained under a versioned host
protocol (`SL_ROMDBG_VERSION 4`, seq/cmd/ack), so growing it is a change to that
contract rather than an addition beside it. **Not modified.**

So a fixed region has to be derived and *proven* outside every allocation.
Measured from the cartridge's own pool table, `g_mempPools` at `0x80063bb0`
(`build/u/ge007.u.map:10726`), `MemoryPool { u8 *start, *pos, *end, *prevpos }`
(`src/memp.h:11-16`), read after 500 video frames of the facility fixture:

```
  pool                    start        pos          end          span
  [0] MEMPOOL_TOTAL       0x0008e360   -            0x002f6000   0x267ca0
  [4] MEMPOOL_STAGE       0x0008e360   0x0028dab0   0x002ac000   0x21dca0
  [6] MEMPOOL_PERMANENT   0x002ac000   0x002f5ca0   0x002f6000   0x04a000
  [1][2][3][5] empty (start == end)
  [7] is MEMPOOL_COUNT - out of bounds, garbage, ignored
```

Two independent checks close on this table. `MEMPOOL_TOTAL` is documented in
`src/memp.h:32` as running "from `_bssSegmentEnd`" to "`_stacksSegmentStart`",
and its span covers every other pool. And the music heap measured earlier,
**0x002c7ca0..0x002f5ca0**, falls inside `MEMPOOL_PERMANENT` and ends exactly at
that pool's `pos` - so the audio arena is accounted for by this table rather
than being a separate region.

**So every game and audio allocation lies below 0x002f6000.**

#### What is NOT yet proven, and why no region is being chosen yet

`0x002f6000` is `_stacksSegmentStart`, so the space immediately above the pools
is **stacks, not free**. And on this hardware the framebuffers live high in
RDRAM - `sched.c` already references `cfb_16[0]` and `cfb_16[1]` - so "above the
stacks" is not free either without knowing where those sit.

The remaining derivation is therefore two measurements, not a guess: the stack
segment's extent, and the framebuffer extents. Only a region proven above all
three - pools, stacks and framebuffers - and inside the Expansion Pak's 8 MB may
be used, and **no region is chosen here**. Picking one now would be exactly the
"ordinary storage that shifts game or audio layout" the instruction rules out,
and a logger that perturbs layout would fail its own perturbation control in the
next step anyway.

#### The logger region, DERIVED - the map closes exactly at 4 MB

The two missing extents, measured rather than assumed:

```
  0x0008e360 .. 0x002f6000   memory pools - every game and audio allocation,
                             from the g_mempPools table read off the cartridge
  0x002f6000 .. 0x003b5000   stacks (0xbf000). 0x002f6000 is the pool table's
                             own upper bound, documented at memp.h:32 as
                             _stacksSegmentStart
  0x003b5000 .. 0x00400000   framebuffers. cfb_16 is a LINK-TIME symbol at
                             0x803b5000 (ge007.u.map:11656); two 320x240x2
                             buffers are 0x4b000
  0x00400000 .. 0x00800000   NOTHING
```

**The three regions tile without a gap and end exactly on 0x00400000**, the 4 MB
boundary - which is the check that the accounting is complete rather than merely
plausible. GoldenEye is a 4 MB title, and the core reports
`retro_get_memory_size(RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM)` = **0x800000**, so the upper
4 MB is addressable by the harness and untouched by the game.

**So the derived region is 0x00400000 and above**, proven above the pools, the
stacks and the framebuffers, with 4 MB of room. It cannot shift game or audio
layout because nothing in the link map or the allocator table reaches it: the
pools are bounded by their own `end` pointers, and the stacks and framebuffers
are link-time placements below it.

**The residual, stated rather than glossed.** This derivation is from the link
map and the allocator table; it is not a proof that no code anywhere writes
above 0x00400000 by some other route. That residual is exactly what the
perturbation control in the next step is for: comparing the uninstrumented
image against the logger-enabled one on task population, ordered counter
progression, command stream, and the map addresses of the music heap, the frame
counter and the effects pointer. If the logger were sharing memory with
anything, those would move.

**Also worth stating:** this region is usable because the instrumented image is
an ORACLE that runs only under this harness, where 8 MB is provided. It is not a
claim about real hardware, where a 4 MB console has no such space, and nothing
about the matching ROM changes.

With this, the storage question for the event logger is settled: reuse
`SIGHTLINE_ROM_DEBUG`'s build path and its two existing controls, and place the
ring at 0x00400000 rather than growing the owner's mailbox struct or adding a
static that shifts layout.

#### The attribution key, controlled - and the two arms disagree, which is the point

`commands=12730` was reported as though attribution were settled. It was an
argument, not evidence: `s->n_cmds` is monotonic across tasks *because* the
interpreter state is initialised once (`sl_acmd_ready`, `sl_ultra_shim.c:148`),
so it cannot alias. A control replaces that argument.

The same events are now attributed a second time using the **task-local** command
index, which *can* alias across a task boundary. Under-counting by the local key
is what proves the monotonic key is load-bearing.

```
  ARM A  decode gate OFF (production default), tasks abort at first ADPCM
    state  monotonicKey=1264  taskLocalKey=1252
    -> the task-local key ALIASES, 12 fewer; the monotonic key separated all 12

  ARM B  decode gate ON (diagnostic), all 449 tasks run to completion
    state  monotonicKey=12730  taskLocalKey=12730
    rsinit monotonicKey=45     taskLocalKey=45
    -> keys agree: aliasing was NOT exercised, so this arm proves nothing
       about the attribution
```

**Arm A is the control that passes.** It contains 12 natural instances of
exactly the construction required - two hits in different tasks landing on the
same task-local command ordinal - and the monotonic key resolved every one into
two distinct commands. That validates **the key**, which is what transfers.

**Arm B, read alone, would have been a false pass.** Its counts agree only
because no two attributed hits ever shared a task-local ordinal there, so its
key was never put under load. Reporting the two arms separately is deliberate:
the earlier `12730` figure came from Arm B, and Arm B is precisely the arm that
cannot certify it. It is trustworthy now because the key is validated in Arm A,
not because Arm B's numbers matched each other.

Arm A's tasks abort at the first ADPCM command, which clusters the surviving
state hits into fewer task-local indices and is why the collisions appear there
and not in the full run.

#### The decode figure was a PROJECTION, not a measurement - now it is measured

`sl_acmd_adpcm_samples` was incremented **before** the decode loop, as
`nf * 16`, where `nf` is the frame count the command intends to process. The
loop can `return SL_ACMD_ERR_DMEM` on its bounds checks, so that was a
statement of intent, not of work done.

The counter now increments **inside** the loop, after both bounds checks:

```
  ADPCM decode (derived, NOT accepted)
    commands=10224  tasks=200 of 449
    decodeFramesCompleted=25514   residuals=408224
```

**Exact unit: decode-loop iterations completed, sixteen residuals each.** It is
NOT a count of verified output writes - whether every residual reaches DRAM is a
further step and is not claimed. `25514 x 16 = 408224` closes, and it equals the
old projection, which means no decode loop exited early on this fixture. That is
now a measured fact rather than an assumption the instrument was making on its
own behalf.

All of this is diagnostic-build only: the production default is
`SL_ACMD_ADPCM 0`, under which `commands`, `tasks`, `decodeFramesCompleted` and
`residuals` are all zero.

#### Upper-memory recon - "nothing" was wrong, and two real users turned up

Withdrawing *"0x00400000..0x00800000 is NOTHING"* and *"storage settled"*. The
bounded search found things the link map alone does not show.

**A memory-size query exists.** `src/game/front.c:1447`:

```c
  #if defined(ISGOLDFINGER) || defined(USEEXPANSION)
      if (osGetMemSize != 0x00800000) { ... no expansion pak window ... }
  #endif
```

So the title was written with an 8 MB expectation available to it. **It is
compiled out of both builds**: the native `DEFS` (`tools/native/build.sh:55`)
carries neither symbol, and `grep -rnE "ISGOLDFINGER|USEEXPANSION" Makefile
scripts/` is empty. Tree-wide, that line is the *only* memory-size query -
`grep -rnE "osMemSize|osGetMemSize|0x80000318" src/ include/` returns it plus
three declarations and nothing else. (It also compares the FUNCTION ADDRESS
rather than calling it - Rare's defect, preserved under non-negotiable 5, and
moot while compiled out.)

**Two fixed addresses inside the candidate region.**
`src/game/debugmenu_handler.c:277-289`, under `LEFTOVERDEBUG` which *is* defined
in both builds:

```
  dword_D_80036FD8 = { 0x80500000, 0x40000, 0x7F000000, 0x7F100000 }
  dword_D_80036FE8 = { 0x80600000, 0x40000, 0x70000000, 0x70100000 }
```

Physical **0x00500000** and **0x00600000**, each with a 0x40000 length - squarely
inside the region I had called empty. **Neither table is referenced**: tree-wide
`grep -rn dword_D_80036FD8 dword_D_80036FE8 src/` returns only the two
definitions. So nothing consumes them on this path, but the addresses are
evidence the region was used by some build, and calling it "nothing" was wrong.

**A third fixed buffer, below the region but correcting an earlier claim.**
`RZIPBUFADDR 0x80300000` (`init.c:37`), used at `init.c:126` as the
decompression target for the code segment. Physical **0x00300000** sits inside
0x002f6000..0x003b5000, which I characterised as "stacks". That range is stacks
**plus at least this fixed buffer**; the earlier tiling was too coarse. It is
below 0x00400000 and does not affect the candidate region, but the
characterisation is corrected.

#### The memory-size probe FAILED its own liveness check, and is not used

```
  osTvType  @0x80000300 = 0x00000001   (NTSC - correct, so the region reads)
  osMemSize @0x80000318 = 0x00000000
```

The adjacent boot global reads a correct value, so the address is live and
decoded; `osMemSize` nevertheless reads zero, which on a direct-boot image most
likely means the boot path that populates it never runs. **So this probe does
not establish what the reference observes for memory size, and no conclusion is
drawn from it** - the same discipline that caught the halfword misread earlier.
The question is moot in any case, since the only consumer is compiled out.

#### The region, stated in the narrowed form

Not "empty" and not "settled". What is established:

> `0x00400000` and above is **outside every known linked, allocator-owned and
> source-identified memory user on this measured emulator configuration** -
> the `g_mempPools` table, the link-time stack and framebuffer placements,
> `RZIPBUFADDR`, and the two unreferenced debug tables at 0x500000/0x600000.

It remains **a candidate emulator-only logger region**, still subject to the
observer control that has to compare an instrumented image against an
uninstrumented one, and it is **not a claim about real 4 MB hardware**, where
no such space exists. If the ring is placed at 0x00400000 it must also avoid
0x00500000 and 0x00600000 outright rather than relying on those tables staying
unreferenced.

#### The control's contract, read before implementing - and it changes the deliverable

Instructed to trace the debug and size-control defines rather than trust the
Makefile comment. Doing so found a result this project has **already measured**
that constrains the whole event-logger plan, so it is surfaced before any logger
is written.

**What `ROM_SIZECTL` actually is.** `const u32 sl_romdbg_sizectl[0x230 / 4]`
(`lv.c:1716`) - inert `const` padding, no code, sized to the mailbox's own
`0x230`. It preserves **nothing** about data placement, BSS, control flow or
runtime writes. It controls for exactly one thing: **image size**. The reason is
`boss.c:389`, `nowCount = osGetCount(); randomSetSeed(nowCount);` - the RNG is
seeded from the CPU cycle counter at boot, so **any** change to the image lands
a different seed.

**So it is not a same-footprint control for a new logger.** Its padding is sized
to the existing mailbox. A logger with different code and data size needs its
padding re-derived to match, or the control is not controlling for that logger.

**The measured result that matters more.** Recorded in this file already:

```
  debug ROM vs parity ROM   diverges tick 79, and at that tick
                            hook_calls == 0 and magic == 0 - the hook had
                            NOT RUN ONCE when the seed already differed
  ROM_SIZECTL vs parity     diverges tick 79, fc=0, globals only - same tick,
                            same shape, same single field
```

and the instrument-isolating control, same image so identical boot seed, only
whether the mailbox was commanded:

```
  run    commands                       game ticks in 7418 frames   diverges
  quiet  none                           2906                        -
  one    ONE FINDTYPE at input idx 424  2394                        tick 529
  busy   FINDTYPE every 20 frames (361) 2571                        tick 529
```

One command diverges at the same tick as three hundred and sixty-one. The main
loop is paced against `osGetCount()`, so added work changes how many game ticks
fit in a frame and frame-rate-dependent state follows. The recorded conclusion:

> On a cycle-paced game any added work changes the run; cheaper only moves the
> divergence later. **An oracle inside the ROM cannot be non-perturbing here**,
> and that is the finding.

**Consequence for the plan, stated plainly.** The proposed acceptance - *no
behavioural oracle change between normal and control, or between control and
logger* - **is unachievable for the first pair**, and not because of any
instrument: the record states it is unachievable "for any change whatsoever,
including a one-instruction one". Requiring it would fail by construction.
`trace.py diff --across-roms` exists precisely because these traces are not
comparable field-for-field.

**What remains achievable, and it is still worth having.** The logger's run can
be validated **internally**, against itself rather than against the parity run:
carry the positive control and the effects events **in the same instrumented
run**. Then

> 435 frame-counter events, values 1..435, strictly ordered, none missing or
> duplicated, **and** zero effects entries

is a sound statement **about that instrumented run**, which shares the recorded
input stream but not the parity run's tick pacing. The absence is then scoped to
the instrumented run and must be reported that way - never as "the reference
does not exercise the effects player", which this instrument cannot establish.

That is a narrower deliverable than the plan assumed, and it is narrower for a
measured reason rather than a suspected one. **No logger is written yet**,
because the scope of what its output can license should be agreed before the
effort is spent.

#### Seed characterisation: the music path IS seed-independent, and the first attempt was vacuous

Instructed not to treat "narrower deliverable" as a conclusion but to measure
how narrow. Done on the **native** side, where the seed is a parameter
(`SL_RNG_SEED`) and the sequence-player instrumentation already exists - no ROM
build needed to answer the scope question.

**The first run looked like a result and was not one.** Four seeds produced a
byte-identical `md5` over MUSICSTART, NOTEOFF, the ordered duration dump,
SFXPLAYER and the `sndPlaySfx` call count. That asserts nothing unless the seed
actually changes the run, so a positive control was required - the same
discipline that caught the halfword misread and the snapshot poll.

**The obvious control FAILED.** Diffing the complete stderr across seeds gave
**four** differing lines, and both were artefacts:

```
  < sightline native: crash reports -> /tmp/sightline-crash-1418026.txt
  > sightline native: crash reports -> /tmp/sightline-crash-1418028.txt      (a PID)
  < sightline native: RNG state 00000000697ec8c8 (explicit SL_RNG_SEED)
  > sightline native: RNG state 0000000011111111 (explicit SL_RNG_SEED)      (the seed echo)
```

A filename containing a PID and the seed echoing itself. **Nothing observable in
that output depended on the seed**, so at that point the seed-independence
result was vacuous.

**A control that works: the harness's own per-tick game-state hashes.**
`SL_TRACE_OUT` arms `sl_state_capture`, which is the instrument the trace gate
itself uses:

```
  seed 00000000697ec8c8   trace sha1 099afdb377e48b11
  seed 0000000011111111   trace sha1 dcf6e8f9c81b750b
  seed 00000000deadbeef   trace sha1 757ba9376d389a61
```

Three seeds, three different game-state traces. **The seed demonstrably changes
the run.**

**So the result stands, and it is the favourable one:**

> Across four seeds whose game-state traces differ, the audio instrumentation
> output is **byte-identical**: `musicTrack1Play` at audio frame 249 and first
> note-on at 250 every time; note-on 44, scheduled 44, processed 32,
> noVoiceToStop 0; the ordered first-64 `(track, duration)` tuples identical
> tuple for tuple; `sndPlaySfx` calls 0.

**What this licenses.** The ordered note-on population is stable under exactly
the perturbation that makes tick-paced parity unachievable. So **note-on events
are usable for cross-side comparison regardless of parity divergence, and item 8
survives intact** - the seed/pacing objection does not reach them. This is what
converts the in-ROM-oracle finding from a blocker into a characterisation.

**Scope, stated narrowly.** This is the NATIVE side, on this fixture, over four
seeds; the compared surface is the first 64 note-on tuples plus the aggregate
counts, not every note-on in the run. The cartridge's own seed-independence is
not measured here - though the mechanism is shared code driven by sequence data
and tempo rather than the RNG, which is why the prediction was worth testing.
And `sndPlaySfx calls = 0` is now **zero across four independent seeds**, which
is the stronger achievable form of that claim, still scoped to native runs on
this fixture and still saying nothing about the reference.

#### The full note-on population is seed-independent - scope limitation removed

The previous entry's result covered the first 64 tuples plus aggregates and said
so. That limitation is now gone: every parsed note-on is recorded, in order,
with the complete tuple.

`SL_NOTEON_OUT` writes one fixed record per note-on at the parse site
(`cseq.c`), which is the one place that has all of it - track, status (hence
channel), key, velocity, the duration, the cursor either side of the varlen, the
bytes it consumed, and how many of those came from the back-reference buffer.
**Not a ring**: the whole ordered population is the oracle, and a ring that
wrapped would silently discard the tail.

**Cursors are recorded as OFFSETS from the first cursor seen, never as raw
pointers.** Absolute addresses differ between builds and between arms, and
comparing them across arms is exactly the mistake to avoid. The record also
tracks which pointer is live: `__getTrackByte` draws from the back-reference
buffer while `curBULen` is nonzero and from `curLoc` otherwise, so reporting
`curLoc` unconditionally would name the wrong pointer inside a back-reference.

```
  0 trk=2 ch=2 key=52 vel=127 curB=+0  curA=+2  bytes=2 dur=768 backupBytes=0
  1 trk=2 ch=2 key=53 vel=127 curB=+5  curA=+7  bytes=2 dur=675 backupBytes=0
  2 trk=2 ch=2 key=58 vel=127 curB=+10 curA=+12 bytes=2 dur=576 backupBytes=0
```

**Result, over the seeds already shown to produce different game-state traces:**

```
  seed 00000000697ec8c8   47 note-ons   sha1 d0cfc95420d7ebea
  seed 0000000011111111   47 note-ons   sha1 d0cfc95420d7ebea
  seed 00000000deadbeef   47 note-ons   sha1 d0cfc95420d7ebea
```

**The complete ordered note-on population is byte-identical across seeds** while
the per-tick game state is not. So the note-on oracle is usable cross-side
despite tick-paced parity being unachievable, and that now rests on the whole
population rather than a prefix of it.

**One number to keep straight.** 47 note-ons are PARSED here; the player counter
reports 44 note-ons PLAYED. Those are different counting points - `cseq` parses
events ahead of playback - and the difference is expected rather than a
discrepancy. The parse-side population is the right one for a parser oracle;
the play-side count is the right one for a lifecycle oracle. They must not be
compared to each other.

Still native-side only. The reference's own note-on population is what the ROM
logger is for, and nothing here measures it.

#### The event log, written - and the matching gate caught three of my mistakes

The logger is in, guarded by `SIGHTLINE_AUDIO_EVENTS` and inert without it.
Header `src/game/sl_audioev.h`; five sites: the frame-counter writer (the
positive control), the note-on tuple at the parse site, effects entry, and the
effect-count increment and decrement.

Design points, all of them forced rather than chosen: a fixed region rather than
linked storage, because a new static would shift the layout it is meant to
observe; **no wraparound** - the ring stops and raises `overflow`, since a
silently truncated log turns a missing event into an apparent absence, which is
the exact error the instrument exists to avoid; no formatting in the ROM, fixed
32-byte records with source-defined type IDs; and cursors logged as offsets,
never raw addresses, because those move between arms.

**Three separate failures, each caught by `make matching`, each a wrong
assumption of mine.** Recording them because the pattern is more useful than the
fix.

1. **Include paths are not uniform.** I checked `Makefile:206` -
   `-I . -I include -I include/PR -I src -I src/game ...` - and concluded both
   builds share it. `src/libultrare/Makefile.libultrare` compiles the audio
   library with a **narrower** set: `-I . -I include -I include/PR
   -I src/libultrare -I src/libultra`. `cseq.c` therefore could not see the
   header at all: *"Cannot open file sl_audioev.h for #include"*. Fixed with a
   relative include rather than widening the sub-make's paths, since adding an
   include directory to a byte-matching build can change which header a name
   resolves to.

2. **IDO is C89 and gcc is not.** My block went in at the top of
   `musicTrack1Play`, above its declarations. The native build accepted it
   silently; IDO rejected it, pointing at `u32 t3;`. Moved below the
   declarations.

3. **An inert macro is not the same as a deleted line, and this is the one that
   matters.** With both of those fixed the ROM compiled and **the checksum still
   failed**: `SL_AEV` expanding to `do { } while (0)` inside a block with an
   `extern` declaration was enough to change IDO's output even though it emits
   no code. The project's own facility states the correct discipline and I had
   departed from it - `sl_romdbg.h`: *"every line the flag adds is inside an
   #ifdef, so the preprocessor deletes all of it from the matching build."*
   Every call site and every `#include` is now inside `#ifdef
   SIGHTLINE_AUDIO_EVENTS`, and the matching build is byte-identical again.

**That third one is why the gate is load-bearing rather than ceremonial.** A
no-op macro is the intuitive way to write optional instrumentation, it is
correct on every compiler I would have tested it on, and it silently broke the
oracle this whole project is measured against. Nothing but the byte comparison
would have found it.

```
  matching MATCH! | trace IDENTICAL 15869 | layering clean
  native-health 900/900 exit 0 crashes 0 | stubs 30
  measurement scaffolding absent from the production binary
```

**Not yet built as a ROM and not yet run.** The define still has to be plumbed
through the direct-boot recipe - a `dflag` line beside `ROM_DEBUG`'s
(`Makefile:607-608`), the consuming files added to the recipe's `touch` list,
and the define added to the cached image's spec string and filename so a stale
image cannot be served. No event has been recorded from the reference yet, and
nothing about it is claimed.

#### The logger builds and the log stays empty - what is ruled out, and what is not

The define is plumbed through the direct-boot recipe following the existing
pattern exactly: a `ROM_AUDIO_EVENTS` variable, a `dflag` line beside
`ROM_DEBUG`'s, the consuming files added to **both** `touch` lists, and the flag
in the cached image's spec string and filename (`.aev.z64`) so a stale image
cannot be served. `make direct-boot LEVEL=facility ROM_AUDIO_EVENTS=1` produces
an image whose sha1 differs from the plain direct-boot image, and the
source-hash cache correctly forced a rebuild on every header edit.

**The log is nevertheless empty.** `header magic=0x00000000 ... count=0` on every
attempt.

**Ruled out by measurement, in order:**

```
  fixed address 0x80400000        all zeros
  uncached alias 0xA0400000       all zeros - so not the data cache
  linked array at 0x8005e950      all zeros - so not the region's mapping
    (address from the instrumented build's OWN map, ge007.u.facility.aev.map,
     not the matching build's, which does not contain the symbol)
  'SLAE' anywhere in 8 MB RDRAM   0 occurrences - the header was never written,
                                  rather than written somewhere unexpected
```

**One inference explicitly NOT drawn.** The scan also reported the magic bytes
absent from the ROM image, which looks like proof the code was never compiled
in. It is not: MIPS materialises a 32-bit constant as two 16-bit immediates, so
`0x534C4145` would never appear as four contiguous bytes in the image whether
the code is there or not. Only the RDRAM result is evidence.

**The region derivation is withdrawn as a basis, though not disproven.** The
fixed-address design rested on `retro_get_memory_size` reporting `0x800000`. A
reported size is not evidence the emulated machine maps that memory - GoldenEye
is a 4 MB title whose own map tiles exactly to `0x00400000`. Moving to linked
storage removed the question rather than answering it, and it remains
unanswered: **"the upper 4 MB is available" is not established.**

**The live suspect, stated as a suspect.** `dflag` reaches the compiler as
`LCDEFS` (`Makefile:627`), and the recipe's own note says LCDEFS changes do not
invalidate object files - which is exactly what the `touch` list exists to fix.
The touch list now names all four consuming files and the image hash does
change, so the define plainly reaches *something*; whether it reaches these four
translation units has not been confirmed. The next step is to confirm it
directly - a deliberate compile-time failure inside the guard, or reading the
instrumented map for `slAudioEvPut` - rather than to keep changing the storage.

**Everything else stays green.** The instrumentation is `#ifdef`-guarded
throughout, so the failure is confined to the oracle image:

```
  matching MATCH! | trace IDENTICAL 15869 | layering clean
  native-health 900/900 exit 0 crashes 0 | stubs 30
```

**No reference event has been recorded.** Every cross-side question this logger
exists to answer - whether the reference enters the effects path, its note-on
population, its request seam - remains unmeasured, and the earlier snapshot
result stays exactly what it was: **counter zero at every sampled boundary**.

#### The log is empty because AUDIO NEVER RUNS in the instrumented image

Three hypotheses tested and refuted before the real one appeared, and the last
control is what separated "the logger is broken" from "there was nothing to
log".

**The define does reach the code.** A deliberate `#error` inside the guard in
`audi.c` fired during the direct-boot build. Two findings from that one probe:
the flag reaches these translation units, and **IDO treats `#error` as
warning 605 and builds anyway** - so an `#error` is not a build-stopping
assertion here.

**The readback was reading the wrong addresses.** The instrumented image is a
different link, and its symbols move: `g_AudioFrameCount` is `0x800230f4` in the
matching build and `0x80023594` in the `.aev` image; `g_sndPlayerPtr` moves
`0x800243f0` -> `0x80024890`. Every earlier read used matching-build addresses
against the instrumented image, which is exactly the mistake of comparing raw
addresses across arms whose layouts differ - committed by me, against my own
notes, one entry after writing them down.

**With addresses taken from the instrumented map, the control finally
separates the two possibilities:**

```
  g_sndPlayerPtr     @0x80024890 = 0x80084010   sane, non-null -> READBACK WORKS
  g_AudioFrameCount  @0x80023594 = 0            after 900 frames
```

`g_AudioFrameCount` has exactly one normal writer, unconditional, one per audio
task. **Zero means `amClearDmaBuffers` never ran, so the audio manager never
ran.** The plain direct-boot image reaches 435 on the same fixture. So the log
is empty because nothing happened to log, not because the logger failed - and
the readback path is proven working by the same measurement.

**BSS size is not the cause.** The obvious mechanism was the log's own storage:
128 KB of BSS added to a memory map that tiles exactly to 4 MB, plausibly
starving the pool the 188 KB music heap comes from. Tested by shrinking the log
to 32 KB - a 96 KB reduction - and `g_AudioFrameCount` is **still 0**.
Refuted.

**So the mechanism is unidentified.** What is established: the instrumented
image builds, the define reaches the instrumented files, the readback works, and
in that image the audio manager does not start at all while the uninstrumented
image's does. Something about this image suppresses audio init, and it is not
the log's size.

That is a much more specific question than the one this pass started with, and
it is the next thing to answer - by comparing audio init on the two images step
by step, using each image's own symbols, rather than by changing the logger
again. Three storage designs have now been changed on hypotheses that turned out
wrong; the fourth change should follow a measurement, not precede one.

```
  matching MATCH! | trace IDENTICAL 15869 | layering clean
  native-health 900/900 exit 0 crashes 0 | stubs 30
```

**Still no reference event recorded**, and every cross-side question remains
unmeasured. The snapshot result stays what it was: counter zero at every sampled
boundary.

#### Two narrowings to the record above (2026-08-31)

Both of these correct wording that was written stronger than the measurements
support. History is not rewritten; the commits stand, and this is the narrowing.

**1. "scope limit removed" (623f045e) claims more than was measured.**

What is established is a native-side fact, and only that:

> Across three NATIVE runs whose game-state traces differ under different RNG
> seeds, the measured complete 47-event native NoteOn population is
> **byte-identical**.

That is strong evidence of native RNG-seed independence for the music path. It
is **not** evidence that the NoteOn path is insensitive to *the instrument*.
Seed independence and instrumentation independence are different invariances:
the first varies game state inside one binary, the second varies the binary.
Nothing in that experiment adds instructions, changes link layout, or changes
cycle pacing, so it cannot speak to any of them.

And the `.aev` image is a direct counterexample at an earlier seam: a reference
ROM whose only change is added, `#ifdef`-guarded instrumentation does **not**
reach the same audio lifecycle as the plain image. So "scope limit removed"
should be read as "the native seed-scope limit is removed"; the observer
relation for an instrumented reference ROM is open, and currently reads
negative.

**2. "the audio manager never ran" is stronger than the measurement.**

The measured statement is:

> In the instrumented `.aev` image the **normal audio-frame handling path never
> advances**: `g_AudioFrameCount` remains 0 after the measured run, while other
> audio-related init state — `g_sndPlayerPtr` — is non-null.

A non-null `g_sndPlayerPtr` means some audio initialisation *did* happen. So the
correct claim is that the frame-handling path never advanced, not that audio
init never began. The exact stopping point between those two facts is
**unresolved**, and locating it is the measurement, not an inference from the
zero.


#### The instrumented image does not fail at audio. It never finishes booting. 2026-08-31

The previous entry asked for a step-by-step comparison of audio init on the two
images. The answer is that there is no audio init to compare: the earliest
divergence is upstream of every audio checkpoint, upstream of the memory pools,
and upstream of the game's first tick.

**Measurement tool.** `tools/native/audioinit.py` reads fifteen lifecycle
checkpoints out of RDRAM, resolving every address from the image's OWN linker
map. It is not instrumentation - every checkpoint is ordinary global state the
game writes anyway - so adding a checkpoint cannot perturb the run it observes.
Two byte-order notes it now carries, both paid for once: RDRAM holds 32-bit
words in host order and must be read through `sltrace.state.Memory`, not as
plain big-endian (a first pass read `g_sndPlayerPtr` as `0x503b0680`); and code
does not live at `0x8xxxxxxx` in this image at all - `.code` is at
`0x70000450` and `.game` at `0x7f000000`, so a symbol filter clipped to the
`0x8` range hides every function name.

**Plain direct-boot, facility, 900 frames - the reference.**

```
  os_scheduler.frameCount   901          g_AudioFrameCount   435
  audio client on the scheduler list exactly once (walked from clientList)
  audio thread id 4 pri 20 WAITING on frameMessageQueue
  music heap base 0x802c7ca0 len 188416 used 186256 free 2160
  __osFaultedThread  0x00000000   for all 600 frames sampled
```

`g_AudioFrameCount == 435` is the source-derived expectation met exactly, which
is what licenses using this image as the control.

**The `.aev` image, same input, same frame count.**

```
  os_scheduler.frameCount   0            g_AudioFrameCount   0
  currentFrameCounter       0            g_mempPools         ALL ZERO
  music heap / banks / synth / sequence players / manager   ALL ZERO
  __osFaultedThread  0x8005dae0
```

**It is executing, and it is executing nothing.** Diffing all 8 MB of RDRAM
between two consecutive frames finds 28 changed bytes, in four runs, and every
one of them is interrupt bookkeeping: `__osViCurr`, `__osCurrentTime`, and two
words of OS state. No thread is running game code.

**The fault, read out of the thread the OS marked.** Walking `__osActiveQueue`
and decoding each `OSThread` - `__OSThreadContext` begins with a `u64` and so
is 8-byte aligned, putting it at `+0x20`, not `+0x1c`; the proof is that
`0x20 + 0x110 + 16*8 = 0x1b0`, exactly the distance from
`g_AudioManager.audioThread` to `frameMessageQueue`, and the idle thread's
saved pc then resolves to `idleproc+0x0`:

```
  thread 0x8005dae0  id=3 pri=10  STOPPED
    cause 0x00000008  ExcCode 2 (TLB load)   badvaddr 0x00000005
    pc    0x7f000bd4  image_entries_load+0x4
    ra    0x70005e50  bossInitMainthreadData+0x30
  thread 0x80069150  id=5 pri=40  RUNNING at crashMain+0x110
```

`ra` is the return address of the `jal 0x7f000bd0` at `bossInitMainthreadData`
+0x28, which is `image_entries_load()` - `boss.c:189`. That call is **the first
jump this boot makes into the TLB-mapped `.game` segment**, and it is one line
before `mempInit()` and five before `musicSeqPlayerInit()`.

The faulting instruction is not in `image_entries_load`; the saved `a0` shows
its own first instruction had not executed. It is `lw $k1, ($k0)` in the TLB
refill handler, `tlb_resolve.s:25`, with an effective address of 5. `crashMain`
is a demand pager for that segment: it services a fault whose `badvaddr` lies
in `0x7F000000/22` and rejects everything else. 5 is not in that range, so it
takes the `else break` and spins in `while (1) {}` - which is where thread id 5
is sitting.

**So the log is empty because the game crashes at boot.** Not because the audio
manager failed to start, and not because the logger failed.

**Two retractions, both mine, both from this morning.**

1. *"other audio-related init state such as `g_sndPlayerPtr` is non-null, so
   some audio initialization happened"* is **wrong**. `snd.c:107` is
   `ALSndPlayer *g_sndPlayerPtr = &g_sndPlayer;` - a static initializer. Its
   value is a link-time fact, present before any instruction runs. It offsets
   from `g_musicHeap` by 0x440 in both images, which is the tell. **No audio
   initialisation happened at all**, and the narrowing written above is itself
   narrowed by this.

2. *"the upper 4 MB is not established as mapped"* was withdrawn on evidence
   that is now known to be **confounded**. The fixed-address log read back all
   zeros, the uncached alias read back all zeros, and `SLAE` appeared nowhere
   in 8 MB - all measured on an image that never reached the code that writes
   them. Those readings say nothing about the mapping. The question is open
   again, and it matters, because the high address is the only storage design
   that does not spend the budget below.

#### The budget: 864 bytes, and this image is 33,984 over it

Not a hypothesis - the pools, read out of the running plain image:

```
  MEMPOOL_TOTAL      start 0x8008e360   end 0x802f6000
  MEMPOOL_PERMANENT  start 0x802ac000   pos 0x802f5ca0  end 0x802f6000  free 864
```

`MEMPOOL_TOTAL.start` is exactly `_bssSegmentEnd`, and the top is exactly
`g_tlbmanageTlbAllocatedBlock` = `(sp_boot & ~0x1fff) - 90*0x2000` = 0x802f6000,
which is fixed by the stack base and identical in both images. **The pool is
bounded below by the link and above by a constant, so every byte the link grows
comes straight out of those 864.**

What the two images cost:

```
                     .code size    _bssSegmentEnd    growth
  plain               0x20940       0x8008e360         -
  .aev                0x20de0       0x80096820      +0x84c0  (33,984)
```

Split: **+0x4a0 of `.code`** and **+0x8020 of `.bss`** (the 32 KB log plus its
header). And the `.code` growth is attributable to the byte:

```
  audi.o                0xb60 -> 0xc50   +240
  libultra/audio/cseq.o 0xac0 -> 0xc20   +352
  music.o              0x1130 -> 0x1230  +256
  snd.o                0x1860 -> 0x19b0  +336
                                        = 0x4a0
```

Exactly the four instrumented translation units, and nothing else in `.code`
moved. `slAudioEvPut` is a `static` function in a header, so each of the four
gets its own copy.

**This is why shrinking the log from 128 KB to 32 KB changed nothing, and it
predicts that no log size would have.** Even at zero log bytes the instrument
still costs 1,184 bytes of `.code`, which is 320 over budget on its own.

**The control that makes the budget a real number rather than an arithmetic
story: the debug ROM, which works.**

```
  facility-pane        .csegment 0x80020d90   _bssSegmentEnd 0x8008e360
  facility-pane.dbg    .csegment 0x80020d90   _bssSegmentEnd 0x8008e5a0   +576
  facility-pane.ctl    .csegment 0x80020d90   _bssSegmentEnd 0x8008e590   +560
```

`ROM_DEBUG` grows the image by 576 bytes and boots; `ROM_SIZECTL` by 560 and
boots. Both are under 864. `ROM_DEBUG` instruments `lv.c`, which lives in
`.game` - TLB-paged at a fixed VMA - so its `.csegment` does not move at all.
The entire audio path lives in `.code`, the resident segment, so instrumenting
it moves everything after it. That difference is the whole reason one debug ROM
works and this one does not.

#### What is established, and what is explicitly not

**Established.** The earliest differing checkpoint is upstream of checkpoint 1:
the instrumented image faults during boot, at the first entry into the
TLB-mapped `.game` segment, three source lines before the memory pools exist.
The plain image never faults in 600 frames and reaches the source-derived 435.
The layout budget is 864 bytes and this image is 33,984 over it. The `.code`
growth is 1,184 bytes and is fully attributed to the four instrumented objects.

**Not established, and not to be inferred.** *Why* the effective address is 5.
Both images' refill handlers relocate correctly and identically in structure -
plain `addiu $k1,$k1,-7004` -> 0x8005e4a4, `.aev` `addiu $k1,$k1,-5820` ->
0x8005e944, each matching its own map - and both images' stored
`g_tlbmanageMappingTableEnd` equals `&g_tlbManagementTable - 0x3F8000` exactly,
so the handler's arithmetic is right in both. `initTLBPrepareContext` sets
`C0_CONTEXT` to 0 in both. Nothing measured yet explains a 5. The boot fault and
the pool budget are **two separate facts**; the budget is not offered as the
cause of the fault, because the pools do not exist yet when the fault happens.

**Also not claimed.** That the repair below will work. It is a plan derived from
the measurement, not a result.

#### Where this leaves the oracle

An in-link log is impossible, not merely difficult: 435 frame-count events at 32
bytes is 13,920 bytes minimum, and the budget is 864. No record size, no
capacity, and no compression closes a 16x gap. So the only surviving design is
storage outside the link - and the reason that design was abandoned is now known
to be a confounded reading.

The measured, non-speculative repair path, in order:

1. Give `slAudioEvPut` a single definition instead of a `static` one per
   translation unit. Measured cost of the duplication: most of 1,184 bytes.
2. Move storage back out of the link, which returns 32,800 bytes.
3. Rebuild and check `__osFaultedThread == 0` and `g_AudioFrameCount == 435`
   **before believing any event output** - the same two numbers the plain image
   already answers, now as an acceptance test on the instrumented one.
4. Only then is the mapping question at the high address answerable, because
   only then is there a run that reaches the code that writes it.

Until step 3 passes, every cross-side question this logger exists to answer
stays unmeasured, and the snapshot result stays exactly what it has been:
counter zero at every sampled boundary.

**No production source changed in this pass.** The only addition is
`tools/native/audioinit.py`, a read-only RDRAM probe.


#### The repair the measurement licensed, and why it did not work. 2026-08-31

The budget above said linked storage was impossible, so the repair was the one
the measurement pointed at, and only that:

- `slAudioEvPut` was `static` in a header and so existed four times over. It
  now has a single definition in `audi.c`.
- The log's storage left the link entirely and went back to the fixed address.

```
                       .code       _bssSegmentEnd    growth over plain
  before repair       0x20de0        0x80096820        +33,984
  after  repair       0x20b80        0x8008e5a0           +576
  ROM_DEBUG (works)   unchanged      0x8008e5a0           +576
```

576 bytes is under the 864-byte budget and is **exactly** what the debug ROM
that works costs. `slAudioEvLog` no longer appears in the map at all. And the
image still does not boot: `__osFaultedThread` non-null at emulator frame 0,
main thread STOPPED, `crashMain` spinning, every audio checkpoint zero,
`g_mempPools` entirely zero.

**So the layout budget is not the cause.** It is a real constraint and it does
bound any future linked design, but it does not explain this fault, and the
repair is what separates the two.

**A retraction of my own reading from earlier in this same entry.** The first
build's fault reported `pc = 0x7f000bd4 (image_entries_load+0x4)` and
`badvaddr = 0x00000005`. The repaired build faults with the identical thread,
state and register file - `v0`/`v1` holding `&g_tlbmanageMappingTableEnd`, `a0`
= 1, `t0` holding the correct computed base - but reports `pc = 0x00000000` and
`badvaddr = 0x00000000`. **Those two fields are not stable across builds, so
neither is evidence of a faulting instruction.** I read a precise site off them
and should not have; a nested exception taken with `EXL` already set does not
update `EPC`. What IS stable, and what the two builds agree on, is the thread,
its stopped state, and a register file still holding `tlbmanage` locals - i.e.
the fault is at the boot position immediately after
`tlbmanageEstablishManagementTable`, which is where the first jump into the
TLB-mapped `.game` segment happens.

#### Three causes ruled out by measurement, so nobody re-runs them

**The direct-boot recipe is not broken.** The plain reference image was a week
old, which would have confounded everything. A plain image rebuilt from this
exact tree (`SL_NAME=facility-boottest`) boots and reaches
`sched.frameCount 901`, `currentFrameCounter 900`, `g_AudioFrameCount 435`.

**The data segment is not corrupt.** `data_compress.sh` carries a
`#fixme as I will fail if vaddr of data gets moved!!!` and emits
`printf: 0x: invalid hex number` on every build, which looked like the answer.
It is not: the error appears on the matching build too, which still reports
`MATCH!`. And `.csegment` decompresses correctly in the instrumented image -
`g_Textures` there holds the raw per-entry sizes `0x754, 0x16a, 0x974, 0x38b`
while the plain image holds their running sums `0, 0x754, 0x8be, 0x1232`. That
is exactly the transform `image_entries_load` performs, so the table is intact
in both and the only difference is that one image ran the function.

**The loop does not run away.** The table terminates 2,698 entries in, at
`0x8004e990`, well inside `.csegment`. `image_entries_load` would complete.

#### What the instrument does that a working debug ROM does not

`ROM_DEBUG` instruments `lv.c`, which lives in `.game` - TLB-paged at a fixed
VMA - so its `.csegment` does not move and `.code` does not grow. The audio
path is `audi.c`, `music.c`, `snd.c` and `libultra/audio/cseq.c`, **all of them
in `.code`**, the resident segment. Instrumenting them necessarily grows
`.code`, which moves `_codeSegmentEnd`, `__dataSegmentVaddrStart`, the `.cdata`
and `.csegment` load addresses and every segment after them.

That is the only structural difference left standing between the debug ROM that
works and this one that does not, and it is not one the instrument can avoid:
there is no way to log an event in the audio path without emitting an
instruction in `.code`.

**Not established, and it is the one control not run.** That `.code` growth per
se is what breaks boot. The experiment that would settle it is inert `.code`
growth - bytes, no reachable code, no new state - built and boot-tested the
same way. `ROM_SIZECTL` is not that control: it grows `.bss` by 560 and leaves
`.code` alone. Anyone returning to this should run that first, before touching
the logger again.

#### Retiring this logger for this oracle

Per the standing rule that a failed oracle architecture is a finding rather than
a reason to stop: **the in-ROM audio event log is retired as the request→NoteOn
oracle.** Not deleted - it costs nothing when the flag is off, the matching
build is byte-identical with it in the tree, and it is in better shape than it
was (576 bytes instead of 33,984, storage out of the link, one writer). It is
retired as a *measurement route*, because none of its call sites has ever
executed and no repair short of the unrun control above is indicated.

Stated plainly so it is not quietly assumed later: **no reference-side audio
event has ever been recorded.** Every cross-side question - whether the
reference enters the effects path, its note-on population, its request seam -
is unmeasured, and the only reference-side audio result that stands remains the
snapshot one: `g_sndAllocatedVoicesCount == 0` at each sampled video-frame
boundary.

Gates on the delivered tree:

```
  matching MATCH! | trace IDENTICAL 15869 | layering OK (baseline 282, no new)
  native-health facility/pinned seed 900/900 exit 0 crashes 0 | stubs 30
  measurement scaffolding absent from the production binary
```

One incidental note for whoever runs the gates next: **the project rules document
the native build as `make sightline`, and no such target exists** - it is
`native-skeleton`, and `native-health` builds it itself. Not fixed here;
the rules document is owner-maintained.


#### The control ran, and it names the mechanism: this image cannot tolerate ANY `.code` growth. 2026-08-31

The previous entry named one unrun control and retired the logger on a
hypothesis. The control is now run, and the hypothesis was right - but the
number is far smaller than expected, which makes the finding much broader than
"the audio logger is too big".

**The control.** `ROM_CODECTL=1` (`Makefile`, `SL_AUDIOEV_CODECTL` in
`audi.c`) adds one function that is **never called from anywhere**, in one of
the same translation units, and nothing else. No reachable code, no new state,
no behaviour, no linked data of its own - volatile stores to a fixed address so
nothing can be folded away. `slAudioEvCodeCtl` is present in the map, so it was
not dead-stripped.

It is a different control from `ROM_SIZECTL`, and that distinction is the whole
point. `ROM_SIZECTL`'s padding is a `const` array in `lv.c`, which lives in the
TLB-paged `.game` segment: it grows `_bssSegmentEnd` and leaves `.code`
untouched. This one grows `.code`, the resident segment, and only `.code`.

**First attempt, and why its result was not usable.** 70 stores grew `.code` by
0x350 - 848 bytes, sixteen under the 864-byte pool budget - and the image did
not boot. That could not distinguish "the segment grew" from "the pool ran
out", so it is recorded and discarded rather than reported.

**The measurement, at a size where no budget argument survives:**

```
                    .code      growth   _bssSegmentEnd   pool headroom left   boots
  plain            0x20940        -       0x8008e360           864             yes
  ROM_CODECTL      0x20990      +0x50     0x8008e3b0           784             NO
  ROM_AUDIO_EVENTS 0x20b80     +0x240     0x8008e5a0           288             NO
  ROM_DEBUG      unchanged      +0x240*   0x8008e5a0           288             yes
                                  * in .game rodata, not .code
```

**Eighty bytes of never-executed `.text` prevents the image from booting**, with
784 bytes of pool headroom still free. The failure signature is identical to the
audio image's in every stable respect: `__osFaultedThread` non-null at frame 0,
main thread id 3 pri 10 STOPPED, `crashMain` running, `TLBload`, register file
still holding `tlbmanage` locals, `g_mempPools` entirely zero, every audio
checkpoint zero.

And for the third time `pc` and `badvaddr` disagree between builds - 0x7f000bd4
/5, then 0/0, now 0x7f000bd0/4. Three builds, three values. Those fields are
noise here, and the earlier reading of a precise faulting instruction off them
stays retracted.

#### What this establishes

**The mechanism is `.code` growth itself, not the instrument and not the
budget.** The 864-byte pool budget is real and still bounds any linked design,
but it is not what breaks these images: 80 bytes of growth with 784 spare is
fatal, and 576 bytes of growth in `.game` rodata is fine.

**So an in-ROM oracle for the audio path is impossible, and the reason is
structural.** `audi.c`, `music.c`, `snd.c` and `libultra/audio/cseq.c` are all
in `.code`. There is no way to log an audio event without emitting an
instruction there, and this build does not survive one. `ROM_DEBUG` works only
because `lv.c` is in the TLB-paged `.game`, where growth costs nothing to
`.code`. **The logger is retired for this oracle with the mechanism named**, not
merely suspected.

**This is bigger than the logger, and it is the part worth carrying forward.**
Any future ROM-side instrumentation of anything in `.code` will fail the same
way, silently, with an empty result that looks like an absence. That is exactly
the failure this sprint spent itself on. Instrument `.game` or do not instrument
in ROM.

#### What is NOT established

**Why `.code` growth breaks boot.** Growing it moves `_codeSegmentEnd`, hence
`__dataSegmentVaddrStart` and the `.cdata`/`.csegment` load addresses.
`tools/data_compress.sh` carries the comment
`#fixme as I will fail if vaddr of data gets moved!!!`, which is the obvious
suspect - but it is only a suspect, and one measurement already argues against
the simplest version of it: `.csegment` decompresses **correctly** in the
instrumented image, `g_Textures` holding valid raw per-entry sizes. Whatever is
size-sensitive is not simply "the data segment fails to decompress".

**Whether this is a defect worth fixing.** A boot path that cannot survive 80
bytes of resident-segment growth is fragile, and it constrains every future ROM
experiment. Deliberately not chased here: it is a boot/loader question, not an
audio one, and it belongs to whoever owns the direct-boot recipe. Recorded as
`B-057` below rather than fixed inside an audio sprint.

**Unchanged and still true:** no reference-side audio event has ever been
recorded. The only reference-side audio result that stands is the snapshot one -
`g_sndAllocatedVoicesCount == 0` at each sampled video-frame boundary.

Gates on the delivered tree, with the control compiled in and flag-off:

```
  matching MATCH! | trace IDENTICAL 15869 | layering OK (baseline 282, no new)
  native-health facility/pinned seed 900/900 exit 0 crashes 0
  measurement scaffolding absent from the production binary
```

### B-057 — the direct-boot image does not survive ANY growth of the `.code` segment

- **Found:**  2026-08-31, running the control for the retired audio event log
- **Owner:**  unclear - boot/loader, not audio. Whoever owns `direct-boot`.
- **Where:** `src/init.c` boot path, `tools/data_compress.sh`, `ge007.ld`
- **Blocks:** every future ROM-side instrument that touches a file in `.code`

Adding 80 bytes of never-executed `.text` to `audi.c` produces an image that
faults during boot at the first entry into the TLB-mapped `.game` segment, with
784 bytes of permanent-pool headroom still free. Growth of the same size and
larger in `.game` rodata (`ROM_SIZECTL`, `ROM_DEBUG`) boots normally.

Reproduce:
```
make direct-boot LEVEL=facility ROM_CODECTL=1 SL_NAME=facility
tools/native/audioinit.py --image facility.cctl --input facility --frames 900
```
A healthy image reports `sched.frameCount 901`, `currentFrameCounter 900`,
`g_AudioFrameCount 435`; this one reports 0, 0, 0 and a non-null
`__osFaultedThread`.

The suspect is that `.code` growth moves `__dataSegmentVaddrStart` and the
`.cdata`/`.csegment` load addresses, and `tools/data_compress.sh` says of
itself `#fixme as I will fail if vaddr of data gets moved!!!`. Not confirmed:
`.csegment` demonstrably decompresses correctly in a failing image, so the
simplest version of that story is already ruled out.


#### RESAMPLE state: the residue is 26 bytes in ONE vector lane, and it is NOT an ADPCM consequence. 2026-08-31

With the ROM oracle retired, the cartridge ACMD capture is the independent
oracle, and it is untouched by any of the logger work: `acmd_census.py`
brackets every task with a before/after DRAM snapshot, and
`tools/native/acmdrslow.c` already scores all 32 predicted state bytes against
it. Fresh capture, 435 aligned frames, 7909 RESAMPLE commands.

**Baseline, and it localises the residue to a single 16-bit lane:**

```
  RESAMPLE commands exercised : A_INIT 1   CONTINUE 803
  last-writer OBSERVABLE      : A_INIT 0   CONTINUE 150
  bytes compared              : A_INIT 0   CONTINUE 4800
  MISMATCHES                  : A_INIT 0   CONTINUE 26

    +0x00..07 history   0      +0x0A..0B align       0
    +0x08..09 phase     0      +0x0C..0F preserved   0
    +0x10..1F quad     26
```

Every field the previous work grounded stays exact. The whole residue is 13
commands x 2 bytes at **+0x10..11 - element 0 of the stored quad**. Bytes
+0x12..1F are byte-for-byte identical to `dmem[P2+2 .. P2+15]` in every case,
which rules out any shifted or rotated source: a shift would move all sixteen.

Every mismatching command shares the same shape: `a0 == 0`, `in == 0x846`, and
`P2 & 15 == 6` - the input base is itself 6 mod 16, so the row the microcode
aligns **relative to `in`** is misaligned in ABSOLUTE DMEM, which is exactly
where RSP vector-load row semantics would bite.

**A hypothesis of mine, tested and refuted.** These commands sit in the task
range where ADPCM appears, so the obvious reading was that the interpreter's
DMEM is missing bytes an unexecuted ADPCM would have written. Measured over the
sampled mismatching frames: **10 of 10 contain no ADPCM at all.** They are among
the 131 tasks that execute to completion. So the residue is a genuine RESAMPLE
semantics gap on clean DMEM, not a downstream ADPCM artifact - the opposite of
what I expected, and worth recording because the wrong reading would have
deferred a solvable question behind a much larger one.

**The state chain is confirmed sound, which is what makes the residue
trustworthy.** For consecutive tasks the incoming state's +0x10..11 equals the
previous task's outgoing value - `0x0283 -> 0x0024 -> 0x00d5`,
`0xff85 -> 0x0021 -> 0xffe8 -> 0xfffb` - so the buffers are being read and
attributed correctly, and the lane is genuinely rewritten each task rather than
preserved. `islast` was checked rather than assumed: it tracks the last
RESAMPLE per state address across the whole task, and the independent
Python pass over the capture agrees on the observable population.

**Candidate sources enumerated and all excluded**, each against all 13
commands: preservation from the incoming DRAM state; the scratch's prior
contents at +0x10 (always 0000); the first and last output samples; the
halfword below `P2`; the pre-alignment address `P1`; and an exhaustive search of
the entire +-64-byte DMEM neighbourhood, which finds the cartridge's value at a
plausible offset in **one** of thirteen cases and nowhere in the other twelve.
The value is not a copy of anything nearby. **The source is unidentified**, and
it is recorded as unidentified rather than guessed - the corpus is silent here
(`gedocs search 'LDV SQV vector load element wrap'` and `'RSP microcode
vector'` both return nothing, and `doc-routing.json` already carries the
`audio microcode / ACMD command set` not_covered entry), so only measurement
can settle it.

#### The ordering in the brief is inverted by measurement

The plan was RESAMPLE first, then ADPCM. The capture says the dependency runs
the other way. Grounding more RESAMPLE state means comparing more
(task, state-address) pairs at end-of-task, and a pair is only soundly
comparable when its LAST toucher is the RESAMPLE we modelled - comparing a
buffer that is rewritten later against an end-of-task snapshot is an error this
harness has already recorded making once.

Counting those pairs over the capture, with the DRAM-writing opcodes
(ADPCM, ENVMIXER, RESAMPLE, SAVEBUFF, POLEF) as the toucher set:

```
  already comparable today (task has no ADPCM)  : 147
  newly reachable without executing ADPCM       :   3
  still blocked behind the first ADPCM          : 1482
```

**1482 of 1632 pairs sit behind ADPCM, and the pre-ADPCM route buys three.**
The number is unchanged whether the toucher set is the conservative
"any command whose operand lands in the region" or the exact DRAM-writer set,
so it is not an artifact of that choice. There is no more RESAMPLE state to
ground until ADPCM executes.

So the residue above is the whole of what this oracle can currently see, and
the next work is ADPCM - which is both the brief's next item and the gate on
1482 further RESAMPLE comparisons.

**Tooling.** `tools/native/acmdrslow.c` gains an `RS_DUMP=1` diagnostic that
prints the DMEM neighbourhood of `P2`, the cartridge quad beside the predicted
one, and the candidate sources. It is env-gated: default output is unchanged,
byte for byte, and no production source was touched in this pass.

**Not claimed.** That the +0x10..11 rule is known. That RESAMPLE is closed -
it is not; 26 bytes remain unexplained on the observable population and 1482
pairs remain unobservable. ADPCM stays fail-loud by default.


#### Decoded ADPCM PCM is grounded, and the whole command stream is now byte-exact. 2026-08-31

The 2026-08-30 note that restored `SL_ACMD_ADPCM 0` stated its objection
precisely: *"no sample here has been compared against anything the console
produced."* That is what changed. It is not a change of mind about the
default-off discipline; the condition that discipline named has been met.

**The measurement**, against the cartridge ACMD capture with per-task
before/after DRAM brackets, 435 aligned tasks:

```
  frames byte-exact 435/435      bytes compared  5227776
  of which nonzero  3320001 (63.51%)
  bytes differing   0            max |err| 0     RMS 0.00
  over 1869567 nonzero written samples
```

For contrast, the same capture with ADPCM fail-loud: 131 frames exact, 304
aborting at their first ADPCM, 1574272 bytes compared. Enabling the decode adds
**3.65 million compared bytes, all of which match** - so the decode's output is
not merely internally consistent, it is reaching the compared DRAM population
through SAVEBUFF and agreeing there.

**A passing score proves nothing on its own, so the decode is challenged.**
Six controls, each breaking exactly one load-bearing decision, with eligibility
counted separately from application:

```
  1 nibble order        eligible 349712   bytes differing 1117034  max|err| 22004
  2 scale-skip removed  eligible  36832   bytes differing  466117  max|err| 16160
  3 predictor book      eligible  21857   bytes differing 1206448  max|err| 24668
  4 half history pair   eligible  43714   bytes differing 1107638  max|err| 16934
  5 accumulator wrap    eligible      0   bytes differing       0  NOT EXERCISED
  6 residual tap        eligible 349712   bytes differing 1026184  max|err|  8247
```

Five of six move cartridge-visible bytes decisively, so the comparison is not
vacuous for nibble order, scale handling, predictor selection, cross-half
history, or the residual tap.

**Control 2 is the one worth naming.** It *removes* the blob's `blez` quirk at
`scale >= 12` - that is, it "fixes" the odd-looking behaviour the decoder
reproduces deliberately - and 194 frames break. The quirk is real,
load-bearing, and correctly reproduced rather than guessed at.

#### The one decision that is NOT grounded, stated before the good news is used

Control 5 perturbs the 48-bit accumulator's low-32 wrap - the `VSAR HIGH:MID`
read - and **its eligibility over the entire capture is zero**. The accumulator
never leaves int32 range on this fixture, so wrapping and plain arithmetic are
indistinguishable here. No amount of byte-exactness on this capture says
anything about that branch.

The wrap is kept, because it is what the microcode's accumulator read implies.
It is **counted, not trusted**: `sl_acmd_ungrounded_adwrap` increments on every
occurrence.

**And that counter is proven live rather than assumed**, which is the rule a
zero counter has to satisfy before it means anything. With its threshold
lowered to 2^20 it reads **158404** on this same capture; at the real int32
threshold it reads **0**; byte-exactness is 435/435 either way, so the lowered
threshold changes only the counting and not the arithmetic. The zero is
therefore a measurement of the fixture, not an absence of instrumentation.

#### The default

`SL_ACMD_ADPCM` now defaults to **1**. This is the change the 08-30 entry
explicitly gated on grounding, and the grounding is above. `-DSL_ACMD_ADPCM=0`
restores the fail-loud path.

What this unblocks, beyond the decode itself: 1482 of the 1632 RESAMPLE
(task, state-address) pairs recorded above were unobservable because their task
aborted at its first ADPCM. They are now reachable.

#### Interface, not scaffolding - and one stale contract this forced out

The counter follows the existing convention: ungrounded counters are declared in
`sl_acmd.h` as **interface**, not left internal, because a caller must be able
to see that production relied on ungrounded behaviour. `sl_acmd_ungrounded_adwrap`
now sits with `_neg`, `_rsinit` and `_state`.

Adding it exposed a contract that the default flip had silently falsified. The
`sl_acmd_adpcm_*` counters' header comment read: *"Gated off by default
(SL_ACMD_ADPCM), so a nonzero value in a production build means unaccepted
arithmetic produced audio."* With the default now 1 that reading is **wrong and
actively misleading** - a nonzero value there is now ordinary, a measure of how
much decoding a run did. The comment is rewritten to say so, and to point at
`sl_acmd_ungrounded_adwrap` as the counter that now carries the warning. Worth
recording: flipping a default can invalidate documentation elsewhere that still
reads as true, and the header was the only place saying it.

The artefact check therefore has TWO directions, and both were run against
`build/native/skeleton`:

```
  INTERFACE, must be PRESENT
    sl_acmd_ungrounded_adwrap   09011204 B     sl_acmd_ungrounded_neg     present
    sl_acmd_ungrounded_rsinit   present        sl_acmd_ungrounded_state   present
    sl_acmd_adpcm_cmds          present
  MEASUREMENT SCAFFOLDING, must be ABSENT
    sl_ad_mut  sl_ad_elig  sl_ad_applied  sl_rs_elig  sl_rs_applied
    sl_am_steps  sl_am_frames                    all absent
```

Gates on the delivered tree:

```
  matching MATCH! | trace IDENTICAL 15869 | layering OK (baseline 282, no new)
  native-health facility/pinned seed 900/900 exit 0 crashes 0 | stubs 30
  interface counters present; measurement scaffolding absent
```

**Not claimed.** That sound works - nothing here has produced a sample through
the native audio path. That the accumulator wrap is correct; it is unexercised.
That RESAMPLE is closed - its 26-byte residue at +0x10..11 stands unexplained,
and the newly reachable pairs have not yet been scored.


#### Narrowing the ADPCM result, and the first measurement of PRODUCTION's state writeback. 2026-08-31

The entry above says "the whole command stream is now byte-exact". **That is
too strong, and the mask is why.**

`acmdreplay` builds its comparison mask from **SAVEBUFF destinations only**
(`op == 6`, sized by the SETBUFF count in force). So its 435/435 and its
5,227,776 bytes are a statement about **the PCM written to DRAM** - nothing
else. The 32-byte RESAMPLE and ADPCM state blocks were never in that mask and
were never scored by it.

This is also what made this harness and `acmdrslow` look like they contradicted
each other. They did not: one scores PCM, the other scores state blocks, and
`0 bytes differing` from the first says nothing whatever about the second. Two
populations, never merged.

**The ADPCM grounding stands, with its scope stated properly.** Decoded ADPCM
output reaches DRAM through SAVEBUFF, so the SAVEBUFF population IS the decoded
PCM, and that is what the five non-vacuous controls challenged. What may NOT be
read from it is any claim about state blocks.

**So the state blocks were scored, on the production path, for the first time.**
A second mask, disjoint from the first, over every RESAMPLE and ADPCM state
destination in the task. Soundness: the whole task executes before comparing,
so a byte written many times is still comparable against the end-of-task
snapshot - last-writer identity matters for ATTRIBUTING a mismatch, not for
detecting one.

```
  PCM   (SAVEBUFF mask)      5227776 bytes   3320001 nonzero     0 differing
  STATE (RESAMPLE/ADPCM)       82592 bytes     63493 nonzero   517 differing
                                              268 frames carry a state difference
  bytes in BOTH masks              0          (measured, not asserted)
```

The disjointness is verified rather than claimed: the harness counts bytes
appearing in both masks and reports zero.

**517 of 82592 state bytes differ - 0.63%.** Production's state writeback is
therefore NOT exact, and that is now a measurement of the shipping path rather
than of a modelling harness.

#### A correction to the RESAMPLE entry above

That entry reported "26 mismatches, all at +0x10..11" from `acmdrslow`.
`acmdrslow` **models RESAMPLE independently** - it never calls `sl_acmd_exec`
for that opcode, by design, so that it can disagree with the interpreter. Its
numbers describe **its own model**, not the shipping code. With ADPCM now
executing it scores 1253 mismatches over 1632 last-writer pairs, against
production's 517 over the full state population.

So the "26 bytes in one lane" characterisation is a property of the independent
model, and the production path's state behaviour was simply unmeasured until
now. The residue is real in both, but the shape recorded above should not be
carried forward as production's shape.

**Not claimed.** That the 517 bytes are localised - they are not, yet. That
either implementation is right where they differ. That RESAMPLE is closed. That
sound works.


#### The 517 state bytes, localised on the production path. 2026-08-31

Same disjoint state mask, now bucketed by offset within the 32-byte block and
split by owning opcode, because RESAMPLE and ADPCM are different state layouts
and merging them would hide exactly the result below.

```
  by offset in the 32-byte block     RESAMPLE            ADPCM
    +0x00..07  history            0 / 13056           0 /  7592
    +0x08..09  phase              0 /  3264           0 /  1898
    +0x0A..0B  align              0 /  3264           0 /  1898
    +0x0C..0F  preserved         49 /  6528           0 /  3796
    +0x10..1F  quad             468 / 26112           0 / 15184
                                          (differing / compared)
```

**ADPCM's state writeback is exact: 0 differing across all 30368 bytes.** That
is a second, independent result for the decode - the earlier grounding was its
PCM through SAVEBUFF, and this is its 32-byte state block, a disjoint
population. Both are exact.

**The entire residue is RESAMPLE's, and it is confined to two ranges.** History,
phase and align are exact across 19584 bytes. What differs is 468 bytes in the
quad and 49 in the range the code calls "preserved".

**The 468 is a convergence worth recording.** `sl_acmd.c`'s own comment at the
quad writeback already said *"468 bytes across the capture remain ungrounded
here"* - a figure derived when that range was being written. This measurement
reaches the same number by a completely different route: executing the whole
task through the production interpreter and diffing DRAM against the
cartridge's end-of-task snapshot. The pre-existing note was accurate, and it is
now confirmed on the shipping path rather than on a model.

**The 49 bytes at +0x0C..0F are new, and they contradict a stated expectation.**
That range is documented as never written by either path, preserved from the
incoming DRAM state on a continuation and carrying the mixer's scratch on an
init - and `acmdrslow` scores it 0. On the production path it is not preserved
in 49 cases. Which of the two is right is NOT established here; what is
established is that the two implementations disagree there, and that the
production one does not match the cartridge.

**Not claimed.** That the quad rule is known - it is not, and the candidate
search recorded above came back empty. That the 49 bytes and the 468 share a
cause. That RESAMPLE is closed. That sound works.
