#### THE THREE MINUTES WERE THE HOST AUDIO QUEUE. The VI retrace ran at 112 Hz. 2026-08-31

The owner reported music playing normally on the paced interactive path and
action effects arriving **minutes** late but eventually arriving. The
discrimination that decides this - is the effect late reaching PCM, or is it
sitting behind a backlog - is a numeric one, and it came back unambiguous.

#### The measurement, over wall clock, from the DEVICE's own format

Queued bytes only become a latency once divided by the rate the device
**granted**, so the obtained `freq`, `channels` and `SDL_AUDIO_BITSIZE(format)`
are captured at open and used as the divisor - never the requested ones. Here
that is 22050 x 2 x 2 = **88 200 bytes per second**.

Facility, windowed, paced, `SL_FPS=60`:

```
  AUDIOLAT wall=  1.01s submitted= 2.17s queued= 105216 B =  1.193s growth=+1.177 s/s
  AUDIOLAT wall=  5.05s submitted=10.23s queued= 460288 B =  5.219s growth=+0.994 s/s
  AUDIOLAT wall= 29.31s submitted=58.76s queued=2602304 B = 29.505s growth=+0.997 s/s
```

**The queue grows by one second of audio per real second**, and the submitted
total is exactly twice the wall clock. The backlog therefore equals the elapsed
play time: three minutes of play is three minutes of latency, about 16 MB
queued. That is the whole of the reported symptom, and it explains why music
seemed fine - continuous music has no external timing reference and sounds
correct behind any fixed delay, while a gunshot has one.

**Effects internals were therefore not investigated**, per the rule that this
discrimination decides it.

#### FIRST WRONG STAGE: the sleep was at the presentation boundary, not the VI retrace

Instrumenting the pacer and the two frame counters directly, rather than
inferring from rates - facility/600 frames, windowed, `SL_FPS=60`:

```
  PACE calls=300  slept=294  total=2.45s   frameAdvance(sim ticks)=300
  POLLBALANCE retraces=599
  AUDIOLIFE steps=299                      wall 5.32s
```

**300 sleeps for 599 retraces.** Two pump services occur per presented frame:
one delivers the completed GRAPHICS task, whose reply goes to `gfxFrameMsgQ` and
so takes the early return before the pacing site, and one finishes the frame.
`sl_pace_frame()` sat after that early return, so it saw half the retraces.

The VI therefore ran at **112 Hz instead of 60**, and every retrace-driven
system ran with it - the input advance, the AI FIFO drain, `__scHandleRetrace`,
and the audio manager, which emitted **~56 tasks a second where the console
emits ~30**. Twice the production against a device consuming at 1x is exactly
+1 s/s of queue.

A sweep confirms the pacer itself was working and only its placement was wrong -
the achieved retrace rate was **exactly 2x the target** at every setting:

```
  SL_FPS= 30   600 frames in 10.32s   58.1 retraces/s
  SL_FPS= 60   600 frames in  5.36s  111.9 retraces/s
  SL_FPS=120   600 frames in  2.87s  209.0 retraces/s
```

#### The fix

One sleep per VI retrace, inside the retrace block, because the retrace is the
clock the hardware runs and `sl_fps` is already documented at its declaration as
*"VI rate for NTSC"*. The presentation site keeps a call only for
`sl_vis_active()`, where the retrace block is never entered and nothing would
otherwise pace.

**No queued audio is dropped and no bounded-latency queue is imposed.** The
production rate is corrected; the queue then stays bounded on its own, which is
what distinguishes a fix from a mask.

```
                        before              after
  PACE calls / retraces  300 / 599          599 / 599
  retrace rate           112 Hz              59.1 Hz
  audio manager          ~56 tasks/s         29.5 tasks/s   (console ~29)
  sim ticks              ~56/s               29.6/s
  submitted vs wall      58.76s at 29.31s    59.19s at 58.98s
  queued latency         29.5s and rising    0.20-0.26s, flat over 59s
                         +0.997 s/s          growth -0.033..+0.025 s/s
```

The control is the same binary with `SL_FPS` swept: it moves the retrace rate
proportionally in both arms, so the pacing site is demonstrably the thing that
changed and not the target.

#### What this does not touch

Headless determinism is unchanged - `sl_pace_frame` returns immediately without
a window, so the canonical fixture is bit-for-bit what it was: 449 tasks, 448
submits, 1 317 184 bytes, peak 13217, rms 2090.72, 98.572% nonzero. Pacing only
sleeps; it never alters state.

**Not claimed.** That effects are now timely - that needs the owner's paced run
with a weapon fired, and there is no native input-replay mechanism to make it a
deterministic in-repo witness (tree-wide: no `SL_REPLAY`, no input-stream reader
in `src/platform/`). That the four retrace-level underruns are related. That the
game's wall-clock speed was correct before - it was not, and 2x retrace rate
means the earlier "60 fps and Rare's game speed" note needs re-taking, which is
recorded here and not re-derived.

**Instrumentation.** `AUDIOLAT` is runtime-gated on `SL_AUDIO_STATS` and its two
helpers are file-local (`nm` shows both as `t`). The pacer counters and
`frameAdvance` counter are compile-gated behind `SL_ALHEAP_TRACE` and verified
absent from the delivered binary.

#### THE SIMULATION CLOCK RAN AT HALF RATE: `sl_ticks_next` returned a constant 1 VI per frame. 2026-08-31

The owner reported the effects delay much improved after the pacing fix but the
whole game feeling about half speed. That is a claim about the **simulation
clock**, which is a different quantity from the retrace rate and from the
presentation rate, and it is settled here against the cartridge rather than
against feel.

#### A correction to my own wording, first

I wrote that the game "had been running at roughly double speed". **That claimed
more than was measured** and is narrowed to:

> The old paced path ran the **retrace, and the retrace-driven audio
> production**, at roughly twice their intended wall-clock rate.

Nothing in that measurement touched simulation speed. What follows is the first
measurement that does.

#### The canonical clock, identified from the timing source rather than invented

`currentFrameCounter` (`frametiming.c:6`) is it. `updateFrameCounters(deltaFrames)`
adds **the number of VI periods that actually elapsed** to it and derives
`lastFrameCounter`, `halfFrameCounter`, `isFrameCounterOdd` and
`halfMinusPreviousCounter` from it (`frametiming.c:44-68`); on hardware
`waitForNextFrame` busy-waits on `osGetCount` and passes exactly that count
(`frametiming.c:80-89`). Every timer, animation and AI delay is derived from it.
No new counter was added.

#### TIMING RELATIONSHIP, per 600 VIs, anchored in steady gameplay

The cartridge is anchored **120 VIs after `mission_state` reaches 1** (video
frame 367) so that both sides are genuinely in gameplay and the load is behind
them; native's load costs zero VIs, so global frame numbers are not comparable
and are not compared.

```
                              CARTRIDGE      NATIVE before   NATIVE after
  retraces / VIs                    600            600            600
  currentFrameCounter delta      ~600*            300            600
  presents (frame boundaries)      336            300            300
  audio tasks                      300            300            300
```

`*` The raw cartridge reading is 995, and it is **not** used as the figure.
Its `deltaFrames` histogram is `{1:108, 2:224, 8:1, 9:1, 17:1, 405:1}` - four
boundaries account 439 of those units, and a single 405-VI step is an emulator
stall, not console behaviour. Excluding those four, **332 boundaries account 556
units over the same VIs: 1.00 per VI**, which is also what the definition
requires, since `deltaFrames` *is* the elapsed VI count. Native before the fix
advanced 600 over 1200 retraces - exactly **0.50 per VI**.

**FIRST WRONG CLOCK: the simulation clock, at half rate.** Audio was already
correct and stays correct - 300 tasks per 600 VIs on both sides, exactly one per
two VIs.

#### The derivation

`osGetCount()` is synthetic natively:
`1000000 + sl_frame * SL_CYCLES_PER_FRAME + sl_count_extra` (`sl_ultra_shim.c:543`).
`sl_frame` advances twice per game frame - once at the pump's presentation site
and once in `sl_frame_advance` - so the clock moves two frames' worth, and
`sl_ticks_next` corrects it with `sl_count_extra += (t - 2) * SL_CYCLES_PER_FRAME`
so that exactly `t` VIs are accounted. `waitForNextFrame` then recovers `t`
through the game's own divisor and hands it to `updateFrameCounters`.

**`t` defaulted to a hardcoded 1** whenever there was no recorded VI-target
stream - which is every ordinary run, since that stream exists only for trace
replay. So the simulation advanced one VI per game frame however many retraces
the frame actually spanned, and a frame spans two.

The fix is the hardware definition rather than an approximation of it: count the
retraces since the last frame boundary and use that.

```c
t = sl_vi_elapsed ? sl_vi_elapsed : 1;
```

**Why this was invisible until now.** With the retrace running at ~112 Hz the
two errors had opposite signs and roughly cancelled: 56 game frames a second at
1 VI each gave ~56 counter units a second against the console's ~60. Pacing the
retrace correctly removed one error and exposed the other. That is worth
recording - a wrong constant hidden behind a wrong rate looks like correct
behaviour right up until the rate is fixed.

#### The recorded-VI-stream path is untouched

`sl_ticks_data != NULL` still takes its `t` from the stream exactly as before, so
trace capture and replay are unaffected by construction, and `make trace-verify`
is IDENTICAL.

#### Wall clock after the derivation, paced, windowed

```
  1439 retraces / 23.32s  =  61.7 retraces per real second
  1438 sim ticks / 23.32s  =  61.7 simulation VIs per real second
   720 presents / 23.32s   =  30.9 presented frames per real second
  audio submitted 23.20s at wall 23.32s  =  1.00 s of audio per real second
  queued latency  0.260s at start, 0.067-0.092s at end, bounded throughout
```

**The queue fix is preserved and is not traded away.** Audio production stays at
one second per real second and the queue stays bounded; the correction moved the
simulation clock only, because the retrace - which drives both the audio manager
and the AI drain - was not touched.

#### The remaining difference, classified rather than fixed

Presents are **300 per 600 VIs against the cartridge's 336**, i.e. native holds a
flat two VIs per presented frame where the cartridge mixes one-VI and two-VI
frames (108 and 224 of them). The simulation clock now matches; presentation is
sparser. **That is a rendering-cadence question, not an audio-timing one**, and
it is recorded here rather than pursued.

**Not claimed.** That presentation cadence matches - it does not, and the gap is
named above. That the cartridge's raw 995 is console behaviour - it is not, and
the stall boundaries are excluded explicitly. That effects are now timely: that
still needs the owner's paced run with a weapon fired.

#### FACILITY AUDIO: functionally closed. The closure measurement, and what it does and does not prove. 2026-08-31

Owner acceptance on the interactive paced path: music audible and correct,
gunshots, screams and explosions in effectively the right temporal position, no
apparent lag in normal gameplay. This entry records the objective closure pass
taken alongside that, and the debt left behind.

#### The oracle used, and why it is the right one after the fixture correction

`acmdreplay` against the cartridge capture. It replays **the cartridge's own
commands over the cartridge's own DRAM brackets**, so its alignment is the
audio-frame key on a single population and is completely independent of the
native fixture, the boot stage and the simulation clock. That is what makes it
still valid after those three things changed. The withdrawn cross-scene
alignment is **not** revived, and no correlation offset is fitted.

```
  frames byte-exact : 435 / 435          frames differing : 0
  bytes compared    : 5 227 776          of which nonzero : 3 320 001 (63.51%)
  bytes differing   : 0
  sample error over 1 869 567 nonzero written samples
    max |err| 0     RMS err 0.00
```

**No first differing sample exists on this population.** There is nothing to
localise.

#### A second grounded population: the derived filter tables

The POLEF coefficient tables are the one piece of *native-derived* data the
audio path feeds to the interpreter, and they are alignable without any
timeline: the same POLEF gain denotes the same filter on both sides.

```
  distinct POLEF gains   native 5   cartridge 5   comparable 5
  coefficient tables EXACT  5 / 5     differing 0
```

So the byte-order correction is complete over the whole population the fixture
exercises, not just the two tables it was found on.

#### Production health, facility, canonical fixture

```
  ACMDEXEC tasks=449 completedWithoutFault=449 commands=330779
  negOverflow hits=0        ADPCM accumulator-wrap branch taken 0
  AI QUEUE submits=448 refused=0 underruns=4 depth=1
  peak 13217  rms 2105.11  nonzero 649190/658592 (98.572%)  silent blocks 4/448
```

Zero faults, and the fail-loud ungrounded refusal never fires.

#### DEMONSTRATED REMAINING OUTPUT BUG: none

Stated precisely, because "none demonstrated" is not "none exists":

- **Proven.** The interpreter reproduces the console's PCM exactly on 435 aligned
  tasks and 5.2 M compared bytes. The derived filter tables are exact on every
  gain the fixture uses. No task faults; no ungrounded semantic is reached.
- **Not proven.** That the native manager's *own* output is sample-exact against
  the console. It cannot be, and the reason is legitimate rather than a defect:
  the native load costs zero VIs where the console's costs 247, so the two runs
  consume the recorded input out of phase and are never in the same game state.
  An exact comparison there would need the same population on both sides, which
  the corrected fixture does not create.

#### PARKED DEBT, carried forward and not worked

- RESAMPLE state residue: 49 bytes at `+0x0C..0F` and 468 at `+0x10..1F` over
  268 frames. Re-measured unchanged on the current oracle; **disjoint from the
  PCM mask, so it is not shown to affect output.**
- The ADPCM accumulator wrap: still ungrounded, still refused by default,
  eligibility zero on every fixture measured.
- The flag-provenance thread: parked, no causal correction ever came from it.
- Task-19 / AI timing: its parity acceptance was void with the scene correction
  and has not been retaken.
- Presentation cadence: native holds a flat 2 VIs per presented frame where the
  cartridge mixes 1-VI and 2-VI frames (300 presents per 600 VIs against 336).
  Simulation clock matches; this is rendering cadence.
- `sndPlaySfx` is never called on the headless fixture because **there is no
  native input replay** - tree-wide, no `SL_REPLAY` and no input-stream reader in
  `src/platform/`. Effects are exercised only by a human at the controls.

A census of the emitted stream across seven levels, 900 frames each:

```
  level        cmds   ADPCM  ENVMIX  RESAMP   POLEF  SETVOL  polefGains
  facility   330779    6609    8189   10434   11225    1410      5
  surface    358647   10104   10628   12873   11225    1715      5
  caverns    352955    8012   10326   12571   11225    2940      5
```

**Two findings worth keeping.** POLEF is 11225 with exactly 5 distinct gains on

ENVMIXER, 3.0x its SETVOL, 1.9x its RESAMPLE.

All seven levels boot, survive 900 frames, and complete 449/449 tasks with zero
faults and plausible PCM (rms 1907-4010, peaks 11508-24355, no full-scale

### B-023 — the perimeter treeline decodes to black/white static on surface and surface2

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, full 20-level visual survey
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** texture decode call site, `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`
- **Blocks:** two campaign levels looking right. Everything else about them renders correctly.
- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-08-25. The tile was paired with the wrong image;
  the interpreter now resolves pixels through the tile's own tmem address.

Both snow levels — **surface (36)** and **surface2 (43)** — render their satellite
dish, terrain, buildings and characters correctly, and then draw the perimeter
treeline/wall around the horizon as **dense black-and-white static**.

It is a texture fault, not geometry: enlarged 2.5x the noise follows the
terrain silhouette exactly, so the mesh is right and the surface on it is
garbage. High-frequency salt-and-pepper is the signature of a decode reading
the wrong bit depth or the wrong stride — a 4bpp image read as 8bpp, or a line
width disagreeing with the tile.

Reproduce:
```
SL_BOOT_LEVEL=36  (or 43)  SL_WINDOW=1 SL_SHOT=/tmp/s/f SL_SHOT_EVERY=60 SL_FRAMES=420
```
then look at the horizon band. It is visible at full frame and unmistakable
enlarged.

Same shape as the last three texture bugs, and the same first place to look:
B-018 (CI palette), B-020 (font swizzle) and the `dxt` rule all turned out to be
the CALL SITE handing a correct decoder the wrong thing. `sl_gfx_tex.c` has 593
self-tests and cannot see a format, dimension or flag chosen by its caller.

Both levels are affected, so it is one asset or one format path rather than a
per-level accident. Dump the offending texture with `SL_TEX_DUMP` and look at it
directly — that is what settled B-018 and B-020 in minutes each.

**Resolved 2026-08-25.** It was the call site again, and neither the bit depth
nor the stride.

Two hypotheses were measured and killed first, both cheaply, and the negative
results are worth keeping. The tile's declared stride (`line * 8`, from F5
settile) was compared against the stride the decoder derives from the width:
**zero disagreements on any level**, so "a line width disagreeing with the
tile" was ruled out as a class. And every plausible re-reading of the offending
bytes — 4bpp and 8bpp, six strides, both byte orders, swizzle on and off — was
rendered offline and looked at. *All* of them were static, which is the result
that matters: when no reading of the bytes is an image, the bytes are not the
image, and the pointer is what is wrong.

`SL_TEX_TRACE=1` (new) logs every FD/F5/F2/F3/BB as it is interpreted, and the
sequence around the treeline says it outright:

```
FD  addr=c83f5d08 fmt=3           <- an IA8 image
F3  loadblock src=c83f5d08        <- no F5 first: tile 7 still holds tmem=0,
                                     so texTrySetTileState elided it
FD  addr=c83f5150 fmt=0           <- an RGBA16 image
F5  tile=7 tmem=128               <- the LOAD tile's tmem, set BEFORE the F3
F3  loadblock src=c83f5150
F5  tile=0 fmt=3 siz=1 line=4 tmem=0   <- tile 0 describes tmem 0, the FIRST image
F2  tile=0 -> 32x32
F5  tile=1 fmt=0 siz=2 line=16 tmem=128 <- tiles 1..6 are the SECOND image's
F2  tile=1 -> 64x17                        LOD chain
```

The interpreter paired "the tile the BB names" with "the most recent F3
loadblock". GoldenEye batches several loads into *different* tmem addresses and
then configures tiles across all of them, so tile 0 (tmem 0) got handed the
bytes of the image loaded into tmem 128 — an RGBA16 image decoded through an
IA8 32x32 description. That is the static.

The old code documented the assumption and dismissed the fix, on the grounds
that "a tile's tmem address is set AFTER the load that fills it". Both halves
are wrong: the *load* tile's tmem is set before its F3, as the trace shows, so
recording tmem -> source at the loadblock is well-defined. The dismissal was
also self-refuting and the evidence was already in the report — c83f5d08 shows
up in the `dxt!=0` table as `drawn 0x0 x0`, loaded every frame and never once
rendered from.

Fix: a 16-entry tmem -> (source, dxt) map, written at each F3 against the tmem
of the tile that F3 names, read at tile-resolve time, falling back to the old
rule when a tmem address has no entry. `dxt` moved into the map with it,
because it belongs to the load and not to the frame: the two images in flight
here were loaded with dxt=512 and dxt=0, so a single global gave one of them
B-020's swizzle rule backwards.

The standing check that proves it, printed per level: **tile fmt vs FD fmt
disagreements**. Both are written from `tex->gbiformat` (tex.c:445 for the
render tile, tex.c:506 for the image), so they cannot legitimately differ.
Before: surface 2 of 64, surface2 4 of 64, and the disagreeing set was exactly
the noisy set. After: **0 on all of surface, surface2, dam, streets, archives,
caverns and Facility.**

Note for whoever touches this next: textures loaded with a non-zero dxt into
tmem 0 are now rendered from where previously they were never drawn at all.
Facility has one such texture. Its capture is unchanged and its census is 0 of
26, but that is the behavioural surface area this change opens.

### B-024 — a solid black untextured box sits on the pedestal in egypt

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, full 20-level visual survey
- **RESOLVED:** 2026-08-25 by the [[B-026]] fix. The reading below was right —
  a transparent surface rendering as opaque black. The case is now a thin
  translucent panel with the pedestal's stone grain reading through it, and the
  black slab overhanging the pedestal's front edge is gone. Nothing
  egypt-specific was needed; no glass-specific path exists.
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** unknown — likely the transparency/blend path, `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`
- **Blocks:** one level looking right. Everything else in egypt renders correctly.

egypt (stage 32) renders its stone chamber properly — tiled floor, sandstone
walls with visible grain, a pedestal, a lit opening in the wall. On the pedestal
sits a **pure black box**: hard-edged, unshaded, untextured, uniformly zero.

Reproduce:
```
SL_BOOT_LEVEL=32 SL_WINDOW=1 SL_SHOT=/tmp/s/f SL_SHOT_EVERY=60 SL_FRAMES=420
```

Not diagnosed. The reading that fits best is a surface that should be
**transparent rendering as opaque black** — a display case around the object on
the pedestal. Supporting circumstance rather than evidence: `glass2.c:696` is
one of the four `G_CULL` call sites the culling work turned up, so glass is a
distinct render path in this game and one this port has never specifically
exercised.

The alternative is simply an object whose texture failed to bind, which would
show as untextured rather than black — so check whether the geometry is being
drawn with no texture, with a zeroed texture, or with a blend mode that
resolves to black. `SL_TEX_DUMP` plus the `sl_tex` per-draw telemetry will
separate those quickly.

Worth checking whether other levels have glass cases or windows that look wrong
in the same way before assuming it is egypt-specific — archives and streets both
have windows.

### B-025 — monitor screens render as a flat solid colour

**LIKELY RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by the B-027 image-bank fix - same root cause.
Needs one frame to confirm.**

The monitors and the crosshair were the same bug, found twice independently.
`texReset` word-swapped the whole 0x1400-byte global image bank, but only the
first 0xAC8 bytes (the globalDL_* lists) are word data; from `s_genericimage`
on the bank is 0xC-byte image declarations whose bytes 0x4..0xB are eight
separate u8 fields. The blanket swap reversed each group of four, so every
image in the bank - monitors included - got its width, height, level and format
shuffled.

The measurement from the earlier B-025 investigation says exactly this, and is
worth keeping because it is the monitor-side half of the proof: every monitor
declaration came back **width=4, height=0, level=32**, so
othermodemicrocode.c's `((height - 1) << 2) + ulst` emitted `lrt = -2` and the
render tile computed a 1x1024 extent no decoder can accept. The crosshair side
measured the same corruption from the other end - `{w=0x20,h=0x20,level=0}`
read as `{w=0,h=0,level=0x20}`.

A flat unshaded rectangle is what a failed texture binding produces: the quad
is the right size in the right place and takes the flat primitive colour. That
is why this looked like a monitor-specific content bug and was not one.

`stash@{0}` holds the earlier WIP. It is SUPERSEDED - its `image_bank.c` and
`sl_swap_model.c` halves implement the same correction the committed fix does,
by un-swapping the byte fields in a second pass rather than swapping the two
regions separately. It is kept rather than dropped because its third file
(`sl_gfx_dl.c`) adds reject-bucket instrumentation that was never merged and
may still be useful. Do not apply the stash on top of the fix - the two would
cancel and reintroduce the bug.

WANTED: one control (stage 23) capture of the large wall screen. Until then
this is inference from a shared root cause, not a confirmed fix.

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, full 20-level visual survey
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** the monitor draw path — a monitor renders from its own `cmdlist`
- **Blocks:** control, and any level with screens. The rest of those levels renders correctly.

control (stage 23) renders the Janus Control Center correctly — tiled floor,
consoles with grated fronts, staircase, ceiling structure, legible caption — and
draws the large wall screen as a **flat, solid, unshaded green rectangle**. No
content, no texture, no gradient.

```
SL_BOOT_LEVEL=23 SL_WINDOW=1 SL_SHOT=/tmp/s/f SL_SHOT_EVERY=60 SL_FRAMES=420
```

**NOT the same defect as [[B-024]], measured 2026-08-25.** That was the natural
reading and it is wrong: egypt's box was translucency and [[B-026]] fixed it,
while control's screens survived the same fix unchanged. The rest of control
improved a great deal — the far wall, the machinery and the console grating all
came back from black — but every screen is still flat green.

The measurement that separates them. With the render-mode telemetry on, one
control frame reports:

```
sl_tex: tris textured=1699 plain=14  ...  no-source=0
sl_tex: ... reject[dim,size,unmapped,pal,decode,fmt,tilesize,nogl]=14,0,0,...
```

Exactly 14 triangles — seven quads, which is the wall screen plus the desk
monitors — fail texture acquisition, all of them in the `dim` bucket, and
`no-source=0` rules out the missing-loadblock case the paragraph below
hypothesises. That bucket is `src == NULL || w == 0 || h == 0 || w >
TEX_MAX_DIM || h > TEX_MAX_DIM` at `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c:1248`, so with
`no-source=0` it is a tile whose settilesize yields a zero or absurd extent.
The quad then draws untextured and takes the vertex/primitive colour, which is
the flat green. None of control's eight render modes carries `cvgxa` or an
unhandled blender, so blending was never going to touch this.

Next step is therefore the tile extent, not the blend path: log `uls/ult/lrs/lrt`
for the rejected tiles and find which command left them degenerate. The
`cmdlist` hypothesis below is still live as the reason the tile is never sized
properly, but it should be tested against those numbers rather than assumed.

Monitors are a distinct object type with their own data and their own draw path,
which this port has never specifically exercised:
`sl_swap_MonitorRecord`, `sl_swap_MonitorObjRecord` and
`sl_swap_MultiMonitorObjRecord` all exist in `src/native/sl_swap_setup.c`, and a
`MonitorRecord` carries a `cmdlist` pointer plus scale/rotation/colour animation
fields. A monitor therefore draws by executing a display list of its own.

The obvious hypothesis, untested: that `cmdlist` is not being resolved or
executed, so the screen quad draws with whatever fill state is current and no
texture. Note the parallel with B-019, where a room display list resolved to an
unset segment and was silently dropped — a `cmdlist` pointer that needs the same
`dl_operand()` ladder would fail in exactly this way, and would explain a flat
fill rather than a crash.

Check `sl_swap_MonitorRecord`'s `cmdlist` handling too: it is `SW32`'d as a
plain word, which is right for a file offset and wrong for something that needs
promoting to a host pointer.

### B-026 — translucent surfaces draw opaque: the 3D path ignores the RDP render mode

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, full 20-level visual survey — three symptoms, one likely cause
- **RESOLVED:** 2026-08-25. B9 is now decoded into a persistent render-mode
  register and mapped to GL state per draw. Subsumed [[B-024]]; did NOT subsume
  [[B-025]] — see the measurement recorded there.
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`, the triangle draw path vs `B9 setothermode_l`
- **Blocks:** shadows, glass and screens everywhere. Probably subsumes [[B-024]] and [[B-025]].

Three separate observations from the survey are almost certainly one defect:

- **train** — each guard stands on a **solid black rectangle**. Character shadows
  are blended dark quads in this game; here they are opaque black.
- **egypt** ([[B-024]]) — a **pure black hard-edged box** on the pedestal, where a
  transparent display case belongs.
- **control** ([[B-025]]) — the wall screen is a **flat solid green rectangle**.
- **aztec** — the clearest example. A floor decal (a yellow hazard marking)
  renders as **disconnected black wedges** with the yellow lines showing
  through. Enlarged 2.6x it is obvious what is happening: the decal is several
  quads, its transparent regions are being written opaque black, and what
  survives looks like fragmentation. Any level with a floor marking will show
  this.

All three are geometry resolving to one flat opaque colour where something
see-through or composited belongs.

**The measurement that ties them together.** `grep -rn "GL_BLEND\|glBlendFunc"
src/gfx/` returns four sites in `sl_gfx_dl.c`: `glEnable(GL_BLEND)` with
`glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)` at 1682-83, and
`glDisable(GL_BLEND)` at 1659 and 2629. **The 3D triangle path draws with
blending disabled.** So every translucent surface the RDP would composite is
written opaque, which is exactly all three symptoms.

**How it was fixed, and two things the fix corrected in the framing above.**

`ucode05.txt` punts B9 to a `SETOTHERMODE_L.HTM` that is not in the corpus;
`ucode05_old.txt` carries the table in full (l.296-350), the same fallback that
already closed F5 settile and FC setcombine. It agrees with `include/PR/gbi.h`
on every shift and length, and `src/boss.c:588` carries a worked example in its
own comment — `gDPSetRenderMode(gdl++, G_RM_VISCVG, G_RM_VISCVG2); //
0xb900031d, 0x0fa54040` — which reproduces exactly under that layout, pinning
the blender mux positions as well as the shift/length packing. The full
citation lives in the render-mode block in `sl_gfx_dl.c`.

Two corrections to what this entry assumed:

1. **The vertex alpha was the other half.** `emit_tri` passed a hard
   `glColor4ub(..., 255)`. Enabling blending against a forced 1.0 alpha still
   writes opaque, so the mode decode alone would have changed nothing.
2. **There was no working alpha-test path to protect.** Jungle's palm fronds
   were believed to be alpha-tested and correct. They are not: `sl_rm` reports
   `cvgxa=0` on all six of jungle's render modes, and the fronds draw under
   `ZMODE_XLU | FORCE_BL` — `G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF2`, ordinary translucency.
   They only *looked* right because their opaque-black transparent regions sat
   against a near-black jungle backdrop. 1871 of jungle's triangles blend now,
   and the fronds gained their serrated silhouettes; before, the quad edges
   were plainly visible where a frond crossed a lit trunk.

Also resolved without being aimed at: aztec's **horizontal yellow streaking**
across the floor, which had looked like a separate tile clamp/extent fault. It
was the same defect and did not survive the fix. And four levels that were not
listed as symptoms improved for the same reason — archives' foreground railing
was an opaque black picket wall and is now grating, caverns' catwalk likewise,
streets' guard had a black shadow slab, and facility's upper walkway was a
black bank.

The RDP render mode lives in the high bits of `B9 setothermode_l` — the
`G_RM_*` macros, where `G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF` and friends select the blender
configuration. The interpreter decodes `B9`/`BA` (that work landed for cycle
type, in the 2D commit) but does not translate the render mode into GL blend
state for triangles.

Do NOT just enable `GL_BLEND` globally — that would composite opaque surfaces
too and is its own bug. The mode has to be read per-draw and mapped: opaque
(`G_RM_AA_ZB_OPA_SURF`) to blending off, translucent (`XLU`) to
src-alpha/one-minus-src-alpha, and the decal/intersect variants to their own
depth behaviour.

Get the bit layout from the notes and cite it — `ucode05.txt` for `B9`, and note
it punts to a `SETOTHERMODE_L.HTM` that is not in the corpus, so `ucode05_old.txt`
is the place to look next (it carried the real table for both `F5 settile` and
`FC setcombine`), with `include/PR/gbi.h`'s `G_RM_*` definitions as the fallback
authority — cross-checked against the notes' own worked examples, which is how
the cycle-type packing was pinned.

Verify by looking, on all four: train's shadows should become soft, egypt's box
see-through, control's screen should show content, and aztec's floor marking
should sit flat on the plating as one continuous decal.

One symptom may NOT belong to this entry: aztec's decal also shows **horizontal
yellow streaking** bleeding left across the floor, which looks like a texture
sampled past its bounds — a clamp/wrap or tile-extent problem rather than a
blend one. Check whether it survives the blend fix before assuming it is the
same bug.

### Visual survey conclusion, 2026-08-25

17 of 20 campaign levels looked at directly (all 20 confirmed drawing real
content). Beyond facility/dam/streets/archives/caverns/statue/jungle/surface/
surface2 already recorded: **depot** train carriage, platform, canopy trusses;
**egypt** stone chamber with sandstone grain; **frigate** plank crates, hex deck
plating, two intact guards; **control** the Janus centre; **train** crates and
plank flooring; **aztec** ribbed metal complex; **cradle** antenna truss
structure; **runway** snow, cliffs, chain-link fencing; **silo** concrete block
walls, hazard-striped drums.

Captions are legible on every level that shows one. Characters are intact on
every level with guards in view.

**Defects found: B-023 (fixed), B-024, B-025, B-026** — the last three almost
certainly one cause, now being worked.

**One false alarm, worth more than it cost.** Runway's left embankment carries a
dark speckled band that at full-frame scale looks exactly like the static that
WAS a bug on surface. Enlarged 3.2x it is plainly a **chain-link fence** —
regular mesh weave with evenly spaced support posts, correctly rendered. It was
not filed.

That is the second time scale alone produced a wrong reading: B-021 was first
filed as "guards sit slightly below the floor" from a full-frame glance and
turned out on enlargement to be limbs scattering. **Enlarge before filing.** A
thumbnail is enough to notice something, never enough to name it.

Also worth recording: the per-level statistics flagged **none** of the four real
defects. surface and surface2 carry the two highest stddev figures of all
twenty, because static is high-variance. The survey's value was entirely in the
looking.

- **facility** (control level, not a symptom) — the upper walkway that was an

No regressions seen. B-024 is closed as a duplicate of B-026.

**B-025 (monitor screens) is NOT part of this** and stays open — measured as 14

### B-027 — the crosshair draws as an untextured white square — RESOLVED 2026-08-25

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, chasing the owner's "no crosshair" report
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `gunDrawSight` (`gunfire.c:6204`) -> `texSelect(crosshairimage)` -> `display_image_at_position`
- **Blocks:** aiming usefully.

**Half of this report was not a bug.** The crosshair only appears while the
player holds AIM, and that is Rare's behaviour, not a defect:
`bondview2.c:5491` calls `gunSetSightVisible(GUNSIGHTREASON_NOTAIMING,
moveData.aiming)`, so the hide-reason bit is cleared only while aiming.
Measured: `gunsightmode = 2` on all 87 `gunDrawSight` calls in a run where
nobody aimed, and the function returns immediately at its
`gunsightmode == 0 && !mpmenuon` gate. That is also why a raw linear scan of
the whole display list found **zero** `E4/E5` texrects — nothing was emitted to
find.

**The real defect:** hold aim and the crosshair appears as a **solid white
square**, roughly 32x32 scaled up, with no crosshair artwork. `gunDrawSight`
does `texSelect(&sp54, crosshairimage, 4, 0, 0)` and then
`display_image_at_position(..., 0x20, 0x20, ...)`. The quad draws; the texture
does not bind, so it takes the flat primitive colour.

Reproduce:
```
SL_PROBE_ROUTINE=aim SL_PROBE_OUT=/tmp/aim2 tools/native/probe.sh facility 20
```
then look at a LATE frame (the aim hold is at the end of the routine). Bond
spawns facing the airlock door at point-blank range, so the routine turns away
first - without that every frame is one wall texture and the test is
inconclusive, which cost one attempt.

Same shape as B-018, B-020, B-023 and the `dxt` rule: four texture bugs in a
row, all of them the CALL SITE handing a correct decoder the wrong thing.
`sl_gfx_tex.c` has 593 self-tests and cannot see a format, dimension or pointer
chosen by its caller. Look at what `texSelect` resolves `crosshairimage` to, and
whether that pointer is an image or an ID - an un-patched declaration names an
image ID rather than an address, and `image_bank.c` word-swaps the
`Globalimagetable` because it holds display lists and declarations, not pixels.

---

**ROOT CAUSE, measured 2026-08-25 — and the last paragraph above is the wrong
lead.** `crosshairimage` resolves to a perfectly good pointer and `texLoad`
patches its ID to a real texpool address on every path. The corrupted thing is
the OTHER eight bytes of the declaration.

`image_bank.c:180` word-swapped the whole 0x1400-byte bank as if it were
uniformly 32-bit. It is not. Per `images text and font/image declarations.txt`
a declaration is 0xC bytes and only the FIRST word is word data:

```
0x0  4  image ID, or offset to image if already loaded   <- word
0x4  1  width      0x8  1  bitdepth
0x5  1  height     0x9  1  clamp/mirror S
0x6  1  level      0xA  1  clamp/mirror T
0x7  1  format     0xB  1  (pad)
```

Bytes 0x4..0xB are eight independent u8 fields. A blanket word swap reverses
each group of four. Measured under gdb at the `gunDrawSight` breakpoint,
before the fix:

```
crosshairimage @ 0xf5ce7d2c:  bc 08 00 00 | 00 00 20 20 | 00 00 00 03
  index=000008bc  width=00 height=00 level=20 format=20 depth=00 pad=03
```

against the declaration in `assets/oddtextures.c:580`,
`{IMAGE_CROSSHAIR1, 0x20, 0x20, 0, G_IM_FMT_RGBA, G_IM_SIZ_32b, WRAP, WRAP, 0}`.
Width and height read 0, format read 0x20 (not a format), and — the part that
decided the visual — `level` read 0x20, so `texSelect`
(`othermodemicrocode.c:370`) took its `level != 0` MIPMAP branch and
`lod = (s32)tconfig->level` (`:506`) became 32.

**The two display lists, dumped with gdb and diffed.** Break `gunDrawSight`,
save `*gdl`, `finish`, dump to `*gdl`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| words emitted | 166 | 42 |
| settile/settilesize pairs | **32** | 1 |
| `loadblock` | `07fff000` — 4096 texels, dxt=0 | `073ff080` — 1024 texels (32x32), dxt=0x80 |
| `settile` line / masks | line=0, masks=0 | line=0x10 (32px @32bpp), masks=maskt=5 → 32x32 |
| `settilesize` | `xxffcffc` — uls==lrs, **zero-area tile** | `0007c07c` — lrs=lrt=124=31<<2 |
| `settimg` fmt/siz | `0x18` RGBA32 (this was always right) | `0x18` RGBA32 |
| texrect | `e42c0207 00240187` | `e42c0207 00240187` — **byte-identical** |

The texrect being identical either side is the whole report in one line: the
quad geometry was never wrong, because `gunfire.c:6263` passes `0x20, 0x20`
literally rather than reading the struct. 144..176 x 97.75..129.75 — a 32x32
rect on the screen centre, exactly where it belonged. Everything that BOUND a
texture to it was wrong: a zero-area tile with zero line stride sampled
nothing, so the rect took the flat primitive colour. A white square, correctly
sized and correctly placed, is precisely what that emits.

**Not a crosshair bug.** Every image in the global bank had the same eight
bytes reversed — ammo icons, explosion and smoke sprites, glass overlays,
monitor screens, the MP radar, sky/water, the MP level icons. The crosshair is
just where it was noticed. Two more measured before/after, both matching their
`oddtextures.c` declarations only after the fix:

```
genericimage     36 36 03 03 | 01 02 02 00    (w=0x36 h=0x36 lvl=3 fmt=IA depth=8b mirror/mirror)
glassoverlay[0]  20 01 06 03 | 01 00 00 00    (w=0x20 h=1    lvl=6 fmt=IA depth=8b wrap/wrap)
```

**Fix** (`src/game/image_bank.c`, inside the existing `#ifndef __sgi` block, so
the matching build is untouched): swap by region instead of blanket-swapping.
The bank's first 0xAC8 bytes are the seventeen `globalDL_*` display lists —
word data, and `texLoadFromDisplayList`'s native branch (`image.c:2334`) relies
on them being native, so they keep the whole-region swap. From `s_genericimage`
to the end it is nothing but declarations, so only each record's leading u32 is
swapped and bytes 0x4..0xB are left as the wire bytes they are.

The boundary is not a guess: `assets/oddtextures.c` is seventeen `Gfx` arrays
followed by nothing but `sImageTableEntry` arrays to the end of the file, and
`nm` puts `globalDL_0xa50` at 0x02000a50 and `s_genericimage` at 0x02000ac8
(0x78 = fifteen Gfx commands, exact). One trap cost a rebuild: segment symbols
carry the 0x02000000 segment VMA, so the offset needs the same `+0xFE000000`
the pointer fixups below it already use — without it the swap ran off the end
and segfaulted, which is how it was caught.

**Verification.**
1. All 196 declaration records dumped from live memory and compared byte-for-
   byte against the raw ROM at 0x29D160+0xac8: **196 records, 0 word0
   mismatches, 0 byte-field mismatches.** Before the fix every record's bytes
   0x4..0xB were reversed in two groups of four.
2. `gunDrawSight`'s emitted DL decoded command by command (table above) — a
   well-formed settimg → settile → loadblock → settile → settilesize → texrect
   run whose every parameter agrees with RGBA32 32x32.
3. `tools/native/build.sh` clean; `make matching` → **MATCH!**, EXIT=0,
   sha1 `abe01e4aeb033b6c0836819f549c791b26cfde83`, equal to `baserom.u.z64`.
4. `make trace-verify` — facility IDENTICAL, 15869 ticks, schema v13; full
   20-level set clean.

**Not proven headlessly.** No frame was rendered — the owner had the display.
Everything above is command-stream and memory measurement, which settles that
a correct 32x32 RGBA32 texture is now bound to the rect, but not that the
crosshair ART is the right pixels the right way up. The one capture that would
settle it: any rendered frame with AIM held. Worth a look when someone does:
the rect's `rdphalf_1` t is 0x3e0 (t=31.0) with `rdphalf_2` dtdy = -1.0, i.e.
the sight samples T inverted from the bottom row up. That is consistent across
before and after and is almost certainly Rare's own vertical flip rather than a
defect, but a rendered frame is what confirms it.

**Correction filed against our own notes.** `sl_gfx_tex.c`'s byte-order preamble
argued the bank swap was safe because the bank "holds DISPLAY LISTS AND IMAGE
DECLARATIONS, not pixels", and treated "declarations are structured data" as a
reason to word-swap them. Declarations are structured, but they are structured
as bytes. That comment is the reasoning that produced this bug and has been
corrected in place.

### B-028 — no arm, no gun; enemies' weapons and hats missing — RESOLVED 2026-08-25

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, chasing the owner's "no arm, no gun" report
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `subdraw()` as called from `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` (`gunfire.c:1580`)
- **Blocks:** Bond's arm and gun. Probably enemies' held weapons and hats too - all attached child models.

**The game does everything right; the draw produces no geometry.** Measured
chain, each step by breakpoint over ~650 gameplay frames of Facility:

1. `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` runs — 137 calls.
2. Bond is armed: `hand_item[0] = 5` from frame 579 (when the intro camera hands
   over), `ptr_hand_weapon_buffer[0]` non-NULL.
3. The per-hand gate passes: `field_87F = 1`, `item = 5` on hand 0, **70 times**
   (hand 1 is `f87F=0 item=0` throughout - correct, Bond single-wields).
4. Execution reaches the gun's draw at `gunfire.c:1580`,
   `subdraw(&renderdata, (Model *)&handptr->field_B68)` — **70 times**, with
   `obj = 0xf5c05810`, a valid pointer.
5. **And the whole function emits 5 commands.** Measured at the call site
   (`bondview2.c:8974`/`:8975`): `gdl` advances `0xf5c085d8 -> 0xf5c08600`,
   `0x28` bytes = 5 commands. Only `0x18` = 3 of them come after the draw
   point, so `subdraw` contributed ~nothing.

The five commands, decoded, are all state and no draw:
```
bc00000e 000001b4   moveword
b6000000 00003000   cleargeometrymode
bc000c06 f5c2ac20   gSPSegment -> segment 3 = 0xf5c2ac20
b6000000 00003000   cleargeometrymode
bc00000e 0000001a   moveword
```
**There is no `06 G_DL` branch.** The viewmodel configures the segment its model
lives in and then never issues the command that would draw it.

`subdraw` itself is entered 6574 times across all callers in the same run and
guards render correctly, so it is not broken in general — something about this
model, or the state it is handed, produces no output.

Two false trails recorded so they are not walked again:
- "Bond is unarmed" — WRONG, retracted. He is armed from frame 579.
- "Execution never reaches gunfire.c:1560" — TRUE but meaningless: 1560 is
  inside the `item == ITEM_ROCKETLAUNCH` block and Bond carries a PP7. Zero hits
  there is correct. Check what a line belongs to before reading a zero as a stop.


**RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — two independent causes, not one.** The entry's guess
that the viewmodel and the enemy attachments shared a root cause was wrong.
They are unrelated bugs that happened to be reported together.

---

**Cause 1 — the viewmodel: `renderdata.flags` was 0, so the gun's DL node
emitted nothing.**

The diagnosis above was right up to its last step and then stopped one frame
short. `subdraw` reached the gun 70 times and emitted only its own
`gSPSegment`; the node walk contributed nothing. The walk ends at
`modelRenderNodeGundl` (`model.c:4102`), which emits **nothing at all** unless
`renderdata->flags & 1`. `flags` was 0.

`gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` builds its ModelRenderData as
`renderdata = *(ModelRenderData *)&D_80035CC0` (`gunfire.c:1496`) — a 0x40-byte
read off a symbol that is four bytes wide. On N64 the following words belong to
`D_80035CC4 = {1, 3, 0 ...}`, so the read yields basemtx=NULL,
zbufferenabled=TRUE, **flags=3**, rest 0. Measured in `build/u/ge007.u.elf`:

```
80035cc0  00000000 00000001 00000003 00000000   (then 12 zero words)
```

Natively the layout does not hold. `u32 D_80035CC0 = 0;` is explicitly
zero-initialised, so gcc puts it in **.bss**; `D_80035CC4` carries nonzero
initialisers and goes in **.data**. Measured with `nm` on
`build/native/skeleton`:

```
08eb72ec 00000004 B D_80035CC0      081e1040 0000003c D D_80035CC4
08eb72f0 00000004 B D_80035D00      081e1080 00000040 D D_80035D04
```

~13MB apart. The 0x40 bytes at `&D_80035CC0` span `D_80035CC0`, `D_80035D00`,
`g_ZeroTriggerState`, `D_80035EA4` … — unrelated .bss — so `flags` came out 0
and every gate downstream did the right thing with the wrong input.

Three sites read a template this way; all three want the same 16 words, and all
three were measured against the matching ELF (0x80035CC0, 0x80035D00,
0x80035D40 — identical, and identical to the properly-declared
`ModelRenderData D_8002CCBC` at 0x8002CCBC). Two were broken; the third
(`gunfire.c:1869`, `D_80035D04 + 0x3c`) is correct today only because both
symbols land in .data adjacent to each other — luck, not a guarantee.

Fix: a native-only `sl_gun_renderdata_template` beside the data in `gun.c`,
used at all three sites under `#ifndef __sgi`. This is the same class of defect
`objecthandler.c` already documents for the ModelHit pool: separate native
objects cannot reproduce N64 packing.

**Standing hazard, not yet swept:** any decomp read that runs off the end of one
symbol into the next is a native landmine, and it fails silently with plausible
values. Only `gun.c`/`gunfire.c` were audited here. See B-029.

---

**Cause 2 — enemies' weapons and hats: `GroupSimple.Origin` was never
byte-swapped.**

Unrelated to the above, and everything on the emit path measured healthy —
which is exactly why it survived. On streets, over 900 headless frames:
`chrRenderHeldWeapon` ran 2334 times, reached its append for all 1167 right-hand
calls (the 1167 left-hand calls correctly find no prop — guards single-wield),
the weapon's two eligible nodes went into the joint list every time, and
`modelRenderNodeGundl` branched to the weapon's own display list 1166 times
primary + 1166 secondary. The DL was emitted. The weapon was simply not on
screen.

The transform said why. A guard's held weapon, measured after
`instcalcmatrices`:

```
             row 0..2 (rotation/scale)        row 3 (translation)
basemtx      -0.0880  0.0403  0.0250 ...      -63.29   -59.10  -247.85
render_pos   -0.0880  0.0403  0.0250 ...      1.75e28 -8.01e27 -4.97e27
chr body      0.0842  0.0141 -0.0520 ...      -74.87    -9.36  -266.57
```

A correct 3x3 with a translation ~1e28 — transformed clean out of the world,
while the body beside it is fine.

The translation comes from `matrix_4x4_set_identity_and_position(
&rodata->GroupSimple.Origin, ...)` (`model.c:1782`, `:1787`). The native swap
pass handled `GroupSimple.Group1`, `Group2` and `BoundingVolumeRadius` and
**not** `Origin`. `grep -rn GroupSimple src/` returns 11 hits tree-wide, of
which exactly three are in `src/native/` — those three SW lines
(`sl_swap_model.c:317-319`). `Origin` was swapped nowhere.

Why the blast radius was exactly "held weapons and hats" is the part the decomp
cannot tell you, and the notes can. `Display Lists and Object Generation/
Objects/object templates.txt` lists the skeleton template of every prop class:
`Pchr*Z` (item pickups — `0015.0000.0000 pos: primary model`,
`0015.0001.0001 pos: gunfire effect`) and `Phat*Z` (hats —
`0015.0000.0000 pos: primary model`) are the **only** classes whose parts are
`0015` (GROUPSIMPLE) commands. Bodies, doors, tanks, vehicles and the
walletbond all position with `0002` (GROUP), whose `Origin` the GROUP case has
always swapped. One missing `sl_coord3d_swap` accounts for the whole reported
symptom set and nothing else. Routing recorded in `docs/doc-routing.json`.

After the fix, same guard, same frame: `render_pos` row 3 is
`-38.15  -62.15  -252.86` — beside its basemtx, in the guard's hand.

---

**What was seen, and what was not.**

Facility with the `aim` routine, before and after, looked at directly: before,
the lower right of the frame is empty wall; after, the PP7 and the hand are
there, in the same frames, at both a wall and a corridor view. That one is
confirmed by eye.

The GroupSimple fix is confirmed by the transform measurement only. The owner
returned to the display partway through, so no frame was captured after it. The
capture that would close it: **streets, `SL_PROBE_ROUTINE=look`, every 20
frames — the guard standing in the alley around f-00080.** The matching
before-image is on disk at `/tmp/after-streets/f-00080.png` (viewmodel fixed,
guard empty-handed and bare-headed); the guard should now be holding a rifle.

Verified: `make matching` MATCHes; `trace-verify LEVEL=facility` IDENTICAL
across 15869 ticks; headless emits zero renderer telemetry (three status lines);
bootsweep 20/20.


### B-029 — decomp reads that overrun one symbol into the next are native landmines

**The casing site is FIXED (2026-08-25).** `gunfire.c:5579` was the only one of
the three luck-dependent sites worth closing now, because it is the fourth
member of the B-028 template family rather than a one-off.

Worth recording that the sweep's proposed one-line fix - reuse
`sl_gun_renderdata_template` - looked wrong at first glance and was checked
before being applied: the casing reads a DIFFERENT symbol from the gun, whose
first 15 words are legitimate data, so substituting a whole template could have
silently replaced them. It survived the check. `g_DefaultCasingModelRenderData`
is `{0, 1, 3, 0, ...}` and maps field-for-field onto the template's leading 15
words, and `CULLMODE_BOTH` is 0 - exactly the value the overrun was picking up
from padding. The substitution is byte-exact, not approximate.

Left deliberately unfixed: the `texpool` overlay (works, but only because
nothing ever names the three sibling symbols) and `bg.c:5600` (works, but only
because all six words carry nonzero initialisers). Both are recorded above
rather than changed, because touching them buys nothing today and each edit is
its own chance to introduce the bug it is preventing.

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, out of B-028 cause 1
- **Owner:**  Phase 2, but the hazard is tree-wide
- **Where:** anywhere the decomp reads more bytes from `&sym` than `sym` holds

The decomp faithfully reproduces reads that run off the end of one symbol into
whatever the N64 linker put next. On N64 that is a fixed data image and the read
is correct. Natively it is not: gcc is free to put the two symbols in different
sections entirely — which is exactly what happened to `D_80035CC0` (.bss) and
`D_80035CC4` (.data), 13MB apart, and cost Bond his gun for however long the
native build has existed.

This fails **silently and plausibly**. The overrun lands on other real
variables, so the result is a well-formed struct full of wrong values, and every
counter downstream reads healthy while the gate they feed quietly says no.

`gun.c`/`gunfire.c` were audited during B-028 and the three sites there are
fixed. **The rest of the tree was not swept.** Worth a mechanical pass: for each
`*(T *)&sym` / `(u8 *)arr + off` read, compare `sizeof T` against the declared
size of `sym`, then check with `nm` whether the native build still places the
neighbour where the read expects it. `objecthandler.c` already carries the
heavyweight remedy for one such block (`tools/native/modelhit_pool.s`, a single
backing object with every symbol aliased at its N64 offset); a native-only named
constant, as `gun.c` now uses, is the cheaper fix when the read is of a fixed
template rather than of live state.

Verification for the sweep: `nm -S build/native/skeleton` for each pair, plus
`make matching` MATCHing and `trace-verify` IDENTICAL after each fix (all such
fixes must be `#ifndef __sgi`-guarded additions).

#### Sweep result, 2026-08-25 — no second live instance

Swept mechanically, cross-referencing every candidate expression against
`nm -S build/native/skeleton` and `nm -S build/u/ge007.u.elf`. **Nothing else is
live.** Three sites work only by link-order luck; the rest are in-bounds or were
already fixed. No source was changed.

Searches run (all tree-wide over `src/`, all `--include=*.c`):

| Spelling | Raw hits | On a global symbol | Overrunning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(T *)&sym` / `*(T *)&sym` | 509 | 32 | 9 |
| `(T *)sym` (array/pointer decay, no `&`) | 190 | 4 non-pointer | 1 |
| `(T *)((u8 *)sym + off)` | 41 | 1 | 1 (already fixed) |
| `memcpy`/`bcopy`/`memmove` from `&sym` | 15 | 0 | 0 |
| constant array index vs. symbol byte size | 68 | 0 real | 0 |
| `&sym` used as a loop bound / sentinel | 16 | 3 | 3 (all already fixed) |

**Works by luck — currently correct, no guarantee:**

- `gunfire.c:5579` — `*(ModelRenderData *)g_DefaultCasingModelRenderData`.
  The array is `u32[15]` = 0x3c; `ModelRenderData` is 0x40. The read takes
  `cullmode` (offset 0x3c) from past the end. N64: `80035eb0 3c` then
  `80035eec dword_D_80035EEC`, adjacent, image `00000000` -> cullmode 0 =
  `CULLMODE_BOTH`. Native: `081e1220 3c D`, next symbol `ammo_related` at
  `081e1260` (32-byte aligned), so 0x081e125c is four bytes of `.data`
  alignment padding — measured `00000000`, so cullmode is 0 there too.
  **This is the fourth member of the B-028 template family and the only one
  still unguarded.** It survives on a padding word, not on adjacency. Cheapest
  fix is the existing `sl_gun_renderdata_template` under `#ifndef __sgi`.
- `image.c:2403`, `image.c:2294`, `tex.c:809`, `initmttex.c:15` — the global
  `struct texpool` is `*(struct texpool *)&ptr_texture_alloc_start`, 16 bytes
  read off a 4-byte pointer. N64: `8008c720/724/728/72c` are
  `ptr_texture_alloc_start`, `ptr_texture_alloc_end`, `ptr_next_available_space`,
  `ptr_last_entry_facemapping` — the four fields, in order, by design. Native the
  order is REVERSED (`08fce5c4/5c8/5cc`) and `ptr_texture_alloc_end` is exiled to
  `08fcef40`, past `g_TexCacheItems`. It still works only because nothing in the
  tree ever names those three siblings (`grep -rn` over `src/ include/ assets/`
  returns their definitions and nothing else), so every read AND write goes
  through the same overlay window — which lands in 12 bytes of `.bss` alignment
  padding before `g_TexCacheItems` (`nm -n` shows no symbol in
  `08fce5d0..08fce5df`). A single 4-byte `.bss` symbol placed there would
  silently alias the pool's `end`/`leftpos`/`rightpos`.
- `bg.c:5600`, `bg.c:5601` — `*(coord3d *)&D_80044904` / `&D_80044910`, 12 bytes
  off 4-byte `s32`s. Both N64 (`80044904`..`8004491b`, six consecutive
  `0x7F7FFFFF`/`0xFF7FFFFF` words) and native (`081d2154`..`081d2168`,
  contiguous `.data`) give the intended `±FLT_MAX` min/max seed. All six carry
  nonzero initialisers so all six land in `.data` — that is what keeps them
  together, and it is not a rule the compiler owes us.

**Overruns that cannot bite:**

- `glass2.c:638` — `*(Vtx *)&D_80040980`, 16 bytes off a 4-byte `.bss` `u32`.
  N64 `0x80040980..0x8004098f` is 16 zero bytes with no symbol after
  `D_80040980` until `80040990`. Native the 12 overrun bytes are
  `PAD_8003C4E4/E8/EC` (`08eb7268/726c/7270`), which
  `assets/embedded/skeletons/standard_object.inc.c` defines as `s32 = 0` and
  which `grep -rn` over the whole tree shows are never referenced again — so
  they stay zero. Doubly safe: of the 16 bytes, `bullet_spark_render` overwrites
  `ob`, `tc` and `cn` on all four vertices, leaving only `v.flag` template-derived.
- `gunfire.c:5058`, `gunfire.c:5375` — `*(coord3d *)&D_80035EA4`, 12 bytes off a
  4-byte `.bss` `u32`. `D_80035EA4/EA8/EAC` are declared in `gun.c:509-513`,
  never written anywhere (`grep -rn 'D_80035EA8\|D_80035EAC' src/` returns only
  the declarations), zero on N64 (`0x80035ea4` = 12 zero bytes) and contiguous
  `.bss` natively (`08eb72fc/7300/7304`). `rot` = `{0,0,0}` either way.
- `snd.c:620` — `(ALEventQueue *)&D_800243E4`. `ALEventQueue` is 20 bytes,
  `D_800243E4` is 12 (`nm`: `08f677bc 0000000c B`). Only `freeList.next` (+0),
  `freeList.prev` (+4) and `allocList.next` (+8) are ever dereferenced — all
  inside the 12 bytes. `allocList.prev` and `eventCount` are never touched.
- `gunfire.c:5521`, `propobj.c:14184` — `(ALSoundState *)&g_CasingSfxState` /
  `&ptr_gas_sound`, 64-byte type over a 4-byte pointer. `sndPlaySfx` writes
  exactly one field of `pendingState`: `pendingState->link.next`, and `link` is
  at offset 0 of `ALSoundState` with `next` at offset 0 of `ALLink`. A 4-byte
  write at +0. That is the whole point of the cast — filling the pointer in.
- `initactorpropstuff.c:176`, `:188` — `(struct StruckAnim *)(&ptr_animation_table)`,
  28-byte type over a 4-byte pointer. `initResolveAnimTable` only ever evaluates
  `*(s32 *)entries`, i.e. offset 0. A decomp typing artifact, not a read.
- `initanitable.c:282`, `:283` — `(s32 *)&animation_table_ptrs1` / `_ptrs2`.
  Both arrays are NUL-terminated and `expand_ani_table_entries` stops on the
  terminator. In bounds.
- `explosion.c:1501`, `setguscale.c:5` — `(Mtx *)&dword_CODE_bss_8007A100`.
  Symbol is 64 bytes, `Mtx` is 64. Exact fit.
- `vtxstore.c:285`, `:290` — `((s16 *)&dword_CODE_bss_8007A0D4)[1]` reads bytes
  2..3 of a 4-byte symbol. In bounds.

**Already fixed before this sweep** (found and guarded during earlier native
work; recorded here so the class has one complete inventory):
`gunfire.c:1503`, `:1616`, `:1884` (B-028, `sl_gun_renderdata_template`);
`bg.c:347` (`specialportalarray` walk bounded by `&g_BgCurrentRoom`);
`front.c:1550` (`legalpage_text_array` walk bounded by `&legalscreen_MRD` —
N64 `8002a9cc + 0xf0` == `8002aabc` exactly, natively a 16-byte gap);
`blood_animation.c:233`, `:251` (`&die_blood_image_end`).

Two adjacent hazards found while sweeping, filed here rather than chased:

- **Stack-local overruns.** Same failure signature, different mechanism — the
  N64 frame layout, not the link order. ~30 sites of the form
  `(BigT *)&small_local`, concentrated in `snd.c` (`(ALEvent *)&evt`),
  `audi.c`/`boss.c`/`sched.c` (`(OSMesg *)&msg`), `image.c:231`
  (`(struct huft *)&scratch`) and `bg.c:3612` (`(struct HitThing *)&tmp`).
  Not part of B-029; worth its own pass if a stack-shaped native bug appears.
- **Hardcoded struct offsets**, e.g. `bondview2.c:3132-3135`
  (`(Model *)((u8 *)g_CurrentPlayer + 0x230)`). Checked: `struct player` +560 is
  `something_with_watch_object_instance` and the fields around it are all
  4-byte scalars, so the native layout reproduces the N64 offsets. Safe today
  because nothing in `struct player` repacks — but it is an unchecked assumption
  wherever it appears.


### B-030 — the ammo HUD is drawn 240 times and never appears

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, owner reported "missing HUD" while playing
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `gunDrawHudInteger`/`gunDrawHudString` (`gunfire.c:5877`, `:5932`), called from `:6025` and `:6035`
- **Blocks:** knowing how much ammo you have.

**I filed this wrong the first time and the correction matters.** When the owner
first said "no HUD", I measured `bondviewRenderGaugeBars` at ZERO calls and
reported that as correct behaviour, because the health/armour bars are gated on
`bondviewGetIfCurrentPlayerHealthShowTime()` and only appear when damaged. That
much is true. But it is not the whole HUD, and the owner was describing the
whole thing.

`gunDrawHudInteger` runs **240 times** in a gameplay run. The ammo readout is
therefore being drawn and not appearing. Checked a captured in-level frame and
cropped the bottom-right corner where the ammo sits: empty wall.

What makes this odd, and what to use as the lever: **the text path works
elsewhere.** The watch renders its header, mission status and weapon name
legibly, and every level caption reads correctly, all through the same font
machinery fixed in `b2e23ff2`. So this is not "text is broken" - it is
something specific to the HUD's own draw.

Worth measuring next, in this order:
1. Whether `gunDrawHudString` actually advances the `Gfx*` it returns. Same
   technique that cracked [[B-028]]: bracket the call and compare the pointer.
   If it does not advance, nothing is emitted and the gate is upstream.
2. If it does advance, where the commands land - `sl_2d: texrect cmds=0` in
   gameplay frames and a raw linear scan of the whole list found `E4/E5=0`, so
   whatever the HUD emits is either not a texrect or not reaching that buffer.
3. Whether the ammo gate itself passes: `:6023` skips the magazine count for
   `WEAPONSTATBITFLAG_NO_CLIP_RELOADS`, and `:6033` skips the reserve unless
   `reserveammo > 0`. Both could legitimately suppress a readout.

**MEASURED FURTHER 2026-08-25 — it is NOT the same as B-028, and it does emit.**

Unlike the viewmodel, the ammo HUD really does write commands. Bracketing the
call site (`gunfire.c:6025` -> `:6033`) over a recorded playthrough: reached
**2491 times**, `gdl` advancing `0xf5c1a600 -> 0xf5c1a630` = 6 commands each
time, with `mag = 7` - the PP7's correct round count. So the game is drawing the
right number in the right place.

Two theories killed by measurement:
- "It writes past the end of the submitted list." NO. The HUD writes at
  `0xf5c1a600` and the task submits `[0xf5c19280, 0xf5c1a698]` - comfortably
  inside.
- "It shares B-028's cause." NO. B-028 emitted no draw at all; this emits six
  commands per call.

**The commands themselves are the lead:**
```
b900031d 00504240   setothermode_l (render mode)
fcffffff fffdf6fb   setcombine
fa000000 00000000   setprimcolor  -> rgba = 00 00 00 00
f6404350 00404350   fillrect
```
`setprimcolor` carries **alpha 0**. The font path renders glyphs through
`prim-replace` (established when B-020 was fixed - the watch text takes its
colour from the primitive colour), so a primitive colour of zero draws nothing
visible.

**RESOLVED 2026-08-25. Root cause: `sprintf` returns an empty string natively.**

Correcting the entry below before anyone acts on it - I decoded the two mux
words against the table in `ucode05_old.txt` and they CLEAR the renderer:

```
MUX A (fcffffff fffdf6fb)  RGB = prim              ALPHA = prim
MUX B (fcff97ff ff2dfeff)  RGB = prim              ALPHA = texel0 * prim
```

MUX A is exactly prim-replace, so this renderer's approximation was right all
along and real hardware would have drawn the same blank rectangle from a
primitive colour of zero. MUX B is the ordinary font-glyph mux. So the suspicion
recorded below - that the combiner approximation was at fault - was wrong.

The actual cause is one level up. `gunDrawHudInteger` (gunfire.c:5935) formats
the number with `sprintf`, and MEASURED at gunfire.c:5936: a correct value (93)
and a correct format ("%d") produced `buffer == ""`, with a NUL written at
index 0. `src/sprintf.c` delegates to libultra's `_Printf`, which IS linked into
the native binary (`nm` shows both symbols) but returns 0 for every call. The
string was empty, so `gunDrawHudString` had no characters to emit; the two
fillrects were the string box, and the zero primitive colour was a SYMPTOM of
the empty string rather than a lost value.

Fixed by giving `src/sprintf.c` a native branch that calls the host `vsprintf`,
under `#ifdef __sgi` so the matching build keeps Rare's implementation and stays
byte-identical (verified: ROM OK, checksum step clean). `vsprintf` is declared
locally rather than via `<stdio.h>` because this file compiles with the N64 SDK
include path, which shadows the host headers. The `written - 1` return is
preserved as-is rather than "corrected" - it is what the call sites expect.

Validated at RUNTIME across the whole tree, not just the one call site it was
diagnosed from: a 6000-frame facility run makes **3413 sprintf calls with zero
empty results**. Every one of those returned an empty string before the fix.

Verified after the fix: `buffer == "93"` (`39 33 0a 00`), and the HUD run grew
from 6 commands to 0x3d8 bytes, now emitting `settextureimage` for the font,
`loadblock`, `setprimcolor 646464ff` (a real grey at full alpha) and a run of
`E4` texrects - the digits.

**This was never HUD-specific: it is 106 call sites tree-wide.** Anything that
formats text through `sprintf` was blank - it is also why the first `sl_gfx_sdl`
screenshot silently wrote to an empty path. Objectives text, the multiplayer
menu, options and the debug overlays all go through it and should be re-checked
now that it works, rather than assumed fixed.

The lesson repeats the file's own refrain: `_Printf` being present in the link
map said nothing about whether it WORKED. Measuring one buffer settled in
seconds what reading the call chain had pointed the wrong way twice.

---

**FULL RUN DUMPED. The digits are FILLRECTS, not texrects** - which is why the
earlier `E4/E5=0` scan found nothing and why this looked like B-028 at first.
One HUD frame, `0xf5c08c20`-`0xf5c08c80`:

```
b900031d 00504240   setothermode_l
fcffffff fffdf6fb   setcombine
fa000000 00000000   setprimcolor  rgba = 0
f6404350 00404350   FILLRECT
b900031d 00504240   setothermode_l
fcff97ff ff2dfeff   setcombine   (different mux)
...same four again with f6420350...
```

Two fillrects, each preceded by `setprimcolor` at zero, with the combiner mux
changing between them.

**This points at OUR combiner approximation, not at the game.** The 2D work
(`d5b21e1f`) established two things that collide here: a fillrect in 1-cycle
takes the **colour combiner** rather than the fill register, and this renderer
approximates the combiner as `prim-replace`. Under that approximation a
primitive colour of zero is invisible - but the real RDP would source those
texels from whatever the mux actually selects, which the two different
`setcombine` words suggest is not prim for both passes.

So the likely fix is in the combiner handling, not in the HUD path. Decode both
`fcffffff fffdf6fb` and `fcff97ff ff2dfeff` against the mux table in
`ucode05_old.txt` (the current note punts on `FC SETCOMBINE`; the `_old` one has
carried the table three times now) and check what each actually selects.

One more observation from the same dump, NOT chased and possibly unrelated: a
`B8 ENDDL` appears at `0xf5c08cb0` with further commands after it in the same
buffer. That may simply be a sub-list boundary the walk returns from, but it is
worth confirming rather than assuming, given B-019 was exactly a list the walker
never reached.

Next step: establish whether alpha 0 is what the GAME intends here - this may be
a shadow or outline pass that is legitimately transparent, with the visible
glyph pass following - or whether the primitive colour is being lost the way
`renderdata.flags` was in B-028. Dump the FULL command run for one HUD frame,
not just the six around the call, before concluding. Note `gunDrawHudString`
takes an `outline` argument, and both ammo call sites pass `1`.

May share a cause with [[B-028]] - the viewmodel emitted five state commands and
no draw - but that is a guess and has not been tested.

### B-031 — Bond's arm missing from the watch on pause

Reported twice by the owner: pausing shows the watch but not the wrist/arm it
should be attached to.

**Two plausible causes ruled out by measurement, so nobody re-checks them:**

- NOT the B-028 template class. `bondviewRenderWatch` (bondview2.c:8436) opens
  with `renderdata = D_8003683C`, which has exactly the shape that hid Bond's
  gun - but `nm -S` puts `D_8003683C` at `00000040` bytes in `.data`, the full
  `sizeof(ModelRenderData)`, properly initialised at bondview.c:466. No
  overrun. (For contrast the B-028 symbol reads `D_80035CC0 00000004 B`.)
- NOT a lost `flags`. The function assigns `renderdata.flags = 3` and
  `renderdata.PropType = PROP_TYPE_WEAPON` explicitly at bondview2.c:8540
  before drawing, so the value cannot arrive as zero.

**What is actually known.** The watch and the arm come from ONE `subdraw` call
(bondview2.c:8553) over `something_with_watch_object_instance`, so the model as
a whole is being submitted - the face demonstrably renders. That makes this a
node-level failure inside a model that otherwise draws, not a missing draw.

The parts are reached through `objheader->Switches[]`: `Switches[3]` for the
face, `Switches[2]->Data` for the hand. Note the asymmetry - `Switches[3]` is
used WITHOUT `->Data` at bondview2.c:8439 while `Switches[2]` uses it. That is
the decomp's own code and the matching build reproduces it, so it is Rare's and
must not be "corrected"; it is recorded only because it will look like a bug to
the next reader.

**Next step, and it needs a frame.** The hypothesis worth testing first is
SWITCH-node selection: if a switch index is read in the wrong byte order the
model would still draw while consistently picking the wrong branch. That is the
project's most frequent bug class and it fits "everything renders except this
one part". Confirming it needs one paused capture, which cannot be taken while
the owner is using the display.

**THE HARNESS CAN NOW RAISE THE WATCH, and the first measurement KILLS the
switch-node hypothesis.**

`tools/trace/mkinput.py pause` now presses START repeatedly rather than once,
and the watch goes up: `watch_animation_state != 0` on 1198 of 1988 calls,
`pausing_flag` true on 1079, and the draw at bondview2.c:8553 is reached.

With the watch actually raised:

```
numSwitches  = 10
Switches[2]  = 0xf5da1400      (the hand)
Switches[3]  = 0xf5da1370      (the face)
anim_state   = 3
```

Both indices are well inside `numSwitches`, both pointers are valid, and the
model draws. **So the standing hypothesis - that a switch index read in the
wrong byte order picks the wrong branch - is wrong.** A garbage index would be
out of range or a junk pointer; these are neither. Recorded so it is not
re-tried.

The watch subdraw's emitted list is now dumped (104 words) and it is NOT empty
or degenerate - it repeats a well-formed per-node group:

```
bc000c06 f5c375e0   moveword           <- matrix/segment setup
bc001406 f5da1060   moveword
e7000000 00000000   pipesync
ba001402 00100000   setothermode_h
fc26a004 1f1093ff   setcombine
b900031d c4112048   setothermode_l
06000000 05007ee8   CALL DISPLAYLIST   <- the node's geometry
```

repeated with different call targets (`05007ee8`, `05008ee0`, ...). So the model
walks several nodes and calls each one's geometry list. That further narrows it:
the arm is not being skipped at the list level in an obvious way, and whether it
is among those calls needs the call targets resolved against the model's nodes.

Next: resolve those `06` call targets to node types and check which ones the
arm should be. If the arm's list IS called, the fault is in its transform (the
B-028 GroupSimple.Origin shape - a correct 3x3 with a garbage translation row);
if it is NOT called, the fault is in the node walk.

What that leaves: the arm is a node inside a model that demonstrably submits,
reached through a valid switch, with `flags = 3` and a correctly sized
`ModelRenderData`. Everything structural on the path measures clean. The next
candidates are the node's own transform (the same shape as B-028's
GroupSimple.Origin, where a correct 3x3 carried a garbage translation row) or
the node type simply not being emitted - both of which want the emitted display
list for the watch draw dumped and decoded, exactly as B-027 was settled.

Earlier attempt, kept because the failure mode is instructive: a single START
press at read 900 delivered NOTHING (`bondviewProcessInput` saw buttons == 0 on
all 1988 calls). 900 reads is not provably past the point where the game acts on
input, and the stream was neutral forever after. The `fire` routine works
precisely because it bursts across the whole stream, so some burst always lands
once the game is live. Synthesised streams should repeat their input, never
press once.

SUPERSEDED - the harness limitation below is fixed:

**Attempt to test this headlessly: the harness cannot raise the watch yet.**
`tools/trace/mkinput.py pause` presses START as a rising edge (4 reads, then
released - bondview2.c:4839 tests `buttons & ~oldbuttons & START_BUTTON`, so
holding it does nothing after the first frame). Measured over a 5000-frame run:

```
bondviewRenderWatch calls : 1988
watch_animation_state != 0:    0
pausing_flag true         :    0
```

`bondviewRenderWatch` runs every frame but both of its early-return guards fire
every time, so the draw at bondview2.c:8553 is never reached. The watch is
never raised, which means this run tested the INPUT, not the arm - B-031 is

The press itself is not obviously wrong: the recorded facility stream's first

the pause stream to confirm START arrives at all before changing the routine -

WANTED: one facility capture, paused, watch raised. Until then this is a
