## B-043 follow-up (2026-08-26). "The fade starts too late OR the camera arrives too early" — NEITHER. Measured, and the premise was false.

**Status:** no code change. The intro-camera schedule and the character fade
are correct and cannot drift apart. Two measurement probes were added
(native-only, `SL_SWIRL_DBG=1`) so this is re-checkable in one run rather than
re-argued. A DIFFERENT, previously unrecorded defect was found on the same
frames and is written up at the end.

### The claim under test

The brief for this session recorded, from the owner's own recorded session
(`/tmp/session.input`):

```
tick 533   currentPlayerStartChrFade(30.0f, 0.0f)   fade begins
tick 540   camera "INSIDE THE HEAD", chrfadealpha still 195  (76% opaque)
tick 562   cancelled, snaps to 255
```

and concluded that the fade is only ~7 ticks into a 30-tick ramp at the head
passthrough, so one side must have drifted.

### Measurement 1 — the swirl data decodes exactly. Facility, dumped AS READ.

`bondview_r.c`, before the `/0x10000` conversion, `SL_SWIRL_DBG=1`:

```
SWIRLREC 0  flags=0x6 rawoff=(0,38993920,-2621440) rawscale=49152 rawdur=1638400 pad=-1
SWIRLREC 1  flags=0x6 rawoff=(-2621440,33423360,0) rawscale=49152 rawdur=1638400 pad=-1
...
SWIRLREC 8  flags=0x6 rawoff=(655360,0,-1638400)   rawscale=49152 rawdur=1638400 pad=-1
SWIRLREC 9  flags=0x2 rawoff=(0,0,0)               rawscale=32768 rawdur=0       pad=-1
SWIRLREC 10 flags=0x2 rawoff=(0,0,0)               rawscale=32768 rawdur=0       pad=-1
SWIRLREC 11 flags=0x1 rawoff=(0,0,0)               rawscale=0     rawdur=0       pad=-1
```

Layout confirmed against `Setup File Microcodes and Paths/Intro Block/Intro
Block Commands.txt`, `7F005BA0 type 3` — 0x20 bytes, `type / flags / X / Y / Z
/ lateral-rot / rate / pad`, with X,Y,Z,rot,rate all divided by 0x10000 at
parse time. Every field decodes to a round number: `1638400 / 65536 = 25.0`
ticks on all nine active entries, offsets `(0, 594.9, -40)` down to
`(10, 0, -25)`, scale `49152 / 65536 = 0.75`, terminator flag `1` on record 11.
**Nothing is byte-swapped wrong and no record stride is off**; `prop.c:1319`'s
8-word swap for `INTROTYPE_SWIRL` is right. Lead 1 of the brief is closed.

Total swirl length: 9 x 25 = **225 ticks**.

### Measurement 2 — the two sides are the SAME accumulator, so they cannot drift

`sp30` (bondview2.c:1373-1378) is the time REMAINING in the swirl. It arms the
fade at `sp30` crossing 30 and it is derived from the same entry durations that
schedule the camera. Per-tick probe, owner's session, Facility:

```
SWIRL t=1067 idx=7 sp30=29  d=27.90  fa=255   <- fade arms here
SWIRL t=1081 idx=8 sp30=22  d=25.68  fa=195   <- the brief's "tick 540"
SWIRL t=1105 idx=8 sp30=10  d=12.13  fa= 93
SWIRL t=1107 idx=8 sp30= 9  d=10.70  fa= 84   <- camera reaches head-sized range
SWIRL t=1125 idx=8 sp30= 0  d= 0.000 fa=  8   <- camera AT the head origin
```

(`d` = distance from the camera to `g_CurrentPlayer->field_3C4/8/C`, the point
the swirl converges on. `t` is `sl_frames_completed()`, which advances 2 per sim
tick; the brief's tick numbers map onto the `sp30` column exactly — its 533 is
`sp30=29`, its 562 is `sp30=0`.)

The camera reaches `d = 0.000` at exactly `sp30 = 0.000`, the same tick the fade
ends. **The fade ramp and the camera approach are locked together by
construction** — both integrate `g_GlobalTimerDelta` through one accumulator, so
no frame-rate or delta-semantics difference can separate them. Lead 3 is closed
too, and closed for a stronger reason than "delta is 1.0": even if delta were
2.5, as it would be on hardware at 24fps, both sides step by the same 2.5.

### Measurement 3 — the brief's premise is false: at fade-tick 7 the camera is 25.7 units from the head, outside it

The brief's "tick 540, camera is INSIDE THE HEAD, alpha still 195" is `sp30=22`,
`d=25.68`. The captured frame at that instant shows the head from OUTSIDE,
frontally, filling roughly a third of the screen. The camera first gets within
head-sized range (`d ~ 11`) at `sp30 = 9` — that is **21 of the 30 ticks into
the ramp, alpha 84, 67% faded**, not 7 ticks and 76% opaque.

### The captured frames, which is what was asked for

`xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 640x480x24" env SL_ROM=baserom.u.z64
SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34 SL_WINDOW=1 SL_INPUT=/tmp/session.input SL_FRAMES=1160
SL_SWIRL_DBG=1 SL_SHOT=... SL_SHOT_EVERY=4`. Interleaving the probe's stderr
with `sl_shot:` lines gives an exact frame-to-alpha correlation, which is the
technique that made this session cheap:

| shot | sp30 | alpha | what the pixels show |
|---|---|---|---|
| 133 | 30-26 | 255 | head opaque (see the separate defect below) |
| 134 | 25-22 | 246-221 | face visible, faintly translucent |
| 136 | 19-14 | 169-127 | door struts read clearly through the face |
| 138 | 11-8 | 101-76 | head mostly gone |
| 140 | 3-1 | 33-16 | head essentially invisible |
| 141+ | — | — | **nothing. No face, no head, no body.** |

After the swirl ends the player model is not drawn at all, so the "face at level
start" is not persisting past the intro. The ramp behaves exactly as the owner
described the original behaving: the model fades away as the camera converges
into the head.

### Verdict

There is nothing to fix on the timing side and no fix was attempted. Anyone
returning to this should not re-derive it: run the probe.

```
SL_SWIRL_DBG=1   ->  SWIRLREC lines (bondview_r.c, records as read)
                     SWIRL     lines (bondview2.c, per-tick sp30/camera/alpha)
```

Both are `#ifndef __sgi` and off unless the variable is set; they use
`sl_detail_log` / `sl_env_s32` rather than `<stdio.h>`, because including
`stdio.h` into a decomp translation unit fails to compile (the ultra64 headers
leave `__gnuc_va_list` undefined under `-std=gnu89 -fno-builtin`).

**Absence claim, with the search that backs it:** `grep -rn "g_IntroSwirl" src/`
returns 17 hits in 5 files and every read of `.unk18` / `.duration` is in the
two functions above — there is no third consumer of the swirl schedule that
could be running on a different clock.

### NEW DEFECT found on these frames: Bond's face draws SOLID BLACK while fully opaque

Not the reported bug, not fixed here, but recorded precisely because it is on
exactly the path this ticket keeps landing on and it is one frame away from the
evidence above.

Two shots, ONE sim tick apart, camera moved 0.5 world units, same angle:

```
shot 266   sp30=30..29   fa=255   face polygons SOLID BLACK, jaw/neck/ear skin correct
shot 267   sp30=28..27   fa=246   same polygons, face texture correct and lit
```

The switch coincides exactly with `chr.c:2993` moving the model from
`PropType = 7` (`PROP_TYPE_VIEWER+1`, opaque pass) to `PropType = 8`
(`PROP_TYPE_EXPLOSION+1`, alpha pass). Geometry, texture, camera and lighting
are unchanged across those two frames, so the difference is the render path.

What that narrows it to, read from `modelApplyRenderModeType3` (model.c:3501 and
model.c:3546) — the two branches' **RGB combiners are character-for-character
identical**:

```
both:  rgb c0  (TEXEL0 - ENV) * SHADE_ALPHA + ENV
both:  rgb c1  (COMBINED - 0) * SHADE + 0
```

They differ only in (a) the cycle-0 ALPHA mux, (b) the ENV alpha byte — `0xFF`
for VIEWER+1 versus the fade alpha for EXPLOSION+1 — and (c) the cycle-1 render
mode, `G_RM_AA_ZB_OPA_SURF2` versus `G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF2`, both behind
`G_RM_FOG_PRIM_A`. **So the blackness cannot come from the RGB combiner.** The
untested candidates are the `G_RM_FOG_PRIM_A` blender (`fogcolour` was measured
at `0x0b160bb4` in the earlier work — RGB (11,22,11), i.e. near-black, alpha
0xb4) and the primary/secondary split, which would explain why only the face
polygons blacken while the adjacent neck and ear do not: the VIEWER+1 branch
only emits a combiner for `isPrimary`, and the secondary list inherits whatever
was bound before it.

The next measurement is therefore: on a frame with `fa == 255`, log the combiner
word, the fog colour, the env colour and the render-mode words the interpreter
actually has bound when it draws the face triangles, and compare them against
the `fa == 246` frame one tick later. Do not patch either branch before that —
this ticket has already produced four plausible-but-wrong fixes.

Also unestablished, and worth stating so it is not assumed: whether the face is
black EARLIER in the intro too. Shots before 261 do not show the face at a
comparable frontal angle, so they neither confirm nor deny it.

The B-043 ENV-alpha fix (aa32c88e) did not cause this. That fix fires only when
the cycle-0 alpha multiplier is ENVIRONMENT, which is the EXPLOSION+1 spelling;
the VIEWER+1 alpha multiplier is SHADE, so `g_cc_a_envscale` is false for the
black draw.

### Gates run for this session

```
make matching                      MATCH!                        EXIT=0
make bootsweep                     20/20 OK                      EXIT=0
make trace-verify LEVEL=facility   IDENTICAL - 15869 ticks match EXIT=0
```

`trace-verify` passing is itself part of the argument above: the native sim
replays the recorded Facility trace tick-for-tick, and that trace covers the
intro, so the native intro-camera schedule is identical to the matching build's
— which is byte-identical to the ROM. There is no room for the schedule to have
drifted.
