## B-043 SOLVED (2026-08-26). Face through the back of the head: the renderer ignored the RSP's cull bits, and its BF triangle decode was wound backwards.

**Status:** fixed in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` (native renderer only; the matching
build does not compile this file). Uncommitted, in the working tree. Two
changes, one of which is a decode correction that stands on its own.

### The starting frames, read correctly this time

`g-00266.ppm` (fade alpha 255) and `g-00267.ppm` (alpha 246), one sim tick
apart, camera behind the head. 266 is a solid black silhouette and is CORRECT.
267 draws the eyes, nose and mouth on top of the hair and is THE BUG. The
previous session had these the other way round; that reading is retracted.

### Candidate 1 - depth writes - is a DEAD END, and it is dead by measurement

The brief's first candidate was that the game asks for depth writes on the
faded character and `rm_apply` drops them. It does not. Probe `SL_FADE_DBG=1`,
owner's session, Facility, the reported frame:

```
sl_fade: frame 533 tris=730  om=c41049d8  zcmp=1 zupd=0 zmode=2 forcebl=1
```

`Z_UPD` is CLEAR because the game cleared it. `modelApplyRenderModeType3`
(model.c:3547) binds `G_RM_FOG_PRIM_A | G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF2` for
`PROP_TYPE_EXPLOSION+1`, and that constant carries no `Z_UPD`. Bit values
confirmed against `Display Lists and Object Generation/ucode05_old.txt:319`
(`0x00000020 depth update`, `0x00000800 depth exclusive`) - the note's table
and `sl_gfx_dl.c`'s `RM_*` constants agree exactly. `rm_apply` is faithful.
**Nothing in the depth path is wrong. Do not re-open it.**

### What it actually is: the game asks to be culled there, and this file declined

Same probe, same frame:

```
cull[none,front,back,front+back] = 2,0,728,0     geom_seen=00002205
```

**728 of the 730 triangles are emitted with `G_CULL_BACK` set.** The bits are
`G_CULL_BACK 0x2000` from `include/PR/gbi.h:360`, and `0x2205` is
`G_ZBUFFER|G_SHADE|G_SHADING_SMOOTH|G_CULL_BACK`. So the mechanism is exactly
what the brief's candidate 3 supposed - and while the model is opaque the depth
buffer hides the far side anyway, which is why the artifact appears on the one
tick the game stops writing depth and not before.

### Why turning culling on broke characters in B-040: a real decode bug, now fixed

`SL_CULL=1` did fix the face-in-head and did open holes - a sliver through the
hair and a background-coloured wedge through the collar, both visible while the
model is still fully OPAQUE. That is not a fade problem and not the camera
being inside the head.

The existing `g_edge_ok`/`g_edge_bad` telemetry says Rare's data is
consistently wound, and it is not wrong so much as blind: it clears its table
on every vertex load, so it only ever compares triangles that arrived in the
same 16-entry batch. A character is hundreds of vertices delivered 16 at a
time. Re-keying the directed-edge table on each vertex's SOURCE ADDRESS, so the
two halves of a shared edge are seen across batches:

```
730 triangles, 2190 directed edges
paired=635  SAME-WAY-TWICE=14  once=1541  repeated-triangles=0
bad-by-slot [tri4 0,1,2,3 | tri1] = 0,0,0,0 | 14
tris-by-slot                      = 193,193,171,158 | 15
```

An edge traversed twice in the same direction is two triangles facing opposite
ways - the exact shape of a cull hole. **All 14 came from the BF single-triangle
command, which contributes 15 of the model's 730 triangles. GE_TRI4's other 715
had zero.**

The BF decode had its vertex order reversed. Authority is
`include/PR/gbi.h:2042-2044`, the plain-F3D branch this build compiles:

```c
__gsSP1Triangle_w1f(v0,v1,v2,flag) =
    _SHIFTL(flag,24,8) | _SHIFTL(v0*10,16,8)
  | _SHIFTL(v1*10,8,8) | _SHIFTL(v2*10,0,8)
```

**v0 is bits 16-23 - the note's `zz` - and v2 is the low byte.** The multiplier
agrees with the note (10 decimal == 0xA), so only the ORDER was wrong, and
reversed order is reversed winding.

`Absolute Basic Rendering Models.txt:83-88` cannot settle this and should not
be blamed for it: it writes both worked examples as SETS (`{0,1,2}`,
`{13,14,15}`), and a set has no winding. Its prose calls the low byte "x" and
says the first point is x, which is what an earlier pass took at face value -
correcting the command **by the note without ever measuring it**, because tri1
is 0 in Facility and dam ROOM geometry, which is all that had been looked at.
Characters use it. That is the same failure mode this ticket recorded before:
a measurement taken outside the event proves nothing about the event.

With the order corrected, `SAME-WAY-TWICE` is **0** and `paired` rises 635 ->
649. Both holes close. The fix is a no-op wherever culling is off, so it
carries no risk of its own.

### The fix that ships

1. `OP_TRI1` emits `(w1>>16, w1>>8, w1)` instead of `(w1, w1>>8, w1>>16)`.
2. `SL_CULL` gains a new default, mode 4: honour the RSP's cull bits **only on
   draws that do not write depth**. `cull_apply` takes the `Z_UPD` bit as a
   parameter (it is defined ahead of `RM_Z_UPD`/`g_om_l`, and `emit_tri` calls
   it before `rm_apply` so neither has established GL state yet).

Mode 4 leaves every opaque draw exactly as it was, which is the property that
makes it shippable: opaque geometry is already handled correctly by the depth
buffer, so the only draws it can touch are ones where this renderer is known to
be showing far-side geometry the console does not.

`SL_CULL=0` restores the old ignore-everything behaviour for bisecting;
`SL_CULL=1` is the full hardware reading; `SL_CULL=3` is the unchanged
draw-only-what-would-be-dropped diagnostic.

### Why NOT `SL_CULL=1` everywhere, which is what the hardware does

Because dam disagrees, and a picture says so. dam intro, shot 16 of a
1000-frame boot: under sense 1 on every draw the truck's near tyre loses most
of its geometry - a full treaded wheel becomes a thin dark crescent with the
chassis grating showing through. Facility, archives and streets are near-clean
under sense 1; dam is not, and one level is enough. That geometry is opaque, so
mode 4 does not touch it.

### Verification - what was actually run

**The frame that was asked for.** Owner's session, `SL_INPUT=/tmp/session.input
SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34 SL_FRAMES=1160 SL_SHOT_EVERY=2` under `xvfb-run`, identical
runs before and after. Shot 267, the reported frame, same camera angle:

- Before: eyes, nose and mouth drawn on top of the hair.
- After: a clean black silhouette. **The face no longer shows through.** Shot
  272 shows the head translucent and coherent as the camera converges, with no
  face-on-hair artifact, which is the behaviour the owner described the
  original having.

**Blast radius, measured not argued.** All 290 shots of the owner's session,
per-frame `compare -metric RMSE`, final binary vs pre-fix:

```
18 of 290 frames differ
  267-280   the intended fix, the fade window   (RMSE 935 - 10324)
  239,249,250,258   RMSE 0.27 - 0.46            (a handful of pixels)
```

The four tiny ones are the tri1 order change moving a shared-edge fill-rule
decision by a pixel or two. The other 272 frames are bit-identical.

**The character was verified, which is the B-040 trap.** Shots 245, 252, 260
and 266 - Bond's model frontal, in profile and from behind, opaque, filling a
third of the screen - are **bit-identical** to the pre-fix baseline. Shot 260
in particular is the profile view where `SL_CULL=1` opened the hair and collar
holes; under the shipped default it is untouched, and under `SL_CULL=1` with
the tri1 fix both holes are closed.

**Independent check that the tri1 fix is load-bearing rather than cosmetic:**
shot 267 under the shipped default is RMSE 0 against (tri1 fixed + `SL_CULL=1`)
and RMSE 4714 against (tri1 unfixed + `SL_CULL=1`).

Gates:

```
make matching                      MATCH!                         EXIT=0
make bootsweep                     20/20 OK                       EXIT=0
make trace-verify LEVEL=facility   IDENTICAL - 15869 ticks match  EXIT=0
```

### What is NOT proven, stated precisely

Mode 4 changes non-depth-writing surfaces on other levels too - archives 14 of
20 shots and streets 14 of 20 at RMSE ~250 (a handful of small scattered
triangles each), dam 19 of 20 with one shot at 1550 where the truck's near tyre
body stops being drawn. On that whole set the winding was measured consistent
(`SL_FADE_DBG=2`, dam: `paired=71 SAME-WAY-TWICE=0` over the ~141 triangles per
frame the mode acts on), so every triangle it drops is one the RSP would also
have dropped **given that this renderer's global winding sense is right** -
which is established only indirectly, by sense 2 being catastrophic and by the
character check above.

**This repository still has no console or emulator reference frame**, so
"the console shows the same thing" is not something any of this proves. The
libretro harness in `tools/trace/` does have a video-refresh hook and a
parallel_n64 core installed; wiring it to dump a reference frame of the dam
intro is the measurement that would close this, and nobody should re-argue it
from source in the meantime.

### Re-running any of it

```
SL_FADE_DBG=1   per-frame telemetry for the faded-character draw: triangle
                count, winding split, cull bits in force, render mode, and the
                source-address edge topology
SL_FADE_DBG=2   the same, widened to every triangle the default cull mode acts
                on (cull bits set, no depth write)
SL_CULL=0/1/2/3/4   ignore / full hardware / inverted / diagnostic / default
```

Both are `getenv`-gated and cost nothing when unset.

### Candidates ELIMINATED, so nobody re-runs them

The depth write/test state on the alpha pass (the game clears `Z_UPD` on
purpose and `rm_apply` honours it); the fade machinery, trigger, ramp, stored
alpha and both render passes; the intro timing; `isPrimary` and the node
classification; "characters have mixed winding" (`ccw=896 cw=658` is what a
closed mesh looks like from outside, not a defect); and "culling destroys
character models" (B-040's test frame had the camera inside Bond's head).

### B-035 — FIXED: the ring inherits a texture the combiner never asked for

- **Fixed:** 2026-08-26. `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` only; no game source changed.
- **Status:** CLOSED, with a captured before/after and a 20-level pixel sweep.

**The ring was never greyscale.** It was the correct hue scaled to 8/255,
which reads as black. Measured by differencing two captures of the same frame,
one with the gauge drawn and one without, and reading the pixels the gauge
actually wrote:

```
health arc (alpha 255, so drawn straight)   rendered r=8 g=1..7 b=0..2
computed by hudMakeDamageSegments           r=255 g=227..20 b=57..5
                                            8/255 = 0.0314; 227*0.0314 = 7
```

Every channel down by the same factor. That is not a lost colour, it is a
MODULATION - `emit_tri` was drawing under `GL_MODULATE` against an inherited
tile whose texel was 8. The armour arc reads as flat grey for the same reason
plus its own alpha: Bond carries no armour in Facility, so all 46 of its
segments sit at alpha 0x30, and 0.19 x (a colour scaled to near zero) over the
background is background.

**Root cause, and the notes state it outright.**
`Display Lists and Object Generation/Objects/Texture application (Rooms).txt`
gives the two patterns a room binary uses, and the untextured one is:

```
FCFFFFFF FFFE793C	;only applies vertex and enviroment color
BB000001 FFFFFFFF	;on, level 0, tile 0, ignore ST
```

`BB` stays ON for untextured geometry. It is the RSP's texture-COORDINATE
switch, not the RDP's sampler; what spells "untextured" is the FC combiner
naming no texel. `tex_apply` gated on `g_tex_on` alone, so every triangle in
the frame drew textured (`sl_tex: tris textured=986 plain=0`), and any list
that declined to re-issue its own `BB` - the gauge among them - got modulated
by whatever tile the previous draw had left bound.

`fcffffff fffe793c` is byte-for-byte the combiner the gauge draw sets
(`gDPSetCombineMode(gdl++, G_CC_SHADE, G_CC_SHADE)`, bondview2.c:8617), and
byte-for-byte the one in the note.

**This also corrects B-034's hypothesis 1, which was refuted on bad evidence.**
It concluded "level is not a texture gate here" and, from that, that no
triangle draws under a texel-free combiner. The first half is right; the second
is false and was measured on the submitted command stream rather than on the
renderer. Live per-frame counts, gate armed: dam 34, streets 68, statue 56,
archives 3, facility 0.

**The fix.** Classify the FC muxes for TEXEL0/TEXEL1 across both cycles,
colour and alpha, and treat "no texel anywhere" as untextured however `BB` was
left. Field layout from `ucode05_old.txt`'s "FC rdp_setcombine" table (a0 =
w0 bits 20-23, c0 = w0 bits 15-19, ... ; mux 1/2 are the texels and 8/9 their
alphas in the 5-bit c slot). Deliberately the widest reading of "uses a texel",
so the gate fires only where dropping the texture is unambiguous.
`SL_CC_TEXGATE=0` restores the old behaviour for A/B capture.

**Reproducing it, which is what had actually blocked this.** Two ways, both
recorded because the first is the cheap one and the second is the honest one:

1. *Forced.* `bondviewRenderGaugeBars` is gated on
   `bondviewGetIfCurrentPlayerHealthShowTime()` (bondview2.c:9422), i.e. on
   `healthshowtime > 0`, which is -1 until damage lands. A gdb breakpoint on
   that function with `set variable g_CurrentPlayer->healthshowtime = 1` and
   `continue` puts the ring on screen every frame, no source change:
   2437 gauge draws in 6000 frames on an idle Facility run.
2. *Natural.* Statue with `mkinput.py idle` shoots at Bond on its own. Frames
   6 and 7 of a 3000-frame capture have him hit, tracer in flight, ring up.
   That is the capture in the record - no forcing anywhere in it.

**What the owner's own recording does NOT contain.** `/tmp/session.input`
(2901 reads) never damages Bond: 0 hits on `bondviewRenderGaugeBars` over 4000
frames at `SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34`. It does raise the watch, which is why the watch
ring was the one available capture. Do not go looking for combat in it again.

**Why the watch ring looked right all along, same geometry and same combiner.**
It is drawn where the previously bound tile is white, so the modulation was a
no-op. The gate fires on the watch path too - 21 reported frames of the session
run, under `fcffffff fffdf6fb` (PRIM/PRIM) and `fffe793c` - and changes
nothing: 0 of 20 captured frames differ.

#### Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| in-game ring, Facility, gauge forced | before: hue x 8/255. after: warm left, blue right |
| in-game ring, Statue, damage taken naturally | same, no forcing (frames 6-7) |
| `make matching` | **MATCH!**, EXIT=0 |
| `make bootsweep` | 20/20 OK, 0 failures |
| `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility` | IDENTICAL, 15869 ticks |
| 20-level capture sweep, gate on vs off | 160 frames, 19 differ, every one inspected |
| watch menu + intro + viewmodel + ammo HUD | 20 of 20 frames byte-identical |

**Why trace-verify is not the relevant oracle here, measured rather than
asserted.** The trace harness runs headless, and `sl_gfx_frame_dl` returns
early without a window. Breakpoints on the two functions this change touches,
over a 2000-frame headless Facility run:

```
  walk                 0 hits      <- the FC classification lives here
  tex_apply            0 hits      <- the gate lives here
  sl_gfx_frame_dl    999 hits      <- called, and returns early every time
```

The zero is a real measurement, not a misplaced breakpoint: the same
`tex_apply` address is reached immediately under Xvfb with `SL_WINDOW=1`, via
`walk -> tri4 -> emit_tri -> tex_apply`. So no renderer change of this shape
can move a trace, and the campaign traces below are a formality rather than
the evidence. Keep this in mind for future src/gfx work - it is cheaper to
prove the code is unreachable than to sit through 117 traces.

The sweep is the part that matters, given B-040. Every level booted twice under
Xvfb with `mkinput.py idle`, 3000 frames, 8 shots each, compared pixel-exact.
Of 160 frames, 141 are byte-identical. The 19 that differ are:

- **statue f-00006/f-00007 (22817 px)** - the ring itself, i.e. the fix.
- **17 frames across bunker1, frigate, statue, runway, silo, bunker2, depot,
  jungle, aztec (4 to 2324 px)** - untextured room trim, brightening by a
  constant ratio: bunker1's door lintel 37 -> 68 (x1.84), frigate's pillar
  13 -> 24 (x1.85). Each is one inherited texel of ~139 no longer multiplying
  vertex colour, and each was looked at as a cropped image, not just as a
  metric.

Across the whole twenty-level sweep only THREE distinct combiners reach the
gate, and all three are the untextured family: `fcffffff fffe793c`
(SHADE/SHADE - the note's own pattern verbatim), `fcffffff fffe7838` (the
1-cycle sibling) and `fcffffff fffe7b3d` (colour SHADE, alpha ENVIRONMENT). A
fourth, `fcffffff fffdf6fb` (PRIM/PRIM), appears only on the watch path in the
session replay. Nothing else in the game draws under a texel-free combiner, so
the gate's blast radius is exactly this list.

**Characters and HUD checked as their own case, not assumed from the room
frames** - B-040 shipped a culling change verified on the intro flythrough and
destroyed every character model. On statue f-00006, which has two guards on
screen and Bond's ammo readout up: 0 changed pixels inside the guards' bounding
box, and the "7 | 93" glyphs are pixel-identical (the 399 changed pixels in
that corner are the blue arc passing behind them). Across the whole sweep no
character, viewmodel, texrect or fillrect pixel changes anywhere.

**Still open, deliberately not fixed here.** `g_tex_on` is still the only gate
on the enable side, so a list that never issues `BB` at all still inherits the
previous tile. That is now harmless because the combiner decides, but the
inheritance itself remains and is the same shape as the single global
`g_tlut_addr` (B-034 hypothesis 4). Converting both to tmem-keyed state is a
separate change.

### B-035 — health/armour ring renders greyscale; the DATA is correct

Owner, with a reference screenshot of the intended look: the left arc should run
red-orange-yellow (health) and the right arc blue (armour). Both render
greyscale.

**Measured: the game computes the right colours natively.** Breaking on
`hudMakeDamageSegments` and reading the buffer it populated:

```
call 7  isArmour= 1   seg0 r=171 g=227 b=255 a= 48   <- light blue
call 8  isArmour=-1   seg0 r=255 g=227 b= 57 a=255   <- yellow
```

That matches the reference exactly. So the vertex colours are correct IN MEMORY
and the fault is downstream, in the draw.

**Two obvious explanations are already eliminated:**

- Not the `isArmour == 0` trap. glass2.c defaults every segment to white
  (0xFF,0xFF,0xFF) and only the `> 0` / `< 0` branches tint it, so a zero flag
  would produce exactly this symptom - but all six call sites tree-wide pass
  1 or -1, and the measurement above confirms both branches run.
- Not the renderer ignoring vertex colour. `emit_tri` (sl_gfx_dl.c:2493) does
  `glColor4ub(v->r, v->g, v->b, tri_alpha(v))`.

**Leading hypothesis, and it is the only route left.** The gauge draw sets a
SHADE-ONLY combiner (`G_CC_SHADE`, bondview2.c:8617) and `buildGaugeBarDL`
(glass2.c:235) emits nothing but `gSPVertex`/`gSP2Triangles` - no `BB`, `FD` or
`F5`. `g_tex_on` (BB's enable byte) is the sole gate on 3D texturing, so
geometry that never re-issues `BB` INHERITS whatever tile the previous draw
left bound. If that inherited texture is applied as REPLACE rather than
modulated, the vertex colour is discarded and what shows is the texture - and
the textures immediately before the watch draw are the greyscale I4/I8 ones.

That fits every fact: right shape, right position, right alpha ramp, no colour.

**This cannot be confirmed headlessly** - `sl_gfx_frame_dl` returns early
without a window, so the interpreter never runs (see the note in B-034). What
would settle it: with a window up, break where the gauge geometry is emitted
and read `g_tex_on` / `g_tex_gl_on` and the bound tile. If texturing is on for
that draw, the leak is confirmed and the fix is to gate 3D texturing on the
combiner actually naming a texel, not on `BB` alone.

Also worth a look while in there: `buildGaugeBarDL`'s vertex address comes from
`OS_PHYSICAL_TO_K0(...)`, the same `| 0x80000000` construct that was wrong on
the bg path (fixed in B-032) and is still unguarded at propobj.c:8601 and 8722.
Here the ring's SHAPE is correct, so the address evidently resolves - but it is
the same latent construct and should be checked rather than assumed.

### B-034 — colour/texture symptoms: what the owner's captured logs settled

**First real renderer telemetry from a windowed session (2026-08-25).** Worth
recording that the counters are PRISTINE and prove nothing:

```
sl_tex: cached=202 decoded=202 hits=1739 uploads=0 binds=182 fail=0
        reject[dim,size,unmapped,pal,decode,fmt,tilesize,nogl]=0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0
```

Zero failures, zero rejects in every bucket. This is the file's own refrain
holding again: counters measure that commands were CONSUMED, not that they were
interpreted correctly.

**Two of my leads died on contact with the evidence. Both recorded so they are
not re-run:**

1. *"The viewmodel's tiles are CI (fmt=2) but the decoder resolved them to
   I8/I4, so the format mapping is wrong."* WRONG. `gbi_to_sl_fmt`
   (sl_gfx_dl.c:975) maps CI+siz=1 to CI8 correctly. The I4/I8 entries in the
   dump are simply different textures from the CI tiles - dump entry 04 IS
   CI8_IA16 with a real 53-entry palette. There is no mismatch.

2. *"The dumped textures show horizontal banding, so the odd-row interleave is
   not being undone."* WRONG, and the mistake was mine at the point of asking:
   the capture was requested with `SL_TEX_ROWSWAP=0`, which FORCES the swap
   off, and every dumped texture reports `dxt=0` - exactly the case B-020's
   rule says SHOULD be swapped. The banding was the forced setting, not a
   defect.

   Proven rather than assumed: undoing the interleave offline on
   `tex-00-tex.ppm` (I4 64x32, 8 texels per 32-bit word, odd rows only)
   resolves the stripes into a clean solid oval on black - a coherent sprite.
   So the dump was genuinely unswapped, AND the swap machinery is correct for
   these loads.

**Net: the captured evidence exonerates the texture path so far and the
symptoms remain unexplained.** What is still needed is a dump under the DEFAULT
rule - no `SL_TEX_ROWSWAP` in the environment at all - so the pixels can be
compared against what the player actually sees. Asking for a forced setting
first was the wrong order and cost a round trip.

Note also that `sl_tex: tile-fmt vs FD-fmt: 0 of 0 disagree` reports zero
SAMPLES, not zero disagreements - that check never ran and is not evidence.

### B-034 — four "wrong colour / weird texture" symptoms: NOT one cause, and the renderer cannot be measured headless

- **Found:** 2026-08-25, owner report against the running native build — "bullet
  and bullet tracers are weird colors", "the health bar doesn't have the proper
  colors", "the arm is present, but the textures are weird", "the hand holding
  the gun is textured weird"
- **Owner:** Phase 2 (renderer)
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` (3D draw path), `src/gfx/sl_gfx_tex.c` (CI decode)
- **Status:** OPEN — diagnosis only, no code changed. Three of the four symptoms
  are unfalsifiable under the no-window constraint; see "the capture that is
  wanted" below.

**The blocking finding, and it governs every other renderer task worded this
way.** `sl_gfx_frame_dl` (`src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c:3079`) begins
`if (!sl_gfx_active()) return;`, and `sl_gfx_active()` is false for the null
backend (`sl_gfx.c:50` — "active" means a REAL window is up). **The display-list
interpreter does not execute at all in a headless run.** No counter it keeps is
produced, no texture is decoded, no `sl_tex:`/`sl_dl:` report line is printed.
So a headless session can measure what the GAME SUBMITS, and nothing whatever
about what the RENDERER DOES with it. Every hypothesis below that concerns
`sl_gfx_dl.c` behaviour was therefore tested against the submitted command
stream only, by dumping it at `rsp.c:242` under gdb and decoding it against the
notes — the B-027 technique.

**Answer to the question asked: it is TWO causes at least, not one, and the
image-bank fix is not implicated in the arm/hand.**

The four symptoms split cleanly on a fact that is not a matter of opinion:

- The **health bar** is not textured geometry at all. `bondviewRenderGaugeBars`
  sets `gDPSetCombineMode(gdl++, G_CC_SHADE, G_CC_SHADE)` (`bondview2.c:8617`)
  and `buildGaugeBarDL` (`glass2.c:235`) emits nothing but `gSPVertex` and
  `gSP2Triangles`. It carries no `BB`, no `FD`, no `F5` of its own. A texture
  DECODE defect cannot reach it. The only way it goes wrong in this renderer is
  the texture-enable leak: `g_tex_on` — the `BB` enable byte — is the sole gate
  on 3D texturing (`sl_gfx_dl.c:1539-1548`), so geometry that declines to
  re-issue `BB` inherits whatever tile the preceding draw left bound and gets
  modulated by it.
- The **arm and hand** are textured geometry, and the measurement below says
  what is distinctive about them.
- The **tracers** go through `texSelect(&gdl, flareimage5, ...)` /
  `texSelect(&gdl, image, ...)` (`gunfire.c:1440`, `:1447`) — i.e. **global
  image-bank declarations**, the same records [[B-027]] repaired. These are the
  one symptom of the four that is genuinely downstream of today's
  `image_bank.c` change, and they share the crosshair's path.

**The one measured discriminator for the arm/hand.** Frame dumped at
invocation 2511 of a Facility gameplay run (`SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34`,
`facility-fire.input`), walked with segment resolution and per-list word-order
sniffing, and split at the gdl pointer `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels`
(`gunfire.c:1495`) was writing at:

| region | `F0` loadTLUT | `F5` settile | render-tile formats |
|---|---|---|---|
| viewmodel | **56** | 212 | fmt=2 (CI) x18 — *every one* |
| rest of frame | **0** | 37 | fmt=2 x1, fmt=3 (IA) x4, fmt=4 (I) x2 |

The first-person viewmodel is essentially **100% paletted CI geometry with
6-level mip chains**, and it is the only thing in the frame loading palettes.
The world is mostly IA/I. That is exactly the shape of "the world looks right,
the arm and hand do not", and it points the arm/hand at the **CI + TLUT decode
path**, not at the combiner and not at the image bank.

**Four hypotheses REFUTED, each by measurement, so nobody re-runs them.**

1. *"`BB` stays on with level 0, so untextured geometry gets textured."* The
   note "Texture application (Rooms).txt" does say `BB000001` (on, level 0) is
   how ROOM binaries spell untextured. It does not hold for runtime lists:
   across every frame walked, **0 triangles** were drawn under a combiner naming
   no texel, and the `BB.on=1 level=0` triangles carry `FC121824 FF33FFFF` =
   `(TEXEL0-0)*SHADE+0`. Level is not a texture gate here.
2. *"The 3D path ignores the combiner, so PRIM/ENV are lost."* The structural
   half is TRUE and worth knowing: `rect_colour()` is the only consumer of the
   combiner classification and is called from exactly two sites, `draw_texrect`
   (`:2307`) and `draw_fillrect` (`:2364`) — both 2D. `emit_tri` never consults
   it; 3D fragment colour is always `glColor4ub(v->r, v->g, v->b, tri_alpha(v))`
   (`:2490`) under `GL_MODULATE`. But it does not explain the arm/hand: the
   viewmodel's actual combiner is `FC26A004 1F1093FF`
   (`G_CC_TRILERP` / `G_CC_MODULATEIA2`), whose cycle 1 is
   `(COMBINED-0)*SHADE+0` — which `TEXEL0 x SHADE` reproduces. The only
   combiner in a Facility frame that the interpreter genuinely mis-draws is
   `FC159804 5FFEDBF8` = `(TEXEL0-ENV)*SHADE_A+ENV`, and a `bt` at
   `modelApplyRenderModeType3` shows it arriving via
   `chrRenderProp` -> `chrpropRender` -> `chrpropsRenderPass`: **guard models,
   not Bond's arm**. (Beware the `+1` offsets in that dispatch —
   `PROP_TYPE_VIEWER+1` is 7 and `PROP_TYPE_CHR+1` is 4 == `PROP_TYPE_WEAPON`.
   Measured: 16096 calls with PropType 4, 3904 with 7, over 20000.)
3. *"`C0` image recall is unhandled."* It is unhandled — there is no
   `case 0xC0` in `sl_gfx_dl.c`, only the `op_in_ucode05` classification at
   `:223`. Irrelevant: an opcode histogram over the whole recursed frame finds
   **zero** `C0` commands. The game expands image recalls into real
   `FD`/`F5`/`F3`/`F0` before submission.
4. *"The palette is mispaired the way [[B-023]] showed the image was."* No. The
   ordered dump shows each viewmodel texture is self-contained and never
   batched: `FD` -> `F5(7)` -> `F3 loadblock` -> `F5(7)` -> `F0 loadTLUT` ->
   `F5/F2` for tiles 0..5 -> triangles. "Most recent `F0`" is the correct
   palette here, so the single global `g_tlut_addr` (`:1527`) is not wrong in
   this stream — though it remains the same *shape* B-023 punished and is worth
   converting to a tmem-keyed lookup on general principle.

Also checked and NOT a clean discriminator: the odd-row swizzle. `dxt == 0`
selects `SL_TEX_FLAG_ROWSWAPPED` (`rowswap_flag`, `:1362`), and the viewmodel's
56 loadblocks are all `dxt=0` — but so are 8 of the world's 10, so the swizzle
path is not exercised by the arm/hand alone. (The notes are silent on the
swizzle; that is already a `not_covered` entry and was not re-searched.)

**Why symptoms 1 and 2 could not be measured at all.** Neither path executes in
headless Facility replay. Breakpoints on `bondviewRenderGaugeBars`
(`bondview2.c:8581`) and on the tracer emit at `gunfire.c:1427` — both verified
by `info line` to resolve to real addresses inside their functions, not comment
blocks — recorded **0 hits over 12000 frames**, at both `SL_TOUGH=1000` and
`SL_TOUGH=0.5`, while `modelApplyRenderModeType3` in the same runs took 58801
and 67801. Bond never takes damage, so the gauge never draws;
`weaponRenderTracers` draws only for characters OTHER than the player
(`propobj.c:6565`), and no guard fires.

**The capture that is wanted** (do not guess at these — three separate things,
and only the third is a window):

1. An **input stream that reaches the HUD gauge bars and the tracers**: Bond
   takes damage, and a guard returns fire. `facility-fire` and `facility-pause`
   both fail to. This is a headless artefact — a `mkinput.py` routine — not a
   screenshot, and it unblocks symptoms 1 and 2 entirely.
2. The `sl_tex:` and `sl_dl:` **stderr report block** from a Facility gameplay
   frame with a window up (they are unreachable otherwise, per the blocking
   finding above) — specifically `reject[...]`, `src-entropy`, the stride
   cross-check and the per-image roughness lines.
3. `SL_TEX_DUMP` output for the viewmodel's CI8 images from that same frame,
   captured **twice** — once with `SL_TEX_ROWSWAP=0` and once with `=1`. That
   knob exists precisely because the notes cannot settle the swizzle, and the
   arm/hand are now the geometry that most depends on it.

**Verification of this entry.** No code changed, so no build was required;
`tools/native/build.sh` and `make matching` were not run and nothing in the
working tree affects either. Every claim above is either a gdb measurement on
`build/native/skeleton` (frame dumps at `rsp.c:242`, breakpoint hit counts,
`bt`, opcode/format histograms) or a tree-wide grep, and the greps that came
back empty are named inline: no `case 0xC0` in `sl_gfx_dl.c`; no `C0` opcode in
any walked frame; no `rect_colour` call from `emit_tri`.

### B-036 — subcalcmatrices SIGSEGV on a garbage `anim2`: what is ruled out by measurement, and the one path never exercised

- **Found:**  2026-08-25, investigating the owner's captured SIGSEGV (`/tmp/run4.log`) after moving into facility's second section
- **Owner:**  Phase 1 — it is a crash, so it is not deferrable; this entry records an
  investigation that did not land, so the next attempt does not redo it
- **Where:** `src/game/model.c:2336`, reached from `src/game/chr.c:2572` (`chrTick` → `subcalcmatrices`)
- **Blocks:** playing facility past the first section on the native build

**NOT ROOT-CAUSED. Not reproduced.** Everything below is a measurement or a
tree-wide grep. No fix was written and none is claimed.

#### What the fault actually is

`objdump -d -l` on `subcalcmatrices` shows line 2336 compiles to

```
mov    0x54(%eax),%eax        # anim2
movzwl 0x4(%eax),%eax         # anim2->unk04   <-- faults
```

so `anim2 == 0x4a312654` and the reported `addr=0x4a312658` is that plus 4.
This was checked against the disassembly rather than trusted from the line
attribution. `LEFTOVERDEBUG` **is** defined for the native build
(`tools/native/build.sh:25`), so 2336 is live code, not a disabled block.

#### `anim2` cannot arrive garbage by assignment — so this is a stray write

Tree-wide `grep -rn "\->anim *=" src/` returns exactly three hits: `model.c:2560`
(inside `modelSetAnimation2`, the only non-init writer), `model.c:6264`
(`animInit`, NULL), and `propobj.c:5751` (a comparison, not a write). `anim2`
itself is only ever set from `model->anim` (`model.c:2503`) or to NULL
(2531/3331/6265). Both `modelSetAnimation` and `modelSetAnimation2` call
`sl_anim_header_swap`, which `exit(2)`s on a pointer outside the animation
table — so a bad pointer arriving by assignment would produce a clean exit with
a message, not a SIGSEGV. A non-NULL out-of-table `anim2` is therefore a stray
write into `Model+0x54`, not a bad assignment.

#### The animation table is NOT the cause — audited clean

Authority: `Actor-Specific Data and Animations/Animation/7F000A00 - expand
animation table entries.txt` (and its caller `7F000AAC - allocate, load, and
expand animation tables.txt`), now added to `docs/doc-routing.json` under
`models-animation`, which did not list them.

The native build agrees with the note on every point. Linker symbols match it
exactly: `_animation_entriesSegmentRomStart = 0x00124AC0`,
`_animation_dataSegmentRomStart = 0x0028E980`. One correction to a naive
reading: `ADDIU T6,T6,E7E0` sign-extends, so the allocation is
`0x10000 - 0x1820 = 0xE7E0`, not `0x1E7E0`; `_animation_dataSegmentEnd -
_animation_dataSegmentStart` measures `0xE7E0`.

The three hazards a relocation pass invites are all absent, each ruled out by
measurement rather than by reading source:

1. **Unswapped offsets.** The entry offsets are compile-time constants in
   `assets/animationtable_data.h`, not ROM bytes. The `+0x08`/`+0x10` fields
   that *do* come from ROM are swapped by `sl_anim_header_swap`
   (`initanitable.c:247`) **before** the base is added.
2. **Sentinel misread.** The 13 value-`1` sentinels and the `0` terminator are
   literal C constants; no byte order is involved.
3. **Double relocation.** Parsing both tables finds 173 relocatable entries and
   **0** duplicate non-sentinel offsets, so no entry is relocated twice.

End state, dumped under gdb after expansion completes: all **173** entries have
entry pointer, `bitDescriptors` (+0x08) and `bitStream` (+0x10) inside
`[base, base+0xE7E0)`, `address` a plausible ROM offset, and a sane frame
count — **0 problems**.

#### Also ruled out, by measurement

- **`dynAllocate` arena overrun reaching the model slots.** Measured layout:
  vtx pool `[0xf5c2aa80, 0xf5c43a80)`, `g_AnimModelSlots` at `0xf5d34250` —
  about 1 MB past the end of the pool. Peak use across the recorded facility
  playthrough is 19616 of 51200 bytes. Forcing every chr through the render
  branch pushes it to 108064 (a 2x overrun) and still neither corrupts `anim2`
  nor crashes.
- **`RwDataIndex` byte-swap gap.** `modelGetNodeRwData` reads `RwDataIndex` for
  exactly 9 node types; `sl_model_rodata_swap` swaps exactly those 9.
  `grep -rn RwDataIndex src/ --include=*.h` finds 9 fields — no gap.
- **`ModelFileHeader` scalars** (`numMatrices`/`numRecords`/`numSwitches`).
  These are compiled-in C data (`chrobjdata`), not ROM bytes, so no swap is
  owed; `sl_model_head_swap` correctly swaps only the file-backed
  `Switches[]`/`Textures[]`. Measured `numMatrices = 4` on a live facility chr.
- **Struct aliasing.** `sizeof(Model) == sizeof(struct AnimModelSlot) == 188`,
  `anim` at `0x20`, `anim2` at `0x54`; the slot stride cannot alias `anim2`.

#### Not reproduced

`tools/trace/inputs/facility.input` (15869 reads) runs 17000 frames clean, as
do the other recorded levels tried. A per-tick scan of every animated model
slot for an out-of-table `anim`/`anim2` fired **zero** times.

#### The one path never exercised — and the recommended next step

The owner's crash run was **windowed**; every run above was headless. Headless,
`sl_gfx_select()` returns the null backend, so `sl_gfx_dl.c:3084` returns before
the GL display-list walker runs at all, RSP task dispatch is gated
(`if (sl_gfx_active()) sl_gfx_task(task)`, `sl_ultra_shim.c:363`), and audio
defaults off. The entire GL walk/texture path that fills the owner's log
(`sl_dl:`/`sl_tex:`/`sl_walk:`/`sl_2d:` lines) appears in **no** headless run.

That gap is not safe to wave away: forcing audio on headless
(`SL_AUDIO=1`) raised the arena peak from 19616 to 31136, so these gated
subsystems do change sim behaviour. And `sl_gfx_dl_swap`
(`src/native/sl_swap_model.c:360`) rewrites display lists **in place** — a
write path, of exactly the shape this bug needs.

Next step is to run the owner's configuration on a **virtual** display rather
than a real one. The Makefile already does this for trace capture
(`XVFB := xvfb-run -a --server-args=-screen 0 640x480x24`, Makefile:462, with
hashes verified identical either way), so nothing appears on the owner's
screen. This was not attempted here because the brief for this task said
headless only; it needs an explicit go-ahead.

#### Worth knowing before the next attempt

`return_null()` (`model.c:244`) is an **empty function**. Every `LEFTOVERDEBUG`
bounds check in `subcalcmatrices` therefore prints and falls through rather
than returning — including the one at 2336. That is Rare's code and must stay
(non-negotiable 5), but it means those guards protect nothing: had the check at
2336 passed, `loadAnimationFrame(arg1->anim2, ...)` would have faulted on the
same pointer moments later.

#### Instrumentation used (written, used, then reverted — recreate if needed)

All three were `#ifndef __sgi` and default-off, and all were removed so the
tree is clean; `sl_dyn_check` in particular should not be left in a hot path.

1. `sl_model_audit(slots, count, stride)` in the shim, called from `propsTick`:
   scans every animated model slot each tick for an `anim`/`anim2` outside
   `[sl_anim_base, sl_anim_limit)` and hexdumps the offending `Model`.
2. `sl_dyn_check(who, size)` in the shim, called from all four `dyn.c` bump
   allocators: reports the arena high-water mark and any overrun past
   `g_VtxBuffers[active+1]`.
3. `sl_force_visible()` forcing `headSwitchVisible = 1` at `chr.c:2524`, to put
   every chr in the level through `subcalcmatrices` instead of only the ones the
   recording happened to look at.

### B-044 — watch equipment list briefly duplicates the LAST item

Owner-reported, with the trigger narrowed by them:

- It happens ONLY when moving off **unarmed** onto the FIRST item in the list.
- The list momentarily shows several copies of the SAME item - and it is the
  LAST item in the list (the detonator), not the one being selected.
- It settles to the correct contents a moment later.

**That shape is diagnostic and worth stating before anyone starts.** "Every
slot holds the last value written" is what a list-building loop produces when
it runs before its per-slot source is populated, or with a count that is stale
on the first pass - each iteration writes the same value, and the value that
survives is whichever the loop touched last. That it CORRECTS ITSELF a moment
later says the data is fine and the first pass is early: a one-frame ordering
problem, not corrupt inventory.

Because it settles, this is cosmetic and low-risk, but it is a genuine
first-pass-ordering defect and may share a cause with anything else that
populates a list from inventory.

Where to start: the watch menu's inventory page build - `mp_watch_menu_display`
and the solo watch equivalent (`trigger_solo_watch_menu`) - and specifically
whatever supplies the per-slot item id on the transition out of unarmed. Check
whether the count and the item array are read in the same pass, and whether the
unarmed state leaves an index at a sentinel the first iteration does not expect.

---

#### ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED, 2026-08-26. It is not a list-build fault at all.

**The framing above is wrong, and worth leaving in place as the record of a
plausible reading that measurement refuted.** The list-building loop is
innocent; so is the inventory; so is `mp_watch_menu_display`, which is the
MULTIPLAYER scoreboard and returns immediately when `getPlayerCount() == 1`.
The duplication is one layer below the game entirely - it is the native
renderer drawing a command the RDP would have drawn nothing for.

**Root cause.** `textRenderGlyph` (`src/game/textrelated.c:329`, the branch
that handles a glyph straddling the BOTTOM edge of a text clip box) emits

```c
gSPTextureRectangle(gdl++,
    /* xl */ ((*x * 4) + text_x),
    /* yl */ ((drawY + curchar->baseline) * 4) + text_y,
    /* xh */ ((*x + curchar->width) * 4) + text_x,
    /* yh */ clipY + clipHeight + text_y,        /* <- no * 4 */
    ...);
```

Every other coordinate in the command is 10.2 fixed point; this one is not.
So `lry` arrives as ~200 against a `uly` of ~776 - an INVERTED rectangle. The
RDP rasterises spans from `uly` down to `lry`, so an inverted rectangle yields
zero spans and draws nothing; on the cartridge the command is invisible. This
is Rare's own arithmetic and `make matching` is byte-identical, so the console
issues exactly the same command. **Rule 5 applies: it is not ours to fix.**

`draw_texrect` (`src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c:2735`) was normalising the corners with
min/max before drawing. That is right for resolving WHICH word holds which
corner, and wrong as a response to an inverted one: it turned the command into
a large VALID rectangle - 144 pixels tall - and with `dtdy = 1024` over a ~10px
glyph the texture tiled about fourteen times down it. The repeated word is the
list's bottom line because the bottom line is the one that clips, and the
bottom line is DETONATOR because the detonator sorts last. Every element of the
owner's report falls out of that one command.

**The fix** is in the renderer, not the game: reject a texrect whose Y ordering
disagrees with its X ordering, which is what an inverted rectangle is.
`SL_TR_INVERT=1` restores the old swap-and-draw for A/B capture, and the
per-frame `sl_2d: texrect ... inverted=N` counter reports how often it fires.
Which word holds which corner is derived per command from the X axis rather
than assumed: `gbi.h:4602` (the plain-F3D branch this build compiles) packs
`xh`/`yh` into `w0`, matching the 225-of-225 measurement already on record and
contradicting `ucode05.txt`'s E4 labelling, and a tree-wide
`grep -rn gSPTextureRectangle src/` finds 19 call sites in 7 files outside
`src/gfx` (debugmenu, spectrum, textrelated, title2, radar, blood_animation,
bondwalk2) with no inverted X among them - `bondwalk2.c:43` is the only caller
that clips at all and it CLAMPS `xl`/`yl` to 0, the correct way to do what
`textRenderGlyph` gets wrong.

**Reproducing it.** `tools/trace/mkinput.py watch` (added here) raises the
watch, steps RIGHT onto the equipment page and scrolls the list down. Facility
gives the owner's exact inventory with no gdb and no scripted pickups -
`unarmed | pp7 (silenced) | remote mine | detonator`, four items, detonator
last:

```
xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 640x480x24" env SL_ROM=baserom.u.z64 \
  SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34 SL_WINDOW=1 SL_INPUT=<stream> SL_FRAMES=2560 \
  SL_SHOT=/tmp/x/f SL_SHOT_EVERY=1 SL_SHOT_FIRST=2478 SL_SHOT_LAST=2560 \
  ./build/native/skeleton
```

`SL_SHOT_FIRST`/`SL_SHOT_LAST` are new (`src/gfx/sl_gfx_sdl.c`) and were the
thing that made the capture affordable: the artefact lasts two frames out of
2500, and `SL_SHOT_EVERY=1` from frame 0 writes about 2.3 GB to reach it. The
window is keyed to `sl_frames_completed()`, the same VI counter every other log
line in the build is stamped with, so a window read off an instrumentation log
lands where it was meant to.

**Timing in that stream is measured, not guessed, and getting it wrong is
silent.** `watch_screen0_navigation` (`options.c:688`) only acts while the
watch is fully open, so a RIGHT pressed during the open animation is swallowed
and the run sits on the mission-status page forever. The first attempt did
exactly that for 6000 frames and produced zero equipment-page draws.
`bondviewProcessInput` is called once per TWO controller reads, and the watch
reaches `WATCH_ANIMATION_0x5` about 140 calls after the START edge; the stream
presses RIGHT 350 reads after START.

#### What was measured

| measurement | result |
|---|---|
| list string, every drawn frame (instrumented `strcat` loop, `options.c:2341`) | `unarmed\|pp7 (silenced)\|remote mine\|detonator` on all 1185 frames - **never** duplicated |
| `textRender` calls per frame during the artefact | 2, then 1 - neither carries repeated text; the selected-name render is suppressed while `watch_inventory_text_is_settled == 0` |
| inverted texrects, whole run | 45, exactly 9 per frame (the nine letters of DETONATOR), on exactly 5 frames: vi 2485/2487/2489 (page open) and vi 2533/2535 (the move off unarmed) |
| their geometry | `w0 y=200`, `w1 y=776` every time -> swapped to y[50.0, 194.2], 144px tall, `dtdy=1024` |
| captured frames, invert-on vs invert-off, vi 2478-2560 | 5 of 41 differ - the same 5 frames, and no others |

Before and after at vi 2535: a column of DETONATOR repeated up the screen over
the correct list, versus the correct list alone with the highlight moving from
UNARMED to PP7 (SILENCED). (Frames are ROM-derived pixels and stay out of the
repo per rule 2.)

**The owner sees it only on the move off unarmed, but it also fires on the
page opening** (vi 2485-2489, the initial scroll settle). Same command, same
cause; the opening one is shorter and lands while the page is still zooming in,
which is presumably why it went unreported.

#### Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| artefact frames, before/after | 5 of 41 differ, all 5 the frames carrying inverted texrects |
| `make matching` | **MATCH!**, EXIT=0 |
| `make bootsweep` | 20/20 OK, 0 failures |
| `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility` | **IDENTICAL**, 15869 ticks, schema v13 |
| blast radius: 6 levels x 15 gameplay frames, invert-on vs invert-off | dam/facility/surface/statue/archives/streets - **0 of 90** frames differ |

`src/game/` is untouched, so `make matching` and `trace-verify` could not have
moved; both were run anyway rather than argued from.

#### Fed back into the notes

`docs/doc-routing.json` gains two areas and a fourth correction to
`ucode05.txt`:

- **`watch-menu`** governs `src/game/options.c`. `solo watch menu.txt` walks
  the stage-load initialiser and names the whole `0x800409xx` state block, and
  it agrees with `build/u/ge007.u.map` symbol for symbol - `watch_screen_index`
  `0x80040994`, `watch_inventory_text_y` `0x800409b0`, `..._target_y`
  `0x800409b4`, `g_curWatchItemIndex` `0x800409b8`, `..._cursor_pos`
  `0x800409bc`, `..._is_settled` `0x800409c0`. `watch equipment.txt` carries
  the per-item watch placement floats the `bondinvGet*ForIndex` helpers read.
- **`mp-ingame-menu`** governs `src/game/mpmenu.c`, with the note that a task
  about the equipment page must not start there.
- **display-lists**: an inverted texrect draws NOTHING. The corner-labelling
  correction was already recorded; what follows from it was not.

### B-045 — gas does not fill the room correctly after the facility tank explosion

Owner-reported: blowing the gas tanks at the end of facility should fill the
room with gas, and it does not look right - described as the volume not
behaving.

**Framing note before anyone starts, so the search does not go somewhere that
never existed.** The N64 has no volumetric rendering. Whatever this effect is,
it is built from ordinary primitives - almost certainly layered sprites or
particles, and/or the RDP's fog. So the question is never "why is the volume
wrong" but "which primitives are missing, mispositioned, or mis-blended". The
same applies to the owner's wording in any similar report.

**Likely related to the explosion defect in the 2D/greyscale cluster** - the
gas and the explosion plausibly come from the same particle/sprite machinery
(see `explosionCreateBulletImpact` and neighbours in src/game/explosion.c, and
`g_ExplosionRenderPartDefaultVertex` / `g_SmokeRenderPartDefaultVertex` at
explosion.c:215-218). If that cluster's cause turns out to be shared, check
this before treating it as separate work.

#### The cause: the gas is FOG. There are no gas sprites anywhere. 2026-08-26

The framing note above was right that this is not a volume, and the leading
hypothesis handed to the investigation - a billboard, because a flat layer
that slides with the camera is what a camera-facing quad looks like - was
**wrong, and measured wrong rather than argued wrong**.

Releasing the tanks calls `init_trigger_toxic_gas_effect` (`propobj.c:14121`).
That makes `handle_gas_damage` (`propobj.c:14154`) call
`fogSwitchToSolosky2(t)` every tick, which lerps the level's environment
record toward its ALT row (`bgfog.c:511`). For facility the two rows are
(`bgfog.c:131-132`):

| row | znear | zfar | sky R,G,B |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LEVELID_FACILITY` | 10 | 5000 | 10,20,10 |
| `LEVELID_FACILITY + ENVIRONMENTDATA_ALT` | 10 | **1000** | **40,80,40** |

So the entire visual is three things: the fog colour becomes green, the
backdrop fill becomes the same green (`sky.c:326` fills the viewport with the
environment colour when the level has no clouds), and the far clip plane comes
in from 5000 to 1000 - `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` passes both to
`viSetZRange` (`bgfog.c:301`), which reaches `guPerspectiveF` at `fr.c:709`.
**Fog is what hides that clip**: geometry reaches full fog colour exactly
where it is cut off.

`grep -rn -i "gas" src/game/*.c src/game/*.h` over the whole tree finds the
timer, the damage, the sound and the AI opcodes (`AI_GasLeakAndFadeFog`,
`chrai.c:4492`) and **no renderer path of any kind** - no sprite, no particle,
no billboard, no quad.

#### What the renderer does with that: nothing. Measured.

`src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` had no fog stage. It stored the `F8 setfogcolour`
register and never read it; `G_MW_FOG` fell through the `OP_MOVEWORD` case,
which handled only `MW_SEGMENT`; and `rm_apply` reads only the blender cycle
that reaches memory, which in 2-cycle mode is the SECOND - while GoldenEye
puts its fog blend in the FIRST (`bg.c:2105-2143` `G_RM_FOG_SHADE_A`,
`model.c:3527` `G_RM_FOG_PRIM_A`). Its own comment said so: "Fog alpha is not
modelled - there is no fog stage here yet".

Measured live on the gassed room, with the `SL_FOG_DBG` probe added in this
task (kept in the file):

```
sl_fog: f301 fill=428442 fogcol=408040ff fm=12800 fo=-12544 cmds=5
        proj[10,11,14,15]=0.9463,0.9276,102.7,120.4682
        fog-geom=1391 clr-fog=2431 a_shade=1391 a_fog=1040
```

- `fogcol=408040ff` is the ALT row's 40,80,40 byte for byte.
- `fm=12800 fo=-12544` is `gSPFogPosition(990, 1000)` exactly
  (`128000/10` and `(500-990)*256/10`, `gbi.h:2777`).
- **1391 room triangles a frame asked for fog and got none**, plus 1040 model
  triangles on the constant-alpha path.
- The projection confirms the clip: solving the measured matrix, `z_ndc = 1`
  is at distance **1002** during the gas and **5026** before it.

So the flat green layer is a **hard far-plane clip against the green backdrop
fill**, with the fade that should have hidden it entirely absent. That is the
owner's report term for term, and it is a missing primitive, not a wrong
volume. Captured before/after: `scratchpad/gas/ab3.png`.

#### The fog band is narrow, which is why nobody had noticed

`min=990 max=1000` fogs only the last 1% of the DEPTH BUFFER, but that buffer
is 1/w, so it is not the last 1% of the world. Solving the measured facility
matrix, the ramp runs **836 to 4927 units** in normal play and **502 to 1000**
during the gas. Normal facility rooms are mostly inside 836 units, and the
normal fog colour is 16,32,16 - near black - so the missing stage was nearly
invisible until the gas turned it green and pulled the plane in.

#### Status: DIAGNOSED. The fix is written, DEFAULT OFF, and NOT verified.

`fog_mode`/`fog_apply`/`fog_coord` in `sl_gfx_dl.c` implement the stage with
GL's fixed-function fog and an explicit per-vertex fog coordinate - under
`GL_LINEAR` with start 0 and end 1 the factor is `1 - coord`, so handing it
the RSP's own value reproduces `(CLR_FOG, A, CLR_IN, 1MA)` term for term.

**It is behind `SL_FOG` and defaults OFF, and it must stay that way until the
verification below is done.** Two separate claims are involved and only the
first has evidence:

1. Fog is what the gas is made of - **established**, above.
2. This fog implementation is safe as a global default - **NOT established**.

The owner built the working tree while (2) was still unverified and played
facility. The gas itself read correctly - "when i blew up the tanks at the
end, it seems like it was more volumetric like the rest of the explosions" -
and the global change did not: "big regression. most textures and such are
flickering and I see random textures go black and i see geometry floating in
the air." Reproduced here on a `surface` capture: the bunker's detail is
replaced by a flat pale wash, a pale wedge appears across the snow that is
absent with fog off, and distant terrain shows flat patches with hard polygon
edges. Mean luma barely moves (0.2269 to 0.2271) because detail is being
REPLACED by flat fog colour, not uniformly darkened.

**The process error is worth recording, because the reasoning was already on
the page.** The A_FOG/model path was gated off with an explicit blast-radius
argument citing B-040 by name. The A_SHADE/room path, which is *wider* - 1391
triangles a frame against 1040, on all geometry on all levels - was given the
opposite default in the same edit. An unverified global renderer change
defaults off; the narrower path being gated while the wider one shipped is the
inversion to look for.

Status of the three defects after a second measurement pass:

- **Flicker - NOT the batch breaks. Disproven.** The hypothesis was that
  `fog_apply`/`fog_off` cut the batch on every transition. Counted per frame,
  the fog stage causes **3 enables, 2 disables and 3 colour changes** against
  1391 fogged triangles, because rooms draw contiguously and the transitions
  land on pass boundaries, not on triangles. Even with the model path forced
  on (`SL_FOG_PRIM=1`) it is 1 enable and 8-13 colour changes. Rewriting fog
  as a never-breaking per-vertex attribute would save under a dozen state
  changes a frame and is not worth the risk. Fog also adds **no temporal
  instability**: consecutive-frame mean RMSE over a 25-frame window is
  **0.00116 with fog off and 0.00116 with fog on**, while all 25 frames differ
  between the two - so fog changes the image without making it less stable.
  **Flicker remains unexplained**, and it is deliberately NOT closed. Note
  that a deterministic replay cannot show a pacing-induced flicker at all, so
  absence here is weak evidence.

- **Black surfaces - resolved, and moot on the delivered tree.** Confirmed on
  the gassed facility frame with defaults: black pixels go **34304 (fog off)
  -> 33783 (fog on)**, i.e. the room fog *reduces* black rather than creating
  it, and the frame measures `const=0` with an empty `A_FOG alphas:` list. The
  black came from the ungated A_FOG path, where `model.c` sets per-model fog
  colours that are BLACK at high alpha (its own worked examples show
  `SetFogColor(0,0,0,38)`) - measured alphas on that frame were
  `00 x2352, 39 x192, c1 x192, d3 x192, fe x192`, and `0xfe` paints a prop
  essentially solid. The owner's build predates the `SL_FOG_PRIM` gating.

- **Floating geometry - the sighting is RETRACTED.** The only observation was
  a "pale wedge across the snow" on a `surface` A/B, and that A/B was one of
  the contended direct-boot runs (see the retraction above). Re-taken cleanly
  on the replay path, `surface` shows 20906 changed pixels of which just 37 go
  dark->bright, and those are near-black fragments lifted toward a pale fog
  colour rather than new geometry. Structurally fog cannot add geometry - it
  recolours fragments that already rasterised. No floating geometry has been
  reproduced on the delivered tree. Still worth the owner re-checking, since
  their report was from live play.

#### The far plane is faithful to Rare - do not "fix" it (rule 5)

The gas legitimately pulls the far clip plane to 1000 while the bottling room
is deeper than that, so hardware clipped it too. The question was whether fog
is meant to hide the cut. **It is, and by construction.** `gSPFogPosition`'s
`max` is 1000 = the far plane, so full fog opacity coincides with the clip.
Solving the measured gassed projection: fog reaches 255 at **998 units** and
the far plane sits at **1002** - a 0.4% gap. And the two colours agree:
fully-fogged surfaces land on `(40,79,40)`, the backdrop fill on `(41,82,41)`,
a 3/255 step that is not visible.

So the large flat green expanse is **not a defect and not ours to remove**.
Measured on the gassed frame, the backdrop occupies **158906 pixels in BOTH
the fog-off and fog-on captures** - identical populations, because fog cannot
fill a region that has no geometry in it. That expanse is Rare's design: the
gas reduces the visible world to 1000 units and paints everything beyond it
green. The N64 showed the same thing.

**This means implementing fog does NOT, by itself, resolve the owner's
reported symptom.** On the gassed facility frame fog changes only **4291 of
307200 pixels (1.4%)**, confined to the receding floor at y 298-430. What fog
removes is the hard high-contrast EDGE where lit near geometry met the green
void; the void itself stays.

#### The remaining defect: the factor saturates

Consistent across two levels, on clean replay captures, one binary, only
`SL_FOG` differing:

| level | pixels changed | share landing on ONE colour |
|---|---|---|
| facility, gassed | 4291 of 307200 (1.4%) | 4126 = **96%** on `(40,79,40)` |
| surface | 20906 of 307200 (6.8%) | 13133 = **63%** on `(96,96,128)` |

A haze should produce a broad distribution; this pins most of what it touches
to full fog. The per-vertex histogram is NOT the cause - on a normal facility
frame it is `1076,102,450,505,313,477,536,49,0,0`, spread across buckets 1-7
with nothing saturating, and `fm`/`fo` are the game's own values. So the
saturation appears between the vertex value and the pixel. Unexplained. This
is the one defect that should block the default flip, and it is the mechanism
behind the owner's "textures go black / flat" report.

#### Recommendation: DO NOT flip the default yet

`SL_FOG` should stay off until the saturation above is explained. The evidence
for flipping is otherwise favourable - the delivered default is inert (18/18),
the gates all pass, flicker is not the batch breaks, the black surfaces were
the gated model path, and the floating geometry does not reproduce - but the
B-048 standard is not met while 63-96% of affected pixels pin to one colour,
because that is precisely what the owner complained about. Fog is also worth
less than expected on the reported scene (1.4%), so there is no urgency.

The A_FOG path (`SL_FOG_PRIM`) is a separate question - a per-object distance
shade on every character and prop, not the gas - and stays off regardless.

#### The oracle: the RSP's fog value, read off the cartridge. 2026-08-27

The saturation above was the one defect blocking the default flip, and every
account of it so far had been reasoned rather than measured. This is the
measurement. **The cartridge over-fogs nothing; we over-fog everything, and
the cause is a unit.**

**Method — no RDP dump, no LLE, no plugin.** The RDP's fog blender is
`out = FOGCOLOUR*a + PIXEL*(1-a)`, and `a` is the shade alpha the RSP computed
during vertex transform. FOGCOLOUR is ours to choose: it is
`g_CurrentEnvironment.Red/Green/Blue`, re-lerped every frame from `fog_tables`
(`0x80044E10`, 48 records of `0x5C`, `Sky.Red` at `+0x28`). Pin every row's
sky colour to `0x00`, render the frame, pin it to `0xF8`, render again, and

    B - A = 0xF8 * a        per channel, three independent estimates

so `a` falls out of two framebuffers with no model of the formula at all. The
tool is `scratchpad/fog/abfog.py`, built on `romshot.py`'s capture path and
`emu_libretro`'s RDRAM pointer; RGB is pinned in `on_tick` every frame because
the gas lerp rewrites it every frame.

**Instrument validation, before believing anything it says.** On frame 11000
of `facility-gas`: **0 of 153600 pixels fall outside `0 <= B-A <= 0xF8`**, so
the blend model holds exactly and both runs rendered the same scene;
`scaledfar` reads `2341.1111` in the control run and in both poked runs, frame
for frame, so the poke did not move the replay. The resulting alpha image is a
clean depth map - crates, the walkway, and two guard silhouettes all resolve -
which is not something a broken probe produces.

**ROM, gassed facility, frame 11000** (env `40,88,40`, near 10, far 2341.1111,
`gSPFogPosition(990,1000)` -> `fm=12800 fo=-12544`), down the receding
bottling-room floor at screen column x=200, 640x240:

| screen y | ROM shade alpha | implied NDC z |
|---|---|---|
| >= 161 | **0** | <= 0.980 |
| 160 | **8** | 0.98064 |
| 152 | **49** | 0.98386 |
| 144 | **66** | 0.98514 |
| 140 | **96** | 0.98750 |
| 136 | **129** | 0.99007 |
| 130 | **167** | 0.99307 |
| 124 | **217** | 0.99692 |
| 120 | **239** | 0.99863 |

39.4% of the frame (60512 px) is at alpha exactly 0. This is the broad ramp
the cartridge draws and that our 96%-on-one-colour does not.

**What the per-pixel value actually is.** Poking `gSPFogPosition`'s min from
990 to 900 - which touches `fm`/`fo` only, not the projection and not AI
visibility, confirmed by the scene coming back **26596 pixels identical, 8
differing** - should leave `alpha_990 = 10*alpha_900 - 2304` true pixel by
pixel, since both are affine in the same variable. It fails, median error
**36.4/255**. The reason is that the RSP **clamps per vertex** and the RDP
then interpolates the already-clamped shade alpha **linearly in screen
space**; at min=990 nearly every vertex clamps to 0 first. Anyone modelling
the ROM's per-pixel alpha as `clamp(fm*z(pixel)+fo)` will get a wrong answer,
and two of this task's own intermediate results were wrong that way.

#### The variable is the NDC z that runs -1..1. We feed it 0..1.

`gbi.h:2760` says "alpha(fog) = (eyespace z) * fm + fo CLAMPED 0 to 255 ...
note: (eyespace z) ranges -1 to 1". `sl_gfx_dl.c:476` computes
`g_vdepth = ((cz/cw) + 1.0f) * 0.5f` - the 0..1 normalised depth - and
`fog_coord` (`sl_gfx_dl.c:2851`) puts that straight through `fm`/`fo`. Reading
that is not evidence, so it was measured from the cartridge.

The two candidates are affine in each other, so no choice of `fm`/`fo` can
separate them, and **the near plane cannot either**: under the 0..1 model the
inferred distance reduces to `d = 1/(2/d_true - 1/f)`, algebraically
independent of `n`. Measured too - a run at near=10 pins alpha at 246.8 down
the whole column, because with `n=10` the 1/w buffer crushes every visible
depth into two alpha counts. The **far** plane does separate them.

So: two runs at near=500 (to lift the scene out of that crush) with
`gSPFogPosition(0,1004)` -> `fm=127 fo=127`, which maps the whole of -1..1
into 0..254 and **cannot clamp** - and where nothing clamps, screen-linear
interpolation of NDC z is exact, so the per-pixel value is again usable. Only
the far plane differs, 2341.1111 against 10000, and neither touches screen x,y.
Solving each pixel for the world distance it implies:

| model | median disagreement between the two far planes | p25 | p75 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **z ranges -1..1** (gbi.h) | **2.89%** | 1.05% | 7.72% |
| z ranges 0..1 (ours) | 23.12% | 12.99% | 31.30% |

2.89% is the framebuffer's own quantisation floor - the N64's 16-bit target
resolves alpha in steps of ~8/248. The 0..1 model is off by an order of
magnitude with a consistent one-way bias. Down x=200 the right model returns
1742/1710, 1232/1234, 1001/965, 648/654 units from the two frames; the wrong
one returns 1388/935, 836/657, 637/507, 376/338.

#### ROM against native, same NDC z, both measured

Native numbers are real dumped vertices, not arithmetic: gassed facility
(`SL_GAS=1.0`), `SL_FOG=1 SL_FOG_DUMP=6000`, frame 349, 782 distinct fogged
vertices, `fm=12800 fo=-12544` - identical constants to the ROM's. Each row
takes the ROM's measured alpha, converts to NDC z, and finds the dumped vertex
nearest the depth our renderer would hold for it; the depths match to 4-5
decimals, so these are the same points on the curve.

| NDC z | **ROM shade alpha** | **native factor** | native raw |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.98064 | **8** | **130** | 130.24 |
| 0.98386 | **49** | **153** | 152.88 |
| 0.98514 | **66** | **159** | 159.46 |
| 0.98750 | **96** | **172** | 171.69 |
| 0.99007 | **129** | **193** | 192.59 |
| 0.99307 | **167** | **211** | 210.57 |
| 0.99692 | **217** | **235** | 235.43 |
| 0.99863 | **239** | **247** | 246.85 |

We over-fog at every depth, by 16x at the near end of the band and converging
to nothing at the far end. That is precisely the reported shape: the ramp is
compressed into the top of the range, so most of what fog touches lands at or
near full fog colour, and the near two-thirds of the floor that the cartridge
leaves untouched gets hazed. `alpha = 6400z - 6144` instead of
`12800z - 12544`: our band opens at z=0.96 where Rare's opens at z=0.98, which
at the gas's own 10/1000 planes is **336 world units instead of 503**.

`grep -rn g_vdepth src/ tools/` returns exactly four sites - the declaration,
`:476`, and the two fog uses at `:3691`/`:3719`. **Nothing anywhere converts
it back to -1..1**, so the value reaching `fm`/`fo` is 0..1 on every path.

#### What is NOT established

- **That correcting the unit fixes the saturation.** No source was changed and
  nothing was re-measured after a fix. The arithmetic above predicts the
  ramp broadens, and that prediction is untested.
- **That this is the only cause.** The same frame's `sl_fog` line reports
  `proj[10,11,14,15]=0.9463,0.9276,102.7,120.4682` - a projection with a
  non-zero `[15]`, which a plain `guPerspective` does not have, and from which
  the probe's own near/far solve returns the nonsense `near=-1912.6 far=52.8`.
  What `g_proj` is holding is a separate open question and it also feeds
  `g_vdepth`.
- **That the oracle is silicon.** It is parallel_n64's RSP, not a cartridge on
  hardware. Angrylion and paraLLEl-RDP were deliberately not installed. The
  evidence that the emulated path is faithful is internal: the blend model held
  for 153600 of 153600 pixels, and the far-plane consistency at 2.89% is a
  quantitative prediction that only the documented formula on the documented
  variable satisfies.
- **The two frames are not the same scene.** The ROM frame is mid-lerp
  (far=2341) and the native frame is full gas (far~950). The comparison is at
  matched NDC z, which is the variable fog is a function of - not the same
  triangle in the same room.

Tooling for all of the above is in the session scratchpad (`abfog.py`,
`solve.py`, `lin.py`, `farplane.py`); nothing was added to the repo and
`build/native/skeleton` was rebuilt only because it predated the in-tree
`SL_FOG_DUMP` probe and lacked its format string.

#### RETRACTED: direct-boot capture is deterministic. The fault was mine.

An earlier revision of this entry claimed direct-boot frame capture was
nondeterministic (13 of 20 frames differing between two runs of the same
binary) and that B-046's and B-048's twenty-level numbers were therefore
invalid. **That was wrong, and it was retracted the same day.**

Re-measured cleanly, with no competing job on the machine:

```
DIRECT BOOT, same binary, two clean runs, 5 levels: compared=20 differing=0
```

The original 13/20 was taken while a twenty-level capture job of my own was
saturating the CPU. B-047 already established that the render path is
load-bearing for game logic in this port, so heavy contention moves frame
pacing and the shot numbers land on different scenes - the same "different
frame counts, different SCENES" trap the task brief warns about, arrived at
from the other direction. The measurement was real; the conclusion drawn from
it was not.

**B-046 and B-048's published numbers stand**, and were independently
re-taken here on the deterministic replay path (`SL_INPUT`, one binary,
identical settings, only the toggle differing):

| claim | re-take | result |
|---|---|---|
| B-046 `SL_CC_TINT` does not disturb the levels | 20 levels, 40 frames | **0 differing** |
| B-048 `SL_CC_TEX1` does not disturb the levels | 20 levels, 40 frames | **0 differing** |

Two caveats on what that re-take does and does not cover. The sweep inputs
contain no explosions and no death overlay, so this re-confirms only the
NEGATIVE half of both claims - that nothing else changed. The positive halves
(fire in the explosion window, the blood-drip overlay) were always measured on
`SL_INPUT` replays and were never exposed to the pacing issue at all.

The real lesson is narrower than the retracted one: **capture is deterministic
but not robust to CPU contention - never run captures concurrently with other
load.** The replay path is the safer default regardless, at 18/18.

#### Verification of the delivered tree

- `make matching` -> **MATCH!**, exit 0. The `src/game` probe is inside
  `#ifndef __sgi`.
- `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility` -> **IDENTICAL**, 15869 ticks.
- `make bootsweep` -> **20/20**, 0 failures.
- **Delivered default is inert**: pre-change binary vs delivered binary with
  `SL_FOG` unset, deterministic replay path, one binary each, identical
  settings - `compared=18 differing=0`.

NOT done, and required before `SL_FOG` may default on: the B-048 standard on
the replay path - character models, viewmodel, HUD, font path and menus, with
differences confined to where fog legitimately belongs.

#### Reproduction

The recorded session does not reach the gas under replay **with
`SL_TOUGH=1000`** - the environment never switches and the fill stays
`102110` for all 11999 replayed frames. That is not evidence that replay
diverges from live play: SL_TOUGH is itself the divergence, since B-048
measured the same session reaching the tank explosion at DL ~3250 without it,
and keeping Bond alive past a blast recorded as killing him puts every later
input somewhere else. What the session does on an UNMODIFIED replay is
untested, because B-049 stalls the run at his death.

So the gas is armed directly, by a probe at the top of `handle_gas_damage`
(`propobj.c:14154`), `#ifndef __sgi`, in the tree and inert unless named -
the same shape as the `SL_TOUGH` hook at `player.c:497`. `SL_GAS` is the
opacity to hold (0..1), `SL_GAS_AT` the tick to arm at:

```
xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 640x480x24" env SL_ROM=baserom.u.z64 \
  SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34 SL_WINDOW=1 SL_TOUGH=1000 SL_GAS=1.0 SL_GAS_AT=300 \
  SL_FOG=1 SL_FOG_DBG=1 SL_FRAMES=900 SL_SHOT=/tmp/g/f SL_SHOT_EVERY=25 \
  SL_INPUT=tools/trace/sessions/facility-full-2026-08-26.input \
  ./build/native/skeleton
```

#### On the notes (non-negotiable 7)

The `not_covered` entry for gas rendering is correct and was not re-searched.
`ucode05_old.txt` "BC rsp_uc05_moveword" IS the authority for the command and
was consulted before the formula was touched: it gives type `00080000` = fog
and states "if fog, fog depth values (2 16bit integers)", which is the two-s16
packing this file decodes. Two corrections follow from measuring against it:

- **The type field sits at bits 0-7, not bits 16-23.** The note tables the
  types as `00080000` etc., i.e. the F3DEX layout. This build compiles gbi.h's
  plain-F3D branch, where `gMoveWd` puts the index in the LOW byte - which is
  what the existing `MW_SEGMENT` decode has always relied on. Measured: read
  at bits 0-7 the fog moveword yields `fm=12800 fo=-12544`, which is
  `gSPFogPosition(990,1000)` to the digit and cannot arise by chance. Same
  shape as the B-021 vtx correction - Rare's uc05 is not F3DEX.
- **The formula and the clamp are not in the corpus.** The note gives the
  packing and stops. Authority for "alpha(fog) = (eyespace z) * fm + fo
  CLAMPED 0 to 255", with that z running -1 to 1 (the perspective-divided z,
  NOT a distance), is gbi.h's own comment above `gSPFogFactor`, and
  `gbi.h:2777` for how `gSPFogPosition` derives fm/fo. A `not_covered` entry
  records the gap.

The blender mux slots are `ucode05_old.txt` "FC rdp_setcombine" as before.
