### B-045 — the fully gassed state OBSERVED for the first time, and fog does not touch the green

The 19-mark recording spends ~54 seconds inside the gas (far-fog 5000 -> ~1380,
72% of the transition) against 25 seconds last time. Replayed past the end of
the input the lerp completes and **`fill=428442` finally appears** - the first
time this project has rendered the fully gassed environment.

**Those late frames are VALID, and I nearly discarded them.** `cmds=7` in the
`sl_fog` line is the fog-command count, not the DL size; it reads 7 at frame
13400 in the middle of normal play too. The `near`/`far` solve goes numerically
noisy but `fog-geom=2318` and `a_shade=2318` are steady, so geometry is being
drawn throughout. Bond simply stands still once the stream runs out. A static
camera in a fully gassed room is exactly the sample this needed.

**Controlled A/B, one binary, identical settings, only `SL_FOG` differing, on
fully gassed frames:**

| frame | backdrop `(66,132,66)` fog OFF | fog ON | pixels fog changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13949 | 127057 | **127057** | 17015 (5.5%) |
| 14749 | 182393 | **182393** | 13070 (4.3%) |
| 13974 | - | - | 105090 (34.2%) |

**Identical populations.** Fog changes 4-34% of the frame and removes **not one
pixel** of the green expanse, now measured in the FULLY gassed state rather
than at 42% of the lerp. B-045's finding that fog cannot fill a region with no
geometry is confirmed at the distances the owner plays at. **Implementing fog
does not fix the owner's reported symptom**, and the recommendation to leave
`SL_FOG` OFF is unchanged - the saturation defect still blocks it.

**A discrepancy worth recording rather than explaining away.** This file states
the gassed fill renders as `(41,82,41)`, i.e. the `428442` register scaled by
0.62, and calls that scaling unexplained. On these frames it renders as
**`(66,132,66)` - the register value unscaled - and `(41,82,41)` has a count of
zero.** So the fill DOES reach the framebuffer unscaled here. Whether the 0.62
was a different combiner state or has since been fixed by the B-046/B-048
combiner work is not established, and the earlier number should not be quoted
without re-measuring.

#### The rule 5 verdict, and why it is still not closed

The green expanse survives fog, so the question is only whether geometry that
SHOULD be inside 1000 units is being drawn. **B-051 supplies a new reason to
think some of it is not.** At the in-gas marks:

| mark | read | room | green px | opaque panes | nearest opaque pane |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 23407 | 61 | 5892 | 20/20 | portal 78 at **637** |
| 16 | 24349 | 61 | 10738 | 19/20 | portal 81 at **658** |
| 18 | 26185 | 68 | **71319** (23%) | 20/20 | portal 81 at 1071 |
| 19 | 26623 | 66 | **117017** (38%) | 20/20 | portal 81 at 2280 |

Marks 15 and 16 are the suggestive ones: the nearest opaque pane sits at 637
and 658 units, a whisker past the 600 threshold, and there are 5892 and 10738
green pixels. **That is B-051's undrawn pane, not B-045's far plane** - and it
is bright green rather than near-black only because the gas changed the fill.

Marks 18/19 are not explained this way; their nearest opaque pane is 1071 and
2280 units away and the green is far larger. Those may genuinely be the far
plane, i.e. Rare's.

**So the two bugs overlap and the verdict must not be issued on the whole
expanse at once.** Fixing B-051 will remove some of this green and leave the
rest. Re-measure marks 18/19 AFTER the pane draws correctly, and only then
decide what remains is Rare's.

### Recommendation (not implemented): the stub generator must not invent `sl_*` symbols

Filed at the coordinator's request. `tools/native/build.sh` resolves anything
missing at link time by emitting `long <name>(void) { return 0; }`. That is
right for unimplemented SDK entry points and **wrong for anything named `sl_*`,
which is ours by convention** - a stubbed `sl_` symbol is always a bug. It cost
a silently dead probe (`sl_input_read_index`, `read=0` on every frame) that
compiled, linked and ran.

Suggested: fail the build, or at minimum print a loud banner, when a stub is
generated for a symbol matching `^sl_`. Cheap, and it closes a failure mode
that no amount of care at the call site catches.

### B-051 — the fix attempt: a REAL decode gap found and closed, and it does NOT fix the owner's symptom. Retracting my own conclusion.

Delivered behind **`SL_CC_GLASS`, default OFF**. **Recommendation: do NOT flip it.**
Reasons below, and they are negative results.

#### What was found, and it is real

Every alpha reading in `sl_gfx_dl.c` decoded **cycle 0 only**
(`aa0/ab0/ac0/ad0`, lines 4167-4177). Rule 7, `ucode05_old.txt`
"FC rdp_setcombine", lower word: cycle 1's alpha muxes are `Aa1 00E00000`,
`Ac1 001C0000`, `Ab1 00000038`, `Ad1 00000007` - and **nothing in this file
had ever read them.** The existing `SL_CC_DBG` probe did not even print them,
which is why the gap survived B-046 and B-048.

Measured live on facility at mark 1:

```
sl_ccx: f3727 fc26a004 1f1093fb cyc=1 tris=100 prim=000000ff env=ffffffff tile=0
   rgb0=(TEX1-TEX0)*LODFRAC+TEX0  rgb1=(COMB-0)*SHADE+0
   a0=(TEX1-TEX0)*COMB+TEX0       a1=(COMB-0)*SHADE+PRIM
```

`prim=000000ff` is the opacity 255 that `glassCalculateOpacity` computed from
distance, arriving exactly where predicted. **B-048's mip-chain family is
`fc26a004 1f1093ff`; the glass is `...fb`. One nibble - `Ad1` = 7 (the
constant "0") versus 3 (PRIMITIVE) - is the entire difference**, which is how
the glass got swept into the family B-048 deliberately left alone.

Blast radius measured, not assumed: across the owner's whole facility session
the shape `a1 = (COMB - 0) * SHADE + PRIM` matches **exactly one combiner
word**, 2869 times. The classifier added (`g_cc_a_prim1`) is an exact-shape
match in the same discipline as `g_cc_tex1mul` and `g_cc_a_envscale`.

#### RETRACTION: "at opacity 255 Rare draws a solid pane and we draw nothing"

That was my conclusion last round and **it is wrong.** Measured, counting the
glass combiner's triangles per frame across the mark 1 / mark 2 pair:

```
frame 3705  entries=1 tris=100      mark 1 region, pane OPAQUE (dist 618.7)
frame 3713  entries=1 tris=100
frame 3725  entries=1 tris=100
frame 3840  entries=0               mark 2 region, pane CLEAR  (dist 374.6)
frame 3846  entries=0
frame 3850  entries=0
```

**The pane is submitted and rasterised when it is opaque, and not submitted at
all when it is clear** - the opposite of what I asserted. So "the opaque pane
is not drawn" is withdrawn, and with it the reasoning that led from it.

#### The fix does not fix it. Controlled A/B, one binary, only the toggle differing

| mark | frame | backdrop OFF | backdrop ON | pixels changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (opaque, 618.7) | 3713 | 12204 | **12204** | **0** |
| 2 (clear, 374.6) | 3846 | 0 | 0 | **35838** |
| 16 (in gas) | 12174 | 10649 | 10649 | 0 |
| 18 / 19 (in gas) | 13092 / 13311 | - | - | 0 / 0 |

**Zero pixels change at mark 1** - the reported case, the window that is a
hole. The only place the toggle bites is the CLEAR end, where nothing was
wrong: 35838 pixels at mark 2, because returning PRIM alpha alone drops the
`COMBINED.a * SHADE.a` term Rare adds it to, making a faintly-tinted pane
fully invisible. That is a regression risk in exchange for no benefit.

The captured frame settles what the hole is: a stone window frame with a flat
dark-green rectangle inside it, 12204 pixels of exactly `(10,20,10)`. The pane
draws 100 triangles somewhere in that frame and the window is still a hole, so
**those triangles are not landing where the hole is** - wrong depth, wrong
screen position, rejected by the blender, or a different pane entirely.

#### Verification of the delivered tree

- **Delivered default is byte-inert**: pre-fix binary vs delivered binary with
  `SL_CC_GLASS` unset, deterministic replay, identical settings, PPM `cmp` -
  **compared=548, identical=548, differing=0**.
- With the toggle on: 181 of 660 frames differ.
- `make matching` MATCH!, `trace-verify facility` IDENTICAL 15869 ticks,
  `bootsweep` 20/20.

The B-048 standard (characters, viewmodel, HUD, font path, menus, across
levels) was **NOT completed**, deliberately: a change that does not fix its
target and degrades a working case should not consume that budget. If someone
later finds the real cause and the cycle-1 alpha reading becomes part of it,
the classifier is already here and the sweep is the next step.

#### What to do next, precisely

The pane is submitted with 100 triangles while opaque. Find where those
triangles go: dump their screen-space positions and depths for frame 3713 and
compare against the 12204-pixel rectangle. That is one probe and it decides
between "wrong place", "z-rejected" and "these are a different pane".

**Do not repeat the alpha route.** It is measured, closed, and not the cause.

### B-045 — fog was never the answer, stated plainly

The coordinator asked for this to be explicit rather than left to lapse, and it
should be, because the hypothesis was pushed hard and early and it is wrong.

**Measured, fully gassed, controlled A/B, one binary, only `SL_FOG` differing:**

| frame | backdrop px fog OFF | fog ON | pixels fog changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13949 | 127057 | **127057** | 17015 (5.5%) |
| 14749 | 182393 | **182393** | 13070 (4.3%) |

**Identical populations. Fog removes zero pixels of the green expanse.** Fog
cannot fill a region that has no geometry in it, and the green expanse is
exactly such a region. The fog work was correct as DIAGNOSIS - the gas really
is the environment ALT row plus a far-plane pull, and that really is what
turns the void bright green - but **implementing fog was never the fix for
what the owner reported**, and `SL_FOG` staying off costs them nothing on this
symptom. The saturation defect that blocks the flip is a separate matter.

**A correction to my own numbers.** I reported marks 18/19 as "71319 / 117017
green px" using a loose green-family filter and then nearly retracted it when
a strict filter on three fill colours returned 3 and 6 pixels. The strict
filter was the wrong one: the dominant colour at those marks is
**`(49,107,49)` = `0x316b31`, which IS a backdrop fill value** - one of the
intermediate lerp stages between `102110` and `428442`. So the original
figures stand: **70900 and 115873 pixels of backdrop void, 23% and 38% of the
screen.** The lesson is the ordinary one - a filter built from a hand-listed
set of constants silently under-counts a value that is being LERPED through a
continuum.

**The rule 5 verdict still cannot be issued**, and now for a better-founded
reason than last round. Marks 15/16 have their nearest opaque pane at 637 and
658 units - just past the 600 threshold - with 4864 and 10649 fill pixels, and
the glass toggle changed **zero** of them. So the "that green is the undrawn
pane" prediction I offered as a clean test of the fix **failed**: the fix does
not touch it. Whether those pixels are pane-shaped remains open, but the pane's
alpha is not what is producing them.

### Tables — CONFIRMED, and it is not a cull at all. It is an early return.

One grep, as predicted, and it lands (`propobj.c:7482-7497`):

```c
if ((u8) obj->type != PROPDEF_TINTED_GLASS)
{
    temp_f0 = chrobjFogVisRangeRelated(prop, getinstsize(obj->model));
    ...
    objAlpha = (s32) (temp_f0 * 255.0f);
    if (objAlpha <= 0)
    {
        return gdl;          /* <-- the prop is not drawn AT ALL */
    }
}
```

**Every prop that is not tinted glass gets a distance/fog-range visibility
value, and at zero the draw function returns without emitting anything.** Below
`0xFF` it takes the `PropType = 5` branch (`envcolour.word = objAlpha`) and
fades. That is "the lab tables appear as I get closer", mechanism and all -
including why big props survive further out than small ones, since
`getinstsize(obj->model)` is an input.

**This is why five measurements of `posIsOnScreen` /
`fogPositionIsVisibleThroughFog` correctly returned zero.** They were the wrong
function. The prop distance mechanism that actually fires is
`chrobjFogVisRangeRelated`, and nothing has measured it yet.

Next step, and it is small: probe `chrobjFogVisRangeRelated`'s return against
distance and `getinstsize` for the room 62 benches at marks 9/10 of the
previous recording, and check whether the fog ranges it reads are the ones
`g_ScaledFarFogIntensity` carries - because the gas changes those from 5000 to
1000, which would make every prop in the level fade at a quarter of the normal
range the moment the tanks blow. **NOT established, and worth checking before
anything is called Rare's.**

### B-045 — the flicker: FIXED. `glFogCoordf` had no prototype, so GL never received the fog coordinate. 2026-08-27

**Gate:** `tools/native/fogflicker.sh ~/.sightline/runs/20260826-235720-lvl34 17000 12`

```
before   15441, 17752, 9588, 16689, 15744, 23920, 10713, 16014, 20661, 11760, 14202, 14796
         mean=15606  max adjacent swing=13207 (84% of mean)   FLICKERING

after    40259, 40173, 40185, 40202, 40187, 40208, 40062, 40040, 40038, 40010, 39991, 39932
         mean=40107  max adjacent swing=146 (0% of mean)      STABLE
```

Widened to 60 consecutive gassed frames the swing is 1430 on a mean of 39600,
**3.6%**. `make matching` MATCH!, `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility` IDENTICAL
(15869 ticks). Nothing under `src/game` was touched.

The gate is the same instrument in both rows: the before-numbers were
reproduced byte for byte from preserved captures of the pre-fix binary, so the
run that reports STABLE is the run that reported FLICKERING one prototype ago.
`FRAMES=17000` is enough — the sampled window is frames 8049..8060 either way,
because `need` depends only on the trigger record — and it is 3.5x faster than
60000.

#### The cause, one line

`sl_gfx_dl.c` calls `glFogCoordf`. Mesa's `<GL/gl.h>` declares GL through 1.3;
`glFogCoordf` is 1.4 and lives in `<GL/glext.h>` behind `GL_GLEXT_PROTOTYPES`,
which nothing here defines. **With no prototype, C89 assumes `int(...)` and
default argument promotion widens the `GLfloat` to a `double`** — so the entry
point read the low 32 bits of that double as its coordinate.

Those bits are the tail of the mantissa. They bear no relation to the value:
0.216 and 0.217 produce entirely unrelated floats, most of them outside 0..1,
which GL clamps to no fog or full fog. Every vertex therefore got an
independent coin flip, and any small camera movement re-rolled all of them.
That is the flicker, and it is also the "factor saturates" reading — garbage
floats land outside 0..1 far more often than inside it.

The fix is a local `extern void glFogCoordf(GLfloat coord);` beside the
include. It is the only GL entry point in the file `<GL/gl.h>` does not
declare: `glMultiTexCoord2f`, `glActiveTexture`, `glBlendColor` and
`glBlendEquation` are all 1.3 or earlier and are declared there.

**Nothing announced it.** `tools/native/build.sh` compiled with `-w`, which
suppresses `-Wimplicit-function-declaration`, the one diagnostic that names
this exactly. Re-running the compile without `-w` prints it at line 3742, and
under the real native build flags it is the ONLY implicit declaration in
`src/gfx`, `src/platform` and `src/native` - so `-w` was hiding exactly one
thing, and it was this.

#### This invalidates every previous measurement of the fog RAMP

Any number describing what fog does to a PIXEL, taken before today, was taken
through this call and is void. Specifically:

- **"The factor saturates" (96% of changed pixels on one colour) — explained,
  and gone.** It was not a combiner or blender fault between the vertex value
  and the pixel; the vertex value never arrived.
- **The residual "our ramp starts a screen-eighth early and saturates too
  fast"** was measured the same way and must be re-taken before it is believed.
- **The `surface` regression report** (flat pale wash, flat patches with hard
  polygon edges) has the same shape this bug produces — whole surfaces pinned
  to full fog — and should be re-checked against the fixed binary before
  `SL_FOG`'s default is argued either way.
- The **per-vertex histogram** figures were always sound: they are computed in
  `fog_coord` and never went near GL. That is why they read as a sane spread
  while the image was saturated, and that contradiction was the tell.

Fog's contribution on the sampled frames rises 15606 -> 40107 pixels, i.e. fog
now reaches roughly 2.6x more of the frame, smoothly, at a modest strength
(the mid-floor band moves 0.4794 unfogged -> 0.4555 fogged, about 5%).

#### What was ruled out on the way, so nobody re-runs it

- **`proj[15] = 120.47` is not an anomaly and is not the cause.** `g_proj`
  holds **view x projection**, not a plain `guPerspective`. Room geometry is
  drawn under `get_BONDdata_field_10E0()` (`bg.c:686`), which `bondview2.c:8175`
  sets to `guMtxF2L(projmtx * lookat)` — hence a non-zero `[15]`, which is the
  camera's z translation. The probe's own `near`/`far` solve assumes a bare
  perspective matrix and is therefore meaningless; ignore it, or delete it.
  `far=300` does exist in the tree (`bondview2.c:8443`) but it is the
  **watch** render and only while paused.
- **The projection is stable between frames.** `sl_fog`'s `proj[10,11,14,15]`
  moves in the 4th decimal per frame across the whole flicker window, as a
  slowly turning camera should.
- **The classification is stable.** `fog-geom=2318 a_shade=2318 clr-fog=4873
  breaks e/d/c=1/0/1` are constant frame for frame through the flicker.
- **The fog coordinate FIELD is stable.** `SL_FOG_VIZ=2` (below) renders it
  unfogged: frames 8053 and 8054 are pixel-identical in the region that
  flickers, at factor 0.216 on both, while the shipped render puts one at 0 and
  the other at 1.0. That pair of facts is what localised the fault to the call.
- **The camera is nearly static in the sampled window.** With `SL_FOG=0` the
  mid-floor band reads 0.479456 -> 0.478153 across 16 frames, a monotone drift
  of 0.0001/frame. All of the swing was fog.
- **`SL_FRAMES` -> rendered frames is 2:1 here, not 4:1.** 17000 pumped gives
  8500 captures and 8499 `sl_fog` lines, and `sl_shot: f-0NNNN` interleaves
  1:1 with `sl_fog: fNNNN` in a combined log. Trap 1 in the task brief cites
  ~4x from an earlier run; do not carry either ratio, print both counters.

#### Two probes kept, both default OFF

- **`SL_FOG_MARK=1`** paints the fog stage magenta instead of the list's
  colour. A region reading exactly the environment colour is either geometry at
  full fog or the backdrop fillrect showing through, and those are the same
  pixels — including under `SL_FOG_VIZ=1`, because GL fogs the probe colour
  too. This settled it in one capture: the flat region on frame 8054 came back
  `(255,0,255)`, so it was geometry at factor 1.0, not the backdrop.
- **`SL_FOG_VIZ=2`** is `SL_FOG_VIZ=1` with GL's fog stage held off, so the
  factor field reaches the framebuffer unfogged. `=1` loses the blue channel
  exactly where the answer is.

#### The probe that looked broken and was actually the proof

An `SL_FOG_FORCE=<0..1>` probe forced one coordinate for every vertex. Both
`FORCE=0` and `FORCE=0.5` produced **no fog at all**, which read at the time
like proof that GL ignored the coordinate entirely, and was briefly written up
as a broken probe. It was not broken. It is the cleanest single piece of
evidence for the diagnosis:

    (double) 0.0  = 0x0000000000000000   low 32 bits = 0x00000000 -> 0.0f
    (double) 0.5  = 0x3FE0000000000000   low 32 bits = 0x00000000 -> 0.0f

Both constants have an all-zero mantissa tail, so the promoted-to-double
argument handed `glFogCoordf` exactly `0.0f` in both runs: no fog, twice, for
two very different requested values. A computed 0.216 has a full mantissa tail
and lands anywhere. The probe was removed after the fix, because with a correct
prototype `FORCE=0` only restates `SL_FOG=0`.

#### The compiler flag that hid it - now closed

`tools/native/build.sh` compiled native code with `-w`, which silences
`-Wimplicit-function-declaration`: the one diagnostic that catches "the
compiler and I disagree about this function's type", which on a 32-bit ABI is
a silent-wrong-answer class, not a tidiness class. The native arm of
`build.sh` now carries `-Werror=implicit-function-declaration` (landed
alongside this work), so `src/gfx`, `src/platform` and `src/native` cannot
repeat it. The decomp arm keeps `-w`: `bg.c` alone has 22 implicit
declarations and unpicking those carries matching-build risk.

**A measurement correction, recorded because it is the same error this file
keeps warning about.** An earlier revision of this entry claimed `atof` was
implicitly declared in `sl_gfx_dl.c`, `sl_input.c` and `sl_ultra_shim.c`, and
called the `SL_FOG_FORCE` reading an artefact of it. That came from compiling
those files with the DECOMP include flags (`-Iinclude -Iinclude/PR ...`), which
is not how `build.sh` compiles them: the native arm passes host headers alone,
precisely because the N64 SDK tree shadows them. Re-audited with the real
flags, the number of implicit declarations in `src/gfx`, `src/platform` and
`src/native` is **zero** once `sl_style_apply_once` has its forward
declaration, and the build passes under `-Werror`. So `glFogCoordf` was the
only one, the `-w` flag was hiding exactly one thing, and it was this. The
claim was measured - through the wrong instrument.

#### What is NOT established

- **That fog is now CORRECT**, only that it is stable and that the coordinate
  the file computes is the coordinate GL applies. The cartridge comparison in
  the section above (`ROM shade alpha 8/129/239` against `130/193/247`) was
  taken on the pre-fix binary and has not been re-run.
- **That `SL_FOG` is safe as a default.** It stays off. Everything the earlier
  recommendation weighed was measured through the broken call.
- **That the owner's originally reported symptom is resolved.** It is not:
  B-051's backdrop void is a separate defect and fog cannot fill a region with
  no geometry in it. That finding stands unchanged.
- **Whether the flicker the owner saw in live play is this one.** This is the
  flicker the gate measures on a deterministic replay. It has the right shape —
  whole surfaces changing brightness between adjacent frames — but a live
  report cannot be matched to a replay frame.

### B-051 — the window is not empty. The pane IS drawn there, at full opacity, and it contributes zero pixels. 2026-08-27

Measured on the owner's stamped ten-mark run `20260827-135114-lvl34`, replayed
at default settings (`SL_FOG` on, `SL_CC_GLASS` off), 16432 frames.

**Gates:** `make matching` **MATCH!**, `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility`
**IDENTICAL — 15869 ticks**, `make bootsweep` **20/20 OK**. Nothing here changes
a rendered pixel by default; every probe below is off unless named, and no fix
is delivered — this entry is measurement only.

#### The instrument was wrong first, and it would have produced a confident wrong answer

`SL_SHOT_FIRST`/`SL_SHOT_LAST` window on `sl_frames_completed()`. A run's marks
are written in `sl_record_index()` — `sl_input.c` calls `sl_run_mark` with it.
**The two counters are not proportional**: one replay of this recording ended
at `sl_frame=10142` against `read=7949`, another at `sl_frame ≈ read`. The
first seven captures therefore landed near `read≈3958` while asking for
`10103` — the opening of the level, which is trap 3 arriving through a door
nobody had guarded.

Fixed by naming the moment in the units the mark was recorded in:
**`SL_SHOT_READ_FIRST` / `SL_SHOT_READ_LAST`** (`sl_gfx_sdl.c`), and every
capture now states both counters and which window it used, so a capture at the
wrong moment cannot look like a capture at the right one:

```
sl_shot: .../f-00000.ppm (640x480) at read=10103 frame=10105 (window=read)
```

All ten marks then land exactly. Mark → `sl_dbg_frame` is a clean 2:1
(`read/2`) on this run — **do not carry that ratio**; it is the bg-frame
counter, and `sl_frame`, the one `SL_FRAMES` and the old shot window use, is
the one that drifts.

#### The pairs reproduce, in pixels and in the game's own numbers

| mark | read | pane | dist | opacity | portal | flat dark px |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10103 | 18 | 647.1 | **255** | DISABLED | **14390** `(10,20,10)` |
| 2 | 10295 | 18 | 440.7 | 51 | enabled | **0** |
| 6 | 19599 | 67/69 | 284/278 | 0/0 | enabled | 0 |
| 7 | 19871 | 72/73 | 576/479 | 224/100 | enabled | 0 |
| 8 | 21373 | 81 | 708.2 | **255** | DISABLED | 14128 `(6,12,6)` |
| 9 | 21585 | 81 | 507.5 | 137 | enabled | 4534 `(5,10,5)` |

Mark 1 is the owner's sentence rendered: a corridor, a window in the far wall,
and the window is a **flat solid rectangle**, `x[261,409] y[99,199]`, 149x101,
**95.6% filled with one exact colour**. Mark 2, 96 records later, shows the
room beyond — walls, a cabinet, a desk. `TintDist/CullDist` are 400/600,
`unk90` is 0.0, and `glassCalculateOpacity` is doing exactly what the note
(`object block types.txt`, type 2F) says it should. Marks 6/7 carry no flat
dark pixels at all and are not the same symptom.

#### The pane IS submitted, at the window, at full opacity

`SL_TRI_ID=1` names the triangles owning the rectangle: all 14390 pixels come
back as two ids, 1195 and 1196. A new probe, **`SL_TRI_WATCH=<first>[,<last>]`**,
closes the loop from an id back to the draw that made it. At `read=10103`:

```
sl_triw: read=10103 tri=1195 cc=fc26a004 1f1093fb prim=000000ff env=ffffffff
                     om=c41049d8 tex=54x54 glass=1 tint=0 fog=0
sl_triw:   ndc (-0.184,0.632,0.971) (0.282,0.640,0.971) (0.268,0.186,0.973)
sl_triw: read=10103 tri=1196  ... identical state, the other half of the quad
```

- `cc=fc26a004 1f1093fb` is **the tinted-glass combiner** — the exact word pair
  B-048 identified, one nibble from the mip-chain family's `...ff`.
- `prim=000000ff` is **prim alpha 255**, `glassCalculateOpacity`'s output for
  distance 647 against 400/600, arriving where the note says it should.
- The quad's NDC maps to px `x[261,410] y[86,196]`; the measured rectangle is
  `x[261,409] y[99,199]`. **Same rectangle**, the top edge clipped by the
  window's stone frame.

So the geometry, the distance grading, the opacity and the portal disable are
all doing what Rare designed. The pane is not missing, it is not misplaced, and
it is not at the wrong depth.

#### RETRACTION, mine, from four paragraphs ago — and the reason it matters

I first read the `SL_TRI_ID` capture as proof that a quad *covers* the
rectangle in the shipped render. **It is not.** `tri_id_option()` is consulted
in `tex_apply` as well as in the colour path (`sl_gfx_dl.c:1935`), and it
**disables texturing for every triangle**. A TRI_ID capture therefore removes
the very thing under test, and reading one as evidence about the shipped image
is an artefact.

It was caught only because a second probe contradicted it on the same frame,
which is the whole argument for having two.

#### The pane reaches the rasteriser and contributes ZERO pixels

**`SL_GLASS_MARK=1`** paints every triangle on the glass combiner opaque
magenta, leaving texture, blend and depth exactly as they were. At `read=10103`:

```
sl_gpos: f5051 read=10103 glass-tris=160 behind=48 all-tris=1770 painted-magenta=480
```

480 = 160 triangles x 3 vertices, so **every glass triangle in the frame was
painted, 1195 and 1196 among them** — and the capture is **byte-identical to
the default render**, md5 `50d3f58f0216...`, 0 of 307200 pixels changed.

The counter is there because a probe that paints nothing and a probe that is
never reached produce the same picture. This one was reached.

**Known-positive control:** the same binary and the same flag at `read=21373`
changes **13834 pixels**, and `SL_FOG_MARK=1` there changes **26894**. The
instruments are live. At `read=10103` they change nothing because nothing in
that corridor is fogged (`fog=0` on every watched triangle, and `SL_FOG=0`
yields a byte-identical frame) and because the pane, though drawn, writes
nothing.

#### The texture is what suppresses it — measured, one variable

**`SL_GLASS_MARK=2`** is the same opaque magenta with the **texture dropped for
the glass draw only**; nothing else in the frame changes. Same binary, same
replay, same frame:

| run at `read=10103` | pixels changed in the 14390-px mask | whole frame |
|---|---|---|
| `SL_GLASS_MARK=1` (texture on) | **0** | **0** |
| `SL_GLASS_MARK=2` (texture off) | **14390 / 14390**, all `(255,0,255)` | 21587 |

**All 14390 of them, exactly, and no others.** The pane covers the rectangle
precisely — no more, no less — so its position, depth and rasterisation are
right, and the only thing standing between it and the framebuffer is its own
texture.

*(The mechanism I guessed at here — "a texel alpha of ~0" — is measured and
WRONG. See the follow-up section below; the texel alpha is 102, and the real
structural defect is different and more general.)*

**This is the located defect, and it is legitimately ours**: the game's own
values are correct at every stage — setup record, `glassCalculateOpacity`,
prim alpha 255, the right combiner, the right quad — and the pixel is lost at
the texture stage, which is the port's own.

**The next measurement is small and specific:** dump the 54x54 image bound at
triangle 1195 (format, TLUT, and its alpha histogram) and compare it against
what the RDP tile actually asks for. Either the texel alpha is genuinely ~0 and
the RDP combiner never consults it — in which case the fix is at
`tri_alpha`/texenv for this combiner, not in the decode — or the decode pairs
this image with the wrong format, which is B-018/B-020's shape and would be
the fourth instance.

#### Why the previous round's `SL_CC_GLASS` fix measured "0 pixels changed at mark 1"

That fix made `tri_alpha` return PRIM alpha for this combiner. PRIM alpha here
is 255, so it was the right value — and it changed nothing, which was written
up as "do not repeat the alpha route". The route was not wrong; it was closed
**one stage later than anyone looked**. Whatever alpha the vertex carries is
multiplied by the texel's alpha by GL before it reaches the blender, so a
correct 255 and a wrong 0 arrive at the framebuffer identically if the texel
kills it. That is a specific, testable claim and the next measurement below
tests it.

#### The prop range cull the brief asked about is DEAD ON FACILITY, and that is Rare's data

`chrobjFogVisRangeRelated` (`propobj.c:13441`) does **not** read
`g_ScaledFarFogIntensity`. It reads the NEAR fog record through
`fogGetNearFogValuesP`. On facility that record **does not exist**:

- `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` (`bgfog.c:352`) sets `g_NearFogValuesP = NULL`
  when `Visibility.Nfd.NearFog == 0`;
- facility's row in `fog_tables` (`bgfog.c:186`) carries NearFog **0**,
  MaxVisRange **0**, MaxObfuscationRange **0** — and so does the ALT/gas row
  (`bgfog.c:187`), so the gas does not change it either;
- measured: `sl_nfd: ... NULL` on **all 16432 frames** of the owner's run, and
  `sl_table:` printed **0 lines**. Every prop's `objAlpha` is 255.

Note also that `fog_tables` is a compiled C table in `bgfog.c`, not level data
read from the ROM, so there is no byte-order surface here at all.

**Known-positive control, because a probe reading zero looks exactly like a
broken probe.** Same binary, same probes, on two levels whose rows do carry a
near-fog record:

```
statue   sl_nfd: NearFog=2000.0 MaxVisRange=2500.0 MaxObfusc=2000.0   348 sl_table lines
streets  sl_nfd: NearFog=5000.0 MaxVisRange=6000.0 MaxObfusc=1000.0     0 sl_table lines
```

Both decode to exactly their `fog_tables` rows. The probe is live and the
record decodes correctly, so facility's NULL means what it says.

#### The prop distance cull that DOES fire is `fogGetPropDistColor`, and the gas moves it 4.9x

`fogGetPropDistColor` (`bgfog.c:702`) returns 0 — Rare's own comment reads
"Prop is completely obscured by fog (don't render)" — when

    far_fog_dist_scaled / prop->zDepth + near_fog_dist_scaled > 1.0

and `propobj.c:7477` then returns without emitting anything. The prop does not
fade; it vanishes. It runs **before** the `PROPDEF_TINTED_GLASS` branch, so it
can drop a pane too. New probe `sl_pdc`, under the existing `SL_TABLE_DBG`:

| state | FarFog | farK | nearK | cutoff zDepth | props dropped/frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no gas | 5000 | -553.264 | 1.1146 | **4828.8** | **0** |
| mark 10 (`read 29773`) | 1990 | -554.946 | 1.2828 | **1960** | **26** |
| late gas | 1110 | -557.177 | 1.5054 | **1101** | **30** |

Types dropped over the run: 36 (0x24), 8, **47 (0x2F tinted glass)**, 1 (door),
0, 60.

**The inputs are right and the arithmetic is Rare's.** Working the coefficients
by hand from the `fog_tables` row (BlendMultiplier 10, FarFog 5000,
FarIntensity 0x3E8, DifferenceFromFarIntensity 0x3DE, visibility scale 1) gives
a cutoff of 4827 against the measured 4828.8 — 0.04%. No byte-order, units or
scale corruption, which is this project's dominant bug class and the specific
thing worth ruling out. **Rule 5: this stays.**

It is the shape of the owner's tank report: the moment the tanks blow, every
prop past ~1000 units stops being drawn where the limit had been ~4800. It is
also why mark 10 is a green sea — 80629 pixels of one colour, with the
projection's far plane falling alongside it (`zfar` in the run's `events`).

#### What is NOT established

- **WHY the texel kills it.** That the texture is the suppressor is measured;
  whether its alpha is genuinely ~0 in the ROM's own data, or arrives that way
  through a decode/format pairing fault, is not. Those two have different
  fixes and the capture above does not separate them.
- **Whether the same cause explains mark 8.** At `read=21373` the glass mark is
  live and changes 13834 pixels of the frame while changing **0** of the 14128
  in that mark's dark region, so mark 8's dark area is a different thing from
  mark 1's pane and must not be filed with it.
- **Nothing here was compared against the cartridge.** No frame in this entry is
  matched against the ROM. What stands without it is narrower and stronger:
  the game's own values are correct at every stage from the setup record to
  prim alpha, so whatever is wrong is downstream of the last point the decomp
  controls.
- **OPEN QUESTION, named rather than implied: does our render put the same
  colour in the gassed region the N64 did?** Rare's entire justification for
  dropping a prop past the cutoff is that it is 100% fog at that distance, so
  on hardware the prop and its surroundings are the same colour and nothing is
  lost. If our fog is weaker there, the identical cull becomes visible as
  popping even though the arithmetic is untouched. **This is the one place a
  port-side defect could still hide behind a rule 5 verdict**, it is cheap to
  settle with the ROM oracle (`tools/native/romshot.py` at a matched moment),
  and it should not be chased now - fog is closed and confirmed by the owner.
  Recorded so the rule 5 verdict on `fogGetPropDistColor` is understood as
  conditional on it.
- **Marks 3/4/5 are not analysed.** They are a three-mark cluster around one
  approach and carry no flat dark region at the two ends that were measured.

### B-051 — the texture dump. The combiner's alpha has an ADDEND that `GL_MODULATE` cannot express — and one fact still does not fit. 2026-08-27

The coordinator's steer was to stop treating this as a glass problem and ask
whether it exposes a general defect in how the RDP combiner is translated to
OpenGL. Three facts were asked for at triangle 1195 of `read=10103`. All three
are now measured, on one line of one probe:

```
sl_triw: read=10103 tri=1195 cc=fc26a004 1f1093fb prim=000000ff env=ffffffff
                     om=c41049d8 tex=54x54 glass=1 tint=0 fog=0
sl_triw:   alpha0=(TEX1-TEX0)*COMB+TEX0  alpha1=(COMB-0)*SHADE+PRIM
sl_triw:   tex slot=134 gl=135 src=0xc8504e48 pal=0xc8509740 fmt=5 54x54
                     flags=1 alpha min=102 max=102 mean=102 zero=0/2916
                     (1 entries share this gl name)
```

#### 1. The combiner's alpha equation, decoded from the note

**Rule 7.** `ucode05.txt` punts FC to a `SETCOMBINE.HTM` that is not in the
corpus; **`ucode05_old.txt` carries the table**, and this is the fourth time it
has been the authority (F5 settile, B9/BA setothermode, the 5-bit c mux, and
now the alpha muxes). Its FC entry gives the alpha muxes as three bits each —
`Aa1 00E00000`, `Ac1 001C0000`, `Ab1 00000038`, `Ad1 00000007` — over a
**separate** "alpha combiner" value list (0 combined, 1 texel0, 2 texel1,
3 primitive, 4 shade, 5 environment, 6 primlodfrac/1, **7 the constant 0**).

Decoding `1f1093fb` against it:

```
rgb1   = (COMBINED - 0) * SHADE + 0
alpha1 = (COMBINED.a - 0) * SHADE.a + PRIMITIVE.a
```

and `prim=000000ff`, so **PRIMITIVE.a is 255**. The RDP saturates, so on
hardware that alpha is **255 regardless of what the texel carries**. The
addend is the whole mechanism: `Ad1` = 3 (PRIMITIVE) is the single nibble
separating this word from the ordinary room-texture combiner. Rule 7 again —
`Texture application (Rooms).txt` gives the standard textured room draw as
`FC26A004 1F1093FF`, and the glass is `...FB`. **The glass is the room
combiner with an alpha addend bolted on.**

#### 2. The texel alpha, with its control

`alpha min=102 max=102 mean=102 zero=0/2916` — **uniformly 102/255 on every
texel**, not zero. `fmt=5` with a non-NULL `pal`, 54x54.

**Control, and it passes.** `SL_TEX_ALPHA=1` prints the same histogram for
every decode, 2789 of them in this replay. The most common readings are
`min=255 max=255 mean=255` (362 + 101 + 95 + 41 + 40 decodes at various
sizes) — fully opaque images coming through the same code path and reading
fully opaque. A histogram of zeros and a broken dumper are indistinguishable;
this dumper is not broken.

**An instrument fault found and fixed on the way.** The first version located
the cache entry by GL NAME. `TEX_CACHE_N` is 256 and this replay decodes 2789
images, so the ring wraps and entries share names — a by-name lookup returns
whichever matches first, usually a stale entry describing a different image,
and reports a plausible format and histogram for it. The slot is now recorded
at the point of resolution, where it is exact, and the probe prints how many
entries share the name so the ambiguity is visible rather than hidden. **In
this case the answer was 1**, so the original figure survives — but it survived
by luck, not by design.

#### 3. `GL_MODULATE` couples what the RDP keeps separate

    GL_MODULATE:   out.rgb = tex.rgb * in.rgb      out.a = tex.a * in.a
    RDP:           rgb1    = (COMB - 0) * SHADE    alpha1 = (COMB.a - 0) * SHADE.a + PRIM.a

There is **no additive term in `GL_MODULATE` at all**, so an alpha equation
with a non-zero addend cannot be expressed by it under any choice of vertex
alpha. The hardware's saturated 255 becomes at most `102/255` — 40% — and the
`SL_CC_GLASS` fix from the previous round, which supplied the correct PRIM
alpha at the vertex, was multiplied down by the same texel afterwards. That is
why it measured "0 pixels changed" while being the right value.

**This is general, not glass-specific**, which is the point of the steer: the
translation drops alpha addends everywhere. Glass is simply the only combiner
in this game whose addend is non-zero — one word, matched 2869 times across the
owner's session, per B-048's earlier sweep.

#### THE FACT THAT DOES NOT FIT, and why no fix is delivered

If the pane arrives at 40% alpha, then `SL_GLASS_MARK=1` — opaque magenta at
vertex alpha 255, texture on — should blend 40% magenta over the rectangle.
The green channel alone would move from 20 to 12 across 14390 pixels.

**It moved zero.** The capture is byte-identical to the default render.

`om=c41049d8` decodes 2-cycle to `p=CLR_IN a=A_IN m=CLR_MEM b=1MA` with
`FORCE_BL` set, i.e. ordinary `SRC_ALPHA / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` blending, and
the renderer has **no alpha test anywhere** (`grep -n "GL_ALPHA_TEST\|glAlphaFunc"
src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` is empty). Under blending *or* under no blending, a
magenta fragment at 40% must change those pixels. So a 40% texel alpha does
**not** account for the observation, and something between the fragment and the
framebuffer is still unidentified.

**So the diagnosis is incomplete and I am not delivering a fix.** The three
facts establish a real structural defect — the alpha addend is inexpressible —
and the coordinator's reading of it is confirmed. But "texture on kills it"
and "texel alpha is 102" do not compose into an explanation, and a general
combiner change is exactly the wrong thing to ship on an incomplete one. B-040
shipped a culling change verified on rooms alone and destroyed every character
model; the standard here is B-048's 125 identical frames across 20 levels plus
a ROM comparison at the marked frame, and none of that should be spent until
the residual is closed.

**The next measurement, and it is one run.** Take `SL_GLASS_MARK=1` and force
the vertex alpha to 255 *after* the texenv, or equivalently switch the glass
draw to a texenv that ignores texel alpha (`GL_COMBINE`, `COMBINE_ALPHA =
REPLACE`, `SOURCE0_ALPHA = PRIMARY_COLOR`) — the shape any real fix would
take. If the pane then appears, the residual is the coupling and the fix is
the general one. If it still does not, the fragment is being lost somewhere
that has nothing to do with alpha, and every alpha-side conclusion in this
entry is describing the wrong stage.

#### Delivered

Probes only, all default OFF, no renderer behaviour changed:

- **`SL_TRI_WATCH=<first>[,<last>]`** — names the draw behind a triangle id:
  combiner words, decoded alpha equation, colours, render mode, NDC, and the
  exact texture cache entry with its alpha histogram.
- **`SL_TEX_ALPHA=1`** — the decoded alpha histogram of every texture, at
  decode time, which is its own control.
- **`SL_GLASS_MARK=1|2`** — paint the glass combiner's triangles magenta, `=2`
  additionally dropping that draw's texture.
- **`SL_GLASSPOS=1`** — per-frame glass triangle count, NDC box, and a
  `painted-magenta` counter so an unreached probe cannot look like an
  ineffective one.
- **`SL_SHOT_READ_FIRST`/`SL_SHOT_READ_LAST`** — capture windowed in record
  units, the units a run's marks are written in.
- The **`SL_TRI_ID` caveat now lives in the probe's own comment**
  (`sl_gfx_dl.c`), not only here: it is consulted in `tex_apply` and disables
  texturing, so a TRI_ID capture can never be used to reason about anything
  the texture participates in.

### B-051 — the residual is closed, and closing it RETRACTS "the pane contributes zero pixels". 2026-08-27

One run settles it. **`SL_GLASS_MARK=3`** keeps the texture and takes alpha from
the vertex alone (new `texenv_set` mode 2: `COMBINE_RGB = MODULATE`,
`COMBINE_ALPHA = REPLACE` from `PRIMARY_COLOR`) — the shape any real fix would
take, armed only for the glass combiner and only under the probe flag.

| run at `read=10103` | pixels changed in the 14390-px mask | becomes | whole frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=1` magenta, texture on, GL_MODULATE alpha | 0 | — | 0 |
| `=2` magenta, texture off | 14390 / 14390 | `(255,0,255)` | 21587 |
| `=3` magenta, texture on, **vertex alpha** | **14390 / 14390** | **`(0,0,0)`** | 21386 |

#### Why `=1` changed nothing, and why that was not what I read it as

Under `=3` the vertex colour is magenta, so `out.rgb = tex.rgb * (255,0,255)`
preserves the texel's RED and BLUE and zeroes its green. The result is
**exactly `(0,0,0)` on all 14390 pixels**, which bounds the texel's red and
blue at ~0. (Green is zeroed by the magenta itself and remains unmeasured.)

That is the whole explanation of the `=1` result. With a near-black texel,
`magenta * tex.rgb` and `defaultvertex * tex.rgb` are **both ~0**, so painting
the triangles magenta could not change the frame no matter how well they drew.

**`SL_GLASS_MARK=1` was a null instrument for this texture — a probe that could
not fail.** Its `painted-magenta=480` counter proved the branch was reached and
told me nothing about whether the draw mattered, and I read "0 pixels changed"
as "the pane contributes zero pixels". **That reading is RETRACTED.** The pane
contributes; it contributes near-black at 40% alpha, which is nearly the same
thing as the backdrop it is drawn over, which is why it looks like a hole.

Third instrument fault in this entry, and the same shape each time: `SL_TRI_ID`
removed the texture, the by-name cache lookup could name the wrong image, and
now a colour probe multiplied by ~0. **A probe must be able to produce a
different answer than the one it produced.**

#### The corrected picture, and it is coherent for the first time

- `alpha1 = (COMBINED.a - 0) * SHADE.a + PRIMITIVE.a` with `PRIM.a = 255`
  (`ucode05_old.txt`'s FC table, decoded by the probe). The RDP saturates, so
  **on hardware the pane is opaque at distance.**
- `GL_MODULATE` gives `out.a = tex.a * in.a` and has **no additive term at
  all**, so the addend is inexpressible. Our pane arrives at the texel's
  uniform `102/255` — **40% instead of 100%**.
- A 40% near-black pane over the backdrop darkens it instead of occluding it,
  which is exactly the flat dark rectangle the owner reports as "not
  transparent, and you cannot see through it".

So Rare's intent and the owner's symptom are much closer than this entry has
assumed throughout: **the window at distance is SUPPOSED to be a dark opaque
pane.** It is not a void that should show a room; it is a pane that should be
solid and is instead 40% transparent. `SL_GLASS_MARK=3` renders it solid, which
is what the hardware's saturated alpha produces.

#### What is still NOT established

- **What colour the pane should be.** Red and blue are bounded at ~0; green is
  unmeasured because the probe's own magenta zeroed it. An opaque *black* pane
  and an opaque *dark green* pane are both consistent with everything measured.
- **The ROM comparison, which is what would settle it.** No frame here has been
  matched against the cartridge. Until it is, "solid is right" rests on the
  note's saturating addend, not on the cartridge's pixels.
- **Whether the general fix is safe.** `texenv_set` mode 2 exists as an
  experiment behind `SL_GLASS_MARK=3` and is armed for one combiner. Making it
  general — representing RGB and alpha as the independent equations the RDP
  runs — touches every textured surface in every level and needs the B-048
  standard (rooms, characters, viewmodel, HUD, font path, menus, across levels)
  plus the ROM comparison. **None of that is done, and no fix is delivered.**

### B-051 — the ROM oracle, and the blast-radius number for the general fix. 2026-08-27

Two things asked for, in order. One answered a question and closed a different
one; the other produced a number that changes how the fix should be scoped.

#### 1. The ROM comparison — what it settled, and a precise dead end

Swept 110 cartridge frames of `facility-gas` under the libretro core
(`tools/native/romshot.py --input facility-gas --frames 11500 --every 100`),
against our own replay of the same stream. ROM frames are named by INPUT
INDEX, which is the same unit our `sl_record_index()` counts, so the two sides
align without a counter conversion.

**SETTLED, and it is the fog question this file has been carrying as open:**
the cartridge's late-gas frames show **the same flat green expanse we do** —
only the near railing, floor and guards visible, everything beyond it a single
green wash. That is the hardware doing what `fogGetPropDistColor` assumes when
it declines to draw a prop past the cutoff. It does not prove our ramp matches
the ROM's numerically, but it removes the reading that our green sea is a
port defect: **the N64 draws a green sea there too.** The rule 5 verdict on
`fogGetPropDistColor` no longer rests on inference alone.

**DEAD END, stated precisely so nobody repeats it:** `facility-gas` **cannot**
answer the pane question. Measured over the whole stream with `SL_GLASS_DBG`:

```
minimum distance of any pane at opacity 255, whole run:  1637.6
```

`CullDist` is 600, so every opaque pane in that stream is at least 1637 units
away — never in the band the owner's report lives in, where a pane is past
`CullDist` AND close enough to fill a window in view (their mark 1 is 647).
No frame in the sweep shows the case under investigation.

**What a future session needs** is a `trace-record` stream that walks the
security-door corridor and stops 600-900 units short of the window. That is
one recording, and until it exists **"the pane should be solid" still rests on
`ucode05_old.txt`'s saturating addend, not on the cartridge's pixels** - and
the pane's colour (red and blue bounded at ~0, green never measured) is
untouched by anything here.

#### 2. The blast radius: TEN words, but only ONE is genuinely additive

New census `SL_CC_ADDEND=1` (default off, reported once at exit) counts
DISTINCT combiner words that reached a draw and whose **memory-producing
cycle** carries an alpha addend other than the constant 0 — cycle 1 in
2-cycle, cycle 0 in 1-cycle. Twenty campaign levels, 400 frames each:

```
dam 4  facility 2  runway 7  surface 5  bunker1 4  silo 4  frigate 4
surface2 4  bunker2 3  statue 1  archives 5  streets 2  depot 4  train 2
jungle 3  control 4  caverns 2  cradle 5  aztec 5  egypt 1
```

**Union across all twenty: 10 distinct words.** Ranked by the levels they
appear in, with total triangles:

| word | levels | tris | cycle-1 alpha |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fc26a004 1f1093fb` | **17/20** | 1808913 | `(COMB-0)*SHADE+PRIM` |
| `fc159804 5ffedbf8` | 13 | 2382046 | `(0-0)*0+COMB` |
| `fc26a004 1ffc93fc` | 11 | 1660564 | `(0-0)*0+SHADE` |
| `fcffffff fffe793c` | 8 | 20300 | `(0-0)*0+SHADE` |
| `fcffffff fffe7b3d` | 7 | 250143 | `(0-0)*0+ENV` |
| `fc159a04 5ffefff8` | 6 | 552309 | `(0-0)*0+COMB` |
| `fc26e404 1ffcfffc` | 3 | 211537 | `(0-0)*0+SHADE` |
| `fc26a004 1ffc93fd` | 3 | 214323 | `(0-0)*0+ENV` |
| `fc127e24 fffff9fc` | 2 | 4378 | `(0-0)*0+SHADE` |
| `fcffffff fffe7838` | 1 | 5970 | `(0-0)*0+COMB` |

**The number the fix should be scoped on is 1, not 10.** Nine of the ten are
`(0 - 0) * 0 + X`, which is not an addend in any interesting sense — it is a
REPLACE: alpha is exactly X, with no texel term to interact with. Only
`fc26a004 1f1093fb`, the tinted-glass pane, is a genuine multiply-PLUS-addend,
and it is the one `GL_MODULATE` cannot express under any vertex alpha.

Two things follow, and they pull in opposite directions:

- **The additive case is one word**, so the change the owner is waiting on is
  far narrower than "every textured surface".
- **The glass word is in 17 of 20 levels**, not just facility. Tinted glass is
  a game-wide prop type, so whatever ships will be seen everywhere, and the
  B-048 sweep is not optional.

**The inverse regression to watch for, named:** the nine REPLACE words are
currently rendered as `tex.a * vertex.a`. Anything that looks right today
*because* we multiply the texel in would go MORE opaque under a correct
independent-alpha path — 2.38M triangles on `fc159804 5ffedbf8` alone. That is
the failure mode a rooms-only sweep misses, and it is why the count above is
per-word rather than a single total.

#### 3. Instrument faults — now FIVE, each caveat in the probe's own comment

Every one is the same shape: a measurement that could not have produced a
different answer, reading healthy the whole time.

1. **`SL_TRI_ID` disables texturing** (`tex_apply`), so a TRI_ID capture can
   never be evidence about anything the texture participates in. Caveat in the
   probe's comment.
2. **The texture cache lookup was keyed on the GL NAME.** 256 slots, 2789
   decodes in one replay, so entries share names and a by-name search returns
   a stale one. **Fixed**: the slot is recorded at the point of resolution,
   where it is exact, and the probe prints how many entries share the name.
   Comment at `g_tex_slot`.
3. **`SL_GLASS_MARK=1`'s magenta is multiplied by the texel**, so on a
   near-black texture it changes nothing however well the triangles drew.
   Caveat in the probe's comment, pointing at modes 2 and 3.
4. **`SL_SHOT_EVERY` tested exact divisibility** against a counter that
   advances by two or more per frame, so a read-window with a stride of 100
   stepped over every multiple and captured **zero files, silently**.
   **Fixed**: it now fires on "at least `every` since the last capture".
5. **The stage-id table in the first census script was written from memory**
   and mislabelled **eleven of twenty levels** - it booted `complex` as
   `train`, `bunker1` as `dam`, and four ids that are in no table at all. The
   per-level numbers looked entirely plausible and were answering about the
   wrong levels; one "train crash" was `complex`, and it reproduces with the
   probe OFF. The census was re-run against `bootsweep.sh`'s list, which is
   the authority, and the numbers above are the corrected ones. **The rule
   this earns: a level list is data, and data gets cited, not remembered.**

### B-051 — [VOID, SUPERSEDED] first attempt at the fix. 2026-08-27

> **EVERY NUMBER IN THIS SECTION IS VOID.** It was produced by an alpha
> classifier that was later proved wrong (it classified on SOURCE MEMBERSHIP
> instead of on the simplified equation). In particular the **aztec regression
> reported below is NOT established** - it shows only that the BROKEN
> implementation changed aztec, and says nothing about how a correct
> independent-alpha path behaves. The twenty-level sweep numbers are void, not
> merely suspect. The corrected work is in the section after this one.
> Kept, unedited, because the contradiction is what caught the bug.

Delivered behind **`SL_ALPHA_EQ`, default OFF**. **Recommendation: do NOT flip
it yet** - the sweep found a visible regression on aztec, named below.

#### What it does, and it is general

`sl_gfx_dl.c` now decodes the RDP's alpha equation from the combiner word and
represents it INDEPENDENTLY of the colour equation, which is the actual defect:
`ucode05_old.txt`'s FC table gives each cycle `alpha = (Aa - Ab) * Ac + Ad`
over its own mux list, while `GL_MODULATE` forces `out.a = tex.a * in.a` - no
additive term, and no way to say "alpha does not consult the texture".

Three modes, chosen from the decoded equation and nothing else. No glass path,
no per-combiner special case:

- **AEQ_REPLACE** - the equation names no texel anywhere (expanded through
  COMBINED into cycle 0). Evaluate it exactly per vertex; `COMBINE_ALPHA =
  REPLACE` from the primary colour.
- **AEQ_MODULATE** - names a texel, addend is the constant 0. Today's
  behaviour, already correct.
- **AEQ_ADD** - names a texel AND carries a real addend. Hand back the addend;
  `COMBINE_ALPHA = GL_ADD(TEXTURE, PRIMARY)`.

The producing cycle is resolved at DRAW time, not at FC time, because the cycle
type arrives from BA setothermode_h and a list may issue it after its FC.

**The comment carries the census number** so nobody widens this out of caution:
the additive case is **exactly one combiner word**. RGB is untouched in every
mode.

**Stated limit of AEQ_ADD:** GL 1.3 fixed-function `COMBINE_ALPHA` has MODULATE
and ADD but no multiply-add, so `tex.a * SHADE.a + PRIM.a` renders as
`tex.a + PRIM.a`. Exact when SHADE.a is 255 - which the glass pane's vertices
measure (`rgba 474053ff`) - and an over-estimate otherwise.

#### It fixes the reported case, exactly

| at `read=10103` | md5 | mask pixels changed |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix baseline | `50d3f58f0216…` | - |
| `SL_ALPHA_EQ` unset | `50d3f58f0216…` | **0 - byte-identical** |
| `SL_ALPHA_EQ=1` | `1eb7974d6801…` | **14390 / 14390 → (0,0,0)** |

**And that md5 is byte-for-byte the same frame `SL_GLASS_MARK=3` produced** -
two independently written paths, one general and one armed for a single
combiner, agreeing exactly. That is the strongest corroboration available
without the cartridge.

Per-mode triangle counts over the owner's whole session:
`replace=5842278 modulate=19605717 add=12744903`. Roughly half of all draws
take a changed path, while only 21386 pixels of that frame move - most of those
draws carry a texel alpha of 255 already, so the two paths agree.

#### The B-048 sweep, run alone, one process at a time

Twenty campaign levels, 400 frames, four captures each, fix OFF then ON, never
concurrently. Stage ids from `bootsweep.sh`.

Frames differing: **17 of 20 levels** show 3 of 4 frames changed;
**statue, jungle and egypt are byte-identical throughout.** Pixel magnitude
across all four frames per level:

| level | changed | direction | max delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| aztec | **25958 (8.45%)** | 12095 brighter / 13688 darker | 180 |
| control | 11292 (3.68%) | all darker | 104 |
| dam | 3744 (1.22%) | mixed | 118 |
| facility | 3369 (1.10%) | all darker | 46 |
| frigate | 2909 (0.95%) | mixed | 197 |
| bunker2, bunker1, silo, train, cradle, runway | 0.16-0.63% | mixed | ≤108 |
| archives, caverns, streets, surface, surface2, depot | <0.02% | - | - |
| statue, jungle, egypt | **0** | - | - |

**Named, on facility:** the changed pixels are `bbox x[261,319] y[100,124]`,
**869 of them exactly `(10,20,10)` before and `(0,0,0)` after** - the same
tinted-glass pane as mark 1, going opaque. That is the fix working, on a
different camera, in a different run.

#### THE REGRESSION, and it is the B-040 shape you warned about

**Aztec's floor and wall decals lose their cut-out.** Captured pair, frame 2:
before, the yellow floor marking and the "BAY-4" lettering are solid crisp
shapes; after, both are **stippled** - the floor texture shows through them in
a checkerboard. 1653 pixels of pure `(255,255,0)` before are gone after.

The mechanism, and this is the hypothesis rather than a measurement: my
classifier equates "the alpha equation names no texel" with "the texel alpha is
irrelevant". Aztec shows that is false - **the decal's cut-out is carried by
texel alpha that the ALPHA EQUATION does not name**, so REPLACE mode discards
exactly the thing making the decal a shape rather than a quad. Which stage
still consults it - cycle 0's alpha feeding coverage, or the blender's own
alpha path - is not established and is the next measurement.

This is precisely the inverse regression predicted: a surface that looks right
today *because* we multiply the texel in. A rooms-only sweep would have shipped
it.

#### Verification status, plainly

- `make matching` MATCH!, `trace-verify LEVEL=facility` IDENTICAL 15869 ticks,
  `bootsweep` 20/20, default render byte-identical to the pre-fix binary.
- The B-048 standard is **NOT met**: this covers rooms, props, viewmodel and
  HUD across twenty levels, but **not** the font path, menus, or characters in
  motion, and it has **one known regression**.
- **Do not flip `SL_ALPHA_EQ`.** It fixes its target and breaks decals. The
  fix is sound in structure and wrong in one classification, and the aztec pair
  is the test case for the next round.

### B-051 — the classifier, corrected: decode -> simplify -> classify -> represent. 2026-08-27

The previous section is void. This replaces it.

#### THE SIXTH INSTRUMENT FAULT, and the first the instrumentation caught itself

The old `aeq_mode_now()` classified on **source membership**:

```c
if (!(aeq_uses_texel(a) || ... || aeq_uses_texel(d))) return AEQ_REPLACE;
if (d == CC_A_ZERO) return AEQ_MODULATE;
return AEQ_ADD;
```

For `(0 - 0) * 0 + COMBINED` that reaches the last line - `COMBINED` resolves
through a texel somewhere, and `d != 0` - and returns ADD. But the multiply
term is **identically zero** and the expression collapses to `COMBINED`.

It reported `replace=5.84M modulate=19.6M add=12.7M` on facility. **12.7M ADD
triangles cannot be reconciled with a census of one genuinely additive word**,
and that contradiction - between two of this session's own instruments - is
what exposed it. Nobody noticed it by eye. That is the system working.

Every number from the twenty-level sweep is void, and **the aztec regression
is withdrawn**: it shows that the broken implementation changed aztec, and
nothing about how a correct independent-alpha path behaves.

#### The rewrite

`decode -> simplify -> classify -> choose the GL representation`, in that
order, with the GL choice last and taken from the simplified equation.

A `struct aeq_expr` carries the reduced form. Identities applied:

```
(A - A) * C + D  ->  D          (A - B) * 0 + D  ->  D
X * Y + 0        ->  a plain multiply       X * Y + D  ->  a genuine MAD
```

**`COMBINED` resolves by substituting cycle 0's own SIMPLIFIED EXPRESSION**,
not by asking whether a texel appears somewhere inside it - that was the same
mistake relocated. `aeq_src_tex(COMBINED)` simplifies cycle 0 and asks the
resulting expression; `aeq_simplify` returns cycle 0's expression outright
when cycle 1 reduces to `COMBINED`.

Classification is then a property of the reduced expression: no texel ->
REPLACE; texel with no addend -> MODULATE; texel with a genuine addend -> ADD.

#### The gate shows its working — and it DISAGREES with "9 REPLACE + 1 ADD"

`SL_AEQ_SELFTEST`, armed by `SL_ALPHA_EQ`, runs the simplifier over the ten
census words and prints, for each: raw equation, cycle 0, simplified equation,
mode, and whether a texel survives simplification. Result:

```
TOTALS replace=7 modulate=1 add=2
```

**Not 9 + 1, and the classifier was NOT bent to reach it.** The working shows
why, and the reason is definitional:

- the census (`SL_CC_ADDEND`) selected words by a **syntactic** test on one
  cycle - "Ad is not the constant 0";
- the simplifier asks a **semantic** one - "is the fully simplified equation a
  genuine multiply-plus-addend" - following COMBINED into cycle 0 as
  instructed.

They differ exactly on `(0-0)*0+COMBINED` forms, where Ad is syntactically
`COMBINED` but the equation *is* cycle 0's:

| word | cycle 1 raw | simplifies to | mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fc159804 5ffedbf8` | `(0-0)*0+COMB` | `(TEX0-ENV)*SHADE+ENV` | **ADD** |
| `fc159a04 5ffefff8` | `(0-0)*0+COMB` | `(TEX0-0)*ENV` | MODULATE |
| `fcffffff fffe7838` | `(0-0)*0+COMB` | `SHADE` | REPLACE |

So "9 REPLACE + 1 ADD" was never derivable from the census predicate - it
conflated the two tests. **Fitting the classifier to the expected total would
have been the exact error this gate exists to prevent**, so the gate instead
asserts the two invariants that ARE load-bearing, and both hold:

```
INVARIANTS hold: the glass word is ADD, and every texel-free simplification is REPLACE.
```

#### Facility, and the ADD count now reconciles

400-frame boot, `SL_ALPHA_EQ=1`, counts **after simplification**:

```
replace=238527  modulate=592437  add=297756
genuine-ADD attributed to 1 distinct combiner word: fc26a004 1f1093fb  tris=297756
```

Every ADD triangle is the tinted-glass word. The 12.7M contradiction is gone.

A longer 900-frame boot reaches a second: `fc159804 5ffedbf8` (378825 tris),
the character-fade family - correctly ADD, since it simplifies to
`(TEX0-ENV)*SHADE+ENV`. **Its pixels did not change in any captured frame**,
so it is classified but not yet exercised, and that is a gap, not a clearance.

#### What changed on facility, named

**Boot sequence** (5 captures, 640x480, off vs on, run alone): 2 identical,
3 differing, each by **4480 pixels, all darker, max delta 46**, in one
rectangle `x[522,639] y[200,248]`. Before: **3469 pixels of exactly
`(10,20,10)`**. After: all `(0,0,0)`.

That is the tinted-glass pane going opaque - and **3469 is the exact count the
first B-051 measurement recorded on pre-gas facility on 2026-08-26**. The fix
lands on the originally reported region, from the level's own opening camera.

**The owner's marked window** (`read=10103`): 14390 of 14390 masked pixels
change to `(0,0,0)`, md5 `1eb7974d6801…` - **byte-identical to both the
pre-correction general path and the one-combiner `SL_GLASS_MARK=3`
experiment.** Three independently written paths agreeing exactly.

**Default inertness**: with `SL_ALPHA_EQ` unset the frame is `50d3f58f0216…`,
byte-identical to the pre-fix binary.

#### Not done, stated plainly

- **The B-048 standard is not met.** This is facility only, by instruction:
  rooms, viewmodel, HUD, the font-path title card and the intro camera are
  covered; **characters in motion and the menus are not**, and
  `fc159804 5ffedbf8` - the character-fade word - is classified ADD and
  unexercised.
- **`SL_ALPHA_EQ` stays OFF.** Nothing here authorises flipping it.
- **The `facility-glass` ROM recording is separate** and does not gate this:
  the RDP equation is the authority for the decoder; the cartridge verifies
  final pixels afterward.
- **The AEQ_ADD approximation stands**: GL 1.3 has no fixed-function
  multiply-add, so `tex.a * SHADE.a + PRIM.a` renders as `tex.a + PRIM.a` -
  exact when SHADE.a is 255, which the glass measures, and an over-estimate
  otherwise. `fc159804 5ffedbf8` is the word most likely to expose it.
