### B-051 — the ROM DEBUG ORACLE: the cartridge now names the object the crosshair is on. Built, measured, and it perturbs the run once you use it. 2026-08-27

This investigation kept losing time to **object identity by inference**. The
live player position could not be read reliably, so which of twenty tinted-glass
panes the owner was looking at had to be guessed, so the glare/material
comparison against the cartridge was blocked. This is the instrument that
removes the guess, plus every control that was run against it - including the
two that came back negative.

**Nothing here is committed and `SL_ALPHA_EQ` is untouched.**

#### What was built

`SIGHTLINE_ROM_DEBUG`: a compile-time mode that puts a debug mailbox inside the
ROM. `make trace-debug LEVEL=facility SL_NAME=facility-pane` builds
`build/u/direct/ge007.u.facility-pane.dbg.z64` alongside - never over - the
parity ROM. Host side is `tools/native/rominspect.py`.

- ROM side is deliberately minimal and lives in `src/game/lv.c` under one
  `#ifdef`, called once per frame straight after `chraiCheckUseHeldItems()`.
  **It is not in a file of its own**: a new object in the link is exactly what
  `make matching` compares byte for byte, whereas an `#ifdef`'d block in a file
  already linked cannot move a byte of the matching ROM. Layout and the rules
  are documented in `src/game/sl_romdbg.h`.
- **SELECT is not a new raycaster.** It calls `sub_GAME_7F04E9BC()` - the
  function a bullet uses - over `g_OnScreenPropList`, the list gunfire walks. A
  second raycaster is a second instrument that can disagree with the first.
- **FINDTYPE** (`--find-type 47`) lists every on-screen prop of one PROPDEF,
  nearest first, with `prop->flags` and whether the prop passes the gate at the
  top of `sub_GAME_7F04E9BC`. Without it, a SELECT that finds no pane cannot be
  told apart from a level with no pane on screen or a pane failing the shot
  gate. `--find-type -1` lists everything on screen.
- **`make matching` is still MATCH!** - verified twice, before and after the
  final source state.

#### Control 2, and it came back NEGATIVE: no pad bit is safe

Asked to bind capture to Select and verify Select is unconsumed. It cannot be,
for two independent reasons, both established rather than assumed:

1. **The N64 has no Select button**, and parallel_n64 reaches only real N64
   buttons - `emu_libretro.py`'s `BUTTON_MAP` was MEASURED against the running
   game and its own comment records that libretro id 8 "this core ignores
   entirely". A Select press cannot physically reach the ROM as a button.
2. **Even the N64's own spare bits are consumed.** `cheat.c:879` calls
   `joyGetButtons(ANY_BUTTON)` and `joyGetButtonsPressedThisFrame(ANY_BUTTON)`
   **during gameplay** and writes the raw pressed-button word into
   `g_CurrentPlayer->cheatInputBuffer`, advancing `cheatInputBufferIndex` and
   `cheatInputCount`. Any bit set - including 0x0040, the hardware's unused one
   - changes player state. Search backing the claim:
   `grep -rn "joyGetButtons" src/ --include=*.c`; the `ANY_BUTTON` / `0xFFFF`
   readers are `boss.c:542`, `cheat.c:879`, `options.c:1143/1247`,
   `ramromreplay.c:334`, `spectrum.c:260`, `lv.c:1217/1501`,
   `bondview2.c:4866`, `front.c:1466/1660`.

**The alternative shipped instead**, and it keeps every property that mattered.
`InputFrame` bit 14 is reserved as `DBG_SELECT`, the recorder maps the
DualSense Create button to it, and it is recorded in the `.input` stream like
any other button - but it is **never handed to the core**. The host writes it
into the mailbox. So the normal ROM cannot consume the trigger *because the
trigger never reaches the console*, which is strictly stronger than an unused
button. One recording still drives both builds, and the four existing
recordings stay valid. Bit 14 is not arbitrary: under the shim's pad encoding
it is the N64 word's unused 0x0040, so the bit means the same thing natively.

#### Control 1, and it came back NEGATIVE TWICE — read both parts

**Part 1: the debug ROM's trace does NOT match the normal ROM's, and no ROM
modification ever could.**

`facility-pane`, 7418 ticks, debug ROM vs the recording's own `.sltrace`:
diverges at **tick 79, `currentFrameCounter=0`, globals only**. Field-level
dump over ticks 75-84 says the ONLY divergent global is `rng_seed`.

Cause, and it is not the instrument: **`boss.c:389` seeds the RNG from the CPU
cycle counter.**

```c
nowCount = osGetCount();
randomSetSeed(nowCount);
```

Measured, not inferred: at tick 79 the debug ROM's seed is `0x1465a73a7` and
`hook_calls == 0` with `magic == 0`, i.e. **the debug hook had not run even
once** when the seed already differed.

**The control that proves it is generic.** `ROM_SIZECTL=1` builds an unmodified
game with ~0x230 bytes of inert `const` padding and no code at all
(`sl_romdbg_sizectl` in `lv.c`). Its trace diverges from the parity trace at
**tick 79, fc=0, globals only** - the same tick, the same shape, the same
single field. So the divergence belongs to the ROM IMAGE, not to the
instrument, and "the debug ROM must reproduce the normal ROM's trace" is
unachievable for any change whatsoever, including a one-instruction one.

`trace.py diff` gained `--across-roms` for exactly this comparison and refuses
everything else that makes two traces incomparable. The debug trace is written
to `build/trace/`, **never** to `tools/trace/traces/`: `trace-verify` globs that
directory and treats every `.sltrace` in it as a level, so a stray
`facility-pane.dbg.sltrace` fails the entire gate hunting for an `.input` that
does not exist. Found by doing it.

**Part 2 - the control that DOES isolate the instrument, and it also fails.**
Same debug ROM image, so the boot seed is identical; the only difference is
whether the mailbox was commanded.

| run | commands | game ticks in 7418 frames | hook_calls | diverges from quiet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| quiet | none | 2906 | 2907 | - |
| one | ONE FINDTYPE, at input index 424 | 2394 | 2394 | **tick 529** |
| busy | FINDTYPE every 20 frames, 361 of them | 2571 | 2571 | **tick 529** |

**One command diverges at exactly the same tick as three hundred and
sixty-one**, on the same two entities. So the cost is not the volume of
commands - it is the per-frame sampling that a command switches on, and it
starts biting about 110 game ticks after the command. The tick counts
themselves differ, which is the tell: the game's
main loop is paced against `osGetCount()`, so the extra work the hook does on
the emulated CPU changes how many game ticks fit in a frame, and
frame-rate-dependent state follows.

**What that licenses, stated as narrowly as it deserves.** A capture is valid
for the frame it is taken on and for every frame before it - the identification
itself is sound, because the state read is the state the game had when the
command was seen. **Everything after a command is a different run.** So:

- "which pane am I looking at, at this marked moment" - **sound**.
- "log this pane every frame for the rest of the recording" - **the log is
  real, but it is a log of a run that has diverged from the recorded one**,
  measurably so from roughly 110 game ticks after the command.

This is not fixable by making the hook cheaper. On a cycle-paced game any added
work changes the run; cheaper only moves the divergence later. An oracle inside
the ROM cannot be non-perturbing here, and that is the finding.

#### What the instrument then MEASURED, and it closes a question

Swept all four ROM recordings (`facility-pane`, `facility-props`,
`facility-props2`, `facility-tank-visibility` - all four share a byte-identical
direct-boot ROM, verified with `cmp`, so one debug ROM serves all four) with
FINDTYPE for `PROPDEF_TINTED_GLASS` (47):

```
facility-pane              2 panes on screen, input index 424-580
facility-props             2 panes on screen, input index 424-780
facility-props2            NONE, whole run
facility-tank-visibility   NONE, whole run
PROPDEF_GLASS (42)         NONE on screen in facility-props2, whole run
```

Both panes are the same two objects, and their distance from the player over
every frame they are visible:

```
prop 0x8006cb58  obj 0x801cfe8c  distance 6641.1 .. 7591.2
prop 0x8006cb24  obj 0x801cfdf8  distance ~7613
TintDist 400   CullDist 600   unk90 0.0   portal 82 (rooms 62 <-> 68)
calculatedopacity 255 on EVERY frame, portal DISABLED on every frame
```

**The distance that decides opacity is the PLAYER PROP's, not the camera's.**
`glassCalculateOpacity` (propobj.c:4203) measures from
`getCurrentPlayerProp()->pos`, and the capture reports exactly that number. It
matters here: at input index 425 the aim origin - the camera - is
`(8270.7, 280.7, -3480.9)`, roughly 1500 units from the pane at
`(6933.8, 159.1, -2178.2)`, while the player prop is still at the spawn,
`(113.6, 392.8, -956.5)`. During the intro fly-through the camera can be right
next to a pane and the game still computes its opacity from the spawn point.
Anyone matching a screenshot to a distance will get this wrong; the capture
publishes both positions so the mistake is visible rather than latent.

**`CullDist` is 600 and the nearest a pane ever gets in any of the four ROM
recordings is 6641.** That is a factor of eleven outside the band the owner's
report lives in, and it is the same shape as the `facility-gas` dead end
recorded earlier in this file (minimum 1637.6 there). **None of the four
recordings contains the case under investigation** - and now that is a
measurement with a named object and a per-frame distance series behind it,
rather than an absence.

Every SELECT fired over indices 400-800, step 4 - the whole window where the
panes are on screen - returned **MISS**. The panes pass the shot gate
(`shot-gate PASS` in every FIND capture), so they are shootable; the crosshair
simply is not on them. At ~6900 units they are a few pixels of an intro camera.

**What is still needed is one recording**: walk the security-door corridor and
stop 600-900 units short of the window, pressing the reserved bit at the pane.
That was already the standing request; this tool is what will make the result
unambiguous when it exists.

#### A seventh instrument fault, caught by the instrument itself

The first version identified a watched prop by its `PropRecord*` plus the
back-pointer check `obj->prop == prop` - which the game's own code uses.
**Measured on `facility-props`: a pane watched at `0x8006cb58` was still being
sampled thousands of frames later as `objtype 11`, at the same address, reading
entirely healthy.** The prop slot had been freed and reused, and the
back-pointer passed just as happily for the new occupant. That is object
identity by inference reappearing *inside the tool built to delete it*.

Fixed: the `ObjectRecord*` and the `PROPDEF` are pinned at selection time and
both must still agree, otherwise the sample publishes `SL_DBG_EV_LOST` and
stops watching. A pointer is not an identity.

Two smaller ones, same session, same shape:

- **The ROM hook does not run on every emulator frame** (~32-40% - the in-game
  render path is reached on a subset). On the others the mailbox still held the
  previous frame's `event` word, so the host reported the same capture two and
  three times: a 361-point sweep produced 527 "captures". Events are now
  counted once per `rom_seq`.
- **`aim_origin` / `aim_dir` read (0,0,0)** on any record a SELECT did not
  produce, because only SELECT filled them. A per-frame sample whose aim vector
  is all zeroes invites exactly the inference this instrument exists to remove;
  they are now published on every record.

#### Deliberate design points worth not re-deciding

- **SELECT does not call `bullet_path_from_screen_center()`.** That function
  calls `RANDOMFRAC()` four times to apply weapon spread, and the RNG cursor is
  hashed by the trace. The deterministic half - the crosshair angle through
  `transformAndNormalizeByLength2Dto3D()` - is reproduced instead, which also
  gives the crosshair CENTRE rather than a spread-perturbed sample of it.
- **SELECT does not test the background**, so it never calls `stanResetHits()`
  and `maxdist` stays unbounded: a prop behind a wall can appear. The whole
  candidate list is published, nearest first, so that is visible not hidden.
- **SELECT does not test characters.** `chrTestHit()`'s side effects are not
  established, and glass is never a `PROP_TYPE_CHR`.
- **The mailbox is treated as a DMA buffer** - `osInvalDCache()` before reading
  the host's half, `osWritebackDCache()` after writing ours. Without it the
  command is served from the data cache and never seen, which reads as "the
  instrument does nothing".
- **One writer, one reader for RDRAM.** `sltrace.state.Memory` already
  centralised the word-swapped reads; `Memory.w32()` is now the single writer.
  `tools/native/romprobe.py` still defines big-endian `u32`/`f32` helpers it
  never calls - they remain a trap, and nothing new copies them.

#### Known-positive controls, because an instrument that cannot fail is worthless

- `hook_calls` advances unconditionally every frame the hook runs; a run that
  ends with it at zero prints FAILED and exits 3.
- The ROM publishes its own `sizeof`; the host refuses to decode if it
  disagrees with the mirrored offset table (`mailbox v3, size 0x230 - layout
  OK`).
- FINDTYPE turns a null SELECT into one of three distinguishable measurements
  rather than a shrug.
- `ROM_SIZECTL=1` is the control for the whole debug-ROM comparison and is what
  turned "my instrument perturbs the boot" into "every ROM image does".

#### Not built, stated plainly rather than left to be discovered

Combiner words, simplified RGB/alpha equations, PRIM/ENV/SHADE ranges, blender
mode, fog state, texture id/format/dimensions and their statistics, and
triangles emitted are **not** in the report. On the cartridge those live in a
display list handed to the RSP, and recovering them means a second decoder in
RDRAM with its own failure modes. The native renderer already decodes exactly
those (`SL_ALPHA_EQ`, `sl_gfx_dl.c`); this capture's job is to say WHICH object
the native side should be compared against. The report says so in its own
output. Treat the absence as unbuilt, not as absent.

Also unbuilt: type-specific decoders beyond glass (doors, guards). Glass first,
because that is the live question.
#### 2026-08-27: the oracle now SPEAKS WHILE YOU PLAY. `make trace-record-debug`

The instrument above was correct and silent, which for two sessions made it
useless. The owner recorded with `make trace-record`, aimed, pressed Create,
and **the terminal printed nothing** - no confirmation the press registered, no
statement of what was targeted. Both attempts produced `hits=0`, discovered
afterwards from a replay, with no way to tell a press that missed from a press
that never happened. That is a usability defect, and it was blocking the one
recording this investigation needs.

**What was built: live feedback, against the DEBUG ROM.** Not the fallback.

```
make trace-record-debug LEVEL=facility SL_NAME=facility-glass AIM_AID=47
```

Builds `ge007.u.facility-glass.dbg.z64`, records against it, and drives the
mailbox from inside the recorder. Every Create press answers immediately:

```
capture 1  frame 4812  HIT   prop 0x800c93f0  type 0x2f TINTED_GLASS  dist 512.4  opacity 255  portal 82  playerdist 588.1
capture 2  frame 5140  MISS  (crosshair on no prop; 14 props on screen)
          on screen, nearest first: PROP 384, DOOR 512, TINTED_GLASS 1840
capture 3  frame 5390  MISS  (not aiming - no crosshair)
capture 4  frame ?     NOT SERVED  the press was recorded, but the game never ran the debug hook
```

**The three cases are separated by a MEASUREMENT, not by a guess.** Mailbox v4
publishes `g_CurrentPlayer->gunsightmode` and `mpmenuon` every frame, which are
the two words `gunDrawSight()` itself tests (`gunfire.c:6276`) - so "no
crosshair" is the crosshair, not a proxy for it, and the reason is named from
the `GUNSIGHTREASON_*` bits (`bondconstants.h:2866`): not aiming, no control,
taking damage. A fourth case falls out of the protocol for free and is worth as
much as the other three: a press the ROM never acknowledges within three
seconds is reported NOT SERVED rather than dropped, which is what a press in a
menu, a cutscene or a pause looks like.

**The aiming aid, default OFF.** `AIM_AID=47` prints the nearest TINTED_GLASS
and its distance - but only when that line CHANGES, so standing still is
silent. It uses a new `SL_DBG_CMD_NEAREST`, which is FINDTYPE's listing with
the watch-taking removed: a periodic aid must never be able to replace the
identity a deliberate SELECT just pinned. The same command answers "what WAS on
screen" after a MISS.

**The recorder says what the recording is, at both ends of the run.** A
debug-ROM stream is an INSPECTION artefact and is not interchangeable with a
parity recording - the debug ROM is knowingly non-matching, and a capture press
perturbs the run from about 110 game ticks later (both measured above). The
banner prints before the session and after it, and names the command to make a
clean recording instead. `trace-record-debug` also REFUSES to overwrite a name
that already has a parity `.sltrace`, because that would silently invalidate
every gate result keyed to that recording's content.

**One mirror, not two.** The mailbox layout, decoder and report moved to
`tools/trace/sltrace/romdbg.py`; `rominspect.py` imports them. Two hand-mirrored
copies of a MIPS struct is two chances to drift from `sl_romdbg.h`.

**Controls, because an instrument that cannot fail is worthless:**

- `--synth-select 400,450,500` synthesises Create presses, so the live path can
  be fired on demand with no pad and no display. Run under xvfb against the
  facility-pane debug ROM: three presses, three capture lines, one aim-aid
  line. The aid reported the nearest pane at **7613 units**; an independent
  `rominspect --find-type 47` on the same ROM reported **7613.0**. Two paths,
  one number.
- `--synth-select 5,...` fires before the in-game hook exists: reported
  `NOT SERVED`, `1 never served`. The failure mode is visible.
- `tools/trace/tests/test_romdbg.py` - 19 stdlib-only tests, no ROM, no core,
  no display - drives LiveCapture against a synthetic mailbox and asserts every
  branch, including the HIT line a headless run cannot reach because nobody is
  holding the controller. It also compares every offset in `romdbg.py` against
  the `/* 0xNN */` annotations in `sl_romdbg.h`, so layout drift is a test
  failure.
- That offset test earned its keep immediately: it caught `PROPDEF_DOOR = 4`
  sitting unused in `rominspect.py` when the enum says **1**. Type names are now
  read from `bondconstants.h` rather than hand-copied, and the wrong constant is
  gone.

**Verified:** `make matching` **MATCH!** before and after (every added line is
inside `#ifdef SIGHTLINE_ROM_DEBUG`); `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility-pane`
IDENTICAL; 65 harness tests pass; the debug ROM's own control reports
`hook ran 131 times` over a 600-frame run.

**Still not done, and it is the same thing as before:** one recording that
walks the security-door corridor and stops 600-900 units short of the window.
The instrument can now tell the owner, live, whether they are there.


### B-051/B-032 — bullet decals on glass: SPAWNED and SUBMITTED, ZERO PIXELS. The cause is the B-032 bitfield read at its SECOND, uncorrected site, and it is on the prop hit path. 2026-08-27

The owner's report: *"bullet decals on glass windows are only visible when there
is a PROP behind the glass. If there is just a wall behind it, the decals do not
appear."*

**Measured end to end on the owner's own native recording**
`~/.sightline/runs/20260827-181853-lvl34`, which turned out to contain twelve
shots into two `PROPDEF_TINTED_GLASS` panes. Nothing here is inferred from a
screenshot or from reading code alone; every number below came out of a run.

#### The three-way split, settled

The brief's split - not spawned / spawned-not-submitted / submitted-not-visible
- resolves to the **third**, and the first two are ruled out by counters that
also have a known-positive:

```
                                       creates  quads/frame  pixels contributed
background decal, wall at spawn             85           85               6147
glass-pane decal, owner's recording         12          3-5                  0
```

The 6147 is the positive control and it matters: **background bullet decals ARE
drawn natively**, which closes the last open item of B-032 ("still unproven, and
it needs the display: that decals are DRAWN"). The instrument is
`SL_DECAL_HIDE=1`, which emits every command of the impact draw EXCEPT the two
triangles, so an A/B of two otherwise identical replays counts exactly the
pixels the decal puts on screen. On glass that count is **0 on every one of the
ten captured frames across the whole shooting window (4050-4650)**, with quads
provably submitted on each.

#### Root cause: `propobj.c` objHit reads the wrong bitfield, and only glass notices

B-032 corrected `chrprop.c:1127` - the BACKGROUND hit - because
`struct image_entry` declares `hitSound:4` then `hitTexture:4`, and IDO fills
bitfields from the most significant bit while GCC fills from the least, so a raw
byte-0 mask selects a **different field on each platform**. B-032 recorded that
the object-model twins "are NOT yet fixed - they are the object-model equivalent
and should be done when object hits are next exercised". This is that.

The site is `objHit`'s `countsAsPenetration != 0` branch:

```c
impact_sounds = g_HitTypeSounds[((u8 *)&g_Textures[texturenum])[0] & 0x0f];
```

Measured, with a probe printing both nibbles at the moment of the hit:

```
12 OBJHIT propdef=47 tex=654 raw-nibble=4 hitSound=4 hitTexture=12 *** NIBBLES DIFFER ***
 7 OBJHIT propdef=3  tex=396 raw-nibble=2 hitSound=2 hitTexture=2  same
 6 OBJHIT propdef=1  tex=687 raw-nibble=3 hitSound=3 hitTexture=3  same
 1 OBJHIT propdef=3  tex=220 raw-nibble=2 hitSound=2 hitTexture=2  same
```

Texture 654 is `GLASS3`. **Blast radius, recounted independently rather than
quoted from B-032:** of 2698 `IMAGE(...)` rows in `assets/images.def` exactly
three have `hitSound != hitTexture` - 653, GLASS3, 655, all `HIT_GLASS` vs
`HIT_GLASS_XLU`. So this one read is wrong for glass and correct for the other
2695. That is why nothing else in the game shows it.

#### Why a wrong nibble makes the decal invisible rather than merely wrong-looking

The two table entries carry **different impact types** (`tex.c:48` and `:104`):

```
HIT_GLASS      glass_impact_types[]             = {0x4, 0x5, 0x6}
HIT_GLASS_XLU  translucent_glass_impact_types[] = {0x11, 0x12, 0x13}
```

and `g_ImpactTypes` (`explosion.c:189`, `s_impacttype = {width, height,
apptype, unk1, unk2}`) gives those two groups different `unk2`:

```
types 4,5,6        {6,8,12 px}  apptype 1  unk1 2  unk2 8
types 0x11-0x13    {6,8,12 px}  apptype 1  unk1 2  unk2 1
```

Same sizes - so the decal does not look different, it lands somewhere different
in the frame. `unk2` is load-bearing twice over:

1. **The pass.** `explosionCreateBulletImpact` (`explosion.c`) classifies with
   `(unk2 < 2) && (unk1 == 2)`: true sets `PROPSTATE_2` (0x02), false sets
   `PROPSTATE_DAMAGED` (0x01) (`bondconstants.h:529-530`). `propobj.c:7426`
   then renders a prop's decals only in the pass whose bit is set,
   `if (obj->state & (1 << arg2))`. So the cartridge's glass decal is a
   **pass-1** decal and ours is a **pass-0** decal.
2. **The render mode.** `texSelect` passes `unk2` as `zbufferMode` into
   `texSetRenderMode` (`othermodemicrocode.c:171`): `>= 2` gives
   `G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_DECAL`, `1` gives `G_RM_AA_ZB_XLU_SURF`. Confirmed in the
   renderer's own histogram - render mode `0c1849d8` (`zmode=2`) appears in the
   corrected arm and in NO frame of the broken arm.

**Where the passes are emitted, and why pass 0 loses.** The panes carry
`flags=0x00000006`, so neither `PROPFLAG_RENDERPOSTBG` (0x01) nor
`PROPFLAG_00000020` is set, and `chrpropsRenderPass` gives them their `arg2=0`
render in **renderpass 0 at `bg.c:682` - BEFORE `bgRenderRoomPrimary` for that
same room**, inside a loop that walks rooms in ASCENDING portal depth
(`unk1`, set by `sub_GAME_7F0B39BC`), i.e. the player's room first and the room
behind the glass later. The `arg2=1` render is `bg.c:773`, in the second loop,
after all background geometry. Decal render modes do not write depth (measured:
every `zmode=3` entry in `sl_rm` has `zupd=0`), so a pass-0 decal on a window
is laid down before the geometry visible THROUGH that window and is painted
over by it.

**The discriminator that makes this the operative half, rather than the render
mode.** The background decals at spawn that contribute 6147 pixels use impact
type 7, which is also `unk1=2, unk2=8`, i.e. the **same `XLU_DECAL` mode** as
the invisible glass decal. So `XLU_DECAL` rasterises perfectly well. What
differs is where in the frame the draw is emitted: background impacts go out
once at `bg.c:732`, after every room's primary geometry; the glass pane's go out
at `bg.c:682`, before the room behind is drawn. Stated as narrowly as it
deserves: this is an inference from two measurements that differ in exactly one
variable, not a direct isolation of pass-vs-mode. Isolating it would need a
build that changes the pass without changing the mode, and that was not done.

#### The fix, and its evidence

`SL_HITTEX=1`, **DEFAULT OFF**, one site, `src/game/propobj.c`, native-only
behind `#ifdef __sgi` / `#else`: read `g_Textures[texturenum].hitTexture` by
name. Same correction, same reasoning and same corroboration B-032 used
(`chr.c:3561` reads `hitTexture` from this table by name).

Its own positive control passes before any pixel is looked at: with the toggle
on, the twelve glass hits create impact types **17/18/19** instead of **4/5/6**,
which is `HIT_GLASS_XLU` exactly.

Four arms of the same replay, differing only in `SL_HITTEX` and
`SL_DECAL_HIDE`, 640x480, one capture every 50 rendered frames:

```
frame   decal px, SL_HITTEX=0   decal px, SL_HITTEX=1   px the fix changes
4000            0                       0                    0
4050            0                     163                  163
4100            0                     595                  595
4150            0                    1529                 1529
4200            0                    1843                 1843
4250            0                   17581                17581
4300            0                    8637                 8637
4350            0                    4582                 4582
4400            0                    5072                 5072
4450            0                    7328                 7328
4500            0                       0                    0     (pane off screen)
4550            0                       0                    0     (pane off screen)
4600            0                     791                  791
4650            0                    2297                 2297
4700            0                       0                    0     (pane off screen)
```

The third column equals the second on every single frame, which is the
containment check: **the only pixels the fix touches are the decal's own.** By
eye at frame 4300 the corrected arm puts six starburst bullet holes on the pane
and the current build puts none.

**Verified:** `make matching` **MATCH!** before and after (every added line is
inside `#ifndef __sgi`); `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility`; `make bootsweep`.
`trace-verify` cannot see this either way - it replays the matching ROM through
the emulator, so a native-only defect on this path is invisible to all 117
traces, which is why the gate has been green throughout.

#### Two zeros that were nearly believed, recorded because the brief warned about exactly this

- **The first A/B compared frame 4700 and reported 0 for all four arms**,
  including fix-vs-broken. The pane is not on screen at 4700 - the player has
  walked into the next corridor. A zero from a frame that cannot show the thing
  is not evidence, and the toggle's create-side control (types 4/5/6 ->
  17/18/19) is what proved the toggle was live before the sweep was rerun.
- **"51059 room rejections"** looked like the answer for about a minute. It was
  a grep artefact: the per-frame summary line contains the text
  `ROOM-REJECTED:0`. The real count of reject EVENTS is a separate line, and
  the correlation that matters came out flat: **0 of 178 background creates in
  the owner's recording were room-rejected within 20 frames of being made.**
  The `getROOMID_isRendered` gate is doing exactly Rare's job - dropping decals
  in rooms you have walked away from - and is not implicated.

#### Ruled out by measurement - do not re-investigate

- **`SL_ALPHA_EQ`.** Not involved. The corrected and broken arms differ only in
  which `g_HitTypeSounds` row is read; the alpha equation is identical in both,
  and the fix restores the pixels with `SL_ALPHA_EQ` at its committed default.
- **Portal traversal / room visibility.** See the 0-of-178 correlation above.
- **The decal never spawning.** 12 of 12 tinted-glass hits create an impact.
- **Polygon offset / decal zmode translation.** `zmode=3` draws are visible -
  6147 pixels of them at spawn, under the same `XLU_DECAL` mode the glass decal
  was using. The renderer's zmode decode also matches the notes exactly:
  `ucode05_old.txt:326-329` gives the depthmode group as `0x00000000` depth opa,
  `0x00000400` interpolate, `0x00000800` exclusive, `0x00000C00` **depth
  decrement**, which is `sl_gfx_dl.c`'s `RM_ZMODE_DEC`.

#### What is NOT established

- **The "prop behind the glass" half of the owner's sentence.** The recording
  contains glass with a wall behind it and nothing else, so the contrast the
  owner describes was never measured. The mechanism above explains the "wall
  behind -> no decal" half completely. The other half is CONSISTENT with the
  shot penetrating the glass and the decal landing on the prop instead - an
  ordinary prop decal, drawn immediately after its own prop's geometry in the
  same pass (`propobj.c:7420-7428`), on a texture whose two nibbles agree - but
  that is a hypothesis, not a measurement. **The recording that would settle it
  is one that shoots a pane with a prop right behind it and a pane with only a
  wall behind it, in the same run.**
- **Whether the pass or the render mode is what zeroes the pixels.** See the
  discriminator paragraph above; the evidence points at the pass, and it was not
  isolated directly.
- **The other two twins.** `propobj.c` `sub_GAME_7F0511B8` still has the two
  `| 0x80000000` texture-number reads B-032 named as unfixed. Untouched here.

#### In the tree, nothing committed

- `src/game/propobj.c` - `SL_HITTEX` (default OFF), plus a read-only
  `SL_DECAL_DBG` probe printing both nibbles at each object hit.
- `src/game/explosion.c` - `SL_DECAL_DBG` (create log with the attached prop's
  PROPDEF, and per-frame counts split by gate: matched / room>=0 /
  `getROOMID_isRendered` / pass / quads emitted) and `SL_DECAL_HIDE`, the A/B
  control that removes only the rasterisation. All `#ifndef __sgi`, all default
  OFF, `make matching` MATCH! with them present.

### B-077 — the large-texture grid/stitch seams are NOT a texture-addressing defect. B-052 REFUTED as their cause. 2026-09-02

Owner observation after `a304d726`: tinted glass is accepted and closed, but
visible grid/stitch lines remain across textured surfaces on **doors, security
consoles and other props with LARGER TEXTURES**. The correlation with larger
textures was the new datum, and B-052 was the standing suspect.

**B-052 does not cause this, and neither does anything else in the tile chain.**
Every stage from the F5 settile through the F3 loadblock to the decoded GL
texture measures CORRECT on Facility. Recording the measurement in full so the
next person does not re-derive it, and so the next objective aims downstream of
here instead.

#### The notes, consulted before the decomp (rule 7)

The unit of a tmem address, and the fact that one load covers several tiles,
are both settled by the corpus rather than by this tree:

- `Display Lists and Object Generation/ucode05_old.txt`, `F5 rdp_settile`
  upper word: `0x000001FF tmem`. Nine bits, 512 addressable units across the
  RDP's texture memory — so **one unit is a 64-bit word, eight bytes**. The
  same entry gives `0x0003FE00 line`, `0x0003C000 mask t` and `0x000000F0
  mask s` in the lower word.
- `images text and font/7F076D68 - generate DL for ImgDecl.txt` is the game's
  own mip-chain generator and steps that cursor in the same unit: line 985,
  `tmem += tilesize`, where `tilesize` is height * width-rounded-up-to-a-word
  (the four depth cases at :864, :884, :904, :924 each round the width to a
  word / doubleword / quadword before multiplying by the height, and the SAME
  rounded figure is written as the F5 `line`). The generator also sets
  `mask s` = "nearest root to width" and `mask t` = "nearest root to height",
  i.e. **ceil(log2(dimension))**.
- One F3 covers the whole chain: `texGetDepthAndSize` (`src/game/tex.c:358`)
  sums `texGetSizeInBytes(tex, lod)` over every lod into the single length
  `texWriteLoadToTmemAddr` hands to `gDPLoadBlock` (`tex.c:514`).

So B-052's proposed arithmetic — `source + (tile.tmem - load.tmem) * 8` — is
the right arithmetic. It is simply never needed by anything Facility draws.

#### Was B-052 repaired between then and now? NO — measured

`git log -S tmem_find --all` returns three commits: `3ef85c17` (B-023, pairs a
tile with the image at its own tmem), `636e4871` (B-048, TEXEL1) and
`fbad9809` (the B-052 doc entry itself). Nothing after `fbad9809` touches the
resolver, and `tmem_find` in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` still matches on
`g_tmem[i].tmem == tmem` alone. B-052's DEFECT is real and still present.

#### The census, and why zero is believable here

A temporary `SL_TMEMCENSUS` arm classified every `tile_texture` resolution
into FIVE classes — EXACT / INTERIOR / BEYOND / FALLBACK-last-load / NO-LOAD —
and printed the counts whether or not they were zero. **Windowed** Facility
(`SL_WINDOW=1`, 960x720, stage 34, 400 frames), because a headless run has no
backend and last round one reported success while producing no renderer
telemetry at all:

```
sl_tmemcensus: tile_texture calls=241654  distinct=27 (lost 0)
  EXACT              draws=241654  of which >32x32=113495
  INTERIOR           draws=0       of which >32x32=0
  BEYOND             draws=0       of which >32x32=0
  FALLBACK-last-load draws=0       of which >32x32=0
  NO-LOAD            draws=0       of which >32x32=0
```

241654 resolutions, 27 distinct tiles, **every one of them tile 0 at
`tile.tmem = 0`, every one an exact load-start match**. The renderer binds
`G_TX_RENDERTILE` and nothing else, and that tile always sits at the load's
own start address, so the interior case B-052 describes is never reached by
consumed output. The class counts are not "measured nothing" — the run drew
1026 textured triangles per frame from 108 decoded images with
`reject[...]=0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0`.

#### The control, and the hypothesis it killed

The obvious replacement suspect was the wrap period. `mask s` / `mask t` are
**decoded nowhere in this tree** — tree-wide `grep -rn` over `src/gfx/` and
`src/platform/` for the field extractions and for `mask_s|mask_t|maskt|masks`
returns only a 4bpp nibble decode and a colour-ID shift, neither a mask — and
`struct sl_tile` has no such member. The renderer instead wraps with
`GL_REPEAT` over a texture sized from the F2 settilesize. If Rare's 2^mask
ever disagreed with that size on a REPEATING axis, every repeat would drift
and show a seam, which is exactly the reported symptom.

Decoded and compared, per distinct tile, on the same run:

```
64x64 fmt=4 siz=0 line=4 | F2 s[2,254] t[2,254] | mask 6,6 -> 64x64 | cms=0 cmt=0 | agrees    | draws=37970
32x32 fmt=2 siz=1 line=4 | F2 s[2,126] t[2,126] | mask 5,5 -> 32x32 | cms=0 cmt=0 | agrees    | draws=102253
64x32 fmt=4 siz=0 line=4 | F2 s[2,254] t[2,126] | mask 6,5 -> 64x32 | cms=0 cmt=0 | agrees    | draws=16980
54x54 fmt=3 siz=1 line=7 | F2 s[2,214] t[2,214] | mask 6,6 -> 64x64 | cms=2 cmt=2 | DISAGREES | draws=434
38x38 fmt=2 siz=1 line=5 | F2 s[2,150] t[2,150] | mask 6,6 -> 64x64 | cms=2 cmt=2 | DISAGREES | draws=656
48x32 fmt=2 siz=1 line=6 | F2 s[2,190] t[2,126] | mask 6,5 -> 64x32 | cms=2 cmt=0 | DISAGREES | draws=2304
32x48 fmt=2 siz=1 line=4 | F2 s[2,126] t[2,190] | mask 5,6 -> 32x64 | cms=2 cmt=2 | DISAGREES | draws=28618
32x33 fmt=2 siz=1 line=4 | F2 s[0,124] t[0,128] | mask 5,6 -> 32x64 | cms=2 cmt=2 | DISAGREES | draws=6912
```

25 of 31 agree, 6 disagree — so the instrument could and did print both
answers, which is the whole point of running it. But **every disagreeing axis
is a CLAMPED axis**: the six are all the non-power-of-two images, Rare sets
`clamp` on exactly the axis whose 2^mask overshoots the real dimension, and
`tex_wrap` already maps that bit to `GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE`. On every axis that
actually REPEATS, `2^mask` equals the size the renderer divides by. The wrap
period is correct everywhere in the level. Hypothesis refuted by its own
control.

#### Everything else in the chain also measures right

- **Stride.** `sl_tex: stride disagreements=0 of 27 distinct` — the padded
  NPOT rows (`54 -> line=7` = 56 bytes, `38 -> line=5` = 40) are decoded at
  the declared `line*8`, not at the width.
- **Format.** `tile-fmt vs FD-fmt: 0 of 0 disagree`.
- **Dimensions.** `reject[dim,size,unmapped,pal,decode,fmt,tilesize,nogl]` is
  all zeros over 108 images; `TEX_MAX_DIM` (256) is never approached.
- **The half-texel window is not an error.** Every world tile carries
  `uls = ult = 2`, i.e. a half-texel inset, and the renderer maps
  `u = s / 32 / w` with no subtraction. That is correct, not a missing term:
  GL's own sample point is `u * w - 0.5` in texel-centre units, which
  reproduces the RDP's `s - SL` exactly. Do not "fix" this.

#### What this means for the objective

The first-wrong-stage assumption the round opened with — texture/tile
resolution on large-texture props — is **refuted**. Nothing between the
display list and the uploaded GL texture is wrong on Facility. The seams
therefore live downstream of the texture's CONTENT and ADDRESS, in how it is
SAMPLED: filtering, minification and the absence of any mip chain are the
untested stage, and a tiling texture minified with `GL_LINEAR` and no mip
level is a textbook producer of regular light/dark banding across a large
surface. That is NOT authorisation to start changing filters — it is where
the next round should point, and it needs the owner to name one prop first.

Two things must NOT be inferred from this entry:

- It does not say B-052 is fixed. B-052's resolver defect is still in the
  tree, still unrepaired, and still blocks any future mip work. It is parked
  because it is not LOAD-BEARING for consumed output, not because it is gone.
- It does not say the seams are imaginary. They are the owner's physical
  observation. It says only that seven measured candidate causes in the tile
  chain are eliminated.

#### Reproducing the census

The arm was temporary and is not in the tree. To rebuild it: classify
`tile_texture`'s resolution against both `tmem_find(t->tmem)` and a
nearest-start-at-or-below lookup, print all five class counts unconditionally,
and run **windowed** — `SL_WINDOW=1 SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34 SL_FRAMES=400`. Capture
stderr with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError`; PowerShell's `>` catches
only stdout from a native exe and silently writes an EMPTY file, which is the
tenth instrument failure this project has recorded.

### B-052 — TMEM resolution cannot address into a loaded block, so no mip level above 0 can ever be sampled. 2026-08-28

Found while trying to measure whether mip content explained the facility glass
pane's residual. It is not that bug's cause, but it is a real renderer defect on
its own and affects **any** multi-tile or mipped texture in the game, not just
glass. Split out so the B-051 glass work does not absorb it.

#### What is measured

The facility tinted-glass pane's display list declares three mip levels and
loads **one** block at `tmem 0`:

```
BB texture  on=1 level=2 tile=0  s=3456 t=3456
F5 tile=0 fmt=3 siz=1 tmem=0    shifts=0  -> 54x54
F5 tile=1                tmem=378  shifts=1  -> 27x27
F5 tile=2                tmem=486  shifts=2  -> 14x14
```

`tile_texture` resolves pixels through `tmem_find(t->tmem)`, which matches a
loadblock's tmem address **exactly**. Tiles 1 and 2 sit at 378 and 486
*inside* the block loaded at 0, so nothing matches and the lookup falls back to
the last loadblock's base pointer **with no offset**. The probe lines say so
directly: `F3 FALLBACK-last-load ... texels=0 fmt=0 siz=0`.

Consequence: an arm that binds tile 1 or tile 2 decodes a 27x27 or 14x14 image
out of the **base level's** byte stream. The mip levels themselves begin
378 * 8 = 3024 bytes in and are never read. Corroborated by texel statistics -
the 14x14 arm returned `rgbmean=13` where a genuine half-scale reduction of a
mean-28 image stays near 28.

This VOIDED both LOD diagnostic arms. Any conclusion drawn from `SL_TEXGEN_LOD`
before this entry is invalid; "neither mip arm helps" was retracted on that
basis.

#### The rest of the LOD pipeline is also unimplemented

Separate from the addressing defect, and each measured on the pane's own list:

- `BA ba001001 00010000` - sft 16 `G_MDSFT_TEXTLOD` = `G_TL_LOD`, LOD mode ON
  (`gbi.h:612`, `:639-640`). `BA ba001102 00000000` - sft 17
  `G_MDSFT_TEXTDETAIL` = `G_TD_CLAMP` (`gbi.h:613`, `:634`).
- `OP_SETOTHH` acts only on sft 14 (`G_MDSFT_TEXTLUT`) and sft 20
  (`G_MDSFT_CYCLETYPE`). Both LOD bits are discarded.
- Combiner `fc26a004 1f1093fb` cycle-0 RGB is
  `(TEXEL1 - TEXEL0) * LOD_FRACTION + TEXEL0` - the mip lerp.
- `grep -rn LOD_FRACTION src/gfx/` returns five hits, all in comments and a
  mux-name table. Never acted on. The renderer binds tile 0 alone, which is
  LOD fraction 0.

#### On the notes - an earlier claim here was WRONG and is corrected

This was initially filed as "microcode-internal, corpus silent". That was the
wrong corpus. `G_TEXTURE_GEN` is an RSP concern; **texture LOD is downstream in
the RDP**, and the notes do cover it:

- `ucode05.txt` BB field table: `Lod` = number of mip levels minus one, `Tile` =
  base mip level, tile 0 being the highest-resolution image. Independently
  confirms the pane's `level=2` -> three levels.
- `ucode05_old.txt`: othermode_h index 0x10 = texture LOD (`0x00010000`),
  index 0x11 = texture detail (`0x00020000` sharpen, `0x00040000` detail).
- `ucode05_old.txt`: combiner muxes D = LOD fraction, E = primitive LOD
  fraction. `ucode05.txt` notes SetPrimColor carries `prim_min_level` and
  `prim_LOD_Frac`.
- `Texture application (Rooms).txt`: what enabling LOD does in practice, and the
  two-image detail family with a `1F10FFFF`-class combiner (Dam's rock walls,
  Grid's stone walls).

Genuinely absent is only the **derivative/level-selection step** - how the RDP
turns screen-space texture-coordinate variation into a level and a fraction.
`grep` for derivative/lambda/screen-space over those three files comes back
empty, and the notes point outward to the `gSPTexture` reference, which is not
in the corpus. **No `not_covered` entry was added for LOD generally**; at most a
narrow one for that single step is warranted.

#### What is NOT established

- **Whether real mip content materially affects the glass pane.** Untestable
  until the addressing defect is fixed. The pane's residual is separately
  accounted for by the normals-as-colour bug (B-051), so this is not expected to
  be that bug's cause - but it has never been measured either way.
- **The blast radius.** No tree-wide census of how many draws declare
  `level > 0` has been run. That census is the right first step if this is
  picked up.

#### Order of work, if picked up

Fix the addressing first - a tile lookup that resolves to `base + (tmem -
block_tmem) * 8` rather than requiring an exact match - then re-run the voided
LOD arms, and only then consider the LOD-fraction pipeline, which needs the one
undocumented step above.

### B-051 — texgen + lighting become the NATIVE DEFAULT after owner visual validation on facility. 2026-08-28

The semantics landed in `3c581b2f` shipped **default OFF**. This entry records
flipping `texgen_on()` and `light_on()` to **default ON**, and exactly what that
is and is not backed by.

The logic change is two lines, one per accessor, matching the `alpha_eq_on()`
idiom already in the file:

```
-    on = (v != NULL && *v != '\0' && *v != '0');
+    on = !(v != NULL && *v == '0' && v[1] == '\0');
```

Verified by execution: `unset -> ON`, `"0" -> OFF`, `"1" -> ON`, `"" -> ON`,
`"00" -> ON`.

#### Why the previous default was wrong, not merely incomplete

Four defects, each measured and recorded in `3c581b2f`: `G_TEXTURE_GEN` was
tracked and never acted on; the `gSPTexture` S/T scale was discarded; the
LOOKATX/Y reflectance basis never entered the renderer; and signed `cn[]`
normals were fed to `glColor` as RGB under `G_LIGHTING`. On facility's tinted
glass the first three meant every fragment sampled texel (0,0) - rgb 0,0,0 -
which was the flat dark pane.

#### The rollback is real, not merely present

`SL_TEXGEN=0 SL_LIGHT=0` remains the rollback. Proved against the **old binary
built from `fbad9809`**, where both defaulted OFF, rather than against the new
binary alone: 100 matched frames of `facility-pane` at 960x720,
**100 identical, 0 changed pixels**. The new default and the previously
accepted explicit arm `SL_TEXGEN=1 SL_LIGHT=1` are likewise **100/100
identical**. A discrimination control confirms the arms are not trivially
equal: default vs rollback differs on 13 of 100 frames, 95269 pixels.

#### Containment, by set logic rather than a bounding box

Against the mark-derived texgen surface set, **zero** candidate-changed pixels
fall outside the surface, on every frame - so there was no escaping pixel to
chase individually. Against generated-coordinates-alone (`SL_TEXGEN=1
SL_LIGHT=0`) the residual is 709 px, all inside the surface, every one black
`(0,0,0)` in both reference arms and lifted to `(1,1,1)`, max channel delta
**1**. Same signature the parent commit recorded.

#### An instrument fault found and retracted here

The `SL_TEXGEN_MARK` locator was first read by exact-matching `(255,0,255)`.
The pane is alpha-blended, so the marker colour blends down and exact matching
silently misses every partially-opaque frame: it reported the surface on 8 of
100 frames when the true count is 13. Measured proof - frames 1, 2, 11 and 13
carry the surface at 10094 px with an identical bbox, painted `(86,0,86)`,
`(171,0,171)`, `(187,0,187)` and `(17,0,17)`. **A magenta count is not a
surface census.** The A/B and containment results never depended on it. Mark-run
alignment was verified independently (a no-surface frame is byte-identical to
the default arm), so the mark perturbs neither sim nor capture cadence.

#### Smoke coverage - NOT cartridge-fidelity certification

Nine texgen levels, windowed under xvfb, 12 frames each from their own recorded
streams, both arms, one process at a time. All `rc=0`. No black or flat
geometry, no palette corruption, no colour explosion, no disappearing geometry,
no crash. Mean/colour-count/saturation statistics track between arms on every
level.

```
level      frames ident differ   chg px  max/frame  %frame   note
egypt        12     11     1       6926      6926    2.25%   env-mapped weapon: black -> gold
bunker2      12     10     2        179        96    0.03%
streets      12     10     2        368       184    0.06%
dam          12      9     3      66116     61170   19.91%   largest; 99.1% texgen, lighting 0
facility     12     10     2       6606      3303    1.08%   the known pane rectangle
surface      12      9     3         39        13    0.00%
bunker1      12     12     0          0         0    0.00%   no texgen surface reached
control      12      8     4      13605     13507    4.40%
surface2     12     11     1          8         8    0.00%
```

Change amplitudes are bounded: median per-pixel channel delta 8-54, max 99,
except egypt's max 212, which is the weapon going from black to gold.

**egypt, the standing caveat, is now the strongest corroboration.** Its texgen
path is 32x32 CI8+TLUT rather than facility's IA8 and had never been looked at.
The environment-mapped weapon on the plinth renders as a **flat black
silhouette** under rollback and as a **gold, textured object** at the new
default - the same "samples texel (0,0)" defect facility's pane had, on a
different texture format. That the fix generalises to a second format is
evidence; it is **not** a certification that egypt's generated coordinates are
correct.

**dam carries the largest change and deserves the most caution.** Attributed
rather than assumed: `SL_LIGHT` alone changes **0 pixels on every dam frame**,
and 65510 of 66116 (99.1%) is texgen. So dam has `G_TEXTURE_GEN` geometry whose
vertices carry real s/t, and the new path correctly replaces them with generated
coordinates per F3D semantics. Visibly the rock faces take a different detail
pattern and the truck windshield goes from a flat pale panel to a dark
reflective one. Both arms render coherent rock and a coherent vehicle, and
nothing is missing or blown out - but **whether dam's generated coordinates are
right is not established**, and no view-matched cartridge frame of dam exists.

One contact-sheet tile read as a black frame on control. Checked rather than
waved off: control's dark frames are **byte-identical between arms** (means 0.00
and 1.81), so they are a level fade, not the flip.

#### What is established, and what is explicitly not

- **Established:** facility is the visually validated surface - the owner
  confirmed `SL_TEXGEN=1 SL_LIGHT=1` there, and that arm is now byte-identical
  to the default. Rollback restores `fbad9809` pixel for pixel. Containment is
  structural (`g_vgen_ok`/`g_vlrgb_ok` are set only in the `G_TEXTURE_GEN` /
  `G_LIGHTING` vertex-load paths) and measured (0 escaping pixels).
- **NOT established:** cartridge fidelity on any level but facility. The eight
  other levels are smoke-tested for gross regression, nothing more. Twelve
  frames from one stream at one difficulty is a thin sample; a defect outside
  those frames would not be seen.
- **NOT established, unchanged:** the S/T slot-to-axis assignment remains
  **RETAINED BUT NOT PROVEN**. slot -> vector is sourced; slot -> axis is not,
  and no view-matched cartridge frame of the pane exists to settle it.
  `SL_TEXGEN_SWAP` stays default OFF. See `docs/doc-routing.json`.
- Mip/LOD remains B-052 and is untouched here.

#### Default-state audit, measured from source

Every gated accessor in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`, read from the tree rather than
assumed. `grep -rn "texgen_on\|light_on\|SL_TEXGEN\|SL_LIGHT" src/` finds **no
use outside `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`** - that tree-wide search came back empty.

```
accessor          env var             default        call sites
texgen_on         SL_TEXGEN           ON  (=0 off)   6501                 1
light_on          SL_LIGHT            ON  (=0 off)   6404                 1
texgen_mode       SL_TEXGEN_MODE      0              7007                 1
texgen_swap       SL_TEXGEN_SWAP      OFF            7005                 1
texgen_neutral    SL_TEXGEN_NEUTRAL   OFF            6423                 1
texgen_lod        SL_TEXGEN_LOD       0              3055,3056,6516,6518  4
texgen_mark       SL_TEXGEN_MARK      OFF            3085,6401            2
                                                              total      11
SL_TEXGEN_DBG / SL_LIGHT_DBG / SL_VTX_NRM / SL_BB_DBG   OFF (NULL-tested, print only)
```

Two call sites belong to the flipped pair; eleven is the total across all seven
gated accessors - the figure `3c581b2f` quotes. Both counts are correct and
count different things. **Only the two defaults changed; every diagnostic and
experimental arm remains OFF or 0.**

#### Gates on this exact candidate

```
make matching                     MATCH!
make trace-verify LEVEL=facility  IDENTICAL - 15869 ticks match (compared on frame counter)
make bootsweep                    20/20 OK, 0 levels failed
```

`src/game` is untouched, so no trace re-baseline is owed.

### B-053 — the facility intro camera: the record walk is CORRECT, the seed is not. 2026-08-28 — FIXED 2026-08-28

Owner report: the cartridge's facility intro shows the first hallway
outside the bathroom looking at the bulletproof vest; the native port shows
the tank room at the far end of the level.

The leading hypothesis - a typed-record walk desyncing on a wrong per-type
size or an unhandled type, which would land the camera on whatever parsed
next - is WRONG and was killed by measurement. Recording it because it is
the obvious reading of the symptom and the next person will have it too.

#### What the notes say (consulted before the decomp, rule 7)

`Setup File Microcodes and Paths/Intro Block/Intro Block Commands.txt`
gives the type codes and each record's stride: 0/spawn 0x0C, 1/weapon 0x10,
2/ammo 0x10, 3/swirl 0x20, 4/anim 0x08, 5/cuff 0x08, 6/camera 0x28,
7/watch 0x0C, 8/credits 0x08, 9/end; unknown -> advance 4 and continue.

`.../Intro Block/7F0057C4 - Intro Block Handler.txt:427-447` is the
authority on SELECTION. Retail does `JAL 7000A450` - that address is
`randomGetNext` (`src/random.s`) - then DIVU/MFHI by the count at
`800364BC`, then follows `0024(entry)`, the prev link, that many times into
`800364C0`. `Camera Modes.txt` confirms camera mode 1 reads `800364C0`.

So `bondview_r.c:356-362` is retail-faithful and `bondconstants.h:4497-4506`
matches the doc's 0-9 numbering.

#### The measurement

Facility is `UsetuparkZ`, LEVELID 34. Its intro block holds FOUR type-6
cameras:

```
cam  position                        pad   where
 0   8669.05, -359.25, -3541.46      104   far / tank end
 1   8447.07, -419.25, -3962.70      104   far / tank end
 2    524.66, -397.93,   565.66        2   bathroom hallway
 3   8270.73,  280.74, -3480.91      104   far / tank end
```

Camera 2 is the only one near the body armour (pad 215 at 801,-452,1274) -
the owner's "vest" camera. Pads 104 (9582,-510,-3623) and 2 (468,-470,571)
are the two rooms.

- NATIVE (gdb on build/native/skeleton): count 4, records at intro+0/40/80/
  120 (0x28 stride), all four decoded, lang1c resolves. Selects **cam 1**.
  Reproduced identically on a second run.
- ROM (libretro, parity image, reading 800364B8/BC/C0): count 4, records at
  0x801d3e0c/34/5c/84 (0x28 stride), **floats identical to the last digit**.
  Selects **cam 0**.

Same data, different index. `boss.c:388` does `randomSetSeed(osGetCount())`;
natively `osGetCount()` is `1000000 + sl_frame * SL_CYCLES_PER_FRAME +
sl_count_extra` (`sl_ultra_shim.c:212`), a deterministic function of the
frame number. On hardware it is the free-running COP0 count at boot.

Confirming experiment: forcing `g_randomSeed` at the decision point selected
cam 2 - x=524.66 y=-397.93 z=565.66 pad=2, the vest camera. The machinery is
correct end to end; only the seed decides.

#### The consequence, which reframes the report

**The cartridge does not always show the vest camera either.** Three of the
four are at the tank end, so a hardware boot shows a far-end camera roughly
three times in four - and the ROM run measured here picked cam 0, a far-end
one. The native defect is therefore NOT "the wrong camera" but **"the same
camera every time"**: a constant seed where the original has boot entropy.

#### Hypotheses killed by measurement

Wrong per-type size (both sides stride 0x28, all four decode); unhandled or
misnumbered INTROTYPE (enum matches the doc, startpadcount 1 at the right
pad); byte-order fault (floats bit-identical to the ROM's, lang1c and the
pad index both resolve); last-vs-first selection (both run the same prev
walk); wrong base pointer (native decodes UsetuparkZ record for record).

#### Resolution (2026-08-28)

Fixed in two commits, in that causal order: replay stopped depending on the
accidental constant, and only then did interactive boot become cartridge-like.

**Facility has four legitimate cartridge intro cameras, and the vest camera
is one of four - not "the" canonical facility intro.** The owner's report was
of a real defect, but the defect was never "the wrong camera": three of the
four are at the tank end, so a hardware boot shows a far-end camera most of
the time. Retail boot timing is what supplies the entropy. Native's
deterministic `osGetCount()` accidentally froze the choice, so the same camera
came up on every single launch. **No camera is hard-coded, and facility is not
special-cased**; the seeding policy is global.

*What was open above is now settled by measurement, not design argument.*
The `tools/` claim was re-verified tree-wide before being relied on: nothing
under `tools/` sets `SL_RNG_SEED`. Restoring entropy moved NOTHING in the
corpus, so there is no divergence and no re-baseline.

**Replay now stores and replays its seed explicitly.** The native run
directory's existing `env` sidecar gains `SL_RNG_SEED=<16 hex>` - the 64-bit
RNG STATE, since `randomSetSeed(x)` stores `(s64)(s32)x + 1` and the argument
is not recoverable from the state. It is injected at the same code point,
`sl_rng_seed_override()`. Recordings predating this have no such line, cannot
have one reconstructed, and replay on the deterministic boot default - the
seed they were recorded on. The corpus is not invalidated.

**Interactive native boot now varies its seed.** `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME)`
folded to 32 bits, fed through the game's own unmodified `randomSetSeed()` -
exactly what the cartridge does with `osGetCount()`. `osGetCount()` itself is
left deterministic; it is useful platform timing with other callers.
Precedence: explicit `SL_RNG_SEED` wins; a replay with no recorded seed keeps
the deterministic default; anything else draws from the host clock.

**The logged seed reproduces an interactive run.** Every native launch prints
its state and, when it was not forced, the line that reproduces it.

Measured, 16 fresh facility launches: 16 distinct seeds, all four cameras
selected, and the vest camera came up naturally (cam 2, pad 2, 524.66 /
-397.93 / 565.66). Counts were 6/5/4/1 across cam 0/1/3/2 - reported as
evidence that it VARIES, which is all 16 runs can support; no distribution
claim is made. Explicit-seed test, two seeds x three runs: same seed, same
camera, every time. Replay with its recorded seed is bit-identical run to run
(end-of-run RNG state `00000001a6dde145` twice); the same replay with no seed
takes the legacy path and lands elsewhere, which is what proves the agreement
is not vacuous.

Gates: `make matching` MATCH!; `make trace-verify LEVEL=facility` IDENTICAL -
15869 ticks, plus runway (4636) and depot (5390); `make bootsweep` 20/20.

#### A real divergence found in passing, never fired

On an UNKNOWN intro type, retail advances 4 and continues (7F005DE0), which
`bondview_r.c` reproduces - but the intro arm of `sl_setup_file_swap`
(`prop.c:1335`) sets `done = 1` and STOPS. No unknown type occurs in the 20
campaign levels, so it has never fired. Fix it if that walk is ever touched.

#### Retracted during this investigation

Native pad 167 reads (113.55, 465.82, -956.50) against (137, 562, -1154) in
`assets/obseg/setup/UsetuparkZ.c`. Flagged as a defect, then withdrawn: it
is the documented `roompos_1` scale at `prop.c:1524-1526`.

### B-054 — a GLSL world shader leaked into 2D rendering, in TWO places. Black boxes around HUD glyphs and bullet decals. 2026-08-28 — FIXED 2026-08-28

Owner reported opaque black rectangles around watch/HUD text and around
bullet decals, intermittently: some launches clean, some not, on an
UNCHANGED binary. Fixed by two commits, `8d16ade5` and `5130c36a`.

#### Why it was intermittent, and why it had never been seen before

Nothing to do with the renderer's inputs. The B-051 alpha program is bound
in texenv mode 5; whether a frame *ends* in mode 5 depends on what the game
happened to draw last, which depends on game state, which depends on the
RNG. Native's boot seed was a constant until `ac2bc38f` (B-053), so every
launch in this project's history drew the same sequence and the leak never
fired. **The RNG work did not cause this. It stopped hiding it**, and the
seeds it produces are now reproduction material.

#### Defect 1 — invalidating tracked state before using it (`8d16ade5`)

`sl_gfx_frame_dl` reset the tracker as:

```
g_texenv = -1;
texenv_set(0);
```

`texenv_set()` emits `glUseProgram(0)` only when the mode it is LEAVING is
5 - that is the single fact it has to decide whether the unbind is owed.
Assigning `-1` first destroyed it. A frame ending in mode 5 left the
program bound while every later `texenv_set()` programmed fixed-function
state the still-bound shader overrode.

Corrected order: `texenv_set(0)` while the tracker still describes GL,
THEN `g_texenv = -1`, THEN `texenv_set(0)` to re-establish completely.

Measured, one variable - same input, same vis, same binary, seed alone:

```
                              broken      clean
  texrects drawn               68161      68161
  drawn with program bound     40936          0
  fixed-function asked
    while shader bound       1564316          0
```

Identical display list, identical resolved texture state, identical decoded
alpha histograms. Only the GL binding differed. HUD-text blackness 0.1131
vs 0.0000, and 0.113 -> 0.000 with the fix.

#### Defect 2 — the fill path never asked (`5130c36a`)

The frame-boundary fix closed the watch and left the intro title boxed.
**RETRACTED: the hypothesis that `draw_texrect` inherits a stale binding.**
Measured false - its textured branch calls `texenv_set(0|1)`, sees mode 5
and unbinds, so texrects self-heal. At the boxed title frame, texrects
drawn with the program bound was ZERO on both arms.

`draw_fillrect` never called `texenv_set` at all, and `mode2d_begin()` did
not either, so the fill path inherited whatever geometry left bound. Using
five owner recordings differing only by seed, at frame 247:

```
                            boxed      clean
  texrects / bound         225 / 0    225 / 0
  fillrects / bound          4 / 1      4 / 0
```

The leaked draw was `rect=[30,203]-[219,219] col=00000000` - **alpha
zero**, invisible under the fixed pipeline, which is why it sat harmless
for the project's whole life. The shader computes its own alpha and never
sees that vertex alpha, so it rasterised opaque black.

Fix: `texenv_set(0)` in `mode2d_begin()`, the gate every 2D draw passes.

**Also fixed by the same statement, and not previously reported:** the
level-intro fade (`rect=[0,10]-[321,231] col=00000094`) leaked identically
and rendered as a FULLY OPAQUE BLACK SCREEN for ~100 frames instead of a
partial fade.

#### Controls, both mandatory, because "the boxes are gone" and "the alpha
#### path stopped running" produce identical framebuffers

- 334164 (then 138276) triangles still take AEQ_SHADER after each fix.
- Historical seed `00000000000f4241`: pixel-identical fixed vs unfixed.

#### The transferable rule, also written at the fix site

**Never invalidate a tracked-state cache before using it to restore the
external state it describes.** `internal := UNKNOWN; restore_external()` is
wrong whenever the restore reads the old internal value to know which
teardown is owed. See `docs/porting-hazards.md`.

### B-055 — the watch briefing header read ERROR: a 32-bit swap across two 16-bit fields. 2026-08-28 — FIXED 2026-08-28

Facility's briefing pages showed `ERROR` where `ARKANGELSK` belongs. Fixed
by `312ace41`.

`ERROR` is **Rare's own fallback**, faithfully decompiled at
`objective_status.c:99-101`, taken when `langGet()` returns NULL. The
defect was a failed lookup, not the fallback. The fallback is unchanged.

Type-23 word 2 is TWO u16 fields, not one u32. `Setup File Microcodes and
Paths/objectives and briefings/7F057104 - return watch text for briefing
A0.txt` gives the record as `00000023 0000000x 0000tttt rrrrrrrr`, and the
disassembly reads the ID with `LHU A0,000A(V0)` - a halfword at 0x0A. That
is `struct watchMenuObjectiveText` (menu 32, reserved 16, text 16,
nextentry 32), not the opaque `setup_objective_text` whose `unk08` spans
both halves. `SW32(r->unk08)` therefore swapped ACROSS the boundary and
displaced the ID into `reserved`.

Measured at the load site (`objective.c:57`), facility page 0:

```
  before  raw[0x08] = 2b 0c 00 00   reserved=0c2b  text=0000
          langGet(text)     = (nil)
          langGet(reserved) = "A R K A N G E L S K"
  after   reserved=0000  text=0c2b
          langGet(text)     = "A R K A N G E L S K"
```

**Positive control**, and what makes this displacement rather than an
unloaded language bank: the other four type-23 records resolved through the
same displaced field to the overview, M, Q and Moneypenny strings.

Page 0 is the STAGE/LOCATION header, not the mission intro title - those
are different strings, and an argument that the string must be sound
because the intro renders it was about a different string and did not hold.

**The trace gate is structurally blind to this.** `src/native` is not in
the ROM build - `GAMEFILES_C` globs only `src/game`, grep for `src/native`
in the Makefile is empty, and `nm` on the ROM ELF finds zero `sl_swap`
symbols. `IDENTICAL - 15869 ticks` means "nothing else broke", NOT "the fix
is right". The load-time measurement is the correctness evidence.

#### Open, deliberately not fixed here

`grep -rn "SW32(r->unk" src/native/` returns **50 sites**. Only `unk08` in
this function is provably wrong; `unk04` (menu) is genuinely 32-bit per both
doc and disassembly. The other 48 are in large opaque structs with **no
record-specific doc authority**, so no claim is made either way. That search
did NOT come back empty, so this is a backlog lead, not an absence result.
Confirming any of them needs a per-record-type doc.

### B-056 — the watch static: the RDP dithers, and we masked the bit that says so. 2026-08-28 — FIXED 2026-08-28

The cartridge's watch face bursts into heavy static for ~1.5s at irregular
intervals, then fades clean. Native rendered it perfectly flat. Fixed by
`359fde76`; owner-confirmed.

**Native's game logic was already correct.** The burst state machine runs:
`options.c:1509` fires on `(D_80040B0C << 0x10) < randomGetNext()`
(P about 1/683 per tick), slams `g_WatchBackgroundGreen` to 0x80 and plays
`WATCH_STATIC_SFX`; `options.c:1516` recovers by `randomGetNext() >> 30`
(0-3) per tick, clamping at 0xE0. Abrupt onset, gradual fade.

The effect itself is the RDP's. While green < 0xE0 the face draws under
`G_RM_AA_PCL_SURF`, and `gbi.h:851-854` shows that mode **embeds
`G_AC_DITHER`** - alpha-compare dither, which kills each pixel when its
alpha loses to a per-pixel noise value. Kill rate scales with (255 - green),
so density tracks the fade. It is a CUTOUT, not an overlay: the face gets
darker, and the noise re-randomises every frame.

Cartridge, 6000-frame dwell: 5 bursts, 86-111 frames each, irregular
intervals (558/210/3270/1242). P=1/683 at 30Hz over 6000 VI frames predicts
4.4 bursts; 5 measured. Quiet vs burst: local 3x3 deviation 2.42 -> 6.62,
mean frame-to-frame difference 0.40 -> 11.58 (29x).

#### The native gap - one line, plus a missing feature

`sl_gfx_dl.c` built its othermode_l mask from the command's shift/length.
`gDPSetRenderMode` passes shift=3, length=29, so the write stripped bits
0-2 - exactly the alpha-compare field. `0050004b` became `00500048`. And
alpha compare was implemented nowhere: `0050004b` appeared **zero times in
7300 frames**.

#### B9 semantics, settled by census rather than assumed

Three readings were possible and the cartridge chose:

- **Mask field-wise** - REFUTED. Over 7300 frames the game emits only two
  B9 shapes (sft=3/len=29 render mode, sft=0/len=2 alpha compare), and the
  only word carrying `ac=3` is the render-mode word. Explicit
  `gDPSetAlphaCompare` fires 8 times, **always `G_AC_NONE`**. Under masking
  dither is unreachable - yet the cartridge dithers.
- **OR the data in unmasked** - REFUTED, and it was the leading hypothesis.
  It predicts dither persisting onto the page-select bars drawn immediately
  after under `G_RM_XLU_SURF` (ac=0). Those bars measure 0.38-0.68x the
  face's frame-to-frame difference, never >=1: they are translucent and show
  the dithered face THROUGH, not cut out themselves.
- **Complete othermode_l value for this one shape** - consistent with all of
  it. The 17 render-mode words carrying ac=0 are what actively CLEAR dither,
  which is what keeps the bars and the quiet face clean.

So the rule is narrow: `if (sft == 3 && len == 29) mask = 0xffffffff;`
Every other shape keeps the field-wise write, so `gDPSetAlphaCompare` and
`gDPSetDepthSource` still touch only their own fields. **The behaviour is
measured; the microcode-level REASON is not established.**

#### Implementation, and why not a shader

Bits 0-1 decoded and held as renderer state (NONE/THRESHOLD/DITHER), no
watch special-casing. `G_AC_DITHER` drives a per-frame-refilled polygon
stipple, chosen over a shader discard deliberately: binding the alpha
program for an untextured `G_CC_SHADE` draw would replace the whole fragment
stage - precisely the "static appears because alpha broke globally" failure
mode. A stipple cannot alter any colour or alpha. Density is the RDP's, not
tuned: 49.2% rejection measured at green=132 against 48.4% predicted, and
31.8% against 31.6%.

#### Controls

Parser positive (`0050004b` reaches geometry, 16 tris); dither OFF flat
(0.99 / 0.05) with the mode still parsing in BOTH arms; ON causation
(15.8 / 18.4 same input and binary); quiet frames **bit-identical** ON vs
OFF, which is simultaneously the quiet negative and the proof that ordinary
alpha and blending are intact.

Blast radius: three `G_RM_AA_PCL_SURF` sites tree-wide. `options.c:1767`
(face) and `options.c:2765` (page text, whose own comment describes pixels
dropping out) are live and get the same effect; `bg.c:2269` is inside a
comment block and cannot execute.

#### Known remaining difference, deliberately not compensated

Native's face darkens less than the cartridge's (luminance ratio 0.95 vs
0.70). **Not a density error** - rejection rate is measured correct. Native
draws a brighter backdrop behind the face, so the hands show through more.
Separate and pre-existing; compensating inside the dither would be tuning
against a screenshot. The sweeping scanline
(`g_WatchStaticScanlineY`, `options.c:1356`) uses `G_RM_AA_XLU_SURF`, which
the renderer handles, and was left alone.

### B-058 — menu key repeat is far too fast: one press can skip to the bottom

- **Found:**  2026-09-01, owner hand-testing the native keyboard/mouse work
- **Owner:**  Phase 1, the same native-input track this was found in
- **Where:**  `src/platform/sl_input.c` `map_kbm`, the `if (menu)` branch
- **Blocks:** nothing structural; it makes the menus unpleasant to use

WASD and the arrows deflect the N64 stick fully for as long as the key is held,
and the menus step on threshold rather than on edge, so a single human keypress
lasting a dozen polls steps the selection a dozen times. The watch's own
`watch_stick_y_nav_ready` latch only re-arms when the stick returns near centre,
which bounds it somewhat, but the front end has no such latch at all.

The fix is the edge-plus-re-arm model the WHEEL path already uses in this file
(`wheel_step`, `SL_WHEEL_HOLD_POLLS`, `SL_WHEEL_GAP_POLLS`): one keypress
becomes one pulse of full deflection followed by a forced return to centre, and
holding the key repeats at a chosen rate rather than at the poll rate. The wheel
path is measured good and should be the template, not rewritten.

Deliberately NOT done in the objective that found it: that objective was scoped
to pitch direction and pointer capture, and this is a separate behaviour.

### B-059 — left mouse button should confirm the highlighted menu item

- **Found:**  2026-09-01, owner hand-testing
- **Owner:**  Phase 1, native input
- **Where:**  `src/platform/sl_input.c` `read_mouse` / `map_kbm` menu branch
- **Blocks:** nothing

Owner wants LMB in a menu to produce the same input Enter does — confirm the
currently highlighted item. Explicitly NOT a pointer system: no hover, no
hit-testing, no pointer targets, no click-to-activate-what-is-under-the-cursor.
The mouse's POSITION stays unread in menus, exactly as the wheel work kept it.

Note `read_mouse` currently returns early in menus before reading buttons, and
that early return is deliberate — it drains the relative accumulator first so
motion cannot be banked and dumped when the menu closes. Whatever implements
this must preserve the drain.

- **Found:**  2026-09-01, implementing the mouse-owns-its-own-pitch decision

- **Where:**  `src/game/bondview2.c:5579`, `src/platform/sl_input.c` `map_kbm`

The owner's ownership boundary is: the mouse always has conventional PC
direction; the CONTROLLER keeps GoldenEye's control style and Look Up/Down
setting. That is what was implemented — the mouse pre-negates its own pitch to
cancel the `invertPitch` block, and the pad path is untouched.

Recorded only so nobody later reads the mouse carve-out as a general intent to
retire the option. It is not. If a pad user ever reports the same complaint it
is a separate decision, not a bug in this one.

### B-061 — Facility direct boot hangs on Windows in `stanDetermineEOF`; Linux boots the same level

- **Found:**  2026-09-01, Win32/i686/PE32 bring-up
- **Owner:**  Windows port
- **Blocks:** Facility on Windows. This is the FIRST BROKEN STAGE of the
              native-Windows chain; everything before it is cleared.

`SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34` (facility) hangs the frame pump. The Windows watchdog
reports it and resolves cleanly:

```
pc  0x0051fa63  stanDetermineEOF  src/game/stan.c:3162
ra  0x00406660  load_bg_file      src/game/bg.c:981
ra  0x004a66a0  lvlStageLoad      src/game/lv.c:422
ra  0x004029ca  bossMainloop      src/boss.c:479
```

**The differential is the useful part.** The same source, the same level, the
same 32-bit little-endian architecture:

| build | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| Linux `build/native/skeleton` | `SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34 SL_FRAMES=300` | `survived 300 pumped frames`, exit 0 |
| Windows `build/win32/sightline.exe` | same | HANG in `stanDetermineEOF` |

So this is not a pre-existing Rare bug and not a byte-order bug in the stan
format — a format defect would hang both hosts identically. Something the
Windows build does differently is producing a different tile walk.

The loop at `stan.c:3162` advances by
`tileSizes[(tile->tail.half >> 0xc) & 0xf]` and terminates on
`*(s32 *)tile == 0`. A zero out of that size table is an immediate infinite
loop, so the first thing to measure is the table's contents and the
`tail.half` values actually being read — not the loop.

Candidates NOT yet eliminated, in the order worth measuring:

1. **`-mms-bitfields`, which MinGW enables by default** (confirmed via
   `gcc -Q --help=target`) and Linux GCC does not. It changes bitfield layout
   to the MSVC rules. `src/game/stan.h` itself declares no bitfields, so this
   is not the direct cause, but any struct on this path that does would be
   laid out differently on the two hosts. `-mno-ms-bitfields` on the decomp
   compile class is a one-flag experiment.
2. **The `segments.o` absolutes.** `gen_segments.py` emits 827 absolute
   symbols plus 26 real segment windows, and the Win32 path rewrites those
   symbol names for PE (leading underscore) via `tools/windows/pe_asm.py`.
   A symbol that should be a window but became an absolute — or the reverse —
   would give a plausible-looking pointer into nothing.
3. Struct padding or alignment differences between the two hosts on the
   specific types this walk reads.

Do **not** start by reading `stan.c`. Per project rule 7 the stan format is a
question for Zoinkity's notes first, and per the measured corollary the answer
should come from comparing the two hosts' actual values, not from the source.

---

**RESOLVED 2026-09-02.** Three independent Windows-only defects, each measured
as the first wrong consumed value, each fixed and re-measured. Facility now
reports `survived 300 pumped frames`, exit 0, on Windows (5/5 runs, including
one from a scratch `build/win32`).

1. **`-mms-bitfields` (MinGW's default; Linux GCC's is the opposite).** Under
   the MS rule a non-bitfield member may not occupy the tail of a bitfield's
   allocation unit, so `bondtypes.h`'s `StandTile` — `u32 id : 24` then
   `u8 room` — laid out `room@4 mid@6 tail@8 sizeof 12` where the N64 layout is
   `room@3 mid@4 tail@6 sizeof 8`. `stanDetermineEOF` advances by
   `tileSizes[(tile->tail.half >> 0xc) & 0xf]` and stops on `*(s32 *)tile == 0`;
   reading `tail` two bytes late produced a size index that never landed on the
   terminator. Measured both layouts directly. Fix: `-mno-ms-bitfields` on both
   Windows compile classes (one binary must not hold two bitfield ABIs; SDL2's
   public headers declare no bitfields, so its interface is unaffected).
   Candidate 3 of the three listed above; candidates 1 and 2 were not involved.

2. **`-fcommon` plus MinGW ld's COMMON ordering.** `image.c` declares
   `ptr_texture_alloc_start` / `_end` / `ptr_next_available_space` /
   `ptr_last_entry_facemapping` as four consecutive tentative definitions and
   then reinterprets the group as one `struct texpool` (`image.c:2536`,
   `tex.c:809`, `initmttex.c:15`) — contiguity the original map confirms at
   `0x8008c720..0x8008c72c`. As COMMON symbols the linker may order them freely,
   and MinGW ld interleaved `g_TexCacheCount` at `start+4`, aliasing it onto
   `pool->end`. Measured: `g_TexCacheCount` read back as `71209600`, a pool
   pointer, so `texInflateZlib` walked off `g_TexCacheItems[150]`. Fix:
   `-fno-common`, which emits them in declaration order. Tree-wide grep: the
   other three names appear only at their own definitions, so nothing else reads
   them by name.

3. **`PHYS_TO_K0` applied to a value that is already a host pointer.**
   `texLoad` patches the word with `osVirtualToPhysical(...)`, the identity
   natively (`sl_ultra_shim.c:921`), so `texSelect` re-tagging it with
   `PHYS_TO_K0` (`| 0x80000000`) pushed it out of the 32-bit map. Measured:
   `genericimage->index = 0x04254180`, tagged to `0x84254180`, faulting in
   `texFindInPool((aa)[-4])` on the first scorch-buffer draw at frame 3. Fixed
   in `othermodemicrocode.c:367` behind `#ifdef __sgi`, following the identical
   precedent already in `bg.c:3448` and `bg.c:3597`. The matching build is
   unaffected: the `__sgi` branch is textually unchanged, verified by diffing
   the preprocessed `-D__sgi` output against HEAD (16016 lines, zero
   difference).
