### B-063 — windowed Facility crashes at frame 3 on Windows; headless survives 300

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, during the PowerShell workflow acceptance
- **Owner:**  Windows port
- **Status:** finding only, NOT a regression, NOT caused by the PowerShell
              workflow — proven differentially, see below
- **Blocks:** the owner actually playing Facility on Windows, which is the
              standing session goal

`SL_WINDOW=0 SL_FRAMES=300` reports `survived 300 pumped frames`, exit 0,
repeatably. The same binary launched windowed via `tools\windows\play.ps1`
opens a real window, initialises SDL and GL, opens the audio device, restores
the control style — and then takes an access violation on frame 3:

```
sightline gfx: SDL video driver = windows
sightline gfx: SDL window 960x720, GL "4.6.0 NVIDIA 591.86"
sightline audio: device open 22050 Hz 2 ch, 1024-frame buffer
sightline native: control style 1 restored
sl_aeq: alpha program ready - ...

sightline native: ACCESS VIOLATION addr 0x01c4f360
=== sightline CRASH ===
  frame  0x00000003
  pc     0x01c4f360
  ra     0x10158b01
```

then a second fault at `pc 0x00560113` while the handler unwinds.

**The differential is the useful part, and it was measured, not reasoned.**
The binary produced by the retired `tools/windows/build.sh` and the binary
produced by the new `tools/windows/build.ps1` crash **identically** — same
frame, same `pc 0x01c4f360`, same `ra 0x10158b01`, same faulting address. So
the PowerShell build is not implicated; this is a pre-existing defect on the
windowed path that had never been exercised on Windows. Every `SL_WINDOW=1`
run recorded in this file before today is Linux under xvfb.

Worth noting the shape: frame 3 is where B-061's third defect (`PHYS_TO_K0`
applied to an already-host pointer, faulting in `texFindInPool`) also landed.
That fix is present and compiled in — verify before re-deriving it — so this is
either a second instance of the same class on a draw path headless never
reaches, or the next fault after it. `pc` is in no mapped code region, so the
first thing to measure is what call transferred there, not `texSelect` itself.

Do not start by reading the renderer. Compare the windowed and headless frame
sequences and find the first call that differs.

---

**RESOLVED 2026-09-02.** A calling-convention mismatch on the GL 2.0 function
pointers. Not a renderer defect, not a missing entry point, and nothing in
Rare's code.

MEASURED on this toolchain, in exactly the include order `sl_gfx_dl.c` uses
(`<windows.h>` then `<GL/gl.h>`):

```
APIENTRY -> __attribute__((__stdcall__))
```

The fourteen typedefs at `sl_gfx_dl.c:5340-5353` declared them bare, i.e.
cdecl, where the CALLER owns the argument bytes; the real Win32 entry points
are `__stdcall` and pop their own. gcc at `-O0` pre-allocates the
outgoing-argument area once in the prologue and never re-adds after a call, so
the drift is CUMULATIVE within a function. `aeq_shader_uniforms` issues seven
of these in a row against a `0x24`-byte frame; by the fifth, the stores to
`(%esp)` are writing over its own saved `ebp` and return address. The jump to a
stack address is what a shredded frame looks like from outside.

Fix: `APIENTRY` on all fourteen. `gl.h` defines it on both hosts, so Linux -
where it is empty and the conventions coincide - is unaffected. Same class as
B-061: a Windows ABI difference invisible on Linux.

**Why no existing gate caught it.** The DL interpreter returns early at
`sl_gfx_dl.c:7868` when no window is up, so the 117 determinism traces and the
300-frame headless acceptance execute not one of these calls. `g_dl_ran` exists
for exactly this reason and it was the right counter to trust.

**How it was found, since the first report pointed everywhere else.** The
original `ra 0x10158b01` was garbage invented by a frame walk that then faulted
inside `sl_report` itself - the "second crash" was the instrument breaking, not
a second defect. Once the reporter printed `ExceptionInformation[0]` (EXECUTE,
not a bad read) and the return address at `[esp]`, the call site resolved to
`aeq_shader_uniforms+0x17f` in one step. See the preceding commit.

Two things NOT wrong, checked and cleared on the way: B-061's `PHYS_TO_K0` fix
is present and compiled in, and `sl_gfx_task` - the one `sl_`-prefixed symbol
among the 29 stubs - is dead code behind `osSpTaskStartGo`, which never fires
natively. The live renderer entry is `rspGfxTaskStart` -> `sl_gfx_frame_dl`
(`rsp.c:242`). Neither was implicated; recorded so they are not re-derived.

Windowed Facility now runs past frame 3 indefinitely. It is not yet PLAYABLE -
see B-066.

### B-064 — the Windows audio-arena reservation failure exists only as a source comment

- **Found:**  2026-09-02 (recorded from prior session recon, re-observed in
              every Windows run)
- **Owner:**  Windows port
- **Status:** parked debt, handled loud and non-fatal

Every Windows launch prints:

```
*** sightline audio: could NOT reserve the audio arena at 0x2c7ca0 (err 487).
*** Address operands will NOT match the cartridge; audio still runs.
```

Measured cause: the reservation at `0x002c7ca0` fails with
`ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS` because the CRT holds a `MEM_RESERVE` region based at
`0x00200000` before `main()` runs. It is handled loudly and non-fatally, and
`sl_audio_arena_live()` reports false, so nothing consumes a wrong value in
silence.

Recorded because it existed **only** as a comment in `sl_audio.c`. A tree-wide
grep of `docs/` for `INVALID_ADDRESS`, `arena_live` and "audio arena" returned
only pre-existing Linux-era audio discussion, so this had no entry anywhere.
Debt that lives only in a source comment is debt nobody finds.

Facility audio correctness is CLOSED and this does not reopen it: the effect is
that address operands do not match the cartridge, which is a diagnostic-fidelity
limitation, not a demonstrated output defect.

### B-066 — windowed Facility renders at ~1-2 frames/sec

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, immediately after B-063 was fixed
- **Owner:**  Windows port / renderer
- **Status:** finding, measured
- **Blocks:** the owner actually playing Facility. B-063 was the crash; this is
              now the thing in the way.

Measured on the same binary, same level, same boot:

| path | rate |
|---|---|
| `SL_WINDOW=0` headless | 2814 pumped frames/sec |
| `SL_WINDOW=1` windowed | 1.0-2.0 pumped frames/sec |

Both exit 0 and both print `survived N pumped frames`, so this is throughput,
not a hang - the hang watchdog (10 stalled seconds) never fires.

The dominant suspect is in the census the interpreter itself prints:

```
sl_dl: frame 1 cmds=602042 vtx=851 tris=529 unknown=600000
sl_walk: zero-words=600000 end-stops=0 guard-stops=6
sl_ops: unknown=600000 distinct=1  in-ucode05=600000
sl_ops: top: 00=600000
```

600,000 of the 602,042 commands walked in a frame are ZERO WORDS, reached at
depth 1, terminated by guard stops rather than by an `enddl`. So the walker is
running off the end of real lists into zeroed memory and grinding to a guard
limit, 600k commands at a time. Fixing that is likely worth ~99.7% of the
frame.

NOT investigated here: this objective was scoped to the crash, and the walker's
bounds are renderer work. Two other things visible in the same census and
deliberately left alone, recorded only so they are not rediscovered as new:
`sl_ndc: on=0 off=1587 (0.0% on screen)` with all-zero matrices, and
`sl_gl: 1 error(s) this frame, first=0x0502` (GL_INVALID_OPERATION).

---

**RESOLVED 2026-09-02.** The game heap was landing INSIDE the address space
display-list operands use for segmented addresses. Not the walker, and not a
renderer defect.

A DL operand is either a segmented address - segment index in bits 24-27, a
24-bit offset below - or a raw host pointer, and `dl_operand` tells them apart
with `(a & 0xf0000000) == 0` meaning "segmented". That is sound only while no
host pointer has a zero top nibble, i.e. while the heap sits at or above
`0x10000000`. Linux held that invariant by accident of its allocator;
`VirtualAlloc(NULL)` returned `0x0f200000` and it silently stopped being true.

MEASURED with `SL_DL_BRANCH_DBG=1`. Every zero-walking branch had an operand of
the form `0f2xxxxx`; every healthy one was `05xxxxxx`:

```
w1=05000490 seg=5  g_seg[5]=0f3865f0 -> 0f386a80  first4=e7000000 ...  ok
w1=0f222eb0 seg=15 g_seg[15]=0f331070 -> 0f553f20  first4=00000000 ...  zeros
```

`0f222eb0` is a raw heap pointer handed to `gSPDisplayList`. Read as "segment
15 + 0x222eb0" it resolved to a different address in the same arena that was
readable and zero-filled, so the walker ground to its 100000-command guard
limit. Six of those is 600000 of the 602042 commands.

Fix in the platform layer, not the renderer: request the heap above the
segmented range with a fallback chain, and complain loudly if it ever ends up
inside it anyway.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| heap base | `0x0f200000` | `0x20000000` |
| rate | 1-2 fps | 38-50 pumped frames/sec |
| commands walked per frame | 602042 | 3803 |
| zero-words / guard-stops | 600000 / 6 | 0 / 0 |
| triangles | 529 | 2307 |
| on screen | 0 (0.0%) | 3719 (53.7%), rising to 79% |
| projection matrix | all zeros | a real perspective matrix |

**Both things this entry flagged as "deliberately left alone" were the same
bug.** `sl_ndc: on=0` and the all-zero matrices were REAL, not a dead
instrument - matrix operands were being lost through the same ambiguous path.
Recorded because the opposite guess was available and would have been wrong.

**Residual, NOT fixed and deliberately so.** The ambiguity in `dl_operand`
still exists; it is simply no longer triggered by the heap. The generated
segment `.bss` buffers live inside the image at `0x013xxxxx`, also below
`0x10000000`, so an operand pointing at one would be ambiguous in exactly the
same way. Nothing observed does - every bad operand measured was a heap
pointer - but the invariant is narrower than it looks. Resolving the ambiguity
properly (for instance by requiring a segment-resolved target to look like a
display list rather than merely to be readable) is renderer work and an owner
decision.

`sl_gl: 1 error(s) first=0x0502` (GL_INVALID_OPERATION) persists and was not
investigated.

Facility is NOT playable as a result of this: it now reaches a further,
deterministic fault. See B-068.

```
without -D__sgi   exit 0, 16079 lines
with    -D__sgi   hard errors in src/bondconstants.h (BITFLAG / PROBE macros)
```

The `__sgi` branch does not preprocess at all through MinGW GCC, and 16016 is
the same order as the native figure. So that check almost certainly measured
the NATIVE branch - whose only change is the new `#else` arm, where a zero
difference is expected and proves nothing about byte-identity. The `#ifdef`
guard still makes a regression unlikely on inspection; the point is that
inspection is what we have.

Provenance, since it matters for who checks what: that line was written by an
earlier session and inherited in the working tree. It was restated in commit
`45f1c236`'s message during the PowerShell sprint without being re-run, which
is how an unverified claim acquired the appearance of a verified one.

**The honest fix is the real oracle, and it is close.** Measured: `make` is
present (GNU Make 4.4.1) and `Makefile:10` sets `IDO_RECOMP := YES`, so
qemu-irix is not needed. `make -C tools/ido5.3_recomp` builds rabbitizer
completely clean and fails at exactly one step - linking `recomp`
(`tools/ido5.3_recomp/Makefile:34`):

```
ld: cannot find -ldl
ld: --export-dynamic is not supported for PE targets, did you mean
    --export-all-symbols?
```

`-ldl` has no PE equivalent (dynamic loading lives in kernel32) and the linker
names the substitution itself. With `-ldl` dropped and `--export-all-symbols`
substituted, the link exits 0 and the binary runs and prints its usage.

NOT done here, deliberately: that is a local delta against a vendored upstream
tool, which is an owner maintenance decision, and it is outside a crash
objective. And it remains UNPROVEN that `make matching` then yields a
byte-identical ROM - `recomp` has not processed a real ELF, and `libc_impl.c`'s
IRIX syscall emulation is only exercised when it does. Linking and printing
usage says nothing about that.

**The pattern worth keeping.** Three separate instruments in one session
reported a clean result while switched off: a preprocessor diff of two EMPTY
outputs printing "IDENTICAL" (`d41d8cd9...` is the md5 of the empty string), a
`grep` over output that a compiler never produced because `mingw32in` was
absent from PATH, and the `-D__sgi` diff above. `sl_gfx_dl.c` already carries a
comment about being fooled this way three times. A null result is only evidence
when the instrument can show it ran.

### B-068 — Facility faults in stanIsSpecialBit1Set at frame 567 once it renders

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, immediately after B-066 was fixed
- **Owner:**  Windows port / game
- **Status:** new first broken stage, fully deterministic
- **Blocks:** the owner playing Facility

With the heap relocated, windowed Facility renders properly and runs ~12
seconds before faulting. Identical across repeated runs - same frame, same
`eip`, same faulting address:

```
sightline native: ACCESS VIOLATION addr 0x00000004
  access: READ
  eip    0x0051e8e5
  frame  0x00000237          (567)
```

Resolved:

```
0x0051e8e5  stanIsSpecialBit1Set      stan.c:2369
0x0051e4cf  sub_GAME_7F0B1DDC         stan.c:2190
0x0051ea85  stanTileDistanceRelated   stan.c:2443
0x0051c7ca  sub_GAME_7F0B0400         stan.c:1158
```

and further out on the stack, `chrpropRegisterRoom`,
`bondviewCalcUpdatePlayerCollision`, `MoveBond`.

Reading address `0x00000004` is offset 4 of a NULL pointer, so a stan tile or
room pointer is null on this path. NOT a wild pointer - a missing one.

**This is almost certainly newly REACHED, not newly broken.** Before B-066 the
renderer drew nothing and the game never got this far; the same pattern B-062
recorded when B-061's fix let level 12 advance from hang to crash. It should be
confirmed rather than assumed.

Note the timing: frame 567 at ~30 rendered frames/sec is roughly where the
intro camera hands over and Bond starts moving, and `MoveBond` ->
`bondviewCalcUpdatePlayerCollision` is on the stack. That is a strong hint
about which transition to instrument, not a diagnosis.

Per project rule 7 the stan format is a question for Zoinkity's notes before
the decomp, and per the measured corollary the answer should come from
comparing values on the two hosts rather than from reading `stan.c`. B-061's
first defect was also in `stanDetermineEOF` and was an ABI difference, not a
logic error; that prior is worth carrying in, without assuming it repeats.


---

**PROGRESS 2026-09-02 — localised, NOT solved. Read this before restarting.**

**1. "Newly reached, not newly broken" is CONFIRMED, with a real differential.**
The pre-B-066 binary (`sl_ultra_shim.c` restored from `e0acd6b7~1`, everything
else identical) faults at the SAME frame 567, same `eip`, same address, so
B-068 predates the heap change entirely. It is also independent of rendering:
the HEADLESS path, which never calls the display-list walker at all,
reproduces it exactly. The 300-frame acceptance simply never ran far enough —
567 > 300. That is a measured differential, not an argument.

**2. The exact path, from `__builtin_return_address` at the fault:**

```
MoveBond                      bondview2.c:7451
  -> stanTileDistanceRelated  stan.c:2452
    -> sub_GAME_7F0B1DDC      stan.c:2194
      -> callbackA(NULL, ...) = stanIsSpecialBit1Set, faults on arg0->mid.half
```

`mid` sits at offset 4 of `StandTile` (the layout B-061 established), which is
exactly the `0x00000004` being read.

**3. The null is the FIRST tile, not a traversal overrun:**

```
sl_stan: NULL tile at tileStack[0] cat=1 startTile=01c4fb24 *startTile=00000000
```

`visitedCount`=0, `cat`=1 — the first iteration. `startTile` is a valid stack
address whose pointee is NULL, so `tileStack[0] = *startTile` stored a null.
`sub_GAME_7F0B1DDC` is NOT at fault: its loop invariant holds
(`while (visitedCount < cat)`, every index below `cat` written). The
`tileStack[39]` -> `[48]` native divergence already in that function is not
implicated.

**4. The caller passes a SNAPSHOT, and that is where to look next.** The
crashing call is the FIRST of four in `MoveBond`, and it is the only one that
passes a local rather than the field itself:

```
sp200 = g_CurrentPlayer->field_488.current_tile_ptr;   /* bondview2.c:7424 */
...
bondviewCalcUpdatePlayerCollision(&move_offset, ...);  /* :7439 */
stanTileDistanceRelated(&sp200, ...);                  /* :7440  <-- CRASHES */
```

The other three pass `&g_CurrentPlayer->field_488.current_tile_ptr` directly.

**5. `current_tile_ptr` ITSELF IS HEALTHY — measured, and it kills the obvious
theory.** A probe on every change of that field reported exactly one transition
in the whole run:

```
sl_stan: frame 3 current_tile_ptr -> 20125c04
```

Set at frame 3 to a valid heap address, never changed, never nulled. So the
null in `sp200` did NOT come from the field going null. Either `sp200` is
uninitialised on the path actually taken (line 7424 sits inside a conditional
block, so a branch that skips it leaves the local holding whatever the frame
held), or it is written between the snapshot and the call.

**NOT ESTABLISHED — the next question.** Whether `sp200` is assigned at all on
this path. That is one probe at `bondview2.c:7424` and one immediately before
the call at `:7440`. It was not run here.

**Classification NOT established either, and it decides who owns the fix.** It
is unknown whether this is a host/ABI difference (the B-061/B-063/B-066 class,
four for four so far) or genuine Rare behaviour the hardware tolerated. Two
things pull in opposite directions and both should be weighed rather than
picked:

- The N64 would fault here too — address `0x00000004` is unmapped there as
  well — so the caller is not supposed to be able to pass NULL. That argues the
  null is OURS.
- But an uninitialised local reading as zero natively, where the N64 stack
  frame happened to hold a live tile pointer, is a host difference in
  everything but name. This function already carries two such divergences
  (`tileStack[39]`->`[48]`, and `sp3C`'s explicit scratch allocation in
  `bondviewCalcUpdatePlayerCollision`), both from the N64 frame layout
  supplying room gcc does not.

Under project rule 5 a crash is fixable, but if the answer is "Rare relied on
frame-layout luck" the fix is a behaviour change and belongs to the owner. Do
not assume; measure first.

The temporary probes used above were reverted once their output was recorded —
two `#ifndef __sgi` call-outs to an `fprintf` helper in
`src/platform/sl_main.c`. Everything they printed is quoted above, and they are
reconstructible from this entry in a few minutes.

---

**RESOLVED 2026-09-02.** `stanTileDistanceRelated` zeroes SIXTEEN words through
its record pointer (`stan.c:2421`, the `for(i=0;;)` HACK loop). `MoveBond`
passes `&curLocus`, and `struct move_bond_temp_struct` is TWO words. The N64
stack frame supplied the other fourteen; gcc does not, so the write ran 56
bytes past `curLocus` into `MoveBond`'s neighbouring locals — `sp200` among
them.

The measurement that settled it, after two wrong guesses about the call site:

```
sl_sp200: ASSIGNED frame=567 value=20125c04     <- valid immediately BEFORE the call
(no probe fired at any of the four call sites)  <- and not NULL at any of them
```

`sp200` was valid going in and NULL inside, so the corruption happens DURING
the call. That is why probes on either side of it disagreed, and why the
"assigned then nulled" and "never assigned" hypotheses were BOTH wrong — the
answer was a third thing neither of them covered.

Cleared on the way, and worth not re-deriving: `sub_GAME_7F0B1DDC` is not at
fault (its loop invariant holds; the `tileStack[39]`->`[48]` divergence is not
implicated), and `current_tile_ptr` is not either (one transition all run,
frame 3 -> `20125c04`, never nulled).

**Classification: host difference, the fifth of the B-061/B-063/B-066 class.**
Not Rare's logic — the original arithmetic and control flow are untouched — so
rule 5's crash exemption applies and no behaviour toggle is needed. The
identical defect had ALREADY been found and fixed for `sp3C` in
`bondviewCalcUpdatePlayerCollision` in this same file, with the same
N64-stack-layout explanation; this simply applies it to the second site. Worth
noting for whoever meets the third: the fix pattern exists, and a record passed
to `stanTileDistanceRelated` needs 16 words whatever its declared type says.

Verified: headless survives 4000 frames (died at 567 before), exit 0. Windowed
survives 1200 pumped frames at 54.7 fps, exit 0, 58.8% on screen, zero-words 0,
guard-stops 0. Headless gate 2/2.

Matching build: pure insertion, `#ifdef __sgi` arm verbatim. Verified by
inspection of the diff, NOT by preprocessing — per B-067 the `__sgi` branch
does not preprocess through MinGW GCC, so that check is still unavailable.

### B-069 — OPEN QUESTION: does a physical keypress reach the movement channels on Windows?

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, native keyboard/mouse mechanism stage
- **Owner:**  project owner — one keypress settles it
- **Status:** OPEN QUESTION, not a defect. The ambiguity is in the INSTRUMENT,
              and it is not known to be in the game.
- **Blocks:** nothing yet. Do not rework input on this entry alone.

**MEASURED.** With a real window up and capture established first
(`own=1 grab=1 ch=1`, so KBM owns the input and the channels are live),
synthetic key events injected with `keybd_event` for W, A, S, D, R and Tab
produced NO change at all: `walk=0 strafe=0`, `button=0000`, and not one
state line moved. Tab is the sharpest of these — `sl_input.c` states it is
unconditionally START, "in play and in the watch alike" — and it produced
nothing.

**NOT ESTABLISHED.** Whether a PHYSICAL keypress reaches those channels. That
was not tested and cannot be tested from here.

**WHY THE GAP IS REAL AND NOT PEDANTRY.** Mouse injection through the SAME
mechanism, in the same run, DID register — the click took capture and motion
produced `turn`/`pitch` deltas. So the injection path demonstrably works for
mouse. But SDL's keyboard path may treat injected events differently from
hardware; a raw-input device-handle check would do exactly that, and would
produce precisely this result on a game that is otherwise fine.

So there are two live possibilities and the evidence does not separate them:

1. Keyboard genuinely does not reach the channels natively — a real defect.
2. `keybd_event` injection is not equivalent to a physical keypress for SDL's
   keyboard path — an artefact, and the game is fine.

**One press on a real keyboard settles it. No counter substitutes for that.**
This is deliberately titled an open question rather than a defect, because
filing "keyboard is broken" on this evidence would put a possibly-false claim
into the permanent record.

Recorded also because of the pattern: this is the SIXTH time in one session
that an instrument's trustworthiness was the actual question rather than the
subject's behaviour — after the crash reporter that faulted inside itself, a
diff of two empty preprocessor outputs, a grep over output a compiler never
produced, the `-D__sgi` diff that measured the wrong branch, and a census
suspected of being a self-inflicted null that turned out to be real. The
lesson holds in both directions: an instrument reporting nothing is not a
negative result, and an instrument reporting something is not automatically
right either.

Context: stages 1 and 3 of the owner's chain passed on mechanism in the same
session — audio opens and survives (`submits=1498 refused=0 underruns=4`,
exit 0 over 53.5s), and mouse capture works through the GENERIC SDL
relative-mouse path with no Raw Input, no ClipCursor and no DirectInput. Delta
signs are consistent with the settled `g_dx_sign=-1, g_dy_sign=-1`. Nothing on
screen was judged: channel values are not a claim about which way the camera
turns, which is the owner's hand-test.

### B-070 — Windows audio is DIGITAL SILENCE: every submitted PCM sample is zero

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, owner physical acceptance ("there is no audible audio")
- **Owner:**  Windows port
- **Status:** OPEN. Root cause NOT established. CASE A confirmed.
- **Blocks:** the owner's runtime chain at the audio stage.

**The owner's ears are the measurement, and they said silence.** An earlier
report that Windows audio "passes on mechanism" was withdrawn: device open,
1498 submits and 0 refusals establish TRANSPORT ACTIVITY ONLY. Consumed is not
interpreted.

**MEASURED, first ordinary windowed Facility run with the detector armed:**

```
submits=448 bytes=1317184 frames=329296 peak=0 rms=0.00
nonzero=0/658592 (0.000%) silent-blocks=448/448
OUTPUT IS DIGITAL SILENCE (every submitted sample was zero)
device queue holds 17792 byte(s) of 1317184 submitted (the device consumed some)
```

So the failure is UPSTREAM of SDL. The device drains what it is handed; what it
is handed is zeros. SDL format, channels, frequency, byte order and device
state are therefore NOT the first broken stage and should not be investigated
first.

**Why this was invisible until now:** `sl_audio_report`'s atexit registration
was gated behind `SL_AUDIO_STATS` while its own comment said unconditional.
Fixed in the preceding commit. The silence detector existed the whole time and
had never fired on an ordinary run.

**LEAD, measured but NOT established as the cause.** Every ACMD task fails:

```
ACMDEXEC tasks=449 completedWithoutFault=0 commands=330779
  physical address outside mapped window 449 task(s)
  first fault: command 5, opcode LOADADPCM, operand 0xfd9348
  window 0x20fd1ca0..0x20fffca0 (the music heap)
```

`phys()` (`sl_acmd.c:415`) is a pure window test — `addr < dram_lo ||
addr + len > dram_lo + dram_size` — and `dram_lo` here is a HOST address
(`0x20fd1ca0`) while the operand is a PHYSICAL one (`0x00fd9348`). Note
`0x20fd9348 & 0x1FFFFFFF == 0x00fd9348` exactly, i.e. the operand looks like a
host pointer with the N64 physical mask applied.

**DO NOT TREAT THAT AS THE ANSWER.** One observation contradicts it and must be
reconciled first: a pre-B-066 log (heap at `0x0f200000`) reported
`operand 0x5199348, window 0x5191ca0..0x51bfca0` — where the operand IS inside
the printed window, yet the task still faulted. So either the printed window is
not the one that was tested, or a different check failed, or `len` pushed the
end past the top. That must be measured before any address-model change.
`completedWithoutFault=0` predates the B-066 heap move, so this is long-standing
and not caused by it.

**NOT ESTABLISHED:** whether the ACMD DRAM faults are the cause of the silence
or a separate defect that coexists with it. The chain still to bisect is
`game/libultra -> manager -> ACMD -> interpreter -> PCM -> AI`. The next
bounded step is to find the first ACMD command whose expected PCM write cannot
resolve, and to reconcile the pre-B-066 log above.

Facility audio CORRECTNESS on the previously accepted platform stays closed;
this is a Windows portability question only. Per `docs/doc-routing.json` the
audio microcode/ACMD command set, reverb/FX config, per-frame scheduling and
ENVMIX_STATE are recorded as NOT covered by Zoinkity's notes — do not spend
time searching them.

Acceptance is the OWNER HEARING music or SFX through
`.\tools\windows\play.ps1`. A non-zero `nonzero=` count is necessary and NOT
sufficient.

### B-071 — Windows mouse look is MIRRORED on both axes (owner physically observed)

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, owner physical acceptance of `.\tools\windows\play.ps1`
- **Owner:**  Windows port, input
- **Status:** REPAIR COMMITTED 2026-09-02, AWAITING OWNER PHYSICAL
              CONFIRMATION. Not closed until the owner's hand says so.
- **Blocks:** playable feel. Not the first broken stage in the runtime chain.

**Owner's physical result, which is authoritative:**

```
LEFT  -> RIGHT
RIGHT -> LEFT
UP    -> DOWN
DOWN  -> UP
```

All mouse looking is mirrored on both axes. Facility launches, runs, and mouse
CAPTURE works — only the direction is wrong.

**This supersedes a weaker synthetic finding of mine.** I reported injected
mouse deltas as "consistent with the settled `g_dx_sign=-1, g_dy_sign=-1`":
raw dx +40 gave `turn=-70`, dx -40 gave `turn=+70`, dy +30 gave `pitch=-70`.
Those numbers are still correct, and they are still not an answer. They measure
CHANNEL VALUES at the input layer, not which way the camera turns. I said so at
the time, but recording "consistent with" against a question only the screen
can answer under-served it, and the owner's result is the one that counts.

**What is NOT invalidated:** the WSL physical acceptance of
`g_dx_sign=-1, g_dy_sign=-1` remains historically valid FOR WSL. It does not
establish that those signs are right for the Windows SDL relative-motion
transport, which is a different path. Whoever repairs this should treat the
convention as settled for its own platform and the Windows transport as
unverified, rather than re-litigating the convention.

**DO NOT change the signs while B-070 is open**, and do not reopen mouse
architecture. The mirroring is on BOTH axes, which is the signature of a single
transport-level negation rather than two independent axis errors — worth
checking before touching `g_dx_sign` / `g_dy_sign`, which are the wrong knob if
the negation is happening in the Windows relative-motion path.

Also still parked and unrelated: B-069 (keyboard, open question).

**REPAIR 2026-09-02 — the negation is ours, it is one seam, and it was
imported from the wrong host.**

MEASURED by git, not by reading code:

```
git log -S "g_dx_sign" --all -- src/platform/sl_input.c
  fbcc3a48   [P1] input: PRE-WINDOWS-PLATFORM CHECKPOINT      <- the only commit
git show fbcc3a48^:src/platform/sl_input.c                    <- read_mouse
  in->look_yaw   += clamp_unit((float) dx * g_sens / ...)     <- NO sign applied
  in->look_pitch -= clamp_unit((float) dy * g_sens / ...)     <- NO sign applied
```

So `dx *= g_dx_sign; dy *= g_dy_sign` and its `-1/-1` defaults were BORN in
`fbcc3a48`, the checkpoint commit taken immediately before the checkout moved
to Windows, on a WSLg/XWayland hand-test. Before that commit the chain applied
no sign at all — an effective `+1/+1` — and that is the state
`docs/decisions/native-input-signs.md` screen-measured CORRECT on the real
renderer in all four directions ("the whole mouse chain, end to end").

**Windows transport, checked before the sign knobs as the entry asked.** Stock
SDL2 (`mingw-w64-i686-SDL2`, provisioned by `tools/windows/setup.ps1`, linked
`-lSDL2`, DLL staged by `build.ps1`). Sightline has no Windows relative-motion
transport of its own: tree-wide,
`grep -rn "mouse\|Mouse\|MOUSE" src/ --include=*.c --include=*.h` finds no
relative-motion handling outside `src/platform/sl_input.c`, and
`SDL_GetRelativeMouseState` has exactly ONE caller under `src/`
(`sl_input.c:516`). `src/gfx/sl_gfx_sdl.c` handles only button-down, wheel and
focus. There is therefore no earlier negation to repair — the sign
application IS the first transformation this repository owns, which is the seam
the fix rule points at.

Cleared without needing a measurement: `g_look_invert` / Look Up/Down are
pitch-only, and a pitch-only knob cannot mirror yaw. The report was both axes.

**FIX:** the default is now per-platform, because the value encodes a HOST
convention rather than anything about the game. `_WIN32` gets `+1/+1`;
every other host keeps the owner-validated `-1/-1`. Nothing downstream of
`dx *= g_dx_sign` changed, and no general controls work was done.
`SL_MOUSE_DX_SIGN` / `SL_MOUSE_DY_SIGN` remain the runtime escape hatch, so
both conventions stay reachable without a rebuild.

Rule 5: host-portability defect of the B-061/B-063/B-066/B-068 class, not
Rare's behaviour — the crash/portability exemption applies and no new
behaviour toggle is needed (the two env knobs already are one).

**Instrument proved before it was believed** — the unconditional banner
`read_env` already prints, on the shipped `build\win32\sightline.exe`, from a
real windowed Facility launch:

```
default          sightline input: mouse convention dx_sign=+1 dy_sign=+1
SL_MOUSE_*_SIGN=-1  sightline input: mouse convention dx_sign=-1 dy_sign=-1
```

The second run is the NEGATIVE CONTROL: the probe ran, and it demonstrably
CAN print a different answer, which is the check the eight instrument failures
in this project keep asking for. Neither run is evidence about physical
direction, and neither is offered as such.

**NO SYNTHETIC INPUT WAS USED, deliberately.** A synthetic pointer probe has
passed twice here while the owner's hand failed twice; the argument above needs
none. The chain from `dx` to the camera is linear with exactly one sign in it,
the owner physically observed the product as inverted on both axes, and that
single sign is the only place this repository can change it.

**NO TEMPORARY INSTRUMENTATION WAS ADDED**, so there is none to remove. The
banner used is permanent, predates this work and is unchanged.

Gates: `.	ools\windowsuild.ps1` OK (234 objects, 1 recompiled — the
change is in the binary); `.	ools\windows	est.ps1 -Runs 2` PASS 2/2,
"survived 300 pumped frames", exit 0. `make trace-verify` was NOT run: `make`
is not on PATH on this Windows checkout (MEASURED, `Get-Command make` →

Determinism is unaffected by construction — the live keyboard/mouse
producer is reachable only via `sl_gfx_active()` with no recorded stream loaded

**B-070 MEASUREMENT 2026-09-02 — the contradiction is reconciled. Repair NOT done.**

Probe placed inside `phys()` (`sl_acmd.c:415`) printing at the point of the
check, condition unchanged, reverted afterwards:

```
sl_physdbg: addr=0x00fd9348 len=32 end=0x00fd9368
            window=0x20fd1ca0..0x20fffca0 lo_fail=1 hi_fail=0
```

**Candidate 3 (len pushed the end past the top) is REFUTED.** `len` is 32 and
the end is `0x00fd9368`, nowhere near the top. **Candidate 1 is refuted for this
build too**: the operand named in the `first fault:` line and the `addr`
actually tested are the same value, so the printed window is the tested window.

It is the LOW bound that fails: `addr < dram_lo`.

**The two logs reconcile, and the arithmetic is the finding.** Both carry the
SAME offset, `0x76a8`, from a base that differs only by the N64 physical mask:

| | `dram_lo` | `dram_lo & 0x1FFFFFFF` | `+ 0x76a8` = addr | inside? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-B-066  | `0x05191ca0` | `0x05191ca0` (unchanged) | `0x05199348` | YES |
| post-B-066 | `0x20fd1ca0` | `0x00fd1ca0` | `0x00fd9348` | NO |

`0x20fd1ca0 & 0x1FFFFFFF == 0x00fd1ca0`. So a physical-address mask IS being
applied upstream of `phys()`, and it was a NO-OP for as long as the game heap
lived below `0x20000000`. B-066 moved the heap to `0x20000000` and made that
mask destructive.

**CAREFULLY BOUNDED CLAIM.** What is MEASURED: the current build fails the low
bound, with the numbers above. What is DERIVED FROM TWO LOGGED VALUES BUT NOT
MEASURED: that `phys()` would have SUCCEEDED at command 5 pre-B-066. The
pre-B-066 binary was not re-run with this probe. Anyone continuing should do
that first — it is one rebuild.

**THIS DOES NOT MEAN B-066 CAUSED THE SILENCE.** Audio was already broken before
it: the pre-B-066 log shows `completedWithoutFault=0` with all 149 tasks
faulting, and the owner heard nothing on a build predating the heap move. What
changed is WHICH address fails and WHERE, not whether audio worked. Two defects
may be stacked here and they must not be conflated.

**Next bounded step, for whoever picks this up:** find where the mask is
applied between the game's audio DMA setup and `phys()` — a tree-wide search
for `0x1FFFFFFF` / `OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL` / `osVirtualToPhysical` on the audio
path — and establish whether `dram_lo` or the operand is the side that is
wrong. DO NOT change `phys()` or the address model until that is measured;
`phys()` is a symptom site, not established as the defect.

Still true and unchanged: submitted PCM is digital silence
(`nonzero=0/438080`, `peak=0`, `silent-blocks=298/298`), the device drains
normally, and acceptance remains the OWNER HEARING sound.

### B-072 — the Facility intro costs 25-50 ms of GAME work per VI, and nothing else on the frame is close

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, measuring the reported intro crackling/slowdown (led to the VI-catch-up repair in `sl_pace_frame`)
- **Owner:**  unclear — this is renderer/sim CPU cost, not audio. Best guess Phase 2 (sim/render decoupling), because that is the refactor that would let the cost be hidden rather than paid on the VI thread.
- **Where:**  `src/platform/sl_ultra_shim.c` `sl_pump` — the cost is everything BETWEEN pump calls, i.e. the game's own frame construction, not the pump.
- **Blocks:** nothing today. The VI catch-up makes the sim and the audio run at
  the right RATE regardless, so the symptom is now judder rather than
  slow-motion-plus-crackle. It will block any acceptance phrased as "the intro
  is smooth".

MEASURED, windowed Facility from boot, 960x720, a phase timer around the pump
attributing each wall second to a phase:

```
                    intro (first ~8 s)      steady gameplay
game frame work     0.97-1.03 s / 1.00 s    0.51-0.70 s / 1.00 s
presenting          0.002 s                 0.002-0.003 s
retrace path        0.005-0.020 s           0.010-0.020 s
sleep (headroom)    0.015-0.032 s           0.29-0.49 s
```

So during the intro the game's own per-frame work saturates the wall clock and
everything the platform layer does is inside the noise. Achieved VI rate fell
to 33-48 Hz against a 60 Hz budget: roughly a 1.6x speed-up is needed to hold
60 Hz through the intro.

**The audio subsystem is EXONERATED as the cost, by A/B, not by argument.**
`SL_ACMD_EXEC=0` disables software ACMD execution entirely. Same level, same
2400 frames: 44.11 s wall with it off, 43.07 s with it on — the interpreter is
*free*, and the intro was still 32-44 Hz without it. The 1052625 audio commands
a 45-second run interprets do not show up in the frame budget.

Not investigated: WHICH part of the game's frame work it is. The intro is a
camera flythrough of the whole level and the DL grows with it (`sl_dl` reports
1963 commands / 720 tris on frame 1 against 5599 / 1486 on frame 121), so the
display-list walk is the first place to look, but that is a hypothesis and no
measurement here separates DL processing from simulation.

### B-075 — the post-1.1 GL paths compiled OUT on Windows, so B-048's fire and B-045's gas were absent from the Windows binary — FIXED 2026-09-02, owner-accepted

- **Found:**  2026-09-02, chasing the Windows explosion colour and Facility gas
  regressions against the already-accepted native behaviour.
- **Owner:**  Phase 2 (renderer), Windows platform surface.
- **Where:**  `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` — the `SL_MULTITEX` (B-048) and
  `SL_FOGSTAGE` (B-045) capability gates, and the new Win32 runtime-resolution
  block above them.
- **Blocks:** nothing further. Closed.

MEASURED, through the preprocessor in this file's include order
(`<windows.h>` then `<GL/gl.h>`) on the toolchain `build.ps1` selects: with
`GL_VERSION_1_3` and `GL_VERSION_1_4` undefined, BOTH capability gates
evaluated false and the two features compiled out entirely. Confirmed in the
shipped binary's PE import table: 31 GL names, every one of them GL 1.1 — no
`glActiveTexture`, no `glMultiTexCoord2f`, no `glFogCoordf`, and no
`glFogf`/`glFogi`/`glFogfv` either, because `SL_FOGSTAGE` had removed those
call sites too. Not a driver limitation: the context is a 4.5 compatibility
profile. Win32's OpenGL *import surface* is frozen at 1.1, so anything past it
must come through the loader.

**Repair:** resolve the three entry points at runtime through the project's
existing `sl_gl_proc` mechanism, behind `APIENTRY`-correct function-pointer
typedefs. `APIENTRY` is load-bearing and its absence was B-063 — these are
`__stdcall`, the callee pops. Every wrapper is NULL-safe, so a driver that
genuinely lacks one degrades to the pre-B-075 behaviour rather than faulting,
and `post11_ok()` says on stderr which way it went. The 60-frame `sl_cc: TEXEL1`
census now reports the RUNTIME resolution state, so `tex1=on` can no longer mean
only that the path was *built*. The non-Win32 build is untouched: the direct
calls stand exactly as they were.

**OWNER PHYSICAL ACCEPTANCE, 2026-09-02**, on the binary built from this repair:

| | verdict |
|---|---|
| B-048 — Windows explosion colour regression (TEXEL1 fire) | **FIXED / looks good** |
| B-045 — Windows Facility gas regression (fog stage) | **FIXED / looks good** |

The acceptance is the owner's own visual test. `tools/windows/test.ps1` is a
Facility smoke and does not evidence visual correctness either way.

**STILL WRONG after this repair, and explicitly NOT addressed by it:**

### B-076 — B-051's tinted glass on Windows: the alpha equation was decoded, classified and compiled, and then thrown away by a texenv mode that did not exist in the binary. 2026-09-02

The same defect class as B-075, one gate further on, and it is why the owner
still saw the tinted-glass transition wrong on the binary that fixed
explosions and gas.

#### The gate

`SL_TEXENV_COMBINE` is defined only where the header declares `GL_COMBINE` and
its operand tokens. MEASURED through the preprocessor in `sl_gfx_dl.c`'s own
include order (`<windows.h>` then `<GL/gl.h>`), on the toolchain `build.ps1`
selects:

```
GL_VERSION_1_1     defined
GL_COMBINE         ABSENT     GL_COMBINE_RGB     ABSENT
GL_COMBINE_ALPHA   ABSENT     GL_SOURCE0_RGB     ABSENT
GL_PRIMARY_COLOR   ABSENT     GL_INTERPOLATE     ABSENT
GL_CONSTANT        ABSENT
GL_COMBINE_ARB     ABSENT     GL_COMBINE_EXT     ABSENT
```

The probe discriminates: `GL_VERSION_1_1` took the DEFINED branch in the same
run, so ABSENT is a reading and not an empty instrument.

So `SL_TEXENV_COMBINE` was FALSE on Windows and **every** arm of `texenv_set`
compiled out — modes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 — leaving only the trailing
`glTexEnvi(..., GL_MODULATE)`. That is precisely the coupled fixed-function
alpha B-051 exists to escape: `out.a = tex.a * in.a`, no addend at any vertex
alpha, the pane flat at every distance.

#### The first wrong CONSUMED value, not a flag reading

400 windowed frames of facility, before the change. The pane draw was proved to
RUN first, because a count of zero must be visible as zero:

- the glass word `fc26a004 1f1093fb` reached a draw with **tris=90228**,
  classified `SHADER`, simplified `(COMB-0)*SHADE+PRIM`;
- `sl_aeq: alpha program ready` — the GL 2.0 program compiled AND linked;
- and then the requested-vs-INSTALLED census read

```
want=5 calls=30076 -> got0=30076      the alpha shader
want=4 calls=60087 -> got0=60087      AEQ_LERP
want=2 calls=65631 -> got0=65631      independent-alpha REPLACE
```

**Not one request of 155794 was honoured.** Corroborated independently by a
per-frame `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` (0x0502): `aeq_apply_env` pushes the shader's
uniforms unconditionally, and `glUniform*` with no program current is exactly
that error.

The whole of B-051 was reaching the last step and being discarded there.
`3c581b2f`, `eaba97e7` and `b51b0756` are all ancestors of HEAD — nothing was
lost, and no cherry-pick was needed.

#### THE NINTH INSTRUMENT FAULT, and it is the loudest one yet

While none of this was drawing, the existing telemetry reported

```
sl_aeq: exactness TOTAL exact=696165 inexact=0
sl_aeq:   fc26a004 1f1093fb ... (shader: exact by construction, not counted)
```

A clean bill of health, "exact by construction", from a path that rendered
nothing. Every `sl_aeq` counter is computed from the DECODED equation and is
true; not one of them observes the installed GL state. This is why the census
above measures the mode actually INSTALLED and not the mode requested — the
requested mode was right all along.

#### Repair

Define the sixteen GL 1.3 texture-env-combine enums for `_WIN32` inside the
existing B-075 block. This is a HEADER limit, not a driver one: the context is
a 4.5 compatibility profile. Unlike B-075 there is **no entry point to
resolve** — `glTexEnvi`/`glTexEnvfv` are GL 1.1 and already in opengl32.dll's
import surface, so only the enum VALUES were missing. They are read from
`mingw32/include/GL/glext.h:197-217` in the same MSYS2 tree rather than
recalled, and each is `#ifndef`-guarded so a header that does declare them
keeps its own. No new dependency, no GLEW/GLAD, no shader architecture.

#### After, same binary, same seed

```
want=5 calls=218 -> got5=218        want=4 calls=161 -> got4=161
want=2 calls=849 -> got2=849        want=0 calls=930 -> got0=930
```

100% honoured, and the per-frame 0x0502 is **gone — 0 GL-error frames**. On the
shipped, probe-free binary the pane word still reaches a draw at tris=91152 in
`SHADER` mode.

`want=5` falling from 30076 calls to 218 is a side effect worth naming: with
`texenv_set(5)` setting `g_texenv = 0`, `g_texenv != want` was true on every
single glass draw, so each one forced a `batch_end()`. That is a 138x reduction
in texenv transitions. It is a CONSEQUENCE, not a performance change — B-072
stays parked and untouched.

#### Default equals the previously accepted ON path

The question this round had to answer was whether Windows DEFAULT equals the
feature-ON path the owner already accepted. It does, for all three:

| feature | DEFAULT | explicit ON | rollback OFF |
|---|---|---|---|
| alpha equation | all 4 modes 100% installed | all 4 modes 100% installed | no transitions: all `GL_MODULATE` |
| texgen | branch taken 1206 / not-taken 0 | 1170 / 0 | 0 / 1170 |
| lighting | branch taken 1206 / not-taken 0 | 1182 / 0 | 0 / 1230 |

texgen and lighting were never gated by a header — they consume through
`glTexCoord2f`/`glColor4ub`, which are GL 1.1 — and were live on Windows all
along. The counters measure the branch actually TAKEN, not the flag.

#### An instrument rejected rather than reported

A pixel A/B across arms was attempted first and is **void**. Its run-to-run
control — default vs default, same seed — differs by 1093947 pixels over 4 of 7
frames, which swamps every feature delta it was meant to resolve. Windowed runs
here are not frame-deterministic, so the method cannot separate a feature from
timing and none of its numbers are reported. The branch counters above replaced
it precisely because a taken/not-taken split is categorical.

#### Not done, stated plainly

- **This is telemetry, not visual acceptance.** `tools/windows/test.ps1` PASS
  1/1 evidences execution only. **Closure requires the owner's own run.**
- **A separate latent defect, filed not fixed:** `#define SL_TEXENV_COMBINE`

  which is the opposite of this round's goal. Facility's LERP word
  `fc159804 5ffedbf8` carries ~180k triangles, so it is worth its own round.
- **`make trace-verify` was not available** — `make` is not on PATH on this

- **Door grid / stitch seams** — unchanged, still PARKED.

### B-078 — the grid/stitch seams are GL_CLAMP, not a missing mip chain. The GL 1.2 clamp enum is absent from the Windows header, so every clamped tile draws a bordered fringe. 2026-09-03

The third instance of the defect class B-075 and B-076 established: a GL token
the Windows `<GL/gl.h>` does not declare, silently degraded at compile time,
losing a behaviour that works on Linux.

#### The hypothesis this round opened with, and its refutation

B-077 cleared the whole tile chain and pointed downstream at
SAMPLING / MINIFICATION / LOD, with the standing suspicion that the affected
surfaces request RDP mip semantics while the renderer uploads only the base
level. **That split does not exist.** MEASURED, windowed Facility, four
replay streams, up to 4.3M textured triangles, with draws attributed to the
submitting prop by a `C0 rdp_noop` tag written into the display list from
`chrpropRender` (ucode05_old.txt line 32 — the RDP ignores C0's payload, which
is what makes it a label that cannot change a pixel):

| | metal sliding door (158) | clean control (112 labbench, 117 gastank) | world geometry |
|---|---|---|---|
| othermode texture LOD | `G_TL_LOD` | `G_TL_LOD` | `G_TL_LOD` |
| othermode texture filter | BILERP | BILERP | BILERP |
| othermode texture detail | CLAMP | CLAMP | CLAMP |
| combiner names TEXEL1 / LODFRAC | YES / YES | YES / YES | YES / YES |
| BB `level` | 5 and 6 | 5, 6, 2, 0 | 0,1,2,4,5,6 |
| GL mip levels uploaded | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| GL min / mag filter | LINEAR / LINEAR | LINEAR / LINEAR | LINEAR / LINEAR |
| F5 shift s,t | 0,0 | 0,0 | 0,0 |

Every LOD-related field is IDENTICAL across the affected class, the clean
control and the world. `BB level` varies with the TEXTURE, not with the object
class — the clean lab bench declares `level=6` exactly as the door does. So
there is no LOD or minification state the affected props exercise and the
control does not, and a missing mip chain cannot explain a defect that spares
the surfaces sharing that same state. **The mip/LOD hypothesis is REFUTED.**
It was not refuted by argument: the instrument printed `level`, `G_TL_LOD` and
the uploaded-mip count per row and could have printed a split.

Minification is likewise not the discriminator — it is heavy everywhere,
including on the clean control (117 gastank peaks at 9.45x, world geometry at
75x) and mild on the door's own largest triangles (1.91x).

#### The first differing CONSUMED sampling state: the wrap mode

Field positions are the corpus's, not gbi.h's:
`Display Lists and Object Generation/ucode05_old.txt`, `F5 rdp_settile` lower
word — `clamp t 0x00080000`, `mirror t 0x00040000`, `clamp s 0x00000200`,
`mirror s 0x00000100`. The renderer maps that bit through one function,
`tex_wrap` (`sl_gfx_dl.c:2266`), reached from exactly two call sites,
`glTexParameteri(..., GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S/T, ...)` at `:2623` and `:2624` — a
tree-wide `grep -rn "GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S\|GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T" src/` returns those
two lines and nothing else, so the whole wrap surface is those two calls.

`tex_wrap` asks for `GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE`, and immediately above it sat

```
#ifndef GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE
#define GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE GL_CLAMP
#endif
```

MEASURED through the preprocessor, in `sl_gfx_dl.c`'s own include order
(`<windows.h>` then `<GL/gl.h>`), on the toolchain `build.ps1` selects:

```
GL_VERSION_1_1        DEFINED        <- controls. Both took the DEFINED branch
GL_REPEAT             DEFINED           in the SAME run, so every ABSENT below
GL_CLAMP              DEFINED 0x2900    is a reading, not an empty file
GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE      ABSENT
GL_MIRRORED_REPEAT    ABSENT
GL_TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL  ABSENT
GL_GENERATE_MIPMAP    ABSENT
```

So the fallback fired and every clamped tile in the game was bound with
`GL_CLAMP`. **The two are not interchangeable.** Both clamp the coordinate,
but `GL_CLAMP`'s filter footprint at the image edge includes the texture
BORDER, default `(0,0,0,0)`. Under `GL_LINEAR` — which every texture here uses,
measured `min=GL_LINEAR mag=GL_LINEAR` on all 54 rows — that lays a half-texel
dark, zero-alpha fringe around the outside of every clamped image. Rare sets
the clamp bit on exactly the odd-sized images B-077 catalogued, and a prop
model is a grid of quads each sampling one of them, so the fringe lands on
every quad boundary at once. That is the reported grid/stitch pattern, and it
also explains B-077's "correlates with LARGER textures": the clamped tiles ARE
the non-power-of-two ones.

#### Requested versus INSTALLED, which is the only reading that counts

B-076's ninth instrument fault was a full set of counters describing the
REQUEST while nothing observed the installed state. So this reads the wrap mode
back out of GL with `glGetTexParameteriv` at the draw. Windowed Facility,
`facility-props2` replay, 4000 frames, distinct material rows:

```
BEFORE                                       AFTER
15  s=GL_CLAMP      t=GL_CLAMP               15  s=CLAMP_TO_EDGE t=CLAMP_TO_EDGE
 2  s=GL_CLAMP      t=GL_REPEAT               2  s=CLAMP_TO_EDGE t=GL_REPEAT
 3  s=GL_REPEAT     t=GL_CLAMP                3  s=GL_REPEAT     t=CLAMP_TO_EDGE
34  s=GL_REPEAT     t=GL_REPEAT              34  s=GL_REPEAT     t=GL_REPEAT
```

Per object, same run:

```
prop=158 PROP_GAS_PLANT_MET1_DO1  a Facility metal sliding door
    32x33 CI8  cms=2 cmt=2  ->  0x2900 GL_CLAMP    ->  0x812F GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE
prop=160 PROP_GASPLANT_CLEAR_DOOR
    54x54 IA   cms=2 cmt=2  ->  0x2900 GL_CLAMP    ->  0x812F GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE
prop=112 PROP_LABBENCH            the clean control
    32x32 CI4  cms=0 cmt=0  ->  0x2901 GL_REPEAT   ->  0x2901 GL_REPEAT
prop=117 PROP_GASTANK             the clean control
    64x32 I4   cms=0 cmt=0  ->  0x2901 GL_REPEAT   ->  0x2901 GL_REPEAT
```

The 20/34 split is identical either side, only the clamp VALUE moves, and the
driver hands `0x812F` back — so this was a header limit and never a driver one.
The minification figures are unchanged to the digit (1.91, 9.45, 3.63, 11.24),
which is what says the repair moved the wrap mode and nothing else.

#### The repair

One `#ifndef`-guarded enum in the existing `_WIN32` block, value read from
`mingw32/include/GL/glext.h:96` in the same MSYS2 tree rather than recalled.
No entry point to resolve: `glTexParameteri` is GL 1.1 and already in
`opengl32.dll`'s import surface, and the context is a 4.5 compatibility
profile. The GL-1.1 fallback stays for genuinely older targets but now carries
a comment saying it is a KNOWN visual defect rather than a neutral
degradation.

Proved in the SHIPPED translation unit, not only in a standalone probe:
`gcc -E` on `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c` with the build's own flags expands
`tex_wrap` to `return (cm & 0x02) ? 0x812F : 0x2901;`.

`GL_MIRRORED_REPEAT` is deliberately NOT added. `tex_wrap` has never honoured
the mirror bit on any platform, and Facility never sets it — over 1.7M textured
triangles the census recorded `cms`/`cmt` values of 0 and 2 only, never 1 or 3.
A tree-wide `grep -rn GL_MIRRORED_REPEAT src/` returns three lines, all
comments. Filed, not fixed.

#### Not done, stated plainly

- **No interactable console draw was ever measured.** Only Facility boots on
  Windows (B-062), and across four replay streams and ~4000 rendered frames the
  props Facility actually submits are doors 155/158/159/160, `PROP_WINDOW`,
  `PROP_LABBENCH`, `PROP_GASTANK` and `PROP_CHRREMOTEMINE` — no `PROP_CONSOLE*`
  in any of them. That the consoles share this path is DERIVED from the repair
  being a property of the F5 clamp bit and of the single `tex_wrap` every draw
  goes through, not MEASURED on a console. If the owner still sees the pattern
  on consoles after this, that inference is what failed.
- **This is telemetry, not visual acceptance.** Closure requires the owner's
  own run.
- **B-052 did NOT become a dependency.** The repair needs no tile above 0, so
  the interior-TMEM defect is still parked exactly where B-077 left it.
- **`make trace-verify` was not available** — `make` is not on PATH on this
  host. The change is renderer-only and touches no game logic, physics, AI or
  entity state.
- **B-072 performance** — untouched, still PARKED.

## 2026-09-03 — B-072 RESOLVED at its first stage: the mapped-memory probe

`[P2] gfx: B-072 - mem_readable asked the kernel per DL operand`

### The discriminator the owner supplied

After the tank-room tanks explode: enemies flood in, gas is present, gameplay
becomes near-unplayable. **Facing a wall recovers the frame rate materially;
facing the doorway the enemies come through collapses it again** — same
enemies, same gas, same level state, only the view direction changes. That
weakened a pure AI/spawn or pure gas-simulation explanation and made a
view-dependent workload the leading hypothesis. It was a hypothesis, not a
finding, and it is now MEASURED.

### One timing split, and it did not need the owner

A temporary env-gated profiler (`SL_FRAMEPROF=1`, since removed) measured, per
presented frame: total frame work (boundary interval minus the pacer's *measured*
sleep), wall ms inside `sl_gfx_frame_dl`, wall ms in swap+poll, and the DL
workload already counted in this file. Upstream game work was DERIVED as the
remainder. Facility spawn, 960x720, 30-frame windows:

```
tot=26.14  dl=25.20  pres=0.21  up=0.72 ms per frame
  inside dl:  walk=24.93   tex=5.50 (958 calls)   memprobe=15.35 (4238 calls)
```

**CASE A, and not marginally.** The native renderer is 96% of frame work;
everything upstream of it — the game's own frame, its visibility work, the
construction of the display list — is 0.72 ms. The wall-versus-doorway arms
were never needed: the defect reproduces on the spawn camera, and the previous
"25-50 ms of GAME work" figure was correct about the magnitude and wrong about
the owner. It is renderer cost, and always was.

### First load-bearing cost

`mem_readable` — the mapped-memory probe every DL operand and every triangle's
texture goes through — called `VirtualQuery` every single time: **15.35 ms of a
26.14 ms frame, 59% of all frame work, 4238 calls at 3.6 us each.**

The Linux and Windows branches of that function look symmetrical and are three
orders of magnitude apart in cost. `mincore()` reads a bitmap the kernel already
holds; `VirtualQuery` walks the VAD tree and marshals a
`MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION` across the user/kernel boundary. The call count
scales per DL command and per triangle — which is exactly the view-dependent
term the owner was feeling through the doorway.

### The repair

`vq_region`, a 16-entry memo of the regions `VirtualQuery` has already
described, cleared at the top of every display list. No probe is skipped and no
answer is invented: `VirtualQuery` already reports the whole *region* containing
an address, and the old loop discarded that and re-asked for the next operand in
the same region. Reserved and committed both count as "not free", so the kseg2
pager committing a page mid-frame cannot invalidate an answer already given —
that is what makes the memo safe rather than merely fast. `SL_DL_MEMCACHE=0`
forces every probe back through the kernel.

### MEASURED A/B, same scene, identical workload

Counters identical across both arms — 930 tris, 1891 cmds, 4238 probes, 958
texture hits — so the two runs consumed the same list and produced the same
draws:

```
SL_DL_MEMCACHE=0   tot=25.95  dl=25.02  memprobe=15.10 (4238 calls)   38.5 fps
SL_DL_MEMCACHE=1   tot=10.83  dl= 9.99  memprobe= 0.41 (4238 calls)   92.3 fps
```

Same probe count in both arms is the load-bearing detail: nothing was elided,
only re-asked. Re-confirmed after the profiler was removed, using the
pre-existing `sl_tick` instrument rather than one written for this
investigation — same 700 frames, cumulative 66.4 -> 145.0 frame/s.

### Not done, stated plainly

- **Not closed from counters.** Acceptance is the owner's tank room: enemies
  flooding the doorway without catastrophic frame-time growth, audio not
  stuttering because the frame is late, fire not feeling frames behind.
- **The wall-versus-doorway arms were never run.** They became unnecessary when
  the split resolved on the spawn camera. If the tank room does NOT improve
  proportionally, that is the measurement to go get, because it would mean a
  second view-dependent term exists that the spawn scene does not exercise.
- **There is more left in the walk.** After the fix, `walk` is still ~9.7 ms for
  930 triangles through immediate-mode `glBegin`/`glVertex`, roughly 10 us a
  triangle. That is the next objective, not this one — B-079 below.
- **`make trace-verify` was not available** — `make` is not on PATH on this
  host. The change is Windows-renderer-only, inside `#ifdef _WIN32`, and
  `grep -rn "mem_readable(" src/` finds no caller outside `sl_gfx_dl.c`; every
  one is inside the DL walk, which `sl_gfx_frame_dl` returns before reaching
  when there is no window. Headless trace replay cannot execute this code.
  `tools\windows\test.ps1 -Runs 2` passed 2/2.

### B-079 — the DL walk is ~10 us per triangle after B-072

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, in the B-072 measurement above.
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`, the `walk`/draw path.
- **Evidence:** post-fix, `dl=9.99 ms` for 930 triangles and 1891 commands, with
  the memory probe now 0.41 ms and `tex_acquire` 0.40 ms. So ~9 ms is the walk
  and the draw submission themselves. The renderer is immediate-mode
  `glBegin(GL_TRIANGLES)`/`glVertex`, and `tex_acquire` runs once per triangle
  with a linear scan of the texture cache.
- **Do not start this before the owner has physically tested the tank room** —
  B-072's acceptance is a person's judgement, not a counter, and a second
  renderer change in flight would confound it.

### B-080 — right-click aim turned the mouse into a virtual N64 stick — FIXED 2026-09-03, pending owner hand test

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, owner physical report: mouse look "somewhat too
  sensitive", and right-click aim "effectively unusable" — crosshair jumps
  around, precision aiming very difficult, "behaves like a mouse being
  converted into digital/stick input".
- **Where:** `map_kbm`'s aim branch and the `ch_on` gate in
  `src/platform/sl_input.c`; the `insightaimmode == 0` gate at the native seam
  in `src/game/bondview2.c`.
- **First wrong stage:** `map_kbm`. Normal look already used the native
  MoveData seam (`analogTurn` / `analogPitch`). Aim mode was the exception: it
  wrote the mouse into the virtual N64 stick and returned, and
  `sl_input_live_poll` withheld the channels with `&& !aim`. So the modern
  mouse seam was deliberately DISABLED for exactly the mode that needed it.
- **Why it read as digital:** GoldenEye's aim mode consumes stick POSITION —
  crosshair offset from `controlStickXRaw/YRaw` (`bondview2.c:6295`), aim turn
  only past `|stick_x| > 60` (`:5309`, `:5318`). A mouse reports a RATE.
  MEASURED at the shipped `SL_MOUSE_SENS = 6`: 13.33 px of motion in one poll
  is full deflection.
- **Fix:** turn and pitch now go through the channels in both modes, the
  mouse-generated stick stays neutral (which is also what centres the
  crosshair), and the seam applies only the two look channels while aiming.
  Live keyboard/mouse only; the gamepad keeps GoldenEye's floating manual aim
  because the pad never comes through the channels. Recorded as D-002 in
  `docs/divergences.md`.
- **Evidence:** an offline probe linking the REAL `map_kbm`, before and after,
  identical look input:

  ```
  BEFORE  aim=1 look_yaw=+0.500  ->  STICK=(+40.0,-40.0)  CH turn=  +0 pitch=  +0
  AFTER   aim=1 look_yaw=+0.500  ->  STICK=( +0.0, +0.0)  CH turn= +35 pitch= -35
  aim=0 rows byte-identical before and after; R button set in both.
  ```

  `tools\windows\test.ps1` passed: `survived 300 pumped frames`, exit 0.
- **NOT closed.** Acceptance is the owner's hands: smooth normal look, smooth
  right-click aim, no crosshair jump, tiny movements usable, rotation stopping
  the instant the mouse does, controller aiming unchanged.

### B-082 — the front end was unreachable: a single-threaded audio deadlock at the gun barrel  — CLOSED 2026-09-03

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, tracing why `play.ps1` always forced Facility.
- **Two separate bypasses, and only one was in the launcher.** `play.ps1` set
  `SL_BOOT_LEVEL`/`SL_BOOT_DIFFICULTY` unconditionally with `-Level` defaulting
  to `facility`. Removing that was necessary but not sufficient: the binary
  then reached GoldenEye's own boot chain and HUNG.
- **Measured, no boot variables set, real SDL window, 600 frames:** `stage=90`
  (`LEVELID_TITLE`), and `current_menu` walked
  `-1 INVALID -> 23 SWITCH_SCREENS -> 0 LEGAL -> 1 NINTENDO -> 2 RAREWARE`,
  then the frame pump stalled. Resolved stack:

  ```
  alCSPGetState          src/libultra/audio/cspgetstate.c:27
  musicTrack1Play        src/music.c:908
  init_menu03_gunbarrel  src/game/front.c:1846
  menu_init              src/game/front.c:8525
  ```

- **Root cause.** `while (alCSPGetState(g_musicXTrack1SeqPlayer));` waits for
  the sequence player to reach `AL_STOPPED`. Only `__CSPVoiceHandler`
  (`csplayer.c:238-297`) moves it there, reached from `alAudioFrame` via
  `sl_audio_step` — which this build drives from the VI retrace
  (`sl_ultra_shim.c:699`). On the console `amMain` owns a thread; natively
  `osCreateThread`/`osStartThread` are no-ops (`sl_ultra_shim.c:871-873`), so
  the spinning thread IS the thread that would have cleared the state.
- **The measurement, and why it could have said otherwise:** instrumented at
  the spin, the gunbarrel's `musicTrack1Play(M_INTRO)` read `state=1` on all
  **2,000,000** iterations with `g_AudioFrameCount` frozen at 679. The same
  probe read `state=0` and exited at iteration **0** for the preceding track,
  so it was capable of reporting either outcome.
- **Fix:** all three spins (`music.c` tracks 1/2/3) now call
  `sl_audio_wait_seqp_stopped`, which pumps `sl_vi_retrace_once()` while
  waiting — the platform's existing answer to a game-thread block
  (`sl_pump`, `sl_ultra_shim.c:732`). The `__sgi` path keeps the original
  text verbatim, so the matching build is untouched.
- **Determinism, stated by the binary rather than argued.** The helper prints
  `pumped N retrace(s)` only when N > 0. MEASURED: `tools\windows\test.ps1`
  (headless Facility, 300 frames) prints it **zero** times over 2 runs, while a
  front-end run prints `pumped 3` and `pumped 4` — so the instrument is
  capable of firing, and the paths traces take do not fire it.
- **Verified:** `test.ps1` PASS 2/2 (`survived 300 pumped frames`, exit 0);
  `play.ps1` alone → no `direct boot level` line, exit 0;
  `play.ps1 -Level facility -Difficulty 1` → `direct boot level 34`, exit 0.
- **Caution for anyone comparing windowed runs:** they are NOT deterministic.
  `sl_pace_frame` injects missed retraces from the wall clock. Two runs of the
  SAME binary, same pinned `SL_RNG_SEED`, differed by exactly as many lines as
  a pre-fix/post-fix pair — 44. Use the headless gate for regression, never a
  windowed log diff.

### B-083 — file select livelocks: the front end reaches it and no frame ever completes

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, immediately after B-082 unblocked the boot chain.
- **Status:** FIXED in code 2026-09-03, AWAITING OWNER PHYSICAL ACCEPTANCE.
  Was the FIRST blocker on the player path. The automated evidence is below;
  frontend visual acceptance is NOT claimed and remains the owner's call.
- **How far the front end gets:** `0 LEGAL -> 1 NINTENDO -> 2 RAREWARE ->
  3 EYE_INTRO -> 4 GOLDENEYE_LOGO -> 5 FILE_SELECT`, driven by a synthesized
  `SL_INPUT` stream pulsing A and START. Input IS consumed — the Nintendo logo
  advanced at frame 275 with input versus 769 without.
- **It is a LIVELOCK, not a spin, and that is measured.** Two runs stalled at
  the SAME frame (`0x1b7`) with the SAME call chain but DIFFERENT pc:

  ```
  run 1  pc 0x0046c17e  fileGetSaveStageCompletedForDifficulty      file2.c:343
  run 2  pc 0x0046cfb5  fileGetHighestStageDifficultyCompletedForFolder file2.c:897
  ra     interface_menu05_fileselect front.c:2349 -> menu_init front.c:8557
  ```

- **RESOLVED 2026-09-03.** Root cause: `LEVEL_SOLO_SEQUENCE` had no negative
  enumerator, so GCC gave it an UNSIGNED underlying type where IDO uses int.
  That made `for (stageid = SP_LEVEL_EGYPT; stageid >= SP_LEVEL_DAM; stageid--)`
  a `unsigned >= 0` tautology. Fixed by `SP_LEVEL_NONE = -1` under
  `#ifndef __sgi` in `src/bondconstants.h` - one enumerator, no logic touched,
  matching build unaffected (pure insertion inside the guard).

- **THE TWO BULLETS BELOW WERE WRONG, and are kept as a worked example of the
  failure mode project rule 7 warns about.** Both were reached by READING the
  C source; both were refuted by one disassembly of the shipped binary:

  > ~~Both helpers' loops are bounded (4 difficulties x ~20 stages), so the
  > unbounded thing is NOT in them.~~
  > ~~**Do not start by re-reading those two helpers.**~~

  The loops are bounded in C and NOT bounded in the emitted code. GCC proved the
  test tautological and deleted it, leaving a bare back-edge:

  ```
  46cfb1:  subl $0x1,-0x4(%ebp)    ; stageid--
  46cfb5:  jmp  46cf82             ; no cmp, no condition
  ```

  `0x0046cfb5` - the pc this very entry recorded as evidence - IS that
  unconditional jump. The instrument had photographed the infinite loop, and
  reading the source talked us out of believing it. The enclosing DIFFICULTY
  loop kept its test (`cmpl $0x0` / `js`) only because `DIFFICULTY_MULTI = -1`
  had already forced that enum signed: same source shape, opposite codegen.
- The "cheap to discriminate" eeprom hypothesis was also wrong in its framing,
  though it pointed at the right trigger by accident: the spin needs a folder
  that EXISTS but has NO completed mission, so the early return never fires.
  A populated save hides it, which is why it took a first-boot player to find.
- **Why it was reported as a GOLDENEYE_LOGO freeze:** the spin happens inside
  the file-select tick before that screen ever presents a frame, so the last
  image on screen stays the preceding logo. The owner's watchdog then abort()s
  after 30 stalled seconds - which is the "and crashes" half of the report.
  One defect, not two.

### B-085 — front end boot sequence renders wrong: logo textures and the gun barrel

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, OWNER PHYSICAL TEST of the d8ef625a build. These are
  eyes-on observations, not harness output, and they OUTRANK any automated
  "reached FILE_SELECT" result for questions about how the front end looks.
- **Status:** OPEN. Recorded, deliberately NOT started. B-083 (the file-select
  livelock) was the blocking defect and was fixed first; these are the next
  front-end work.
- **Observed, in boot order:**
  - `LEGAL` — looks correct.
  - `NINTENDO` — runs, textures VISIBLY WRONG.
  - `RAREWARE` — runs, textures VISIBLY WRONG.
  - `EYE_INTRO` — no gun-barrel look-around and no Bond walk-on; the
    presentation is simply absent rather than merely misdrawn.
  - `EYE_INTRO` — freezes/stutters around the shot.
- **NOT closed by the B-083 fix.** Advancing past a screen is not evidence that
  the screen is correct. The B-083 fix removed a spin in `file2.c` reached from
  `interface_menu05_fileselect`; it touched no texture, no combiner and no
  animation path, so it cannot have changed any of the above.
- **Probably at least two defects, not one.** The logo texture corruption is a
  decode/format question; the missing gun-barrel presentation is an animation
  or sequencing question; the stutter may be the audio pump. Do not assume a
  single root cause.
- **Prior art worth reading first:** the 2026-08 note at backlog line ~19254
  lists "boot logos in weird tones" and the gunbarrel at `title.c:168` as
  already-suspected items. Check whether this is the same defect resurfacing
  before opening a new investigation.
- **Verification when this is picked up:** owner physical test. There is no
  automated oracle for "the logo looks right", and windowed textual diffs are
  explicitly not a determinism oracle on this project (B-082).

#### UPDATE 2026-09-03 - the NINTENDO texture cause is found and fixed. It is NOT shared.

Owner re-tested the `f6d4df6b` build and added two observations: `GOLDENEYE_LOGO`
textures are also wrong, and `FILE_SELECT` is now REACHED but its textures are
wrong too. That raised the obvious question - is one defect surviving all the way
through the front end? **Measured: no.** Four screens, at least three causes.

**The NINTENDO cause, measured end to end.** The texture is not at fault at any
stage. `sl_texprobe` on the logo draw reports a clean chain - `F3` loads 512
texels at `dxt=512` from `200de878`, the tile resolves `fmt=4 siz=1`, and the
decode produces a 32x32 I8 chrome ramp with `rgbmean=82,82,82` and a live alpha
range. Source bytes, byte order, palette, format/size and the GL upload are all
correct; the six-way question the round was framed around answers **"the draw
state"**, and specifically the TEXTURE COORDINATE.

`sl_tg` reports 32 of 32 recorded surfaces as `basis=ABSENT`, and with
`SL_TEXGEN_DBG` the generator says so itself:

```
sl_texgen: DECLINED - geom has TEXTURE_GEN (mode=00062205) but the
           reflectance basis is incomplete (lookat_seen=0, cmds=0).
```

so all 3036 vertices keep their stored `s=t=0` and the entire 1012-triangle logo
samples texel (0,0) under `fc127e24 fffff9fc` = `(TEXEL0 - 0) * SHADE + 0`. One
flat tone. The SHADE is NOT the problem and that was checked rather than assumed:
`ninlogolight` (front.c:323) is `gdSPDefLights1(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF, 0,0,0, 0,0,0)`,
and the renderer read back exactly that - `L0{col=0,0,0 dir=+0,+0,+0}`,
`L1{col=255,255,255 AMBIENT}`. Ambient white, no directional light, by Rare's own
data. This **supersedes B-046 cause D**, which read the rainbow as unimplemented
RSP lighting; lighting and texgen both landed in `3c581b2f`, and what remained was
narrower than cause D described.

**Why the basis was absent, and what it should be.** The basis is RESIDENT DMEM
state that persists across display lists. `constructor_menu01_nintendo`
(front.c:1688) issues `gSPNumLights` and two `gSPLight` and NO `gSPLookAt`, so it
generates against whatever is already there - and this renderer started
`g_lookat` at all zeros, which is not "no basis" but a DEGENERATE one: both dot
products are identically 0 for every normal, so every coordinate collapses to the
midpoint. The sibling screen settles what the resident value should be.
`constructor_menu04_goldeneyelogo` (front.c:1964) calls
`guLookAtReflect(&m, la, 0,0,4000, 0,0,0, 0,1,0)` and
`constructor_menu01_nintendo` (front.c:1739) aims its camera with
`matrix_4x4_set_lookat_target(&m, 0,0,4000, 0,0,0, 0,1,0)` - the same eye, target
and up - and the GE logo was measured live uploading
`lookR=(+127,+0,+0) lookU=(+0,+127,+0)`, the identity. So the seed is the basis
the game itself installs one screen later for the same view, not an invented
constant.

**Fix:** seed `g_lookat` to the identity in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`.
`g_lookat_cmds` still counts only real uploads and `g_lookat_default` stays set
until one arrives, so `basis=ABSENT` and the DECLINED line keep telling the truth
about where the basis came from. `SL_TEXGEN_DEFBASIS=0` restores the old zero
basis and the decline from the same binary.

A/B on one binary, NINTENDO window: declines `1 -> 0`, surfaces
`32 basis=ABSENT -> 32 basis=COMPLETE`, and the generator produces real varying
coordinates (`gen=(16203.2, 6.7)`, `scale=0x0800` -> texel S=15.82 T=0.01, over a
32x32 map, which is the documented `32768*scale/65536/32 = width` relation).
Containment measured on Facility: **0 declines in BOTH arms**, 40
`basis=COMPLETE` in both, identical movemem census - the changed path is never
entered there. It can only affect a `G_TEXTURE_GEN` draw issued BEFORE the first
`gSPLookAt` of the process.

**NOT VISUALLY ACCEPTED.** The counters prove the coordinate is now generated
rather than collapsed; they do NOT prove the pixels are right. Owner physical
test still owed, and the S-vs-T axis assignment remains the unsourced arm
(`SL_TEXGEN_SWAP`, and the doc-routing `not_covered` entry for it).

**The other three screens are NOT this defect** - measured, per screen:

| screen | combiner(s) measured | texgen | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NINTENDO` | `fc127e24 fffff9fc` | declined, basis ABSENT | **this defect, fixed** |
| `RAREWARE` | `fc119623 ff2fffff`, `fc169003 1f0c93ff` | ~~none, 0 declines~~ **WRONG - see B-088** | **combiners right, texgen claim REFUTED** |
| `GOLDENEYE_LOGO` | `fc26a004 1f1093ff` | basis already COMPLETE from its own `gSPLookAt` | different cause, OPEN |
| `FILE_SELECT` | `fc129a25 ff37ffff`, `fc26a004 1f1093ff`/`1ffc93fc`, `fcff97ff ff2dfeff` | none | different cause, OPEN |

So the cross-screen answer the round asked for is explicit: **one repair does not
cover all four.** RAREWARE, GOLDENEYE_LOGO and FILE_SELECT keep their own entries
below and none of them is a texgen problem. Screen-to-frame attribution came from
a temporary `frontChangeMenu` probe (removed): LEGAL <255, NINTENDO 255-270,
RAREWARE 271-300, EYE_INTRO 301-329, GOLDENEYE_LOGO 330-518, FILE_SELECT 519+.

> **CORRECTION 2026-09-03 (B-088). The `RAREWARE` row of the table above was
> wrong about texgen, and the error came from the FRAME WINDOW, not the
> instrument.** The screen-to-frame attribution recorded just above gives
> `RAREWARE 271-300`. It is not. `retrieve_display_rareware_logo` runs
> `intro_eye_counter` up to `RAREWARE_LOGO_EYE_COUNT2` = 290 (title.c:394), so
> the screen lasts 290 frames, and 271-300 lands almost entirely inside
> NINTENDO. Measured live this round with a per-frame probe keyed on
> `gSPClearGeometryMode(-1)` (`geomseen=ffffffff`, which only
> `load_display_rare_logo` emits): **RAREWARE is DL frames 384-673**, exactly
> 290 of them. In that window it draws 268 triangles a frame of which **260
> are `G_TEXTURE_GEN`**, with 0 declines because ce524325's seeded basis is
> already in force. So RAREWARE *does* use texgen and ce524325 *did* reach it,
> which is what the owner physically observed and what this table denied. The
> COMBINERS in the row were correct; only the texgen column and the verdict
> were wrong. The residual defect is B-088 and is NOT a texgen fault.
>
> Attribution confirmed independently: the 8-triangle `fc169003` draw carries
> `prim=f0d0f0ff`, which is title.c:364's `gDPSetPrimColor(..., arg4*0xF0/0xFF,
> arg4*0xD0/0xFF, arg4*0xF0/0xFF, 0xFF)` at full fade, byte for byte.

Still OPEN and untouched this round, as scoped: the gun-barrel / `EYE_INTRO`
presentation, and keyboard/mouse input in the front end (controller works).
