### B-086 - the mission briefing crashes on a null text pointer in `textWrap`

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, incidentally, while driving the front end to
  `FILE_SELECT` with a synthetic input stream for B-085. NOT investigated - the
  B-085 round was scoped to textures and this was left alone deliberately.
- **Status:** OPEN, not started.
- **Reproduce:** replay a stream that presses A/START every 30 frames from boot;
  it walks `FILE_SELECT -> 0x06 -> 0x07 -> 0x08 -> 0x0a` and dies on entry to
  `0x0a`. Seen on two independent runs at the same place.
- **Measured:** `ACCESS VIOLATION addr 0x00000000, access READ`, resolved with
  `addr2line` against the crashing binary:

```
textWrap                             src/game/textrelated.c:797
print_objectives_and_status_to_menu  src/game/front.c:6695
constructor_menu0A_briefing          src/game/front.c:6784
menu_jump_constructor_handler        src/game/front.c:8639
lvlRender                            src/game/lv.c:702
```

- **Unmeasured:** whether the null is the objective text itself, a language-table
  lookup, or state that direct-boot normally initialises and the front-end route
  does not. Do not assume it is a text defect - the null arrives at `textWrap`,
  it is not necessarily born there.
- **Why it matters:** it is on the ordinary keyboard-free path from the title
  sequence into a mission, so it is reachable in normal play, not only under a
  synthetic stream.

- **RESOLVED 2026-09-03.** The null is `textWrap`'s **`src`** — the second
  parameter, the text to wrap — and it was NOT born in the text engine. It came
  from four seams upstream, in the briefing FILE.

  `Ubrief*Z` is read straight off the cartridge by `load_briefing_text_for_stage`
  (`front.c:6509`) and nothing byte-swapped it. `Main Menus/Solo Menus/briefings.txt`
  is the authority and gives the layout as 0x30 bytes in which **every field is a
  halfword**: four page text IDs, then up to ten `{text ID, lowest difficulty}`
  objective entries. That is `struct BriefingData` exactly, with no 32-bit field
  anywhere in it — so unswapped, every field in the record is wrong.

  Measured on Dam, with a probe at the load point and at `langGet`:

  ```
  loadbrief page=1 stage_id=33 name=UbriefdamZ bankidx=11 bankptr=200E8670
  brief[]= 002c 012c 022c 032c            <- want 2c00 2c01 2c02 2c03
  obj[0] textid=042c diff=0100            <- want 2c04, diff 1
  obj[1] textid=052c diff=0200            <- want 2c05, diff 2
  obj[2] textid=062c diff=0200            <- want 2c06, diff 2
  obj[3] textid=072c diff=0000            <- want 2c07, diff 0
  langGet slot=0x072c bank=1 bankptr=00000000 slotidx=812 off=0x00000000
  objloop i=3 textid=0x072c seldiff=2 objdiff=0 text=00000000
  textWrap ww=320 src=00000000 dst=01C7F0F0 chars=200DB1D4 font=200DAF30
  ```

  `langGet` takes the bank from `slotID >> 10`. `0x072c >> 10` is bank **1**,
  which was never loaded, so the guard added in `0f830ccd` correctly returned
  NULL — and that NULL reached `src`. The correctly-ordered `0x2c04 >> 10` is
  bank **11**, which is exactly the `bankidx=11` the same function had just
  filled. The bank number the file wanted and the bank number the loader
  provided agreed all along; only the byte order disagreed.

  The difficulty halfwords were wrong the same way and mattered just as much:
  `0x0100`/`0x0200` instead of 1/2 meant `selected_difficulty >= enabled_difficulty`
  failed for objectives 0-2, so **three of Dam's four objectives were silently
  skipped** and only the one with a zero difficulty reached `textWrap` at all.
  The crash was the visible half of a defect that was also quietly dropping
  content.

- **Fix:** `sl_swap_halfwords(ptrbriefingdata, sizeof(struct BriefingData) / 2)`
  at the one choke point the file is read in at, under `#ifndef __sgi`. Nothing
  was deleted or altered, so the matching build is untouched by construction.
- **Not** a `textWrap` guard. A NULL check there would have stopped the crash and
  still shown a briefing missing three of its four objectives.
- **After:** all four objectives resolve to real strings
  (`Bungee jump from platform.`, `Install covert modem.`, `Intercept data backup.`,
  `Neutralize all alarms.`), `textWrap` receives valid pointers on every call, and
  the front end proceeds past the briefing into `lvlStageLoad`. It then meets a
  separate, pre-existing blocker — see B-087.


  Line 456 is Rare's own `while (1) {}` LOC-error trap, taken when `hasError` is
  set while linking the path table. So the game is deliberately freezing on data
  it considers malformed — this is a data/validation failure, not a runaway loop.
- **Facility is the exception, and that is why it went unnoticed:** the health
  gate, `test.ps1` and the vertical-slice target are all Facility, the one level
  in the sample that loads.
- **Same stack as B-084** (attract-mode demo stage load). B-084 is very likely
  this defect seen from a different entry point rather than a separate bug;
  whoever picks this up should read them together.
- **NOT caused by the B-086 fix.** Direct boot never calls
  `load_briefing_text_for_stage` — measured with the probe still compiled in: the
  frontend run printed 1 `loadbrief` line, the direct-boot dam run printed 0, and
  hung at the identical pc.
- **First thing to check:** whether the path table is byte-swapped natively at
  all. B-086 was exactly this shape one file over.
- **Verification when this is picked up:** the sweep above, expecting
  `survived 300 pumped frames` on every level, plus a front-end run that reaches
  gameplay.

### B-088 - the Rareware logo sampled a 3-texel strip of its reflection map

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, owner physical test of the `ce524325` build. RAREWARE
  substantially better but NOT ACCEPTED - geometry present, texture present,
  reflective/material finish wrong.
- **Status:** FIXED in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`. Owner physical test still owed.

**Cause: settilesize is the CLAMP RECTANGLE, not the image extent.** On a
repeating axis the RDP wraps at `2^mask` and samples that whole span; `uls/lrs`
only bound the clamp window. `tile_texture` sized every GL texture from the F2
span alone, and the F5 `masks`/`maskt` fields were **never parsed at all** -
confirmed tree-wide by `grep -rn` over `src/` for `masks|maskt|mask_s|mask_t`
(the only two `src/gfx` hits are comment prose) and by
`git log --oneline -S "t->masks" --all` coming back empty. That sizing is right
only while the F2 span happens to equal `2^mask`, which B-077 measured to be
true on every repeating axis in Facility. That is a fact about Facility, not a
property of the RDP.

**Where they disagree, measured.** `assets/rarewarelogo.c:1245` (`D_02004758`)
issues its own tile state:

```
gsSPTexture(0x1C81, 0x1426, 0, 0, 1),
gsDPSetTileSize(0, 46, 116, 124, 124),
```

over a tile `title.c:363` loaded with `gDPLoadTextureBlock(..., G_IM_FMT_RGBA,
G_IM_SIZ_16b, 32, 32, 0, G_TX_WRAP, G_TX_WRAP, 5, 5, ...)`. So `cms=cmt=WRAP`
with `masks=maskt=5` - the RDP wraps at 32x32 - while the F2 span is
`((124-46)>>2)+1 = 20` by `((124-116)>>2)+1 = 3`. The renderer decoded and bound
a **20x3** image, so **242 of the logo's 260 triangles sampled a three-texel-tall
strip of a 32x32 environment map**. The other 18 take the sibling tile, which
carries `gDPLoadTextureBlock`'s own `0,0,124,124` and was therefore always
32x32 - which is exactly why the logo drew with its shape and a texture but the
wrong material finish.

Per-draw evidence (`SL_TEXPROBE` on `fc119623 ff2fffff`), before the fix:

```
sl_tex: dxt!=0 load 0: src=200e3458 ... texels=1024  drawn 32x32 x18
sl_tex: dxt!=0 load 1: src=200e4460 ... texels=1024  drawn 20x3  x242
sl_tex: stride BAD src=200e4460 fmt=1 20x3 line=8 (64 bytes) want=40
```

`18 + 242 = 260`, the whole logo body.

**Two rival hypotheses were REFUTED first, both by measurement rather than by
argument.** (1) *Byte order.* The logo tile decodes with `rgbmax=0,16,90` - red
maxing at exactly 0 over 1024 texels - which is precisely what an RGBA5551
endianness fault looks like. Decoding the dumped source bytes both ways offline
killed it: big-endian gives `Rmax=0`, little-endian gives `Bmax=0`, and NEITHER
is a plausible image. (2) *Corrupt load.* The runtime bytes were then compared
against `assets/rarewarelogo.c:1549` and match the checked-in asset exactly
(`0x00950095, ...`), so `romCopy`, segment resolution and byte order are all
correct and that tile genuinely is a dark near-black image. It is simply not the
tile those 242 triangles should have been sampling.

**Fix:** parse `masks`/`maskt` from F5 and, on an axis that repeats (`cms`/`cmt`
clamp bit clear) and names a non-zero mask, size that axis as `2^mask` instead
of the F2 span. Field positions from `include/PR/gbi.h:3415` `gsDPSetTile`
(`_SHIFTL(maskt,14,4)`, `_SHIFTL(masks,4,4)`) and `ucode05_old.txt:972,:976`;
`G_TX_CLAMP=0x2` from `gbi.h:393`. Deliberately narrow - a **clamped** axis
keeps the F2 span bit for bit, which is what leaves B-048's shifted explosion
tiles and B-077's six NPOT clamped tiles untouched. `SL_TILE_MASK=0` restores
the old sizing from the same binary.

**A/B on one binary, RAREWARE window:** `drawn 20x3 x242` becomes
`drawn 32x32 x242`, and `stride disagreements` goes `1 -> 0`. The stride is an
INDEPENDENT corroboration rather than a restatement of the same fact: the tile's
own declared `line=8` is 64 bytes is 32 texels at 16bpp, so the RDP's row stride
agrees with 32 and never with 20.

**Containment, measured in both arms rather than argued:**

- LEGAL and NINTENDO: resize counter `0`, identical textured-triangle counts.
- Facility direct boot: resize counter `0` in BOTH arms, identical 1026 textured
  tris / 27 distinct textures / 0 stride disagreements.
- Whole boot sweep: the counter is exactly 0 through DL frame 361 and first
  becomes non-zero at 421, then grows at exactly 242 per frame and stops when
  RAREWARE ends - it fires on the Rareware logo triangles and nothing else.

**NOT VISUALLY ACCEPTED.** The counters prove the full 32x32 reflection map is
now bound and sampled where a 20x3 strip was before; they do NOT prove the
pixels are right. Owner physical test is still owed.

**Known-unimplemented, deliberately not changed here.** The RDP also subtracts
the tile's `uls`/`ult` from the incoming coordinate before masking. For this
tile that is a texture-space offset of (11.5, 29) texels: it rotates which part
of the env map lands where, but not the extent. No defect was measured for it
this round, so it was left alone rather than changed on an argument. UNMEASURED.

- **Verification:** owner physical test of RAREWARE; `test.ps1`; direct Facility
  boot.

### B-089 — the EYE_INTRO gun barrel: 30 vertices built correctly, then addressed as if this were an N64

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, owner physical test of `c992c8f7`. Reported as "Bond
  renders and walks, but the moving circular aperture and the surrounding mask
  are simply absent, and the sequence stutters badly at the shot."
- **Status:** FIXED in code 2026-09-03. **Owner physical acceptance still owed —
  no pixel claim is made below.** This closes the B-085 sub-item "`EYE_INTRO` —
  no gun-barrel presentation".
- **Where:** `src/game/title.c:476` (`initializeGunBarrelIntro`).
- **Authority:** `ucode05.txt`, the `04` vertex entry — the lower word is
  `0f000000 segment / 00ffffff offset in point table`. Routed via
  `docs/doc-routing.json`, which had **no entry for `title.c`** until this round;
  `gedocs for src/game/title.c` answered "no mapped area governs". Both the
  mapping and a `not_covered` entry for the intro sequence itself are now
  recorded.

#### What the game builds, and where the native path stopped matching it

The gun barrel is not a texture and not a video. It is geometry the game
constructs at runtime, in three layers drawn in this order every frame:

```
insert_sniper_sight_eye_intro   title.c:159  the barrel interior - a 440x299
                                             RLE-expanded 8-bit image drawn as
                                             299 one-pixel-tall texrects under a
                                             black->white vertical gradient
insert_sight_backdrop_eye_intro title.c:128  THE APERTURE - the circular hole
                                             geometry, scaled 2.7 x 2.57
insert_bond_eye_intro           title.c:297  Bond and the PPK
```

`createGunbarrelRenderHole` (`title3.c:15`) writes 30 `Vtx_t` records: a
radius-64 semicircle sampled every pi/15, mirrored in x, with a per-vertex grey
ramp `143 + 111*cos(t)`. `sub_GAME_7F01BFF8` (`title3.c:75`) wraps them as two
`gSPVertex` batches of 16 and 28 `gSP1Triangle`s, terminated by `G_ENDDL`.

#### The eight questions, measured on ONE windowed run

The frame window came from a positive in-band signal, not an assumed offset: a
probe inside `renderGunbarrelEyeIntroSequence` printing every `gunbarrel_mode`
transition. **EYE_INTRO is DL frames 404-699** in that run (`mode -1 -> 2 at
dlframe 404`). B-088's lesson applied.

| # | question | answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | does `initializeGunBarrelIntro` execute? | **yes**, at DL frame 404 |
| 2 | does `createGunbarrelRenderHole` produce data? | **yes** - `vtx0 (0,-64,0)`, `vtx1 (13,-62,0)`: the top of the radius-64 circle, correct |
| 3 | is `barrelDisplayListPtr` submitted? | **yes** - the built list reads `04f00100 a00de470 bf000000 00828c96 ...` |
| 4 | which commands make the effect? | `04` vertex x2, `bf` tri1 x28, `b8` enddl |
| 5 | does the interpreter encounter them? | **yes** - 56 triangles counted per frame |
| 6 | does it emit geometry? | **the triangles yes, the VERTEX LOADS no**: `vtx=0`, `unres=4` every frame |
| 7 | if not, why? | the operand does not resolve - see below. Not offscreen, not clipped, not depth- or alpha-rejected |
| 8 | why is Bond visible and the aperture not? | Bond's geometry arrives through the ordinary model path, which carries real host pointers. This is the only list in the tree that converts its own address |

#### Root cause

```c
sub_GAME_7F01BFF8(gunbarrelgfxListPointer, barrelDisplayListPtr + 0x80000000, 0x1E);
```

`+ 0x80000000` is KSEG0 -> PHYSICAL, spelled as a 32-bit wrap-around ADD rather
than the subtraction `OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL` uses. Same constant, so on the N64 the
two are indistinguishable — and it has to be physical, because the RSP resolves
the operand through segment 0, which the cartridge leaves at 0.

Natively there is one flat address space and no segment 0 to subtract through,
which is exactly why **B-019 already made `OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL` the identity**
(`include/PR/os.h`). This call site did the arithmetic by hand, so that fix never
reached it. Measured: the vertices lived at `0x200de470`, the list named
`0xa00de470`, and `dl_operand()` returned NULL — the top nibble `a` is not a
segment the walker will try, `0xa00de470` is not mapped in a 32-bit Windows
process, and the `+0x80000000` fallback only fires below `0x80000000`. All four
batches dropped, and all the triangles naming them drawn against an unloaded
vertex buffer. **The aperture was being drawn every single frame, degenerate.**

`grep -rn "+ *0x80000000" src/ --include=*.c --include=*.h` finds this line and
nothing else, so the fault is not a class. (`bg.c:3449`, `bg.c:3598`,
`propobj.c:8831`, `propobj.c:8965` use `| 0x80000000`, the opposite direction on
a value read out of level data — a different idiom, untouched, not on this path.)

#### Fix

Guarded, `#ifdef __sgi` carrying the original line **verbatim**, native arm
routed through `OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL`. Preprocessor depth verified 0 either side of
the guard and 0 at end of file; the `__sgi` arm is byte-identical to `HEAD`'s.
`make trace-verify` is **NOT AVAILABLE** on this host (`make` exists at
`C:\msys64\usr\bin\make.exe` but is not on PATH), so the trace implication is
argued structurally and labelled **DERIVED**: the guarded arm is unchanged text,
so the matching build's preprocessed output is identical and no trace can move.

#### Containment, measured rather than argued

A/B of two windowed runs of the same probe build, differing only by this change,
comparing per-frame `cmds`/`vtx`/`tris`:

- **DL frames 1-403 (LEGAL + NINTENDO + RAREWARE): 403 of 403 lines byte-identical.**
- DL frames 404-699 (EYE_INTRO): 295 of 296 differ — `vtx=0 -> vtx=64`.

So the change cannot have touched the three screens the owner has already
accepted. After the fix the sequence also runs to completion for the first time:
`mode 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> 8 -> 9` at DL frames 641, 875, 896, 977,
1085, 1116, 1147, and mode 9 is what `isGunBarrelInMode9` hands to
`MENU_GOLDENEYE_LOGO`. Every inter-mode interval matches Rare's own constants
(21, 81, 108, 31, 31 frames against `intro_eye_counter = 20`,
`INTRO_EYE_COUNTER_CASE_4 = 108`, `0xF7/8`, `0x1E`).

#### What is NOT proven

That the pixels are right. The counters prove the aperture geometry now loads,
transforms and draws; they say nothing about its colour, its alpha, or how it
composites against the barrel backdrop. `createGunbarrelRenderHole` writes
`unkF = 0` — **alpha zero on all 30 vertices** — and
`manipulateGunbarrelAndLogoMatrices` sets `gDPSetPrimColor(..., 0xE6,0xE6,0xE6,
0x00)`, also alpha zero. Whether that is Rare being deliberate (the combiner in
force takes colour from PRIMITIVE, not from vertex alpha) or a second defect is
**UNMEASURED**. If the owner reports the aperture as present but wrongly shaded,
start there and not at the vertex path.

- **Verification:** owner physical test of `EYE_INTRO`; `test.ps1`; direct
  Facility boot; the 403-frame containment A/B above.

### B-090 — the frame pump stops for a third of a second every 60 frames, inside a debug print

- **Found:** 2026-09-03, while looking for the B-085 "freezes/stutters around the
  shot". It is not at the shot. It is everywhere.
- **Status:** FIXED in code 2026-09-03. Owner physical acceptance owed for
  whether this is the stutter they saw.
- **Where:** `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`, the `if ((frames++ % 60) == 0)` census at the
  foot of `sl_gfx_frame_dl`.

**There is no shot-specific stall, and that is measured, not assumed.** With a
per-DL-frame `QueryPerformanceCounter` delta and an in-band probe on
`gunbarrelTimer == BOND_EYE_FIRE_SHOT` to pin the exact frame, a 60 Hz windowed
run put the shot at DL frame 1114 and the mode change at 1117. Frame times across
the whole transition are flat:

```
mode 3 (walk in)   n=230  mean 17.50 ms  max 25.74
mode 4 (SHOT)      n=21   mean 21.08 ms  max 33.83
mode 5 (blood)     n=79   mean 21.41 ms  max 31.25
mode 6 (recoil)    n=106  mean 22.38 ms  max 35.85
```

Nothing above 34 ms anywhere in frames 865-1000. The audio sprint was **not**
reopened; no evidence pointed at it, and per instruction none had to.

**What the spikes actually were.** Every frame-time outlier above 45 ms in the
log sat on a multiple of 60. Bracketing the census block itself with QPC, in a
1400-frame windowed front-end run: **12 of 12 censuses cost between 276.18 ms and
527.49 ms.** The block prints roughly a hundred lines — opcode histogram, texture
census, both matrices, fog and combiner tallies — and stderr is unbuffered, so
each line is its own `WriteFile`. The pump is single-threaded, so that is the main
loop stopped dead roughly every two seconds, **in every windowed run, including
every run a player has ever seen.** It was gated on nothing.

This is native-only instrumentation, not Rare's pacing, so rule 5 does not protect
it. Gated on `SL_DL_CENSUS=1`, default off. The suppressed path still prints ONE
line on the same cadence carrying the headline counters and naming the variable
that turns it back on — because a silent instrument and an instrument that
measured nothing are the two things this file is at pains not to let a reader
confuse. Reports living *inside* the block (`SL_BB_DBG`, `SL_CC_DBG`, the texture
and matrix tallies) now need `SL_DL_CENSUS=1` too, and the heartbeat line says so.

Measured A/B on one binary, 400-frame windowed Facility direct boot: stderr 35
lines off / 228 lines on, with `sl_tex:` and `sl_mtx: proj` present only when on.
Same 1400-frame front-end run: 30.0 s -> 24.6 s wall against a 23.3 s ideal at
60 Hz. **That second figure is corroborating, not causal** — the 30.0 s arm also
carried this round's temporary probes. The causal number is the bracketed
276-527 ms.

**A caution recorded because it nearly became a wrong conclusion.** The first
frame-time table this round ranked frames 1082, 842, 962 and 782 as the worst in
the run, and every one of them is a census frame. Had that table been read before
the periodicity was noticed, it would have produced a confident, specific and
entirely wrong claim about where the game is slow. The instrument was the subject.

- **Verification:** the bracketed QPC measurement above; `test.ps1`; the gate A/B
  on one binary.

### B-091 — the front end updated at 30 Hz behind a correctly paced 60 Hz VI: a finished graphics task was being charged a vertical retrace. 2026-09-03

**Reported.** Compared against the cartridge, the Nintendo and Rareware logos
rotate too slowly and turn too few times. (The same report also put the Legal
screen at ~5 s against ~10 s on the console; see "not proved" below.)

**The two clocks.** Rare drives the boot screens from two different clocks, and
the routing table pointed at neither until this round.

- The transition TIMERS accumulate `g_ClockTimer` — elapsed VIs — so they are
  frame-rate INVARIANT. `Menu 01 - Nintendo Logo/7F00ACC8` is the authority:
  it loads `80048374`, annotated "advance timer using CPU clock", adds it to
  the menu timer at `8002A8CC` and compares against 501.
- The ANIMATION advances a fixed step per CONSTRUCTOR call, so it is frame-rate
  DEPENDENT: `ninLogoRotRate += 0.017453292` (front.c:1718) and
  `D_8002A89C += 2.4` (title.c:340), once per rendered frame.

Halve the update rate and the durations stay right while every rotation halves.
That is exactly the reported pair of symptoms, and it is why "the front end runs
at half speed" would have been the wrong diagnosis.

**Corroboration from the game's own constants**, not from the notes: the PAL/NTSC
pairs are all exactly 50:60 — legal 201/241, `NINTENDO_TIMER_MAX` 417/501,
`RAREWARE_LOGO_EYE_COUNT2` 241/290. Rare scaled the per-frame counters for the
refresh rate, so they are designed for ONE FRAME PER VI.

**MEASURED before** (windowed, SL_FPS=60, default settings; stage boundaries taken
from live `current_menu` transitions, never a guessed frame window):

```
LEGAL      dur=4.030s  vi=242  retrace=242  game frames=121  clk{2:121}
NINTENDO   dur=8.378s  vi=502  retrace=502  game frames=251  clk{2:251}  rot=250 calls
RAREWARE   dur=9.710s  vi=582  retrace=582  game frames=291  clk{2:291}  logo=241 calls
```

`g_ClockTimer` was 2 on 663 of 663 frontend frames. The histogram bucketed 0..5+
and the boot transition printed `clk{1:1 ... 5+:2}`, so it could and did print
other buckets — the constant 2 is a measurement, not a degenerate instrument.

**Not the catch-up.** `SL_VI_CATCHUP=0` reproduced 242/502/582 and the same
`clk{2:N}` histograms exactly, and `paced missed=0` printed as an explicit zero
in every steady stage. d2608e02's VI catch-up is not implicated.

**First wrong value.** Pump service accounting: `gfxsvc=242 taskret=121
retrace=242` over the Legal screen. TWO pump services occur per game frame — one
delivering the completed graphics task, one finishing the frame — and BOTH ran a
`sl_vi_retrace_once()`. So every game frame was charged two VIs: `sl_vi_elapsed`
2, `sl_ticks_next` 2, `deltaFrames` 2, `g_ClockTimer` 2. On hardware the reply to
a finished RSP/RDP task arrives on its own interrupt and costs no retrace at all.

**The repair** is one block moved: the task-reply delivery in `sl_pump` now sits
AHEAD of the retrace instead of behind it — which is what that block's own comment
("deliver its reply first") always claimed, and what the code did not do. No
timer, threshold, animation step or FPS constant is touched, and the VI itself
still runs at 60 Hz.

**MEASURED after:**

```
LEGAL      dur=3.960s  vi=238  game frames=237  clk{1:236, 2:1}
NINTENDO   dur=8.350s  vi=501  game frames=501  clk{1:501}  rot=500 calls   (was 250)
RAREWARE   dur=4.859s  vi=291  game frames=291  clk{1:291}  logo=241 calls
```

One cause covered all three. The VI-locked durations are unchanged (Legal 4.0 s,
Nintendo 8.35 s); the Nintendo rotation exactly doubled to one step per VI; and
Rareware — whose whole sequence is a per-frame counter, `intro_eye_counter`
against `RAREWARE_LOGO_EYE_COUNT2` — went from 9.71 s to 4.859 s against a derived
intent of 290/60 = 4.83 s.

**Not a divergence.** The change is confined to `src/platform/`, which the
matching build never compiles: the Makefile globs `src/*.c` and `src/game/*.c`
only (Makefile:164,167). The simulation clock is untouched — Facility direct boot
measures `tick/s = 60.0` steady before and after, so game SPEED is unchanged and
only the render/update rate doubled.

**What is NOT proved.**

- `make trace-verify` was not run: make is not on PATH on this host. The
  structural argument is that the recorded-VI-stream path is unaffected BY
  CONSTRUCTION — the retrace block is already guarded by `if (!sl_vis_active())`,
  and with that guard false the service does exactly what it did before. That is
  DERIVED, not measured.
- Gameplay code that advances per FRAME rather than per tick now advances at
  60 Hz where it previously ran at 30. On the cartridge those already ran at a
  variable rate (the hardware histogram is `{1:108, 2:224}`), so this is inside
  Rare's own model, but no per-frame gameplay effect was individually audited.
- **The Legal screen was never wrong.** It measured 4.03 s before and 3.96 s
  after, against a derived intent of 241 ticks / 60.4 ticks per second = 3.99 s.
  No mechanism in the game can make it 10 s: the timer accumulates elapsed VIs
  and is frame-rate invariant. The ~10 s console figure is unexplained and needs
  the owner's physical re-check, not a code change.
- Final perceived timing is the owner's physical test. Counters prove cadence,
  not acceptance.

- **Verification:** the before/after BOOTPROBE measurements above; the
  `SL_VI_CATCHUP=0` A/B; display-list census identical in sequence across the
  boot chain (35/0, 2902/12, 906/1018, 464/268, 113/56 aperture, 3420/28,
  5461/776); Facility direct boot `tick/s=60.0`; `test.ps1` PASS 1/1.

### THE FRONT END'S FRAME CADENCE IS WORKLOAD-DETERMINED ON HARDWARE, AND THE NATIVE HARNESS HAS NO WORKLOAD. 2026-09-03

The owner re-compared 4ff45cca against the cartridge and refuted the engineering
acceptance: LEGAL about half the ROM's duration, NINTENDO the right length but
rotating slower than the ROM, RAREWARE much closer than before but still slow,
and EYE_INTRO now roughly 2x too FAST - Bond visibly speed-walks. That is owner
physical evidence and it outranks the counters 4ff45cca was accepted on.

Two claims from that round are WITHDRAWN and must not be built on: "Rare's front
end is designed for one game frame per VI everywhere" - an inference from the
PAL/NTSC constants that the constants do not support - and "LEGAL was never
wrong".

#### The scheduling rule, from Rare's own scheduler rather than from constants

`__scHandleRetrace` (`sched.c:339-342`) ends each retrace by walking the client
list and sending `retraceMsg` when
`(*((s32*)client + 2) == 0) || ((sc->frameCount & 1) == 0)`.

`*((s32*)client + 2)` is byte offset 8, which is exactly the word `osScAddClient`
writes from its FOURTH argument (`sched.c:200`, `c[1].next = next`, `OSScClient`
being 8 bytes). So that argument selects the delivery rate: zero means every
retrace, non-zero means every SECOND retrace.

- `init.c:246` passes `NULL`. **The graphics client - the main loop - is woken on
  EVERY VI.**
- `audi.c:662` and `audi.c:813` pass `1`. The audio manager is woken every second
  VI, which is the already-measured `{2: 434}` video-frame gap histogram recorded
  earlier in this file. The reading of the predicate is therefore confirmed
  against a measurement rather than freshly guessed.

The main loop's own two gates are both permissive. `MAIN_LOOP_TICK_INTERVAL`
(`boss.c:68`) is `INTERVAL_INTER_MATH - 2688` = 387,937 cycles against a
781,250-cycle NTSC VI period - HALF a VI, not two. `pendingGfx < 2U`
(`boss.c:517`) is double-buffer back-pressure that bites only when the RCP is
more than two frames behind.

**Rare's rule is therefore: up to ONE completed update per VI retrace, throttled
only by how long the frame's own CPU and RCP work actually took.** Nothing in the
scheduler caps the front end at 30 Hz. The hypothesis that it does is refuted by
the source that implements it.

#### The achieved cadence is not a constant - it varies with the scene

Already recorded in this file, measured against the cartridge in steady gameplay:
336 presents per 600 VIs = **1.67 VI per completed update**, with a `deltaFrames`
histogram of `{1:108, 2:224}`. That histogram covered GAMEPLAY - 600 VIs anchored
120 VIs after `mission_state` reaches 1 - and NOT the front end. Both 1 and 2
occur, so the console holds no single ratio.

Against that, the owner's physical test puts the RAREWARE logo at roughly one
update per VI (a black clear plus one 32x32 textured model) and the gun-barrel
eye intro at roughly one update per TWO VIs (a full character model, a gun, a
backdrop and the aperture). Those are different scenes with different RDP costs,
and they are supposed to differ.

#### Four clocks, per stage, MEASURED

Windowed 960x720, stage boundaries taken from live `current_menu` and
`gunbarrel_mode` transitions printed by the probe itself - never a guessed frame
window. BEFORE is the pre-4ff45cca ordering restored behind a temporary toggle in
the same binary; it reproduces the historical figures (242/121, 502/251, rot=250)
exactly, which is what validates it.

```
                 BEFORE (pre-4ff45cca)             AFTER (4ff45cca = HEAD)
  stage        VI   upd  VI/upd upd/s  wall      VI   upd  VI/upd upd/s  wall
  LEGAL       242   121   2.00  29.99  4.035s   238   238   1.00  59.87  3.975s
  NINTENDO    502   251   2.00  30.02  8.360s   501   501   1.00  60.07  8.340s
  RAREWARE    578   289   2.00  29.99  9.636s   289   289   1.00  60.01  4.816s
  EYE_INTRO  1484   742   2.00  30.00 24.7s     742   742   1.00  60.03 12.37s
```

`deltaFrames` summed over each stage equalled the VI count in EVERY row of both
configurations, and `currentFrameCounter` advanced by the same figure. **The
simulation clock is correct in both and was never the defect**: 1.00 tick per VI,
which is the console's own definition.

Constructor calls, taken from the game's in-band counters rather than from frame
numbers - `ninLogoRotRate` advances exactly one degree per Nintendo constructor
call, `intro_eye_counter` and `gunbarrelTimer` likewise:

```
                          BEFORE   AFTER
  NINTENDO rotation          250     500   calls (= degrees of travel)
  RAREWARE counter           289     289   calls, against EYE_COUNT2 = 290
  EYE_INTRO gunbarrelTimer   716     716   ticks, at exactly 2.000 per call
```

#### Bond's animation clock: PER LOGICAL FRAME, not elapsed ticks

`insert_bond_eye_intro` (`title.c:308`) calls `sub_GAME_7F007F30(gdl, 2, ...)` on
NTSC and `(gdl, 1, ...)` on PAL, and that count is the trip count of a loop whose
body is `gunbarrelTimer++` and `modelTickAnim(chrModelInstance, 1, 1)`
(`title.c:211-235`). MEASURED: `gunbarrelTimer` advanced 42 over 21 updates, 162
over 81, 216 over 108 and 62 over 31 - exactly 2.000 per constructor call in
every sub-phase.

`g_ClockTimer` does not appear in `title.c` at all: a tree-wide
`grep -rn "g_ClockTimer" src/` returns its hits in `bondview2.c`, `chr.c`,
`chraction.c`, `propobj.c`, `explosion.c`, `front.c` and `lv.c`, and none in
`title.c`. So Bond consumes **one fixed advance per logical frame** and never
elapsed VI ticks. He is frame-rate DEPENDENT by construction, which is precisely
why doubling the update cadence doubled his walking speed. The same holds for the
whole eye intro (`renderGunbarrelEyeIntroSequence` advances `g_TitleX`,
`intro_eye_counter` and `word_CODE_bss_80069584` per call), for the Nintendo
rotation (`ninLogoRotRate += 0.017453292f` per call) and for the Rareware
sequence (`intro_eye_counter++` against `RAREWARE_LOGO_EYE_COUNT2`).

LEGAL and NINTENDO **durations** are the opposite: `g_MenuTimer += g_ClockTimer`,
and `g_ClockTimer` is `speedgraphframes` (`lv.c:997`), i.e. elapsed VIs. Rare
drives the boot screens from two clocks and only one of them is frame-rate
invariant. That half of 4ff45cca's diagnosis stands.

#### What the LEGAL interval actually contains

MEASURED, and it settles the owner's report in the negative. `MENU_LEGAL_SCREEN`
runs until 241 accumulated `g_ClockTimer` units, and those units ARE elapsed VIs,
so the screen occupies 241 VIs = 4.02 s **at any cadence whatever**. Three
independent cadences confirm it: 4.035 s at 2 VI/update, 3.975 s at 1 VI/update,
and - from an instrument fault that turned out to be a useful control - 4.053 s
at 3 VI/update. No scheduling change and no cadence can make this screen 8-10 s,
and the timer must not be doubled to fake it.

What is NOT established is which wall interval the owner timed on the cartridge.
Natively the two black `MENU_SWITCH_SCREENS` gaps bracketing the legal screen
cost 13 VIs and 4 VIs (0.220 s and 0.063 s), because
`init_menu00_legalscreen`'s `load_object_fill_header` and `fileValidateSaves`,
and `init_menu01_nintendo`'s ROM copy and music load, all cost ZERO VIs natively.
On the cartridge those are real PI DMAs and real EEPROM reads. The re-check
wanted is: time from the first VISIBLE legal frame to the first VISIBLE Nintendo
frame, separately from the black either side of it.

#### The first wrong value, and why there is no scheduling repair to make

4ff45cca's task-reply ordering is **KEPT**, on evidence. A finished RSP/RDP task
replies with `OS_SC_DONE_MSG` (`boss.c:667`), a different message from the
scheduler's `OS_SC_RETRACE_MSG`, and it arrives on the RCP's own interrupt.
Charging it a VI retrace was a real bookkeeping error; reverting the fix would
reinstate one.

The first wrong value is elsewhere: **the native graphics task's completion
latency is zero VI.** On hardware that latency is however long the RSP and RDP
take to draw the frame, and it is the only thing deciding how many VIs a frame
spans. Natively the display list is translated and presented immediately, so no
frame ever overruns a VI period and the loop always achieves the ceiling of
Rare's rule - one update per VI - however heavy the scene. Before 4ff45cca it
always achieved two, because of the bookkeeping error; that happened to suit the
eye intro and was wrong for the Rareware logo and for gameplay.

**Neither 1 nor 2 is the console's answer, because the console does not have
one.** Reproducing the achieved cadence requires estimating RDP cost per frame,
which the harness cannot currently do. Every alternative available without it is
on the forbidden list - a global 30 Hz, a global 60 Hz, or a per-screen timing
exception - so no timing change was made this round. That is the precise blocker:
**an RDP cost model, feeding a per-frame graphics-task completion latency
expressed in VI periods.** It is renderer work, "correct" for it is a judgment
call rather than a test, and it wants a supervised session.

#### Effect on Facility GAMEPLAY, re-measured rather than assumed

MEASURED at HEAD, Facility direct boot, windowed, `SL_TICK_DBG`: `tick/s` settles
at 59.85-60.01 and `tick/frame` at 0.5000, i.e. 118-120 pump frames per second =
**~59.2 logical updates per second** against a 60 Hz VI. The simulation clock is
60.00 ticks per wall second - identical to the cartridge's 1.00 per VI and
identical to what it was before 4ff45cca.

So 4ff45cca doubled Facility's RENDER rate from 30 Hz to 60 Hz and did NOT change
its speed. Gameplay is overwhelmingly written against `g_ClockTimer` - the
`for (i = 0; i < g_ClockTimer; i++)` and `+= g_ClockTimer` idiom runs through
`bondview2.c`, `chr.c`, `chraction.c` and `propobj.c` - so it is invariant to the
cadence, and the console's own 1.67 VI/update was itself a workload artefact
rather than an intent. `make trace-verify` could not be run (`make` is not on
PATH on this host), so this is a measurement of rate and clock, not a state-hash
equivalence proof. DERIVED, not measured: the recorded-VI-stream replay path is
unaffected, because `sl_ticks_next` takes `t` from the stream whenever one is
loaded and the retrace block is guarded by `!sl_vis_active()`.

#### One next objective, NOT started

The pump sends exactly one `OS_SC_RETRACE_MSG` per game frame, where hardware
sends one per VI and lets `boss.c`'s own `mainTickElapsed` gate decide which of
them produce an update. Retraces the pacer runs to catch up produce no message at
all, so under load the native build silently drops updates the console would have
run. At 60 Hz with `missed=0` this is unobservable, which is why it is recorded
rather than fixed: it is a behaviour change to the pump that wants
`trace-verify`.

### B-092 — the Nintendo logo ends a quarter turn short: its angle advances per RENDERED FRAME, and the native front end renders 417 frames where the cartridge renders 499. 2026-09-04

Status: **OPEN, NOT REPAIRED.** The first wrong value is identified and measured.
The repair lands in global VI accounting and was therefore not made - see
"Why there is no repair in this commit" below.

The owner captured both systems immediately before the Nintendo portion ends:
the cartridge shows the logo essentially FORWARD FACING, Sightline shows it
roughly a quarter turn away. Screen duration is correct on both and is
owner-accepted.

#### The magnitude check that governed the round

A previous round compared the two systems' whole-stage angle totals and found
8.70917 rad (ROM) against 8.74407 rad (native) - a difference of 0.0349 rad,
**exactly 2.00 degrees**. A quarter turn is 1.5708 rad. A 2-degree internal
difference cannot produce a quarter-turn visible endpoint, so that comparison
was never going to reach the defect, and every candidate this round was required
to state its predicted magnitude before being tested.

That prior native figure no longer reproduces, and is superseded: at this HEAD
the native stage runs **417** constructor calls to a final 5.881740093 rad
(337.0 deg), not 501 to 8.744 rad.

#### STATE END IS NOT VISIBLE END, on either system

`make trace-verify` is unavailable on this host (`make` is not on PATH), so
everything below is oracle and probe measurement, not a state-hash proof.

MEASURED, `tools/windows/rom-reference.ps1`, 1000 frames of `baserom.u.z64`
under parallel_n64. NINTENDO_LOGO's STATE runs frames 311..811 (501 frames,
8.348 s) but its PICTURE runs 343..776 (432 frames, 7.198 s). **The cartridge
hides the last 35 frames of the stage**, because `constructor_menu01_nintendo`
(front.c:1697) fades the ambient light to zero on a `g_MenuTimer` schedule that
expires before the stage does. Comparing state endpoints therefore compares two
moments the player never sees.

| | ROM | native (clean run) |
|---|---|---|
| last VISIBLE frame | 776 | - |
| `g_MenuTimer` there | 466 | 467 |
| `ninLogoRotRate` | 6.702040 rad | 5.375597 rad |
| degrees | 384.0 | 308.0 |
| from face-on | **24** | **52 short of 360** |

**76 degrees apart at the last frame the player sees.** That is the quarter
turn, and it is 38x the 2 degrees the whole-stage comparison could account for.

#### The metric, and what it proves is NOT wrong

`tools/trace/silhouette.py` measures the lit silhouette's horizontal span over
its vertical span. Rotation about Y changes the first and not the second, so the
ratio tracks orientation and cancels scale (the logo zooms in over its first
~54 frames) and resolution (640x480 emulator frame vs GL back buffer). Both
sides run that same code - the ROM half through `bootprobe.frame_bbox`, the
native half through `ppm_metrics` over `SL_SHOT` captures - so the two numbers
cannot drift apart through duplicated logic.

Its control: LEGAL_SCREEN, a static image, reads a constant aspect 2.957 for all
67 visible frames, while NINTENDO_LOGO sweeps. A metric that could not tell
those apart would be worthless.

MEASURED, `span_x` against angle mod 360:

* ROM - minima (edge-on) at 94 and 274 deg, `span_x` 104; maxima (face-on) at
  ~0 and ~180 deg, `span_x` 432.
* native - minima at 85-93 deg, `span_x` 104-112; maxima at ~355-13 and
  ~169-193 deg, `span_x` 424.

**At equal angles the two systems draw equal orientations**, to within one
8-pixel sample cell. So the matrix chain is NOT the defect: not row/column
major, not a transpose, not multiplication order, not a missing model-local
base transform, not the fixed-point `Mtx` conversion. None of those were
"ruled out by reading" - the rendered geometry was measured against the ROM's
at matched angles.

Presentation is not the defect either: the captured sequence advances
monotonically 4 deg per capture with no repeated and no skipped orientation, so
distinct generated orientations equal distinct presented orientations.

#### The first wrong consumed value

`speedgraphframes`, set from the `deltaFrames` the native `waitForNextFrame`
computes (`src/game/frametiming.c:53`), consumed one line later as
`g_ClockTimer` (`lv.c:997`).

MEASURED, per-frame, over NINTENDO:

* ROM: `g_ClockTimer` == 1 on **499 of 501** frames (== 3 on 2).
* native: `g_ClockTimer` == 1 on 332 frames and **== 2 on 84 of 416** (20.2%).

That is the whole defect, and the arithmetic closes exactly:
`332*1 + 84*2 = 500`, which is the `g_MenuTimer` travel that ends the stage at
`NINTENDO_TIMER_MAX` 501.

The two clocks in this screen are not the same clock:

* the stage's LENGTH comes from `g_MenuTimer += g_ClockTimer` (front.c:1653) -
  elapsed VI, so it is time-correct on both, which is why duration is right and
  owner-accepted;
* the logo's ANGLE comes from `ninLogoRotRate += 0.017453292` (front.c:1718) -
  once per CONSTRUCTOR CALL, i.e. per RENDERED frame, and exactly 1.000 degree.

On the cartridge those coincide, because the front end renders one frame per VI.
Natively `g_ClockTimer` averages 1.20, so the stage ends after 417 renders where
the cartridge gets 499, and the logo is short by precisely the missing calls.
**Nothing is wrong with the increment, the initial value, or
`NINTENDO_TIMER_MAX`; all three measured correct on both sides.**

It is not a global cadence problem. LEGAL_SCREEN ran `g_ClockTimer` == 1 on
**240 of 240** frames in the same boot. The double-VI frames appear only on the
heavier Nintendo frame, which is the workload-determined cadence B-091 and the
section above it already describe - and it is the concrete instance of the
"one next objective" recorded there: under load the native pump silently drops
updates the console would have run.

#### Why there is no repair in this commit

The fix is in VI accounting - `sl_ticks_next` and the frame pump - which feeds
`speedgraphframes` for every level and every timer in the game. That is the
scheduler work this project has already swung back and forth on twice, and it
would move Facility timing and the eye intro, both of which are outside this
round's scope. It needs the RDP cost model the section above names as the
blocker, and it wants `trace-verify`, which this host cannot run.

The tempting local patch - scaling the Nintendo increment by `g_ClockTimer` -
was rejected. It would be a no-op on the cartridge (where `g_ClockTimer` is
always 1) and would hide, not fix, a front end dropping 20% of its frames; the
same deficit is still distorting the Rareware logo, the eye intro, and every
per-frame animation in the game. Fixing one screen's symptom would cost the
evidence that found it.

#### What is NOT proven

That repairing the VI accounting is sufficient. It is proven that the angle
sequence is short by the exact number of dropped renders and that the geometry
is right at every angle tested; it is NOT proven that no second defect appears
once the frame count is correct. Owner physical re-check is still required.

### B-093 — the Nintendo deficit is HOST-LOAD DEPENDENT, not a VI-accounting defect: clean runs render 500-501 where the cartridge renders 499, and 417 was an instrumented run. 2026-09-04

Status: **B-092's mechanism is confirmed and its MAGNITUDE claim is withdrawn.**
No production change was made, on evidence. Owner physical re-check still governs.

This round was authorized to make the minimum causal repair to VI accounting.
The mandatory reproduction gate refused it: **the deficit does not reproduce on a
clean run**, and the run condition that produces it is host load, not a
scheduler semantic. What follows is why, measured.

#### The reproduction gate, MEASURED

Windowed 960x720, scratch EEPROM, normal front-end boot, no capture, no
per-frame disk output, memory-only counters printed once at stage exit. Five
consecutive clean runs of the SAME binary at HEAD 90c67458:

| run | NINTENDO constructor calls | `g_ClockTimer` | pacer `missed` | duration | final angle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 501 | 1 x 501 | 0 | 8.326 s | 421.0 deg |
| B | 501 | 1 x 501 | 0 | 8.327 s | 421.0 deg |
| D | 500 | 1 x 499, 2 x 1 | 1 | 8.338 s | 420.0 deg |
| E | 501 | 1 x 501 | 0 | 8.327 s | 421.0 deg |
| F | 500 | 1 x 499, 2 x 1 | 1 | 8.329 s | 420.0 deg |

Cartridge, same stage: **499** constructor calls, `g_ClockTimer` == 1 on 499 of
501 frames. Native clean is at parity, or **two constructors AHEAD** - which is
the "exactly 2.00 degrees" an earlier round measured and could not explain.
**417 never occurred in any clean run.**

LEGAL in the same boots: 238-241 frames, `g_ClockTimer` == 1 throughout,
`missed` == 0.

#### 501 vs 417: resolved. It is the INSTRUMENT.

The 417 figure was recorded as a "clean run". Reconstructed here: the same boot
with `SL_SHOT_EVERY=1` PPM capture running gives **233** constructor calls,
`g_ClockTimer` {1:6, 2:185, 3:42}, `missed` = 270, final angle 153 deg. The
capture is a full-window `glReadPixels` plus a file write per frame against a
16.67 ms budget, and it drops more than half the renders.

So there is a monotonic spectrum on one unchanged binary - clean 500-501,
lightly loaded ~475, captured ~233 - and every historical figure sits on it.
The prior round's own note that "a capture run is SLOWER than a clean run" was
correct and was not carried into the number it published.

**The title of 90c67458 - "native renders 417 where the cartridge renders 499" -
is withdrawn.** Native renders 500-501 when nothing else is competing for the
frame. The 76-degree endpoint deficit in that commit was measured on a run that
was not clean.

#### The load experiment: the deficit is manufacturable on demand

32 CPU spinners (one per logical processor) started before launch, stopped
after:

```
LEGAL     frames=241  clk{1:241}            missed=0   dur=4.005s
NINTENDO  frames=475  clk{1:449, 2:26}      missed=26  dur=8.325s  final 395.0 deg
```

`449*1 + 26*2 = 501` - exactly the `g_MenuTimer` travel that ends the stage.
The stage DURATION is preserved and the ANGLE is short by precisely the missed
VI periods. This is the same arithmetic B-092 reported (`332*1 + 84*2 = 500`),
reproduced deliberately.

**This is also the answer to the Legal control that B-092 could not give.**
Legal is untouched at 241/241 with `missed` = 0 in the very same loaded boot.
It is not that Legal has a different clock; it is that Legal's frame fits inside
one VI period with room to spare and Nintendo's does not, so only Nintendo is
ever late enough for a whole period to be declared missed.

#### One `g_ClockTimer` == 2 event, traced backward with values

From the captured run, NINTENDO frame 410, `dt` from the previous boundary
0.0326 s (1.96 VI periods):

| question | answer | value |
|---|---|---|
| two real VI periods elapsed? | **yes** | `sl_pace_frame` returned `missed`=1 at the previous boundary |
| two retrace messages generated? | **no** | `retraces`=2, `retrace_msgs`=1 |
| both queued? | **no** | one `OS_SC_RETRACE_MSG` reached `gfxFrameMsgQ` |
| did the game consume both separately? | **no** | `recv_retrace`=1: one `boss.c` iteration, one constructor |
| two VIs collapsed into one update? | **yes** | `vi_pending`=2 -> `sl_ticks_next` t=2 -> `speedgraphframes`=2 -> `g_ClockTimer`=2 |
| is wall-clock catch-up producing it? | **yes** | see the A/B below |
| a completed graphics task delaying the game? | **no** | the `OS_SC_DONE_MSG` reply takes the early return and spends no retrace (4ff45cca) |
| message-queue coalescing? | **no** | the queue never held two retrace messages; only one was ever sent |

Internal consistency, printed rather than assumed: `clk[i] == vi_pending[i-1]`
held on **every** NINTENDO frame in every run (501/501, 475/475, 233/233,
mismatches 0). The tick the game consumed is exactly the VI count the pump
accumulated. There is no third party.

`SL_VI_CATCHUP=0`, same 32-spinner load, is the A/B discriminator - **evidence,
not a fix**:

```
NINTENDO  frames=501  clk{1:501}  missed=0  dur=8.790s  final 421.0 deg
```

Full angular progression restored, and the stage runs **5.6% long**. That is
the trade the catch-up exists to make: it spends animation updates to keep
wall-clock duration honest.

#### Why no repair was made

The structural asymmetry is real - the pump posts one `OS_SC_RETRACE_MSG` per
GAME FRAME where hardware posts one per VI, and catch-up retraces post none.
But posting the missing messages does not restore the lost updates, because
**collapsing N elapsed VIs into one update with `deltaFrames` = N is Rare's own
behaviour, not a native divergence.** `boss.c:511` gates every retrace on
`mainTickElapsed < MAIN_LOOP_TICK_INTERVAL`, so a retrace arriving immediately
after an update is discarded by the game itself; and the cartridge's measured
Facility histogram is `{1:108, 2:224}` - the console spends most of its frames
at `deltaFrames`=2 and loses the corresponding per-frame animation steps exactly
as native does.

So the first divergence is **not** in VI accounting. It is that the native
Nintendo frame intermittently costs more than one VI period of wall time, where
the cartridge's does not. That is renderer/frame-cost work, a different round,
and nothing in the scheduler will fix it.

DERIVED, NOT MEASURED - and this is the one claim here that was reached by
reading code rather than by measurement, so it is the one to distrust: that
`boss.c`'s own `mainTickElapsed` gate would discard the extra retrace messages
if the pump posted them. It was not tested, because testing it means making the
change this round declined to make.

The rejected patch stays rejected for the same reason as before: scaling the
Nintendo increment by `g_ClockTimer` is a no-op on the cartridge and would
conceal a real frame-cost problem.

#### Refuted here, so nobody re-walks it

**Audio is not the cost.** The obvious candidate was
`init_menu01_nintendo`'s `musicTrack1Play(M_INTROSWOOSH)` - Nintendo has music,
Legal does not, and the audio manager runs on every second retrace. Measured,
same 32-spinner load, `SL_AUDIO=0`:

```
NINTENDO  frames=474  clk{1:447, 2:27}  missed=27
```

Indistinguishable from the 475/26 with audio on. The hypothesis was tidy and it
was wrong. What DOES make the Nintendo frame expensive is **not measured** here.

#### Instrument faults caught in this round

* **A pacer-slack metric that lies when the pacer is behind.** The probe
  recorded `sl_next_due - now` as per-frame headroom. Under `SL_VI_CATCHUP=0`
  it read a mean of **-0.1209 s** on frames that were demonstrably 17.5 ms
  apart - impossible as per-frame lateness. With catch-up off, `sl_next_due`
  only ever advances one period per frame, so the quantity becomes an
  ACCUMULATING DEFICIT, not headroom. Any "Nintendo costs N ms more than Legal"
  figure taken from it is unsound and is not stated above. The sound
  discriminator is `missed`, which counts whole elapsed VI periods.
* **Probe contamination, bounded rather than asserted.** The probe's own wall
  cost was measured at 0.0007 s over 752 frames (1.0 us/frame) against a
  16667 us period. Independently, a run with the probe compiled in but
  `SL_B092` unset produced identical always-on `sl_dl` census transitions to a
  probe-on run (Nintendo geometry frames 301..721, Rareware at 781), so the
  probe does not move the stage boundaries by even one 60-frame census
  interval. Bound: +/- 60 frames. Not a null test.

#### What is NOT proven

* That the owner's original quarter-turn screenshot was a loaded run. It is
  consistent with one - the measured spectrum brackets it, 22 deg short under
  light load and 247 deg short under capture, against the reported 76 - but the
  conditions of that session were not recorded and cannot be recovered.
* What the native Nintendo frame actually spends its time on. Audio is ruled
  out; the renderer is not ruled in.
* `make trace-verify` is unavailable on this host (`make` not on PATH). DERIVED,
  not measured: no production file changed this round, so the trace corpus
  cannot have moved. `git diff` against the starting HEAD touches `docs/` only.
* Whether Rareware, the eye intro or gameplay show the same load sensitivity.
  NOT MEASURED. They consume the same `speedgraphframes`, so they are exposed to
  it by construction, but no number was taken.

#### Regression checks, this round

`tools/windows/test.ps1`: PASS 1/1, "survived 300 pumped frames", exit 0.
Facility direct boot, `SL_TICK_DBG`: `tick/s` settles at **60.01** and
`tick/frame` at **0.5000** - identical to the figure recorded for B-091, so no
2x or 0.5x simulation regression. Legal remains **OPEN and PARKED**; its
threshold and duration were not touched.

### B-094 — the Nintendo frame is RENDERER-BOUND: `sl_gfx_frame_dl` is 87-94% of the interval, and the screen has 4-9% headroom on an idle machine. 2026-09-04

Answers the question B-093 left open ("what the native Nintendo frame actually
spends its time on. Audio is ruled out; the renderer is not ruled in"). The
renderer is now ruled IN, by measurement.

#### The instrument

`SL_PHASE=1` (off by default), a four-bucket split of every presented frame,
built on the `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` timer that already existed at
`src/platform/sl_ultra_shim.c`. One summary line per frontend menu, emitted on
`current_menu` change - no per-frame output, no file, no capture.

    A  game/frame work    previous frame end -> the retrace block (INCLUDES B)
    B  sl_gfx_frame_dl    accumulated in src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c, drained per frame
    C  retrace/platform    VI retraces, audio service, present, window events
    D  sleep/headroom      wall time MEASURED inside sl_pace_frame

D is measured, not derived. A pacer-slack figure computed from the schedule
reports accumulating deficit as negative headroom and lies exactly when the
loop is behind; wall time inside the pacer cannot go negative. `residual` is
printed on every line and read `+0.0000s` on every interval of every run, so
A + C + D is the frame by measurement rather than by assertion.

#### The two arms, MEASURED, same binary, same machine

Loaded arm manufactured with 32 CPU spinners (the B-093 technique).

    NINTENDO   frames  wall     fps    A game        B dl          C rt/plat     D sleep
    quiet        500   8.350s   59.9   7.297 (87.4%) 7.262 (87.0%) 0.274 (3.3%)  0.779 (9.3%)
    loaded       324   8.369s   38.7   7.890 (94.3%) 7.846 (93.8%) 0.478 (5.7%)  0.000 (0.0%)

    LEGAL      frames  wall     fps    A game        B dl          C rt/plat     D sleep
    quiet        241   4.028s   59.8   0.201 ( 5.0%) 0.161 ( 4.0%) 0.072 (1.8%)  3.755 (93.2%)
    loaded       237   4.030s   58.8   0.383 ( 9.5%) 0.335 ( 8.3%) 0.186 (4.6%)  3.461 (85.9%)

    quiet  NINTENDO clk{1:499,2:1,3+:0}  catchup=1    slept=117/500
    loaded NINTENDO clk{1:165,2:148,3+:11} catchup=178 slept=1/324

#### The mechanism, stated as numbers

The Nintendo interval takes the SAME 8.35 s of wall time in both arms - its
duration is set by the VI timebase, not by the frame rate, and that is correct.
What changes is only D. On an idle machine `sl_gfx_frame_dl` already consumes
7.26 s of the 8.35 s interval - **14.5 ms of a 16.7 ms VI period** - leaving
0.78 s of headroom across the whole screen. Ordinary contention adds ~0.6 s to
B and C, the frames cross 16.7 ms, the VI catch-up fires (178 catch-ups,
`clk` 2 on 148 frames) and 176 rendered updates are lost while the screen's
duration stays right. Legal, whose whole DL costs 0.16 s and which sleeps 93%
of the time, is untouched under the same load - 241 -> 237 frames.

So there is no "magic invocation". The endpoint moves because the margin is
4-9%, and any host jitter exceeds it.

#### Cost attribution inside the walk, and two suspects REFUTED

One-level subdivision of the 7.05 s walk (quiet Nintendo, temporary
scaffolding, since removed):

    vertex transform   0.057 s   ( 0.8%)
    emit_tri           3.762 s   (50.7%)  - of which tex_apply 0.952 s (12.8%)
    everything else    3.608 s   (48.5%)

No single stage dominates. Per triangle the whole walk costs **14.6 us on
Nintendo (1018 tris/frame) and 20.8 us on Legal (12 tris/frame)**, and
`emit_tri` alone costs 7.4 us and 8.8 us respectively. The cost is intrinsic
per-triangle interpreter work, near-constant across screens; Nintendo is simply
the first boot screen to draw ~1000 triangles.

Refuted with free counters, so nobody re-walks them:

* **VirtualQuery is NOT the cost here.** 3 calls per frame on Nintendo. B-072's
  region cache is doing its job.
* **`mem_readable` is NOT the cost.** Legal makes MORE calls per frame (3490)
  than Nintendo (2610) while its entire walk costs 0.25 ms/frame - an upper
  bound of ~0.07 us per call.
* **The triangle batch is NOT being broken per triangle.** 3 `glBegin` per frame
  on Nintendo, 6 on Legal. Immediate-mode batching is intact.
* `edge_check` is an O(1) 32x32 bit matrix, not a quadratic scan.

#### Why there is no repair in this commit

The split identifies the load-bearing STAGE (`sl_gfx_frame_dl`) with certainty,
but the one-level subdivision does not isolate a single repairable sub-stage -
the ~14.6 us/triangle is spread roughly evenly between `emit_tri` and the rest
of the walk, and the three obvious mechanisms are refuted above. Reducing
per-triangle interpreter cost is a renderer work item with real correctness
risk (`tex_apply` running once per triangle rather than per state change is the
most obvious structural candidate, at 12.8% of the walk). Choosing and scoping
that is not a measurement, so it is left to the coordinator rather than guessed
at here.

#### Instrument faults caught in this round

* **The `tex` bucket was nested inside the `tri` bucket.** `tex_apply` has
  exactly one call site and it is inside `emit_tri`, so the first "other =
  walk - vtx - tri - tex" line double-subtracted 0.95 s. Corrected to
  `walk - vtx - tri` before any conclusion was drawn from it.
* A format-string edit twice emitted a real newline where a literal \n escape
  was intended. Both times this failed the compile rather than silently
  printing the old format, which is the only reason it was cheap.

#### Probe cost, BOUNDED rather than asserted

A probe-on and a probe-off run produced **identical** always-on `sl_dl` census
transitions - Nintendo geometry frames 301..721, Rareware at 781 - so the probe
does not move a stage boundary by even one 60-frame census interval. Probe-on
Nintendo rendered 500 frames, inside the 500-501 recorded for clean runs in
B-093. The per-triangle scaffolding used for the subdivision was removed; what
remains is per-frame only (four clock reads) and off unless `SL_PHASE` is set.

#### What is NOT proven

* WHAT the ~14.6 us/triangle is actually spent on below the named stages. The
  subdivision bounds it; it does not explain it.
* That Rareware, the eye intro or gameplay have the same margin. Rareware
  measured 40-50% of its interval in the DL with ~50% headroom, so it is
  exposed but not yet critical; the eye intro and gameplay were NOT measured.
* Any GPU-side attribution. All four buckets are CPU wall time on the pump
  thread; nothing here separates driver time from GPU time.
* `make trace-verify` is unavailable on this host (`make` not on PATH).
  DERIVED, not measured: no ROM-scope file changed - `git diff --name-only`
  matches nothing under `src/game/` or `src/*.c`, and the Makefile globs only
  those two sets (`CODEFILES`, `GAMEFILES_C`), so the matching build and the
  trace corpus cannot have moved.

#### Regression checks, this round

`tools/windows/test.ps1`: PASS 1/1, "survived 300 pumped frames", exit 0.
Exe-vs-newest-source mtime check performed directly (test.ps1 carries no such
check; `grep -rn 'stale\|LastWriteTime' tools/ --include=*.ps1` finds it only in
`agent-parity.ps1` and `build.ps1`): exe newer than every file under `src/`.
Facility direct boot, `SL_TICK_DBG`: `tick/s` settles at **59.94** against the
60.01 recorded for B-091/B-093 - no 2x or 0.5x simulation regression.
`check_layering.py`: 282 violations, baseline 282, no new violations.

### B-095 — Bond's gun-barrel shadow LIGHTENED the floor it should darken: the RDP fetches a texel for RGBA/8b and the native backend fetched none. 2026-09-04

Bond walks across the gun barrel with a flat shadow under him. Natively that
shadow was a pale wash that made the floor BRIGHTER; on the cartridge it is a
dark smudge. The quantity that matters is the RELATIONSHIP, never a colour:
framebuffer luminance beneath the shadow versus immediately outside it.

#### The draw, MEASURED

One windowed run to the walk (`gunbarrelTimer` advancing, probe fired at
`gbTimer=2`; the run was carried to 3000 frames because 1400 does not reliably
reach the eye intro and 1600 never does). The quad is `doshadow`'s
(`model.c:4906`), reached through `MODELNODE_OPCODE_SHADOW`, and its image is
`tconfig=2013181C index=20123868 w=32 h=32 level=6 fmt=0 depth=1`.

`level = 6`, so `texSelect` takes its **`level != 0` branch**
(`othermodemicrocode.c:504`, the 2-cycle one) — not the `level == 0` branch a
previous round's cause chain described. Confirmed twice: the probe printed the
branch directly, and the branch is the only one that emits the measured
`G_RM_PASS / G_RM_CLD_SURF2` 2-cycle mode (`texSetRenderMode(&gdl, arg2, 2,
arg3)`).

On that branch `format`/`depth` come from `tex` when `texFindInPool` finds one
and from the image declaration otherwise. It found none:

    aa[-4]=1980 (0x7BC)  tex=00000000
    globalpool{start=20034E80 end=200D6680 left=2004E5E8 right=200D63D0}
    poolwalk: [2186] [2185] [2184] [2183] [2182] [2181] [2180] [2179]
              [2178] [2177] [2176] [2136]  walked=12

The pool is populated and walkable — the lookup is not broken, texture 1980 is
simply not in it. `texSelect` searches the GLOBAL pool (`texFindInPool(aa[-4],
NULL)` → `&ptr_texture_alloc_start`, `image.c:2411`) while Bond's model
textures were loaded into a **stack-local** one: `title.c:453` declares
`struct texpool texturePool;` in the frame, `texInitPool`s it at `title.c:519`,
and `load_object_fill_header` → `sub_GAME_7F0762E0` → `texLoadFromModelFileHeader`
loads the tuxedo into it. `ModelFileTextures` (`bondtypes.h:802`) has exactly
`sImageTableEntry`'s layout, so `texLoad` patched the very declaration
`shadow->image` points at, with a pointer into the local pool. `texSelect`'s
own `texLoad` therefore never runs (`index` is already ≥ NUM_TEXTURES) and its
lookup cannot succeed.

**This is Rare's behaviour, not a port defect.** The authority disassembly of
this function — goldeneye_docs `images text and font/7F076D68 - generate DL for
ImgDecl.txt` — shows the cartridge doing the same at `//7F076E60`:

    JAL 7F0CBB0C   ;V0=offset to matching image list slot, or NULL if no match
    OR  A1,R0,R0   ;A1=0: NULL (table at 8008C720)

and taking the same fallback at `//7F07744C`: `LBU S1,0007 (S7) ;S1=img.decl.+7:
format`. Every step of the pool choice is in code with no `__sgi` variant. The
declaration's own bytes say `fmt=0 depth=1` — RGBA/8b, on an image the bank
stores as CI8 — and `image declarations.txt` confirms the field meanings
(0x6 level, 0x7 format 0=rgba, 0x8 depth 1=8bit). Rule 5: reproduce it.

#### The first wrong value

`gbi_to_sl_fmt(RGBA, 8b)` returned **-1**. RGBA/8b is not an SDK-expressible
pair, so the decoder had no entry for it — but the RDP still fetches a texel
for it, and -1 made `tile_texture` answer `TR_FMT`, which leaves texturing
DISABLED. A disabled unit reads white, so the quad took the combiner's
non-texel term at vertex alpha 0x50 and lightened the floor.

Everything downstream of that was already correct and is not touched: vertex
`ffffff50`, prim `fefefeff`, env `000000ff`, cc `fc26a004/1f1093ff`, blend
`GL_SRC_ALPHA/GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`. **The vertex colour is white on the
cartridge too** — `D_800363F8` is `FF FF FF` with `D_800363F0` = 0x50, copied
into all four vertices by `doshadow`. The darkness was never in the vertex
colour on either platform, so nothing about the colour was changed.

#### The fix

One line in `gbi_to_sl_fmt` (`sl_gfx_dl.c`): RGBA/8b decodes as **I8** — the
byte replicated across R, G, B and alpha. Native-only by construction;
`src/gfx` has no `__sgi` build, and no file under `src/game/` or `src/*.c`
changed.

It can only affect pairs that previously returned -1, i.e. draws that today get
no texture at all, so no working consumer's format resolution moves. 8b only:
RGBA/4b is equally undefined but nothing measured reaches it, and it keeps
returning -1 rather than acquiring a guess.

#### Why I8, and what the control proves

    ROM (parallel_n64, gunbarrelTimer=90, x548..571 y152..165)
      background gradient +2/row, interpolated through the shadow rows
      beneath  203..215      outside  220..226      dip  -10 .. -19

    NATIVE A/B — same pinned RNG seed 0000000063413ba1, same record index,
    same pixels (x745..768 y462..481), one line of source different
      before   228..231  against an interpolated 217..220   +11 .. +12  LIGHTER
      after    203..213  against the same 217..220           -7 .. -15  DARKER

The control is the strongest available: identical binary lineage, identical
seed, identical frame, identical pixels, and the ONLY difference is
`if (siz == 1) return SL_TEX_I8;` compiled in or out. That isolates the fill.

What it does **not** prove: that I8 is the RDP's true silicon behaviour for
RGBA/8b. It proves the sign is reversed and the magnitude lands inside the
cartridge's range. Two further facts point the same way. The texels, dumped
from the texpool, are a radial coverage blob — 32x32, 177 distinct values, 0 at
the rim and 189 at the centre, 195 zero bytes — and the backend decoded exactly
that (`slfmt=7 name=45 decoded=32x32 rowswapped=1 rgbmax=189,189,189 alpha
min=0 max=189 zero=195/1024`). IA8 lands in the same arithmetic range but takes
alpha from the LOW nibble of a smooth ramp, which cycles 0..15 every few
texels; it would render this blob as speckle, and the cartridge's is smooth.

#### What is NOT proven

* The RDP's actual RGBA/4b behaviour. Untouched, still -1.
* That the cartridge's `texFindInPool` fails. It is DERIVED — from the
  authority disassembly passing the same NULL pool, and from the pool choice
  living in un-`#ifdef`'d shared code — not measured on hardware.
* Anything about mip level selection. The combiner is the LOD-lerp family and
  the base tile is still drawn alone, exactly as before.
* `make trace-verify` is unavailable on this host (`make` not on PATH).
  DERIVED, not measured: `git diff --name-only` matches nothing under
  `src/game/` or `src/*.c`, and the Makefile globs only those two sets, so the
  matching build and the trace corpus cannot have moved.

### B-096 — the direct-boot dev path leaves `briefingpage` at -1, and any front-end screen that reads briefing data after the level dies in `strcmp`. 2026-09-07

Found while building a controlled post-mission measurement for the demo
showcase sprint; NOT on the demo's own path, which is why it is here rather
than fixed in that sprint.

`SL_BOOT_LEVEL` skips the front end, so the only thing that ever sets
`briefingpage` on that path is `set_solo_and_ptr_briefing` (`src/game/file.c:115`):

    briefingpage = pull_and_display_text_for_folder_a0(stage);

`stage` there is a **LEVELID** — facility is 34 — but
`pull_and_display_text_for_folder_a0` (`src/game/front.c:3291`) scans
`mission_folder_setup_entries[].mission_num`, which is the **SP_LEVEL** domain
— facility is 1. Nothing matches, and it returns -1. The front end's own caller
passes the right domain (`front.c:3573` passes `mission_difficulty_highlighted`),
so a normally-booted game never carries the bad value.

It stays harmless until a front-end screen reads briefing data, which on the
direct-boot path only happens after the level ends. Then
`init_menu0C_missionfailed` -> `load_briefing_text_for_stage` (`front.c:6849`)
indexes `mission_folder_setup_entries[-1]`, hands the garbage name to
`fileNameLoadToAddr`, and `fileGetIndex` faults in `strcmp`.

MEASURED, not derived: exit `0xC0000005`, resolved with `addr2line` against the
faulting binary —

    strcmp                        src/str.c:34
    fileGetIndex                  src/game/ob.c:395
    fileNameLoadToAddr            src/game/ob.c:181
    load_briefing_text_for_stage  src/game/front.c:6849
    init_menu0C_missionfailed     src/game/front.c:7212
    menu_init                     src/game/front.c:8908

Reproduce: `SL_BOOT_LEVEL=34` and end the mission (die, abort, or complete).

NOT investigated: whether `set_solo_and_ptr_briefing`'s other caller,
`ramromreplay.c:476`, passes a LEVELID or an SP_LEVEL, and therefore whether
attract-mode playback has the same latent value. That is the first thing to
check before choosing where the fix belongs — the caller in `boss.c:378`, or
the domain mismatch inside `set_solo_and_ptr_briefing` itself. Do not "fix" it
by changing `pull_and_display_text_for_folder_a0`; both of its front-end callers
depend on the SP_LEVEL keying.

Owner: whichever phase makes the direct-boot path a supported way to play a
level through to its end. Today it is a bring-up shortcut that is always killed
by the frame limit before the mission can finish, which is why no gate has ever
hit this.

### B-096 — RESOLVED. `set_solo_and_ptr_briefing` mixed the two mission id spaces; the failure is not uniformly -1, and on Bunker 1 it names the WRONG MISSION. 2026-09-07

Closes the B-096 entry above, on branch `sightline/full-sp-native`. The filed
diagnosis was correct and INCOMPLETE, and the incomplete half is the part that
matters.

**Scope, established by tree-wide grep rather than by sampling.**
`grep -rn set_solo_and_ptr_briefing src/` returns exactly three call sites, and
ALL THREE pass a LEVELID:

    src/boss.c:378                 g_StageNum                    (direct boot)
    src/game/ramromreplay.c:476    ptr_active_demofile->stagenum (attract mode)
    src/game/ramromreplay.c:572    ptr_active_demofile->stagenum (attract mode)

`stagenum` is declared `enum LEVELID` at `ramromreplay.h:14`, and the function's
own parameter is declared `LEVELID stage`. So no caller is wrong; the domain
error is INSIDE the function, which fed that LEVELID to
`pull_and_display_text_for_folder_a0` — keyed by `mission_num`, an SP_LEVEL.
B-096 was filed as a direct-boot-only defect; the two attract-mode call sites it
listed as "NOT investigated" are on the ordinary front-end path.

**MEASURED, all twenty campaign missions, direct boot, one probe line per run
out of `set_solo_and_ptr_briefing` itself (temporary, removed before commit):**

| | briefingpage | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 19 of 20 | `-1` | no row has `mission_num` == 33, 34, 35 … |
| bunker1 | `15` | row 15 is **Statue** (`stage_id=22`, `mission_num=9`) |

`LEVELID_BUNKER1` is 9 and `SP_LEVEL_STATUE` is also 9, so the two ranges
OVERLAP and the scan matched. **That is the finding B-096 missed:** the defect
does not always produce the -1 sentinel. Where the ranges overlap it produces a
confident, wrong mission, which walks straight past the `-1 < briefingpage`
guard at `file.c:42` and would record Statue's unlock and Statue's target time
for a Bunker 1 completion — silent save corruption rather than a crash. The -1
cases are the loud half (B-096's measured `0xC0000005` in `strcmp`) and the
merely-skipped half (`end_of_mission_briefing` does nothing, so nothing
unlocks).

**Fix.** `sl_briefing_page_for_stage_id` (`front.c`) scans the SAME table by the
column that matches the domain — `stage_id` — with the loop shape, terminator
test and `-1` return deliberately identical to its SP_LEVEL-keyed sibling. There
was no such derivation anywhere before: `grep -rn mission_folder_setup_entries
src/` returns 30 uses and not one scans `stage_id`. Negative arguments are
rejected up front, because MISSION_HEADER rows store `stage_id = LEVELID_NONE`
and would otherwise match. No per-mission special case; no change to
`pull_and_display_text_for_folder_a0`, whose two front-end callers depend on its
SP_LEVEL keying — the thing B-096 explicitly warned against.

**AFTER, same probe, same twenty runs: 0 mismatches / 20.** Every mission
resolves to the row whose `stage_id` equals the booted LEVELID, and — as an
independent cross-check on a column the fix never reads — every resolved row's
`mission_num` equals that mission's campaign position, DAM=0 … EGYPT=19.

**Matching safety.** `-E -P -x c`, includes stripped, before (master) vs after:

    file.c    __sgi     3368 b vs   3368 b   IDENTICAL
    front.c   __sgi   254221 b vs 254221 b   IDENTICAL
    front.h   __sgi     6306 b vs   6306 b   IDENTICAL
    (native arms differ, as intended)
    POSITIVE CONTROL: perturbing file.c's __sgi arm DOES diff, so the
    comparison is not vacuous.

The first attempt at this comparison produced two 0-byte files and reported them
IDENTICAL — `.src` made gcc treat the input as a linker input, not C source.
Caught only because sizes were printed. `-x c` is required; this is the third
time this project has recorded that failure class.

**Regression.** `SL_TRACE_OUT` state traces, pinned `SL_RNG_SEED=1234abcd`, 3000
frames / 1499 ticks on each of the twenty levels, before vs after:
**20/20 byte-identical, 0 diverged, 0 zero-byte.** `make trace-verify` is NOT
runnable on this host (no MIPS toolchain, Windows venv); this stands in for it
and is the same state schema the harness hashes.

#### Still open, and NOT claimed

* The end-to-end debrief was NOT driven on this branch. Bond survives 40000
  headless frames idle AND with the `fire` input routine on facility and
  bunker1, so no run here reached mission end. What is proven is that the VALUE
  the debrief consumes is now right on all twenty; the downstream fault itself
  remains B-096's original addr2line measurement.
* Front-end mission select, difficulty and briefing were never driven by input
  on this branch — see the coverage matrix note below.
