### B-097 — Dam has no sky: the sky is built from RAW RDP TRIANGLES pushed through `rdphalf`, and the native interpreter discarded every word of them. 2026-09-08

- **Found:** 2026-09-08, owner-reported: Dam's sky/background absent in the
  level intro and still absent once gameplay begins.
- **Ours, not Rare's.** `src/game/sky.c` is byte-identical to the upstream
  decomp (`md5 a63ce4e60936e0cbab1e067d71926347` against
  `D:\Projects\007\src\game\sky.c`), so the cartridge issues exactly these
  words. Nothing in `src/game` was wrong. Fixed in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`; no
  `src/game` edit.

**The mechanism.** GoldenEye does not draw the sky with `gSPVertex` /
`gSP1Triangle`. `sky.c` assembles RDP triangle commands BY HAND and pushes
them two words at a time through the ucode's rdphalf pair. `ucode05.txt` is
the authority and names the caller: its `B2 rsp_uc05_rdphalf_cont` entry says
the command "Follows B4 rdphalf_1", "continues with the given lower word", is
"used only when operators longer than 64bits are in use", and is "Used by sky
and water generators in GE". Its worked example assembles into an `0xCE`
`G_TRI_SHADE_TXTR` triangle (`gbi.h:219`).

This interpreter implemented `B4`/`B3` only as texrect s/t operands, ignored
unless a texrect was pending, and did not decode `0xB2` at all.

**Measured** on a dam direct boot, `SL_DL_CENSUS=1`, every frame:

```
sl_ops: unknown=19 distinct=1  in-ucode05=19  off-command-set=0
sl_ops: top: B2=19
sl_2d: texrect cmds=0 ... orphan-halves=21
```

19 + 21 = **40 words dropped per frame**, and 40 is exactly one `0xCE`
primitive: 8 edge + 16 shade + 16 texture. `texrect cmds=0` on those frames,
so all 21 halves were the sky's.

**Facility is not a witness and never was.** Its environment row sets
`clouds=0` (`bgfog.c:131`), so `sky.c:320` takes the fill-rectangle path and
never builds a primitive: it measures `unknown=0`, `orphan-halves=0` before
the fix and `assembled=0` after. A passing Facility gate is *consistent with*
this defect, not evidence against it.

**The trap, which cost a wrong first fix.** An RDP "triangle" is not
necessarily a triangle. It carries three independent edges — major H over
YH..YL, minor M over YH..YM, minor L over YM..YL — so when the minor pair is
not collinear the primitive rasterises a **trapezoid**. `skyRenderFull`
exploits this deliberately: it sets XH to the left screen edge and XM to the
right, both with zero slope (`sky.c:2209`, `:2212`), and covers the whole sky
band with ONE command. It has two triangle headers in an if/else but only one
shade block and one texture block, so those 40 words describe a
four-cornered shape. Decoding them as three vertices drew half the band and
left the rest showing the backdrop — which still looked like "Dam has no sky".
The fix walks the boundary as a polygon; a genuine triangle is the degenerate
case of the same code.

**Decoded, verified against the environment table.** With the polygon reading,
a Dam intro frame decodes to `yH=10.0 yM=yL=43.0`, `XH=319.8` and `XM=0.0`
both with zero slope — a full-width band across the top of the 320x240
viewport — shading from `(70,94,132)` at the top to `(16,48,96)` at the
bottom, and `(16,48,96)` is exactly Dam's `Red/Green/Blue` triple
`0x10,0x30,0x60` at `bgfog.c:129`.

**Result.** Every `clouds=1` level now assembles and draws its sky primitive
(dam, surface, statue, runway, streets, depot: `assembled=1 drawn=1`),
facility correctly assembles none, `unknown=0` everywhere, and
`non-triangle-halves=0 overflow=0` everywhere — the word stream never
desyncs. Texrects are unaffected (surface: `texrect cmds=333 drawn=333
textured=333`). `SL_RDPTRI=0` restores the discard from the same binary.

**METHOD note, worth more than the bug.** The first A/B capture looked like a
3.8% pixel win. It was almost entirely the level-title **caption**, which
appeared in one run and not the other; the sky band itself had moved 827
pixels by a mean of 7, i.e. essentially nothing. Counting differing pixels
over a whole frame is not evidence that the thing you changed changed. Band
the diff to the region under test, **and look at the image** — the two frames
side by side settled it in seconds after the count had misled for a while.

### B-098 — the sky was ~90% right and read as stormy twilight: the RDP lerps the cloud texture from the SKY BASE COLOUR toward the shade, and GL_MODULATE dropped the base entirely. 2026-09-08

Follow-on to B-097, which made Dam's sky *draw*. The owner's verdict on that
was "geometry and texture substantially correct, but the ROM is visibly
BLUER — Sightline looks like stormy twilight/night".

**The hypothesis handed to this round was refuted.** The brief proposed that
the white cloud contribution was missing or under-applied. It is not. The
decoder's shade reconstruction is correct, and the same run that found the
real defect proves it: `SL_RDPTRI_DBG=1` on Dam measures the sky primitive's
vertices at `rgba=70,94,132` along the top edge and `rgba=16,48,96` along the
bottom, which is exactly `skyChooseCloudVtxColour` (`sky.c:186-188`) at the
two ends of its ramp — Dam's white cloud (255,255,255) blended in at the top,
bare sky at the horizon. The cloud colour was arriving. What was missing was
the **base underneath it**.

**The actual defect, one line.** `sl_gfx_dl.c` ended the B-097 decoder with

    texenv_set(0);          /* shade * texel, the sky's combiner */

That comment was an assumption, and it was wrong. The sky's combiner is
measurably

    rgb = (SHADE - ENV) * TEXEL0 + ENV
    a   = (0 - 0) * 0 + SHADE

GL_MODULATE computes `SHADE * TEXEL0` and has **no addend at all**, so the
whole `ENV * (1 - TEXEL0)` term was dropped. ENV is the sky base colour, so
the deficit is largest exactly where the cloud image is darkest — i.e. over
most of the sky — and it is *coloured*, not neutral: Dam's ENV is
`16,48,96`, so dropping it removes six times as much blue as red. A dark blue
sky rendered without it collapses toward black through neutral grey. That is
the reported "stormy twilight instead of blue", and it is why the base colour
looked *approximately* plausible while the picture was wrong.

**Rule 7 first, and the docs settled the format before any source was read.**
`Background File Data/Fog Water and Sky/NTSC fog and sky.txt` records the
cartridge's own sky display list (its "sample cloud mapping" listing), and its
combiner word is literally

    FB000000 280000FF        <- SetEnvColor
    FC40FE81 55FEF97C        <- SetCombine
    B4000000 CE8002A1        <- rdphalf_1 carrying the CE triangle
    B2000000 0               <- rdphalf_cont

Decoded through the mux table in `Display Lists and Object Generation/
ucode05_old.txt` ("FC rdp_setcombine"), `FC40FE81 55FEF97C` is
`(SHADE - ENV) * TEXEL0 + ENV` in both cycles with alpha `(0-0)*0+SHADE`.
That is an authority independent of our tree, and it agrees exactly with what
`sky.c:1281` encodes — so the word is not an artefact of the decomp.

**MEASURED IN THE CONSUMED BINARY**, Dam, `SL_CC_DBG=1`:

    sl_ccx: f0 fc40fe81 55fef97c cyc=0 tr=1 prim=00000000 env=103060ff tile=0
       rgb0=(SHADE-ENV)*TEX0+ENV  rgb1=(SHADE-ENV)*TEX0+ENV  a0=(0-0)*0+SHADE

The backend was already decoding the word correctly into `g_cc_ra/rb/rc/rd`.
Nothing read it at the sky draw. `env=103060ff` is Dam's fog row read back at
draw time (`bgfog.c:184`, red `0x10` green `0x30` blue `0x60`).

**Note on the cited table.** The brief cited `bgfog.c:120/:129`, which is the
`VERSION_EU` block. This build compiles `-DVERSION_US` (`build.ps1:206`), so
the row that actually applies is `bgfog.c:184` — different column layout,
*identical* values for Dam, so the numbers held.

**ALPHA was a second, independent darkening.** The RDP's alpha here is a plain
REPLACE with the vertex alpha, which `sky.c:190` sets to `0xff` — the sky is
opaque. GL_MODULATE instead computes `TEXEL0.a * SHADE.a`, so the cloud
image's alpha was blending the sky against whatever lay behind it. Both halves
are fixed by honouring the one measured word.

**The fix.** A narrow classifier `cc_skylerp()` — `a` must be SHADE, `c` must
be TEXEL0, `b` must be a real colour register and must equal `d` — plus
texenv mode 7, which is GL_INTERPOLATE with the register in the texture
environment CONSTANT and `OPERAND2_RGB = GL_SRC_COLOR` so the factor is the
texel **per channel**, as the RDP's `c` slot is. Alpha is REPLACE from the
vertex. `SL_CC_SKYLERP=0` restores the previous behaviour from the same
binary.

Blast radius is one call site: `grep -rn "cc_skylerp" src/` gives the
definition and exactly one caller, inside `draw_rdp_tri`, which is reached
only from `rdphalf_push` — the raw-RDP-triangle path nothing but the sky uses.
`modelApplyRenderModeType3`'s `(TEXEL0 - ENV) * SHADE + ENV` has `a` and `c`
the other way round and is rejected by both tests, so it keeps drawing as it
did.

**Verified, camera-aligned A/B from one binary** (`SL_CC_SKYLERP=0` vs `1`,
frame 60 of the Dam intro; frames outside the sky band differ by a mean of
0.08/255, so the camera and the whole rest of the picture are the same).
Pure-sky rect `(300,24)-(420,46)`:

    OFF  mean (16.1, 18.6,  26.2)  min (13,15,23)  100% of pixels BELOW ENV
    ON   mean (42.3, 70.7, 113.5)  min (27,57,103)   0% of pixels below ENV

The derived prediction for that rect at mid-texel is
`ENV + (SHADE-ENV)*0.502 = (43, 71, 114)`; measured `(42.3, 70.7, 113.5)`.
The structural prediction is the sharper one and it holds exactly: the RDP's
lerp is bounded below by ENV, so **no** sky pixel may fall under
`(16,48,96)` — 0% do with the fix, 100% did without it, because
`SHADE * TEXEL0` has no floor at all.

**An arithmetic overclaim, corrected.** A first pass predicted
`ON - OFF == ENV * (1 - TEXEL0)` per pixel and measured only 6.6% agreement.
That model is wrong, and stating it plainly matters more than the fix: the old
path was *alpha-blended*, so `OFF = SHADE*t*a + dst*(1-a)`, not `SHADE*t`.
Two things changed at once — the RGB lerp and the alpha replace — and the
difference does not reduce to a pure RGB addend. Both halves are derived from
the same measured word, but they are not separately toggleable, and the band
means therefore move in a ratio (1 : 2.3 : 4.1) that is *not* ENV's 1:3:6.

**A second false positive, caught.** The large flat blue region in the lower
left of the Dam intro vista measures exactly `(16,49,99)` — the ENV colour —
and was briefly taken as proof the fix worked. It is not: the **OFF** build
renders that same region at the same `(16,49,99)`, 100% of pixels, so it is
the fog-coloured backdrop and is unaffected by this change. It is, separately,
where B-099 below is visible.

**All `clouds=1` levels classify, each from its own fog row** — dam
`env=103060`, surface `606080`, statue `000008`, runway `103040`, streets
`101820`, depot `000008` — `skylerp=1` on every sky primitive, zero GL errors
in the end-of-frame drain (so the driver accepted the GL 1.4 colour-valued
`OPERAND2_RGB`; a rejection would have raised `GL_INVALID_ENUM` and silently
kept the alpha operand).

**Facility is not coverage.** Its row sets `clouds=0`, so it never enters the
sky path: `assembled=0 drawn=0 skylerp=0`. A green Facility gate says nothing
about this change, and should not be read as if it did.

RECORDED ONLY, not investigated. Causal stage unknown — do **not** assume

### B-099 — SOLVED. The dam's dry-side face is missing because a portal polygon shared by several table records was byte-swapped once PER RECORD, and an even reference count put it back in big-endian. 2026-09-08

**Symptom.** One of Dam's six seeded intro cameras looks along the crest from
the dry side. The long downstream face of the dam does not draw and the
backdrop shows through. Present before B-098 and unrelated to it; B-098 only
made the exposed backdrop legible blue instead of near-black.

**Reproducing it, since the shot is seeded.** `bondview_r.c:357` picks the
intro camera with `randomGetNext() % g_SetupIntroCameraCount`, and Dam's setup
declares six `FixedCam` records (`assets/obseg/setup/UsetupdamZ.c:1171-1183`),
so the shot is a function of the RNG seed. `SL_RNG_SEED=0000000000000003` (and
`...0006`) on `SL_BOOT_LEVEL=33` lands on it; the default boot lands on the
truck camera and never shows the defect. **A round that boots Dam and does not
set the seed is not looking at this bug.**

**The measured chain, in order.**

1. *The region is drawn, and it is not fog.* It measures a flat `(16,49,99)`
   over an 88000-pixel sample with only TWO distinct values (the second is the
   letterbox black). That is not the GL clear, which is `(13,15,23)`
   (`sl_gfx_sdl.c:107`). It is `skyRenderFull`'s water-region fill rectangle
   (`sky.c:849`), issued in `G_CYC_FILL` with the environment colour: dam's
   row is `0x10,0x30,0x60` (`bgfog.c:184`), and the 5551 fill register expands
   it to exactly `(16,49,99)`. Logged from the consumed binary as
   `[0,42]-[319,229] cyc=3 col=16,49,99,255 tris-so-far=0`, i.e. BEFORE any
   geometry — it is the backdrop, drawn first, and the world never covered it.

   Note the discriminator, because it is the whole reason this did not become
   another "far plane" round: a fully FOGGED surface would read the 8-bit fog
   colour `(16,48,96)`, not the 5551 fill colour `(16,49,99)`. Not one pixel
   of `(16,48,96)` exists in the region. Nothing was rasterised there.

   A depth-buffer readback was tried first and is NOT the evidence. Dam's far
   mountains are visibly drawn and also read depth 1.0, so "depth is cleared"
   does not mean "nothing drew". Recorded so the next round does not re-run it.

2. *It is a visibility decision, not clipping, culling, texture or matrices.*
   With the portal algorithm bypassed (the branch Cradle takes), 79 rooms are
   marked instead of 31 and the dam face renders correctly and completely.

3. *Which rooms.* The camera sits at `(8947, 2920, 4098)` — OUTSIDE every
   room in the level (the largest room x is 6344), which is what a cinematic
   camera does, and why the healthy gameplay measurement could not be carried
   forward. The rooms the portal path omits include 62/63/64/65 and 56-61, a
   vertical stack directly beneath the crest rooms 53/54/55: the dam face.

4. *Why they are omitted.* Every one of the sixteen portals joining 53/54/55
   to 62/63/64/65 is rejected by the facing test in `sub_GAME_7F0B7F84` with
   **every metric zero**:

   ```
   sl_backfaceA: portal=115 room=53->62 pm=0.00 pom=0.00 min=0.00 max=0.00 n=(0.000,0.000,-0.000)
   ```

   The test is `metric.max <= playermetric - portalmetric`, i.e. `0 <= 0`, so
   it is TRUE from every position on every frame. `sub_GAME_7F0B96CC` builds
   that normal as a cross product of the polygon's first three points, so
   zeros mean the POINTS are zero.

5. *Why the points are zero — the root cause.* Dumping the table shows
   portals 103/107/111/115 all naming offset `2012a66c`, 104/108/112/116 all
   naming `2012a6b8`, and so on: **four portal records per polygon.** The docs
   say this is legitimate — "the portal table consists of offsets to actual
   portal polygonal data and a list of rooms interlinked" (`Background File
   Data/background data.txt`, Portal Data Table), and the Global Visibility
   Microcode reaches the same polygons by offset too (same file,
   `64000000 0Fxxxxxx  offset within file, typically to portal data`).

   `sl_bg_file_swap` (`bg.c`) walked the table and swapped each record's
   polygon — **once per record**. A polygon named twice was swapped twice and
   returned to big-endian, where its float coordinates decode as denormals;
   the cross product underflows, `sqrtf` returns 0, the `dot != 0.0f` guard
   leaves the scale at zero, and every derived quantity collapses.

**The rule is exactly PARITY, and that is what rules out the alternative.**
Measured on Dam: 194 records naming 160 distinct polygons. 139 polygons have
one reference and every one decodes to real coordinates; 14 have two and 6
have four, and all 20 decode to `(0,0,0)`; **one polygon has THREE references
and decodes correctly.** No "shared portals are just degenerate in the file"
reading survives an odd-reference-count polygon coming out right.

**The fix.** Swap each portal polygon on its FIRST reference only. A few lines
in `sl_bg_file_swap`, entirely inside `#ifndef __sgi`. Not a Dam special case
and not a renderer change: it restores the file's documented meaning for every
level.

After the fix the same portals decode to integer-valued coordinates — portal
103 reads `(2800,0,400) (2017,0,-158) (1500,0,-400)` — which is an independent
check, because the docs state "to properly integrate them with clipping, each
float should be an integer value" (same file). Denormal garbage has no reason
to land on integers.

**Blast radius, measured, all 19 bootable campaign levels.** Only three levels
share portal polygons at all:

```
LEVEL      records polygons shared broken
dam            194      160     21     20
depot          118      111      6      5
frigate         94       88      2      2
archives 103/103, aztec 95/95, bunker1 30/30, bunker2 75/75, caverns 76/76,
control 141/141, egypt 51/51, facility 109/109, jungle 59/59, runway 27/27,
silo 94/94, statue 43/43, streets 61/61, surface 101/101, surface2 101/101,
train 64/64   -- all shared=0 broken=0
```

Sixteen of nineteen levels have a strictly one-to-one record/polygon mapping,
so the swap loop performs the **identical sequence of swaps** before and after
this change on all of them. That is inertness by construction, not by
sampling, and it is a stronger statement than any A/B capture.

**Facility is not a witness and the green gate is not coverage.** Its portal
table is 109 records over 109 polygons, zero shared, so `tools/windows/test.ps1`
passing says only that nothing else broke. **depot** is the real second
witness — five broken polygons — and it renders healthily afterwards, with one
frame that was a dark void before now showing its fence geometry.

**A/B capture is NOT a valid instrument here and was withdrawn.** Two builds of
the same level with the same seed drift apart from frame 5 onward
(`read=10,12,16,19` against `read=11,14,...`) because the launch is real-time
paced, so whole-frame pixel counts differ on **facility**, which this change
provably cannot touch. Counting differing pixels would have "confirmed" a
regression that cannot exist. The structural argument above replaces it.

**`__sgi` PROOF, non-vacuous.** The whole change lives inside `#ifndef __sgi`.
`gcc -E -P -fdirectives-only -D__sgi -x c` over the include-stripped file, HEAD
against working tree: **169020 bytes each, `cmp` exit 0, sha256 identical.**
`-fdirectives-only` is required — a plain `-D__sgi` preprocess of this file
fails outright (exit 1, no output, `osSyncPrintf` arity in
`bgGetPortalBetweenRooms`), which is the "instrument switched off" failure this
document already records twice. Positive control, same command without the
define: 183455 vs 185844 bytes, `cmp` exit 1 — the instrument can fail, so its
null result means something.

**`make trace-verify` was NOT run and is not claimed.** This host has no MIPS
toolchain. Standing in for it: `tools/windows/build.ps1` exit 0,
`tools/windows/test.ps1` PASS 1/1, the `__sgi` byte-identity proof above (the
matching build cannot have changed), and the sixteen-level structural
inertness result.

**Not claimed to fix anything else.** The missing tower section, the
gun/ground-arrow disappearance in the security-door area, the explosion
rendering regression and B-100 were parked this round and were not
investigated. Rooms 56-61 and 62-65 becoming visible plausibly touches some of
them, but nothing here measured that and it must not be assumed.

### B-099 side-finding — the RDP scissor is decoded and then discarded. CORRECTNESS DEBT, deliberately not fixed here. 2026-09-08

Found while tracing B-099, worth its own entry, and it is NOT what caused B-099.

`sub_GAME_7F0B3C8C` draws every visible room under its own scissor rectangle —
the portal-derived screen box (`bg.c:687`, `bg.c:753`, through
`bgScissorCurrentPlayerViewF`). Measured on the Dam intro, most rooms get the
full viewport `[0,10]-[320,230]` but several get tight boxes:
`[20,16]-[54,89]`, `[95,10]-[121,97]`, `[59,71]-[253,127]`, `[166,84]-[319,230]`.

`OP_SETSCISS` in `sl_gfx_dl.c` decodes those coordinates correctly into
`g_sciss[]`, and the only other thing it does with them is derive the 2D ortho
height. A tree-wide `grep -rn "glScissor\|GL_SCISSOR" src/` returns
**nothing** — the rectangle is stored and never applied.

The sign matters: an ignored scissor makes this renderer draw MORE than the
RDP would, never less, so it cannot produce a missing surface and it is not
B-099. It can produce room geometry bleeding outside its portal box wherever
the depth buffer does not already remove it. Not fixed here because it is a
broad rendering-behaviour change with no measured witness attached to it, and
B-099 needed a narrow fix. **Wanted next: a witness where a room visibly
bleeds outside its portal box, before anything is changed.**

### B-101 — the RDP scissor: a witness was demanded before applying it, the witness was BUILT, and the answer is DO NOT APPLY IT. 2026-09-08

Follow-on to the B-099 side-finding above, which asked for exactly this: *"a
witness where a room visibly bleeds outside its portal box, before anything is
changed."* The witness exists now. It does not say what it was expected to say,
and the register is still not applied.

**The absence claim, re-verified.** `grep -rn "glScissor\|GL_SCISSOR" src/`
over the whole tree returns **nothing** (exit 1, zero hits, 2026-09-08).
`OP_SETSCISS` decodes the box into `g_sciss[]` and the only consumer is the 2D
ortho height added by `71565a5c`. That consumer is untouched by this round.

**Why a witness was required rather than just switching it on.** An ignored
scissor can only make this renderer draw MORE than the RDP would, never less.
So enabling it will usually look fine, and looking fine proves nothing. This
shape had been right twice in a row (B-097, B-098), which is exactly why it
needed evidence instead of a third assumption.

#### The instrument: one frame, one list, two walks

`SL_SCISS_WITNESS=<read index>` renders a frame **twice from the same display
list in the same process at the same instant of game time** — once as the build
normally does, once with every `ED` honoured through `glScissor` — and writes
both images and their difference.

Two builds captured at the same moment is the obvious instrument and it is
**not available here**: the windowed launch is real-time paced
(`sl_ultra_shim.c:424`), so two runs of one level with one seed diverge in read
index from frame 5 onward. B-099 already records that whole-frame pixel counts
then differ on levels a change provably cannot touch. Two walks of one list
have no such freedom, and the null control below proves it.

**Both controls were run, and neither is optional.**

* **NULL control** (`SL_SCISS_WITNESS_NULL=1`) — the second walk runs in full
  and never calls `glScissor`. The difference must be **zero**, not small.
  Measured: frigate **75/75 samples `all-diff=0`**, dam **79/79 samples
  `all-diff=0`**. The re-walk is bit-faithful, so every differing pixel below
  is the scissor and nothing else.
* **POSITIVE control** (`SL_SCISS_WITNESS_SHRINK=20`) — every box inset by 20
  framebuffer pixels before it reaches GL. Measured on dam read=1701:
  **interior-diff=161717, to-clear=106416**, and the image is the world clipped
  visibly inward from all four edges. `glScissor` is live, the framebuffer to
  window mapping points at the right part of the window, and the read-back and
  the diff can both see a change. A null result here means something.

**One measured false positive, excluded by construction.** The frame carries
`[0,0]-[320,240]`, `[0,10]-[320,230]` **and** `[1,10]-[319,230]` together —
they do not agree to the pixel. Honouring the last trims one framebuffer pixel
off each side, which at 960x720 is a ~3px outline present on **every** frame
whatever is drawn (3774 pixels on the first dam sample). Counting it would be a
permanent false positive. The reported number is therefore the **interior**
difference: inside the intersection of the full-screen boxes, inset by two. The
excluded total is printed alongside it so the exclusion stays checkable.

#### What was measured, over recorded playthroughs

Levels driven by `SL_INPUT` from `tools/trace/inputs/`, not by a parked camera.
Facility is deliberately absent — 109 portal records over 109 polygons, zero
shared, and a weak witness for anything about rooms.

```
LEVEL     samples   frames with any interior difference
dam           143   0
depot          89   0
frigate        95   21
```

**On dam and depot, honouring the scissor changes literally nothing** — 232
sampled frames, threshold one pixel. There is no defect to fix on either.

**On frigate it does change things, and the largest change is a REGRESSION.**
At read=2048 the frame carries four boxes, of which one is the narrow strip
`[1,10]-[57,230]`. Geometry drawn under that box paints a solid band at
framebuffer `x=138..149`, spanning `y=28..227` — **81 pixels outside its own
box.** So room geometry bleeding past its portal box is REAL and is now
witnessed.

But applying the scissor removes that band and shows sky and sea through it.
In the as-built image the band reads as ship structure continuous with the
deck; in the scissored image there is a hole. `interior-diff=10482`,
`to-clear=974` — most of the removed pixels fall back to *other* geometry, 974
to the clear colour.

#### The decision, and it is the point of the round

**The scissor is NOT applied.** The round's stop condition — no witnessed
defect, do not change it blind — is met in a stronger form than expected: not
"applying it would be invisible", but **"applying it has a demonstrated visible
cost on at least one level and no demonstrated benefit on any."**

A hypothesis for the frigate band, recorded as a hypothesis and **not
established**: the surface may be one the cartridge draws from a room Sightline
is currently not drawing, or the portal box may be derived too small, and the
ignored scissor is currently masking that. If so, switching the scissor on
without fixing the underlying visibility first would convert a hidden defect
into a visible hole. Nothing here measured that and it must not be assumed.

**Honest limits.** Seven frigate samples (reads 150-334) report an interior
difference of exactly 1-2 pixels; those are the interior mask failing to
exclude a corner of the edge outline, not a finding. `make trace-verify` was
NOT run and is not claimed — no MIPS toolchain on this host. The change is
confined to `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`; **no file under `src/game/` was touched**, so
no `__sgi` proof is owed and the matching build cannot have changed. Standing
in: `tools/windows/build.ps1` exit 0 and `tools/windows/test.ps1` PASS.

**Default behaviour is unchanged.** `g_wit_pass` is zero unless
`SL_SCISS_WITNESS` names a read index; with it unset the witness block, the
`glScissor` call site and `sciss_gl_apply` are all unreachable. The per-frame
cost added to a normal run is one 4-int `memcpy` and three assignments.

**What the owner should replay to check this claim.** Frigate, stage 26,
replaying `tools/trace/inputs/frigate.input`, around read index 2048 — that is
the frame where the band is. The open question the ROM would settle in one
look: at that moment, does the cartridge show ship structure there, or sky?

### B-102 — B-100 does NOT reproduce on the default seed, and at HEAD it does not reproduce at all: camera, projection, shot duration and truck path all match the cartridge exactly. 2026-09-08

**The reproduction in the brief is wrong, and that is the first thing to fix.**
The round was told "the truck camera is what you get with the DEFAULT seed —
confirm that yourself". Confirmed, and it is false. Dam's setup declares six
`FixedCam` records (`assets/obseg/setup/UsetupdamZ.c:1171-1183`) and
`bondview_r.c:357` picks one with `randomGetNext() % 6`. The **default** boot
lands on the wide vista over the crest from the wet side — the
"Byelomorye Dam, Arkangelsk, USSR" / "Nine years ago" shot, camera at
`(7424.92, 1160.29, 3484.91)`. **The truck camera is `SL_RNG_SEED=...0004` and
`...0005`**, camera at `(17608.08, -59.79, 17408.57)`. A round that boots Dam
on the default seed is not looking at B-100, and this one burned most of its
budget discovering that. The seed table so far: 3 and 6 give B-099's dry-side
vista, 4 and 5 give the truck, the default and 1/2 give the wet-side vista.

**The camera does not move. The TRUCK does.** The seed-4 FixedCam holds
`(17608.08, -59.79, 17408.57)` unchanged for the whole shot. The thing that
approaches is object prop **279**, the green truck, driving its own path. So
"the camera penetrates farther" is really "the truck arrives closer", and the
stage list to trace is the truck's transform and the shot's duration, not the
camera path.

**Both hypotheses in the brief are REFUTED by measurement.**

*The near plane.* The brief proposed that Dam's intro runs at near 30 (the
`DAM + ENVIRONMENTDATA_CINEMA` row, `bgfog.c:185`) against gameplay's near 5,
and that a too-near near plane clips less and exposes more interior. Measured
on both sides, per frame: the cinematic uses **exactly two** projection states
and they are the same two on both. `(near 30, far 15000, fovy 60, aspect
1.45455)` while a FixedCam is up, and `(near 5, far 15000, fovy 60, aspect
1.45455)` for the SwirlCam flythrough that follows. Native and cartridge agree
on the value AND on where it changes. `viSetZRange` is fed
`Visibility.BlendMultiplier` and `Visibility.FarFog` at `bgfog.c:301`, which is
why the fog table's first column is the near plane at all.

*The camera path.* Joined ON VALUE rather than on frame index (the two counters
are not comparable): over the whole cinematic, the **maximum distance from any
cartridge camera position to the nearest native one is 13.26 units**, on a path
spanning roughly 8000. The paths are the same curve.

**Everything else measured also agrees.**

```
                                        native            cartridge
FixedCam (truck) held for               542 frames        525 frames
truck closest approach to that camera   195.04 units      193.04 units
frames from shot start to closest       ~385              ~372
projection states in the cinematic      {(30,15000),(5,15000)} both sides
```

**And the picture agrees too.** Paired at MATCHED TRUCK WORLD POSITIONS (native
frames 765/781/813 against cartridge 3928/3936/3952 — the truck within 4.6
units at each pairing), the two renderings of the penetration are comparable in
degree, and where they differ **the cartridge exposes MORE**: at the matched
beats the ROM's sky gap through the truck body is larger and the small rear
panel that the native build still draws is already gone. The cartridge also
dithers the truck translucent as it closes, which the native build does not —
that is a real difference, it is the opposite sign from the report, and it was
not chased here.

So **B-100 as written is not reproducible at HEAD** and no fix was made. Making
one would be authoring a divergence against a measurement.

**B-099 is NOT the explanation, and that was tested rather than assumed.**
The obvious story — that `d7ed8d2d` restored Dam rooms 56-65 and quietly fixed
this — is wrong. `src/game/bg.c` was reverted to `d7ed8d2d~1`, rebuilt, and the
same three seed-4 frames captured: **byte-identical, sha256 for sha256, 2073615
bytes each.** This shot does not touch the portal fix.

**What is actually needed next: owner re-observation.** Everything measurable
agrees with the cartridge, so either the report predates something else that
has since landed, or it was made under a setting this round did not reproduce
(screen size, control style, or a real-time-paced play session rather than an
unpaced capture). The concrete ask is a seed-4 replay on a build at or after
`73f8fb61`. Nothing should be changed in the renderer until that comes back.

**Two instruments were built, and they are the durable part of this round.**

*Native capture is now DETERMINISTIC.* `SL_FPS=0` makes `sl_pace_frame`
(`sl_ultra_shim.c:562`) return immediately, so a WINDOWED run is unpaced and
byte-reproducible. Verified: two runs, twenty frames each, **20/20 identical
sha256, 2073615 bytes per frame.** This retires the standing caution that
"two builds of the same level with the same seed drift apart from frame 5
onward" — that is true of a PACED run and false of an unpaced one, and it is
why frame-indexed A/B was previously unusable. Every native measurement in this
entry was taken this way.

*The cartridge can now be made to pick a NAMED intro camera.*
`tools/native/introcam.py`. Natively the shot is selectable with `SL_RNG_SEED`;
on the cartridge it was not selectable at all, so every seeded shot — B-099 and
B-100 both — had no ROM oracle and any comparison silently answered a different
camera. `introcam.py pick` prepends k neutral records to a recorded stream,
which shifts the level load by k frames and re-rolls `osGetCount`. Nothing about
the ROM is modified; only the controller stream changes. **Shift 2 on `dam`
lands on the truck camera**, and `introcam.py read` then dumps camera mode,
world position, projection and object-prop positions per frame in the same
units the native `SL_CAM_DBG` probe prints.

**A trap that cost this round an hour, recorded so it costs nobody else one.**
The recorded input streams hold buttons CONTINUOUSLY, so any live record inside
the intro delivers a skip edge. Zeroing `dam.input` from record 3602 left the
truck camera up for **98** video frames; zeroing from 3560 left the same camera
up for **525**. The 98-frame version looks exactly like a port that cuts the
shot early, and it is entirely an artefact of where the stream was cut. `--cut`
must be set earlier than the intro, not merely before the moment of interest.

**A second trap, same shape.** `chrprop.c` links the active prop list
head-to-tail, so `g_ActivePropsTail` must be walked through `->prev`. Walking
`->next` from the tail reaches ONE element, returns a plausible short list of
viewer props, and supports the confident wrong conclusion that no object prop
ever comes near the intro camera. Both halves of the probe made this mistake
before it was caught by the prop count (137, not 1).

**What was NOT investigated**, and must not be assumed from any of the above:
the missing tower section, the gun / ground-arrow disappearance near the
security door, and the explosion rendering regression. This round changed no
rendering behaviour at all.

### B-099 — CLOSED 2026-09-08, owner acceptance on replay.

The owner replayed the dry-side Dam intro on a build carrying `d7ed8d2d` and
confirms the dam face renders. The fix — a portal polygon shared by several
table records being byte-swapped once PER RECORD, so an even reference count
put it back in big-endian — is accepted. Gitea issue #1 closed with the
acceptance recorded there.

### B-100 — FAILED owner acceptance, and this round's near-plane candidate is MEASURED AND REFUTED. 2026-09-08

**The owner's replay says the defect is plainly still there**, and it came with
a SECOND, INDEPENDENT witness found during ordinary play:

* **Witness A, cinematic.** Dam truck intro (`SL_RNG_SEED=...0004`/`...0005`):
  exterior truck surfaces disappear as they approach and cross the camera,
  exposing a large amount of internal geometry.
* **Witness B, gameplay.** With the camera very close to tower/wall geometry,
  nearby surface geometry disappears and the player sees through the structure
  into the geometry/tunnel behind it.

Witness B is the stronger one — no truck animation, no intro-camera selection,
no cinematic timing — so B-100 is not a camera-path problem and its scope is
now the shared symptom rather than the truck. Gitea #2 was re-scoped in place,
NOT duplicated.

**Two claims from the previous round are WITHDRAWN.** "Near-plane hypothesis
refuted" only ever established that the game-side configured znear VALUE agrees
with the ROM; equal znear does not establish equal CONSUMED clipping. And
"none in the B-100 chain" is withdrawn outright — the owner's replay is a
consumed-output mismatch. What stands, and what this round built on rather than
re-litigating, is that camera position, truck world transform, projection
parameters and shot timing all agree with the cartridge.

**The candidate this round tested, and why it was a good one.** Native submits
eye-space vertices and lets GL apply the game's own projection
(`sl_gfx_dl.c`, `emit_tri` then `glVertex3f(e[0],e[1],e[2])`, modelview held at
identity), so GL clips clip-space z against -w and +w. The RSP's PROGRAMMABLE
clip planes are four and they are the sides — the G_MW_CLIP moveword takes
`clip -x`, `clip -y`, `clip +x`, `clip +y` and nothing else
(`ucode05.txt:567-570`, identically `ucode05_old.txt:483-486`; rule 7 makes
those the authority, and both revisions of the note agree). So GL discards
every triangle nearer than znear — 5 world units in Dam gameplay, 30 in the
cinematic — and that predicts the reported symptom exactly.

**The population is real and was measured, not inferred.** A new census,
`SL_NEARWIT=1` (`nearwit_note` in `src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c`), classifies every
triangle by its near-plane relationship: FRONT / STRADDLE / INSIDE (wholly
between the eye and znear: w > 0 but z_clip < -w, which GL drops in full) /
BEHIND. On the truck cinematic **up to 244 triangles per frame are INSIDE**,
and GL draws none of them.

**And the fix is still wrong. This is the measurement that decided it.**
`GL_DEPTH_CLAMP` removes exactly the near and far clip tests and clamps depth
instead, which is the closest thing GL has to the RSP arrangement. Turned on it
closes the truck's exposed interior and the picture looks better — and it moves
that picture AWAY from the cartridge.

Paired ON TRUCK WORLD POSITION rather than on frame index, because the two
counters are not comparable: native f779 against ROM f3932, prop 279 within
**0.24 world units**. Both sides resampled to a common 320x240 grid (the ROM
framebuffer is 640x240 with non-square pixels — a first pass that skipped this
banded the wrong rectangles and produced numbers that were void), and
classified by band rather than by whole-frame pixel count:

```
                    sky        green
   cartridge       15.2%       29.9%
   clamp OFF       15.0%       24.9%     <- agrees with the ROM on sky
   clamp ON        14.1%       13.4%     <- and the body is now wrong too
```

"sky" is the see-through measure — background showing where the truck body
should be. **The cartridge and the UNCLAMPED build agree on it to 0.2 points.**
At the beat where the truck is closest, this build is not letting more
background through than the cartridge does, and switching the near clip off
moves it toward the cartridge on neither number.

**A second measurement, and it is the one that matters for Witness B.** Over
**3007 frames** of the recorded `dam` GAMEPLAY stream the INSIDE population is
**zero on every single frame**. znear of 5 is too close for that stream ever to
reach. The instrument was confirmed live on the same run rather than assumed —
`front` reaches 2850 and `straddle` reaches 3 in those same frames — because an
all-zero census is otherwise indistinguishable from a probe that never ran, and
the first attempt at this run WAS such a probe: it reported
`front=0 straddle=0 INSIDE=0 behind=0`, which is not "nothing is near the
camera", it is "no triangles were emitted at all". Read as a null result it
would have been a confident wrong answer.

**So the first divergent stage was NOT found, and no production behaviour was
changed.** The chain is now cleared as far as the clipping/rejection decision:
camera, model/view transform, eye-space position, projection matrix and
clip-space w all agree, and the near-plane relationship — the one stage that
had never actually been measured rather than argued from a configured value —
has now been measured on both sides and does not explain either witness.

**What ships from this round** is the instrument and the refutation:
`SL_NEARWIT` (the census, reports only) and `SL_DEPTH_CLAMP` (**default OFF**,
a bisect handle carrying the measurement above in its comment). The default
path is proved inert: same seed, same frame, no environment set, the capture is
**byte-identical to the pre-change build, sha256 for sha256, 2073615 bytes** —
non-zero, so not the two-empty-files false pass this document has recorded
before.

### B-103 — Witness B has no recorded reproduction, and that is now the blocker. 2026-09-08

The owner's close-wall witness cannot presently be replayed by anyone but the
owner. Every recorded stream in `tools/trace/inputs` is a traversal; none of
them presses the camera against a surface, which is why the gameplay census
above is flat zero and why this round could only test Witness A.

Without a recorded stream that reproduces it, Witness B has no ROM oracle, no
frame-matched A/B, and no way to tell a fix from a coincidence — the same hole
`introcam.py` was written to close for the seeded intro shots.

**Wanted next, and it is one thing:** a short recorded input stream on `dam`
that walks the player into the tower/wall the owner describes and holds there.
`tools/trace/` already records; the missing piece is a stream that visits the
place. With it, `romshot.py` gives the cartridge side for free and the census
above says immediately whether near-plane clipping is even in the frame.

Until that exists, the hypothesis classes still open for Witness B are the ones
this round did not reach: room/portal visibility at close range (the same
`bg.c` machinery B-099 was in, and `sub_GAME_7F0B5528` does its own eye-plane
clipping of portal polygons at z=0, which is exactly the code a camera pressed
against a portal stresses), and the cull/depth interaction. Culling is the
cheaper of the two to clear: the default `SL_CULL=4` culls only where a draw
does NOT write depth, so opaque room geometry is not culled at all today, which
argues against it — but that is a reading of the code, and this document's own
standing rule is that readings of code lose to measurements.

**Not investigated, and not to be assumed from any of the above:** the missing
tower section (Gitea #3), the gun / ground-arrow disappearance near the

demonstrated no mechanism, so it unified nothing and closed none of them.

### B-104 — the recorder cannot record the way the owner plays: native keyboard and mouse never reached the input stream, so both Dam seam witnesses are non-empty and inert. 2026-09-08

**B-103 asked for a recorded stream that walks the player into the wall. Three
were delivered and none of them contains a step.** This is not an owner error —
they played the level, twice, deliberately, and the second attempt was recorded
specifically to be a better instrument than the first.

Decoded straight out of the files (`byte0` stick y, `byte1` stick x, `byte2/3`
buttons, per the format note at `sl_ultra_shim.c:1276`):

```
  dam-seam-00.input    3545 records   stick nonzero    0   buttons: Z x240, B x7, START x3
  dam-seam-01.input    3021 records   stick nonzero    0   buttons: Z x5,  START x3
  dam-truck-00.input    562 records   stick nonzero    0   buttons: none at all
```

**Zero stick deflection in every record of all three, and no d-pad in any of
them.** With no stick and no d-pad there is no movement and no turn under any
control style, so the streams cannot express the thing they were recorded to
capture. `dam-seam-01` is the sharper evidence of the two: the owner was asked
to approach and back off several times, tried harder, and the file came out
*more* inert than the first — 8 button records in 3021.

**Confirmed by replay, not only by decode.** `SL_CAM_DBG=1` over
`dam-seam-00.input`: the intro camera runs to frame 2401, and from there to the
end of the run — ~5000 pumped frames, about 42 s — the player is at
`20167.34, 60.28, 16892.50` and never moves one unit.

**The positive control is the same file with four bytes per record changed.**
Injecting `stick_y = +70` from record 1250 (nothing else altered) walks Bond off
the spawn, down the causeway and into the rock face. So the replay path applies
movement correctly and the instrument detects it; the owner's stream simply has
none. This control matters because an all-zero census is otherwise
indistinguishable from a probe that never ran, and this document has been
burned by that three times.

**THE MECHANISM.** Native keyboard and mouse **do not drive the N64 stick**.
They publish four movement channels and a linear look pair through
`sl_move_channels_set` / `sl_mouse_look_set`
(`src/native/sl_move_channels.c`), consumed at the seam in
`bondviewProcessInput` (`bondview2.c:5539`). `sl_input_record_vi` wrote
`sl_live_btn/x/y` and nothing else, so all six numbers were dropped.
Tree-wide, `grep -rn "sl_move_channels_set\|sl_mouse_look_set" src/` returns one
producer (`sl_input.c:1931`) and **no file writer at all** — nothing has ever
recorded them.

A gamepad session records fine, because the pad *is* the stick. That is why
the 119 emulator streams and `dam-sweep-*` are unaffected, and it is why this
stayed invisible: the defect only bites the input device the owner actually
uses.

**This is the worst shape a witness can have.** The file is present, non-empty,
the right size, replays without error and reproduces nothing. It passes every
"did it record?" check there is.

**THE FIX — a sidecar, `SL_MOVE` / `SL_MOVE_RECORD`.** Same pattern and same
argument as `.vis`: the 4-byte-per-retrace input format is unchanged, so all
119 streams in `tools/trace/inputs` stay valid as-is. 16 bytes per retrace —
flags, the four channels as `s8` in the game's own +/-70 unit, and the look pair
as raw IEEE754 bits so there is no scale to get wrong. Recorded and consumed in
`sl_input_vi_advance`, one record per retrace, matching the `.input` stream
record for record — deliberately not in frame units, which is the 2026-08-26
fidelity bug repeated. A withheld frame is recorded as withheld, so letting go
of the keys replays as itself rather than as the last active frame repeated.

`SL_INPUT=<p>` picks up `<p>.move` automatically when it exists, and
`sl_main.c` writes `<run>/input.move` beside `<run>/input` on every captured
session, so the owner sets nothing. A missing sidecar is silent and inert; only
an explicitly named `SL_MOVE` that cannot be opened is fatal.

**Measured, both halves:**

* **Inert by default.** The same replay command on the pre-change and
  post-change builds, 50 captures each: **50 of 50 byte-identical, sha256 for
  sha256, 103680750 bytes each side** — non-zero, so not the two-empty-files
  false pass recorded elsewhere in this document.
* **The replay half works.** A synthetic sidecar carrying `walk=+70` from
  retrace 1250, over the owner's own `dam-seam-00` stream, walks Bond down the
  causeway and into the tunnel.
* **The record half round-trips.** Replaying with `SL_MOVE_RECORD` set
  reproduces the input sidecar **byte-identically over all 3545 records**; the
  output is longer only by the retraces past end-of-stream, correctly recorded
  as inactive.
* `tools/windows/test.ps1` passes (Facility, 300 frames).

**WHAT THIS ROUND DID NOT DO, said plainly.** No native-vs-cartridge divergence
was located, because there is still no stream that reaches the place. Nothing
was learned about the missing tower (#3), the gun/arrow disappearance (#4), the
world seams, or the explosion corruption (#5), and none of them may be assumed
from anything above. `SL_NEARWIT` was **not** run against these streams: the
census would have been flat zero and would have meant only that Bond stood at
the spawn. The near-plane thread stays parked exactly where B-100 left it.

**Wanted next, and it is still one thing:** the owner re-records the approach on
a build carrying this change. `<run>/input` and `<run>/input.move` are both
written automatically; both are needed, and the `.move` is the half that has
never existed before.

### B-104 addendum — the three streams are removed, the seed now travels with the stream, and two claims from the round brief are corrected. 2026-09-08

**The three void streams are NOT in the tree.** `dam-seam-00`, `dam-seam-01`
and `dam-truck-00` were committed earlier this round as evidence and have been
removed: sitting in `tools/trace/inputs/` they look like usable witnesses, and
an empty stream yields a stable, plausible, completely wrong "no divergence
found". Their decoded fingerprints are recorded in B-104 above, which is the
part worth keeping.

**`make trace-roundtrip` CANNOT run on this host, and would not have covered
this defect if it had.** Two separate facts:

* It needs `xvfb-run` for its record half (`roundtrip.py:91`), which is
  Linux-only and absent here. `make` also defaults `PYTHON` to `.venv/bin/python3`;
  `PYTHON=.venv/Scripts/python.exe` gets past that and the run then dies on
  `xvfb-run` with `FileNotFoundError`.
* More importantly it drives the **libretro emulator** with a scripted N64 pad
  (`roundtrip.py:44-47`, `InputFrame(START)`). It exercises the emulator's
  record/replay link. **The native keyboard/mouse channel is outside its scope
  entirely** — which is precisely why this defect survived a green harness.

A NATIVE round-trip was run instead, on a deliberately VARYING stream (constant
input round-trips through almost any bug — a recorder that latched the first
record or dropped every second one would still reproduce it):

```
   handed to replay   8326 records   nonzero 6116 (73.5%)   distinct 6117
   written by record  8527 records   nonzero 6116 (71.7%)   distinct 6117
   -> first 133224 bytes IDENTICAL (all 8326 records); the output is longer
      only by the 201 retraces past end-of-stream, recorded as inactive
```

For contrast, `dam-sweep-00.input` — a working stream — is 70.5% nonzero with
797 distinct values, so the round-tripped sidecar matches it in character and
exceeds it in richness.

**CORRECTION 1: "`play.ps1` does not pass `SL_INPUT` to the child" is REFUTED.**
The variable table SETS four values; it does not define the whole child
environment, and the default path invokes the exe directly with every other
`SL_*` inherited. Measured, this file at HEAD against a modified copy, same
stream and frame count: **both children printed
`sightline native: input stream ...rt2.input (8326 reads)`.** Adding `SL_INPUT`
to the table changed nothing and would have cost something — `-MeasurementMode`
clears every `SL_*` the table does not name, so naming it there would exempt it
from that sweep and quietly turn a measurement run into a replay.

What was really observed: no run directory from a replay has `SL_INPUT` in its
`env` sidecar, because **a replay produces no run directory at all**
(`sl_main.c:212` returns early when `SL_INPUT` is set, deliberately). Absence of
the run dir was read as absence of the variable. The finding is recorded in
`play.ps1` as a comment so it is not "fixed" again.

**CORRECTION 2: the recorder does not sample "upstream" of the kbm injection —
there is no sample point that would work.** `map_kbm` sets the stick to zero
(`sl_input.c:1686-1687`) and the ONLY places it is written again are inside the
`if (menu)` branch (`:1694-1695`). In gameplay the keyboard/mouse stick is
neutral **by construction**, and the comment at `:1699-1735` says why: routing
the mouse through the stick was itself the measured defect fixed on 2026-09-03
(crosshair floats off `controlStickXRaw`, no turn until |stick| > 60, snap to
centre on stop). The four channels plus the linear look pair are six numbers;
the pad stick is two signed bytes. So the data never exists as pad state
anywhere, and encoding it there would be lossy AND would reintroduce a defect
that was deliberately removed. This is why the fix is a sidecar and why the
`.input` format is untouched — the same shape `.vis` already uses, and proved
inert at 50/50 byte-identical captures.

**THE SEED NOW TRAVELS WITH THE STREAM.** A stream is not replayable without the
RNG state it was recorded under, and that state lived only in the run
directory's `env` file — so a stream copied out and handed on replayed under the
boot default instead. It replayed cleanly; it replayed a different run. The
three Dam recordings each carried a different state (`000000007a91b2e1`,
`00000000527d4edd`, `0000000000000004`).

`sl_run_note_rng_seed` now also writes `<run>/input.spec` as
`LEVEL=<n> DIFFICULTY=<n> SEED=<16 hex>`, and replay reads `SEED=` back from
`<stream>.spec` or `<base>.spec`. Parsed BY KEY, so every existing sidecar stays
valid: `dam-sweep-00.spec` has no `SEED=` and measurably falls through to the
same deterministic default (`00000000000f4241`) it always used. An explicit
`SL_RNG_SEED` still wins. The no-seed message now says outright that the run is
NOT the recorded one, which is the thing that was silent before.

**Inertness re-verified for this round's changes.** A stream with no `.spec`
produces RNG state `00000000000f4241` on the pre-change build and
`00000000000f4241` on the post-change build — identical value, wording only.
`tools/windows/test.ps1` passes.

### B-105 — the fix is ACCEPTED IN THE OWNER'S HANDS: two sessions recorded with movement. One of them terminates early on replay. 2026-09-08

The owner re-recorded twice during this round, on a build carrying the
sidecar. Both carry real movement, and the pad half of both is as inert as ever
- which is the fix working exactly as described:

```
                        pad stream (.input)              movement sidecar (.move)
  dam-test    2490 rec  stick nonzero 0, 14 buttons      1196 nonzero (48.0%), 335 distinct... 228 distinct
  dam-seam-02 2399 rec  stick nonzero 0,  8 buttons      1124 nonzero (46.9%), 335 distinct
  dam-sweep-00 (emulator, for contrast)                  70.5% nonzero, 797 distinct
```

So a keyboard-and-mouse session now records a stream comparable in character to
a working emulator stream, and **the pad half is still all zeros in both** -
third and fourth independent confirmations that the pad cannot carry this input
and that the sidecar is where the data has to live.

**`dam-test` replays faithfully and visibly reproduces the recorded movement:**
Bond walks the causeway, follows the hazard barrier and ends pressed against
dark geometry with a sliver of sky at the frame edge. Exit 0 over 5200 frames.
Both sidecars load and the seed comes from the stream's own `.spec`.

**`dam-seam-02` reproduces the movement but EXITS 1 before the stream ends, and
this is NOT yet characterised.** Two runs stopped at **different** DL frames -
2221 and 1261 - so a deterministic crash at a fixed point is REFUTED by the
measurement. No crash report is written and no fatal message is printed; the
hang watchdog (10 stalled seconds) is armed on every run and is the leading
candidate, with host load during windowed capture as the trigger. Three other
windowed runs this round were also cut short, two of them with a clean
`window closed at frame N`, so external interference is not excluded either.

**Not claimed:** that this is a game defect, that it is in the replay path, or
that it relates to any Dam rendering bug. It is an open question about the
witness, and it must be settled before `dam-seam-02` is used to conclude
anything - an early exit is exactly the shape that produces a confident wrong
"no divergence found".

**Both streams are committed with their `.spec` seeds** (`dam-test` =
`000000006d219d49`, `dam-seam-02` = `0000000056cc03ed`), matched to their run
directories by frame count. They are controller-derived, not ROM-derived.

    005  17374.209  59.278  9617.319   111   gun ABSENT, arrow ABSENT
    006  16649.004  59.429  9575.428   111   gun VISIBLE, arrow VISIBLE
    delta   -725.205   0.151  -41.891         726.4 units apart

**1. THE VIEWMODEL'S DISPLAY LISTS ARE NOW IDENTIFIED, BY MEASUREMENT.**

`gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` (gunfire.c:1495) emits its geometry as
segment-5 (`SPSEGMENT_MODEL_COL1`, bondconstants.h:2980) branches, one per
model part. A probe over the words that function itself writes
(`SL_GUN_DBG`, off by default) reports nineteen of them in Dam gameplay:

    05006138 05004038 05004958 05004a80 05004c48 05004dc0 05004fe8 05004808
    05004660 05004528 05004390 05004158 05005188 05005398 05005ab0 05005c78
    05005e00 05005b68 05005fc0

That is byte-for-byte the set at `ord=29..47` of the owner's **mark-007**, in
the same order. So an F8 record CAN name the viewmodel, and mark-007 shows it
present with the gun on screen. This is what the record was previously unable
to answer, and it is the round's one solid new fact.

**2. THE A/B COMPARISON THE ROUND WAS BUILT ON IS CONFOUNDED, AND THE
"GUN NOT SUBMITTED IN 005" READING IS WITHDRAWN.**

`submitted-lists` records **depth-1 branches only** (sl_gfx_dl.c, recorded
under `if (g_mark_on && depth == 0)`). In six of the eight marks the depth-0
list ends by transferring into a single list high in the game heap, and every
one of those is the LAST entry in its table:

    mark   depth-0 branches   trailing list   room 111 primary reached at
    003    13                 20048068        nested
    004    13                 200596d0        nested
    005    12                 20059668        nested, depth 3
    006    14                 20048218        nested
    007    45                 NONE            depth 1, ord=16
    008    11                 20047e00        nested

From that transfer onward the frame runs at depth >= 2 and the table records
nothing. **mark-007 is the only mark whose table covers a whole frame** - and
it is the only one that lists the viewmodel.

The consequence is decisive and negative: the nineteen viewmodel branches are
absent from GOOD `mark-006` for exactly the same reason they are absent from
BAD `mark-005`. Their absence in 005 is **not** evidence that the viewmodel
was not submitted. Any conclusion of the form "the gun's list was never
handed to the interpreter" drawn from these six records is unsupported.

The same applies to the ground marking. Room 111 owns a secondary list
(`2000cd68`), which mark-007 shows drawing 34 triangles at depth 1; in the
other five marks the secondary pass falls after the transfer and is invisible
to the table. Neither the gun path nor the arrow path can be traced to a first
divergence from this dataset.

**3. WHAT THE TRAILING LIST IS, IS NOT ESTABLISHED.** It is not a room list -
Dam's room primaries and secondaries all sit below `0x20013000`, per the
marks' own room tables - and it is not reproducible here: 400 consecutive
frames of Dam gameplay measured `maxdepth=1` and `branch=0`, i.e. a completely
flat frame, with the viewmodel's nineteen branches at depth 0 like everything
else. Whatever makes the owner's frames nest is a function of somewhere the
synthetic input does not reach.

**4. TWO LATENT INTERPRETER DEFECTS FOUND, NEITHER DEMONSTRATED TO FIRE.**

  * `walk()` (sl_gfx_dl.c) returns immediately for `depth > 8`. A frame that
    nests deeper than that has its tail silently dropped, and a call refused
    at the cap looks exactly like a model that drew nothing.
  * `walk()` recurses for BOTH uses of opcode 06. "Display Lists and Object
    Generation/ucode05.txt" gives them as `xx00xxxx push display list` and
    `xx01xxxx branch to display list`, and B8 `rsp_enddl` as "if the current
    list was called by an 06 command, returns from branch": a BRANCH replaces
    the running list and consumes no stack level. Recursing for it inflates
    depth toward the cap above and mis-attributes every list under it.

**Deliberately not fixed.** The measurement says `branch=0` and `maxdepth=1`
in every frame reachable here, so both are currently inert, and "fix the thing
whose trigger you measured as never firing" is the ninth silent-instrument
failure waiting to happen. `SL_DEPTH_DBG` is committed so the next capture
answers it: if a marked frame reports `refused` above zero, the cap IS the
cause and the fix is already written above.

**UPDATE 2026-09-08 - the `branch=0, maxdepth=1` population was the wrong
one, and the margin on the cap is now a number.** That reading came from a
scene with no characters in it. Replaying `dam-seam-02.input` at room 111 -
the owner's own scene - measures `branch=6, maxdepth=7, refused=0` on 232 of
599 frames, and an F8 mark on one of those frames reports **max-call-level 1
against max-walk-depth 7**. The arithmetic is exact and it is the whole
finding: 1 + 6 = 7, so every level of walker recursion past the first is a
tail transfer that the RSP would not have put on its stack. The cap is 8. One
more chained transfer in any scene and `walk()` returns early, dropping the
remainder of the frame silently.

Still deliberately not fixed, and the reason has changed. `refused=0` on every
frame of every run measured - the cap has never actually fired - so there is
no consumed-output mismatch demonstrating the current behaviour is wrong for
the game, and production `G_DL` semantics stay untouched. What has changed is
that the F8 record now MODELS the distinction even though the interpreter does
not: a branch node takes its predecessor's parent and its predecessor's call
level, so the report says what the RSP would do while `max-walk-depth` says
what this interpreter did. The two numbers disagreeing IS the instrument for
this defect, and it is now printed on every mark rather than behind an
environment variable.

**5. TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE LYING, AND ARE FIXED.**

  * `sl_cam`'s `pos=` is `player->pos`, an intro-camera field. Over the
    owner's 12255-frame session it holds 133 distinct values, **all of them
    from before frame 531**, and reports `16659.31,480.98,19463.86` unchanged
    at all eight marks, whose eyes are hundreds of units apart. Anyone
    locating a player from that line gets a confident wrong answer. An
    `sl_eye:` line now prints `viewtoworldmtxf` m[3] - the field the F8 record
    itself names as authoritative - beside it.
  * `SL_CAM_EVERY` could never fire on an even stride. The caller reaches the
    probe only on odd frame numbers, so `SL_CAM_EVERY=100` produced ZERO lines
    over 3000 pumped frames where the same run with the stride unset produced
    1499. The stride now counts the probe's own calls.

**6. THE MARKS RUN CANNOT BE REPLAYED, AND NATIVE WINDOWED RUNS ARE NOT
RUN-TO-RUN DETERMINISTIC.** Replaying `dam-seam-03.input` with its `.move`,
`.vis` and its `.spec` seed ends in the front end (`pos=0,0,0`,
`near=100 far=10000`, 164 triangles/frame) instead of at the truck. Worse, two
runs of the SAME binary with the SAME seed and the SAME synthetic stream
diverge: 754 of 999 logged eye samples differ. So no frame-exact before/after
diff of Dam is available as a regression control at present, and none is
claimed in this entry. This is the B-105 debt, now measured on a third stream.

**NOT CLAIMED, explicitly.** That the world/tower disappearance is explained,
reproduced or fixed - this capture does not clearly contain it. That the gun
and the ground marking share a cause. That either path's first divergence has
been found. That any fix for the reported defect is in this commit.

`submitted-lists` recorded `G_DL` only at depth 0, so the table stopped
describing the frame at the first submission that carried the rest of it. In
Dam that is a chain of tail transfers into the game heap, and everything after
the first one - props, characters, room geometry, the first-person viewmodel -

MEASURED on a `dam-seam-02` replay at room 111, the owner's scene: 136

## B-107 - Dam water texture/appearance flicker (PARKED 2026-09-09 - CORRECTNESS DEBT, OWNER-DEFERRED)

STATUS: PARKED. Classification CORRECTNESS DEBT - OWNER-DEFERRED. Gitea #11.
NOT closed as fixed, and the defect is NOT claimed to have disappeared
permanently. Owner decision 2026-09-09: removed from the single-player
coverage sprint's acceptance critical path. If it becomes frequent or
reproducible on a later mission, REUSE the witness and issue below rather
than starting over.

OWNER ACCEPTANCE RESULT, 2026-09-09, after `fb2d812f` was built and replayed
extensively: the obvious texture-state switch did NOT reliably reproduce.
Occasional minor flicker may remain. The owner considers it too infrequent
and too minor to chase now and does not want engineering time spent on it.

CAUTION ON READING THIS ENTRY. Two different claims below must not be
conflated. (1) The six-mark CORRELATION between the nested `01000000` call
and the untextured condition was never, on its own, promoted to a
demonstrated causal mechanism. (2) Separately and independently, a
source-level mechanism WAS measured - the bitfield-layout defect and its
4000-tick before/after numbers - and a fix for it landed in `fb2d812f`. The
residual flicker the owner still sees is NOT explained by either, and the
texture re-decode churn recorded at the end of this entry is an
uninvestigated candidate.

The same Dam water surface changed appearance as the player moved: sometimes
textured, sometimes a flat vertex-coloured sheet. Owner run
`20260909-084608-lvl33`, primary A/B pair mark-005 (bad) / mark-006 (good),
controls mark-001 (bad) and 002/003/004 (good).

SAME SURFACE, established before anything else: both marks' centre draws are
seq 250/251/252, class room-primary, room 35, dl-top and dl-inner both
`200088e0 + 0x0150`, nesting-depth 1, submission-ord 6, identical source
vertices, identical eye coordinates, identical combiner `fc272c04 1f1093ff`,
identical `om_l=0c192078`, identical blend/depth/cull/scissor/viewport. The
first divergent consumed state is the texture binding - `0x0 fmt=-1
cache-slot=-1 src=00000000` in 005 against `16x32 fmt=9 cache-slot=41
src=2009e3f0` in 006 - and the combiner names TEXEL0 in both, so 005 falls
back to flat shade.

CAUSE, in `src/game`, not in the renderer. `Gloadtile` (include/PR/gbi.h:1681)
is declared `int cmd:8; unsigned sl:12; unsigned tl:12`. That declaration only
describes an RDP command word when the compiler allocates bitfields MSB-first,
which IDO on MIPS does and i686-w64-mingw32-gcc does not, and nothing in gbi.h
switches it on endianness (`grep -n IS_BIG_ENDIAN include/PR/gbi.h` -> one hit,
line 1743, guarding a pointer-width union). The Dam/Complex water animation
`sub_GAME_7F092E50` (src/game/unk_092E50.c) rewrote the two `G_SETTILESIZE`
commands of `MipMap2C_Something2_Setup` through those field names every frame,
so `tl` landed in bits 20-31 and OVERWROTE THE OPCODE BYTE, which became
`tl >> 4`. Sixteen of the 256 values `tl` cycles through make that byte `0x06`
- rsp_uc05_displaylist, per `Display Lists and Object Generation/ucode05.txt`
l.437-447 - and the settilesize's own lower word, `01000000` for tile 1, was
then read as its operand: segment 1, offset 0, the font list bound at
lv.c:692. Executing it stomped the tile binding and cleared G_FOG.

That is exactly what the marks show. `MipMap2C_Something2_Setup` is at
`005ab520` in `build/win32/sightline.exe` (`nm`), the address room 35's DL
calls from its `+0x00a0`, and `+0x0018` is array index 3 - the entry the
animation writes. Across all six marks the correlation is binary and perfect:
the two frames whose `005ab520` list calls `01000000` are the two whose water
is untextured and whose geometry mode lacks `0x00010000` (G_FOG); the four
that do not call it are the four that are textured.

MEASURED, before and after, by linking the REAL production object
`src_game_unk_092E50.o` and driving Rare's real `sub_GAME_7F092E50` for 4000
ticks. BEFORE: the opcode byte of BOTH settilesize entries is wrong on
4000/4000 ticks, and entry 3 becomes `0x06` on 160 of them (4.0%); the tile
origins reaching the RDP are nonsense (uls 1540, ult 2050 against an intended
0-255). AFTER: 0/4000 wrong, opcode always `0xF2`, and the origins are exactly
what the source authors - at tick 4000, tile0 (232,144) and tile1 (66,38) =
((232+90)&255, (144+150)&255). So the fix does not merely stop the corruption;
it turns the water scroll on for the first time natively.

FIX: the cartridge path stays verbatim under `#ifdef __sgi`; the native build
writes the same word explicitly, per ucode05.txt l.888-905 (F2 rdp_settilesize,
upper word `00FFF000` upper-left s / `00000FFF` upper-left t, opcode in the top
byte via `_SHIFTL(c, 24, 8)`). `MipMap2C_Something_Setup`, the Caverns water
list (tex.c:971, texnum 1508), carried the identical defect and is fixed the
same way.

`__sgi` PROOF, non-vacuous. `gcc -E -P -fdirectives-only -D__sgi -x c` over the
include-stripped file, HEAD against working tree: 26557 bytes each, sha256
identical, `cmp` exit 0. Positive control, same command without the define:
26540 vs 28750 bytes, `cmp` exit 1 - the instrument can fail, so the null
result means something. Both preprocesses exited 0, so neither side was empty.

`make trace-verify` was NOT run and is not claimed - no MIPS toolchain here.
Standing in for it: the `__sgi` byte-identity above, `build.ps1` exit 0,
`test.ps1` PASS, headless dam 600x2, facility 600x2 and runway 300 all PASS.

No explosion regression was run and none is needed: the change writes only
`MipMap2C_Something_Setup` and `MipMap2C_Something2_Setup`, and a tree-wide
`grep -rn 'MipMap2C_Something' src/ include/ tools/` finds those two arrays
referenced ONLY inside `src/game/unk_092E50.c`. They leave it solely through
`sub_GAME_7F09343C(gdl, TRUE)` and `sub_GAME_7F09365C(gdl, TRUE)`, whose only
callers are tex.c:971 (texnum 1508, Caverns water) and tex.c:983 (texnum 1511,
Dam/Complex water); sky.c:858 calls the `arg1 == 0` branch, which builds fresh
commands and never touches the arrays. Nothing in the explosion, bullet-impact,
gun or sky paths can reach them.

STILL OPEN, not this bug: the water's decoded GL texture identity churns
between marks (`cache-slot` 30 / 41 / 73, `gl` 31 / 42 / 74 for the same
`src=2009e3f0`), so the texture is being re-decoded rather than reused. That is
a cache-key question, unrelated to the opcode corruption, and it was not
investigated.

ISSUE: filed as Gitea #11, private issue #11,
and updated to PARKED. It is deliberately left OPEN.

The earlier note here that no `GITEA_TOKEN` was available was a true
observation with a wrong conclusion. The token was correctly set at User scope
the whole time; Windows delivers setx/GUI environment changes only to
processes started AFTER the change, so the long-running editor handed every
shell and subagent a stale environment block. Resolved by reading the store
directly instead of relying on inheritance - `tools/windows/gitea-token.ps1`.

WITNESS, retained: owner run `20260909-084608-lvl33` under the user's
`.sightline/runs` directory, strongest A/B mark-005 (BAD) against mark-006
(GOOD), controls mark-001 (BAD) and mark-002/003/004 (GOOD). These captures
are the reason a later investigation would not need to start from nothing.

## B-100 / Gitea #2 — the close-wall see-through wedges ARE the near clip, and the near clip is FAITHFUL. Near-Z is CLOSED. 2026-09-09

Owner run `20260909-100313-lvl33` (Dam - `LEVELID_DAM` is 33), 18 marks with
bitmaps. This round did not produce a production fix, and the reason is a
measurement, not a shortfall: the mechanism was identified exactly and then
shown to be what the cartridge does too.

### What was measured

The see-through wedges are the OpenGL near-plane cut of specific wall
triangles, established by FITTING rather than by argument. For each candidate
triangle F8 recorded, the near cut was computed from the recorded clip-space
vertices alone - the two edge crossings of `z_clip = -w_clip`, projected
through the recorded viewport - and the resulting straight line compared with
the sky/geometry boundary read out of the mark's own `.bmp`:

| mark | room | source DL + tri offset | side | rows sampled | worst residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 011 | 115 | `2000c6d0` +0x05f0 (seq 333) | left  | 4 on-screen of 11 | 0.5 px |
| 011 | 115 | `2000c6d0` +0x05c8 (seq 321) | right | 4 on-screen of 11 | 1.1 px |
| 004 | 136 | `2000e870` +0x05a8 (seq 160) | left  | 7 of 7 | 0.9 px |
| 004 | 136 | `2000e870` +0x0598 (seq 156) | right | 4 on-screen of 7 | 1.3 px |
| 003 | 132 | `2000a170` +0x0fb0 (seq 756) | left  | 6 on-screen of 7 | 1.0 px |

Five triangles, three marks, two independent screen sides. Rows where the
predicted line leaves the window are exactly the rows where the measured
boundary saturates at 0 or 959. The mesh edge through the same vertices was
checked as a control and misses by 400+ px, so the boundary is the CLIP line,
not a triangle edge.

That settles the visual signature: a triangular wedge here is not a missing
triangle, not a material or alpha effect, and not a depth artefact. It is one
wall triangle being cut at eye depth 5.0, with nothing behind it.

### Why that is not a fix

`znear` is 5 and `zfar` 15000 for Dam, from `fog_tables[]` (bgfog.c) through
`viSetZRange` (bgfog.c:301) into `guPerspectiveF` (fr.c:709) - decomp code and
decomp data, so Rare's. The matrix the interpreter receives is the ROM's own
16.16 matrix (`-1.000656 / -10.003326`, back-solving to n = 5.00003), not a
reconstruction. Dam's `levelinfotable` row carries levelscale 0.23363999 and
visibility 0.2, and `bondview2.c:8476-8478` multiplies the world-to-view matrix
by the visibility scale; the marks' vertex scale of 0.856 is exactly
(1/0.23363999) x 0.2, so Sightline's transform chain reproduces that arithmetic
to six digits. Nothing in the chain diverges.

And the cartridge near-clips at the same plane. AUTHORITY: the ROM's own RSP
microcode, `D:\Projects\007\rsp\graphics\gmain.s`.

- `:512-524` — the vertex routine's `vch`/`vcl` pair against the vertex's own
  UNSCALED w, `cfc2 $vcc`, masked `0x703` / `0x7030`. In the F3DEX `$vcc`
  layout the low byte is `coord <= +w` per lane and the high byte
  `coord >= -w`, lanes 0-2 being x, y, z. Those masks take x,y from the
  positive side and x,y,z from the negative side: five planes, no far test,
  and the fifth is `z >= -w`. The missing far test is the cross-check - it
  reproduces the N64's well-known absence of far clipping, which the opposite
  byte assignment would invert.
- `:784-794` — the triangle routine. `AND` of the three clip codes masked
  `0x7030` rejects; `OR` masked `0x4343` sends the triangle to the clipper.
  `0x7030` is that unscaled set, near included. `0x4343` is the scaled +-x/+-y
  bits plus bit 14, which is the unscaled near bit after the `sll $8, $8, 4`
  at `:519`. So the RSP both rejects on and retessellates against `z = -w`.

Zoinkity's notes are SILENT on this - `G_MW_CLIP` enumerates only the four
PROGRAMMABLE side planes (ucode05.txt:567-570), which says nothing about a
fixed near test compiled into the microcode. Reading "four programmable
planes" as "no near-z clipping" is the overclaim this round was sent to avoid
repeating; it is now refuted with the mechanism, and a `not_covered` entry
points the next reader at the microcode.

This also agrees with the cartridge-paired truck measurement of 2026-09-08
(sky band: cartridge 15.2%, unclamped build 15.0%, `GL_DEPTH_CLAMP` 14.1%).
Two independent lines, one from the picture and one from the mechanism.

### Instrument caveats found while doing this - F8 is CLOSED, these are notes

1. The `eye` and `eye-dist` lines in a mark are NOT eye space. They are the
   source vertex times the modelview's uniform scale (exactly `source x 0.856`
   on Dam, verified on every vertex sampled), with no rotation and no
   translation. The clip row is computed from the real `g_veye` and does not
   reproduce from the printed `eye`. USE `w`: for this projection `w = -e_z`,
   so `w` IS the eye depth and `w < 5` is precisely GL's near test. All of the
   fitting above uses `w` only.
2. A vertex with `w <= 0` is printed as `ndc 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000`, which is
   inside the centre box, so EVERY triangle with a vertex behind the eye lands
   in the candidate list regardless of where it is on screen. That is why
   `vertices-in-front = 2/3` correlates with the see-through marks - it is a
   filter artefact. mark-001, classified SOLID, carries a 2/3 triangle too
   (seq 772, `w = -13.096`).
3. `nearwit_note` returns on `nbehind != 0` before classifying. Every one of
   the owner's close-wall witnesses is in that BEHIND bucket - a wall running
   past the camera necessarily has a vertex behind the eye - so the all-zero
   INSIDE census over 3007 Dam frames was measuring a population the bug is
   not in. It was not the exoneration it read as, in either direction.

### Checked and eliminated this round

- Submission (stage A): the room-request count does not separate the classes.
  SEE-THROUGH marks span 1 to 8 requested rooms (004: 1, 011: 2, 003: 4, 005:
  8, 010: 8) and SOLID marks span 6 to 28. No signal.
- Emission (stage D): `emit_tri` has no `w`-based or NDC-based early return.
  `g_tri_clipped` and friends are census counters, not drops. Sightline hands
  every triangle to GL; GL does all the clipping.
- Culling: the witness triangles record `cull gl=0 option=4` - culling is off
  for them, so no cull decision is involved.

### Where the next round should look, and where it must NOT

MUST NOT: the near plane, the projection matrix, `GL_DEPTH_CLAMP`, the clip
inequality, triangle emission, or the clip-space transform. All measured, all
faithful. This is the second refutation and the first with a mechanism.

SHOULD: everything that decides `w` before the renderer sees it - how close the
camera is permitted to get to a wall, and the eye height and standoff that puts
a 5-unit near plane (25 model units on Dam) within 1.6x of the nearest wall the
player can reach (`centre-depth-eye` is 6.8 to 9.5 across the marks). That is a
game-side question, and it needs a paired cartridge witness at a comparable
pose, which run 20260909-100313-lvl33 cannot supply. B-103's ask - a recorded
stream that walks the player into a wall - is still the blocker for that.

WITNESS, retained: owner run `20260909-100313-lvl33`, marks 003, 004 and 011
with their bitmaps. The fit above is reproducible from the mark text alone.
