## 2026-09-11 - B-116: native world-texture enhancement layer (owner-ruled feature)

Owner overruled comment-113's "faithful low-res is acceptable": Sightline
now intentionally enhances low-res world textures. Shipped 6f7293df,
Gitea #15 (cross-ref #10 comment 115). NOT a fidelity fix - a deliberate,
SL_TEX_ENHANCE-toggleable presentation divergence.

Architecture: at the tex_acquire upload seam, each distinct WORLD texture
is resampled once (Catmull-Rom bicubic, integer factor within the 256px
decode cap - 4x for 32x32) and the enlarged image is uploaded into the
same cached GL object. has_enh is part of the cache key.

Asset rule honoured: NO ROM-derived pixels stored/committed - the enhanced
image lives only in the live GL texture, regenerated from the user's ROM
each launch. Repo carries only the algorithm.

Scope by generic characteristic (never level/room/address): 3D world only
(g_tex_world, set at tex_apply's tile_texture call - g_2d_on is unreliable
because draw_texrect binds before mode2d_begin); animated/multi-tile water
+ mip-lerp family EXCLUDED via g_cc_tex1lerp (Dam water upload byte-
identical); <=64px per side only.

Preserved: S/T frequency (GL normalises to [0,1]; seam grid identical OFF/
ON), alpha (fence cutout intact), wrap/clamp (seamless), lighting (dome
stays dark). Measured 93 of ~186 Surface textures enhanced; one-time load
cost, nothing per frame. Witnesses mark-001/mark-005 checkerboard ->
coherent rock; Dam control mountains sharpen, water/HUD/gun sane;
surface/facility/dam 400 PASS.

Working knowledge: g_tex_world is the reliable 2D-vs-3D discriminator at
texture-upload time (NOT g_2d_on). The enhancer is upload-only - it never
touches the DL, texcoords, wrap, or game state, which is what makes the
water exclusion and S/T preservation structural rather than tuned.

## 2026-09-12 - B-119: LOD_FRACTION is per pixel, the alpha is the
## strip's own, and the c=13 family has a SECOND authored shape

Round input, owner triage of ae77f478: trees improving but not fixed -
LOD "switching at incorrect times", tree tops "cardboard" (should be
sky), dome still off, treeline sections still undraw. Fresh witnesses
20260912-055925-lvl36 marks 1-6.

What was wrong with ae77f478's estimator, numerically: (1) per-TRIANGLE
constant where the RDP computes LOD_FRACTION per PIXEL - pops at every
triangle edge, the owner's "clear at one point, a mess at others";
(2) measured in TILE-0 texels - the x4-shifted DETAIL - where the RDP's
LOD is the MAP's (tile 1) density: 4x hot; (3) stale f inherited when
all edge pairs degenerated; (4) 1/32 quantization stepped visibly.

Fix (texenv mode 9): K = rho x z is constant across a planar wall, so
K is measured per triangle over edge pairs in TILE-1 texels and f is
evaluated PER VERTEX: f = clamp(2(K/z)-1, prim_lod_min/255, 1) -
shared vertices get equal f, the blend is continuous, and f rides the
vertex alpha into crossbar INTERPOLATE(TEX1, TEX0, PRIMARY.a), Gouraud
per pixel. The vertex alpha is free because the authored alpha equation
(FC 1f14ffff, muxes per ucode05_old.txt "FC rdp_setcombine") is
(1-0) x TEXEL1 + 0 - the STRIP's alpha, which is what mode 9's ALPHA
emits: REPLACE from TEXTURE1. That term is the cardboard fix (sky
between tree tips, mark 3). The strip gets a box-generated GL mip
pyramid + trilinear (authored 64x17 -> 32x9 can't be GL levels). Floor
= the FA minlevel byte (gbi.h gsDPSetPrimColor), not invented.

THE UNDRAW WAS NEVER CULLING (owner's mark-005 record is the witness):
wall tris of room 10's secondary DL contain the centre pixel, all
vertices in front, CCW - and the pixel is background at depth 1.0.
ae77f478's mode-8 ALPHA was MODULATE(unit-0 texture x vertex): the gap
sections' unit-0 record carried tile-0's shape with tile-1's bytes
(32x32 from 200a4150, the strip base) - transparent where sampled -
whole sections multiplied to alpha 0. Mode 9's alpha comes from the
strip; measured post-fix: the exact mark-5 centre ray draws trees.

THE FAMILY'S SECOND SHAPE, caught pre-ship as a white-out: with mode 9
in, the dome pose rendered the whole bunker opaque white (census: 2290
TEXEL1-unresolved tris/frame vs 20 binds). The c=13 family has two
authored layouts: TWO-IMAGE detail blend (treeline: detail at tmem 0,
strip at tmem 128, both tiles name LOADED addresses - resolve, mode 9);
and ONE IMAGE + AUTHORED MIPS (dome shell, snow ground: one loadblock,
tiles 1..n point INTO the block at offsets no load named - TEXEL1 can
never resolve, and a crossbar mode over a disabled unit samples
undefined = opaque white). Fix: variant detected at the tile-1 tmem
lookup; the single-image shape draws single-unit with a mip pyramid on
its one image - GL trilinear IS (T1-T0) x LOD_FRAC + T0 across adjacent
levels - plus a guard dropping any failed mode-9 draw to plain
modulate. Unresolved at the dome pose 2290 -> 655 (all fall back
safely); building renders dark metal again; snow ground regained its
texture (it was silently in the same failure class).

behind them; the low reference keeps every graded edge texel, so the
accepted soft look is intact. SL_TREE_ZWRITE=0 restores the cartridge's
order-only resolution for A/B.

## 2026-09-12 - B-123: the depth buffer out-resolved the cartridge -
## 24-bit split authored coplanar ties that 10-bit screen-Z cannot express

Owner on ce53f12f: "Dome looks a little better... still not acceptable
yet." Fresh witnesses 20260912-203549 marks 1/2 (mark 3 = the owner's
tracer witness, attached to issue #16 c129 without investigation:
two solid gold rectangular slabs by the muzzle path, pose banked).

What still differed (diagnosis before code): residual checker (i) plus
scattered dark distribution (iii) - clean half-quad TRIANGLES among the
dark shapes, one at the crown under the crosshair.

ZMODE checked FIRST per the round brief: both passes om_l c8102078 -
zmode OPA both, no DECAL requested. Decal semantics are not the fix.

The measured mechanism, completing B-122's: the two passes' clip rows
are BITWISE IDENTICAL at every shared vertex (same matrices), but the
dome quads are NOT planar (~0.3 world units of warp), so the two
triangulation diagonals describe two different tent surfaces whose
interior depths genuinely differ (~1e-6 window) either way per half.
Under a 24-bit buffer each pass wins one half-quad whatever the compare
function - B-122's GL_LEQUAL fixed only exact ties.

The authored pipeline cannot express that difference: gbi.h:1219
G_MAXZ 0x03ff, "10 bits of integer screen-Z precision" (the corpus is
silent on the RDP compare's own storage format - not_covered stands).
GL quantizes BOTH depth-compare operands to the buffer's fixed-point
precision, so the fix is the buffer itself: request a 16-bit depth
buffer (smallest standard size, still finer than the authored grid) at
window creation. The warped-quad tents then quantize to the same
bucket, tie, and GL_LEQUAL resolves later-wins - the cartridge
outcome. SL_Z_QUANT=0 restores 24-bit for A/B.

Post-fix: 203549 mark 1 - dome mostly white, ONE contiguous dark band
(the authored slit), scattered crown/mid shards gone; mark 2 (inside) -
white marble with the slit assembly as one coherent arc + open sky
slit; 200311 mark 1 angle consistent. Protections: treeline overlap fix
holds at 184156-m2 with the accepted look; Dam water identical at the
accepted pose; Runway boots and renders; Facility boots. Liveness
surface/dam/facility/runway 420 - PASS. Owner replay is final.

## 2026-09-12 - B-124: the dome's two skins are resolved by COARSE DEPTH,
## and B-123's 16-bit request was inert - an FBO makes the quantization real

Owner rejected b9c95a11 as complete (dome "still not acceptable"; the
"residual checker is fixed" claim is WITHDRAWN). Fresh witnesses
20260912-222555 marks 1-8: 1-2 outside (dark-patch aim / white aim),
3-5 inside looking up, 6-8 tracer attempts from the deck (banked to
issue #16 with the rainbow-streak signature; also visible there: the
dome's dark left flank, and the corrupted tracer as a solid gold
pillar standing on the snow).

Pixel-ownership forensics at mark 1 (centre 262626, window depth
0.992996):
- The covering set is BOTH passes of the same cap DL (200153b0): the
  shaded pass (+0x110..+0x188, shades 1b1b1b..ffffff GRADED - the
  checker pattern is IN its vertex shades) and the white pass
  (+0x1c8.., d2d2d2..ffffff), same material/om (fc26a004/c8102078),
  opposite diagonals, overlapping ndc z - contested pixels, dark
  first-drawn wins under the 24-bit compare. Case B.
- OPPOSITE WINDING measured between the passes on the same quad, BUT
  honouring the cull bits mis-culls one MIRRORED half of the dome
  (SL_CULL=1 and =2 each fix one half and break the other, plus =2
  breaks terrain) - the same mixed-winding wall as B-114's Dam massif,
  and if hardware honoured them one half would show sky holes the ROM
  does not have. So the skins resolve by DEPTH on hardware, not cull.
- B-123 WAS INERT: the stored centre depth reads back as an exact
  multiple of 1/(2^24-1), not 1/(2^16-1) - SDL_GL_DEPTH_SIZE is a
  minimum and the driver gave 24. Recorded here as the correction to
  the B-123 entry; its semantic was right, its mechanism never engaged.

Fix (B-124, src/gfx/sl_gfx_sdl.c): an offscreen framebuffer with an
explicit GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT16 renderbuffer (plus RGBA8 colour), bound
for the whole frame and blitted to the window at swap. GL quantizes
both compare operands to the attachment's width, so the two skins
quantize to the same bucket, tie, and B-122's GL_LEQUAL gives the tie
to the later (white outside / marble inside) pass - the cartridge
outcome. Every readback (SL_SHOT, F8 BMP, centre probe) happens with
the FBO bound, so instruments read the presented rasterization; the
mark record now reports 16 depth bits when active. Entry points via
SDL_GL_GetProcAddress with APIENTRY typedefs (the B-063 lesson); any
failure falls back to the window buffer, reported. SL_Z_QUANT=0
disables the FBO wholesale.

dithered transition patches, dark only at the slit region; inside
(3-5) - white marble dominant, wedges as dithered patches + the solid
slit + open sky; interior bunker walls still render (the fix does not

  surroundings, on a regular lattice INSIDE the dome triangles' interiors,
  not along their edges. Ownership switches, so Case C (an AA/coverage/
  dither overlay rendered solid) is excluded - an overlay keeps its
  triangle's id.
- SL_Z_QUANT=0 (24-bit): the broad dark gores return. Precision was
  trading one artifact for another. (Both captures landed un-aimed at the
  mark's standpoint; usable for classification, not a strict same-pose A/B.)

The proof is the mark's own record. Both passes of the four candidate
quads around the crosshair are in [candidate-draws] with exact clip rows
(dark 99/100 115/116 123/124 125/126, white 155/156 171/172 179/180
181/182 - the white pass reloads the SAME four world points per quad and
triangulates the opposite diagonal). Software-rasterizing both tents at
the mark's viewport, quantizing to 16 bits as the FBO did, LEQUAL + draw
order, against the .bmp (shade-based classifier per pass, crosshair
excluded): 84% pixel agreement, 289 of the 348 pixels predicted dark ARE
dark; the 24-bit prediction agrees 45% (it predicts the gores). The
white-minus-dark tent difference at the quad CENTRES: Q1 +2.71e-5,
Q2 +4.52e-5, Q3 -1.94e-5, Q4 +2.75e-5 window units = +1.8, +3.0, -1.3,
+1.8 sixteen-bit buckets. Not sub-bucket. The difference is a pyramid
over each quad (zero on its four edges), so 16 bits gave solid dark cores
where |D| > 1 bucket and a lattice where |D| ~ 1 - plus GPU interpolation
noise where D -> 0 near the edges. Fable's "16 bits makes them ties
again" is CORRECTED: it made some pixels tie. No storage width can make
these ties; Case A stands, and the answer is a compare TOLERANCE.

The RDP compare (reference behaviour; the corpus documents only the
triangle's z-coefficient block, ucode05_old.txt l.709-720 - doc-routing
not_covered updated): an opaque fragment passes when
    sz - 8 * max(dzpix, dzmem) <= oz
with dzpix the primitive's max |dz/dx|,|dz/dy| rounded up to a power of
two in the 18-bit z domain (screen z 0..G_MAXZ with 8 fraction bits,
gbi.h:1219), dzmem the stored one, floored at 16/8/4 for stored z above
0x20000/0x10000/0x8000 (window depth 0.5/0.25/0.125). A far-range redraw
always passes within 128 z-units = 4.9e-4 window, ten times the dome's
whole D; the WRITE is the fragment's own z. GL's polygon offset is that
slope term but it moves the write as well as the test, so applied to
both skins it cancels - which is why three rounds reached for
quantization instead.

Fix (B-125): build the asymmetry, for authored redraws only.
- src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c: a per-depth-1-submission set of the eye-space
  positions of every drawn triangle (8192-slot open addressing,
  generation-tagged, reset at each depth-1 call/branch and per frame). A
  G_VTX load whose positions were ALL already drawn by this submission
  flags its slots; a triangle whose three slots all carry the flag is an
  authored redraw. Its colour pass tests with the tolerance (polygon
  offset: factor 16 x window/320 for 8 per N64 pixel doubled for the
  power-of-two round-up; units = the range floor / 262143 in depth-buffer
  units), writes NO depth, and marks the pixels it won in the stencil
  plane; a depth-only pass (colour off, ALWAYS, alpha test off) writes the
  exact z through the mark and clears it. Non-redraw geometry keeps GL's
  exact 24-bit compare - the cartridge's far-range pop-through is not
  imported. Decided per LOAD, not per triangle: the second triangle of
  every quad in a mesh has three seen vertices, but its load brought new
  ones. SL_Z_REDRAW=0 kill switch; inert without a stencil plane.
- src/gfx/sl_gfx_sdl.c: SDL_GL_STENCIL_SIZE 8 requested beside the
  24-bit depth; granted bits printed at context creation and in the mark
  record (depth-bits / stencil-bits, GL_DEPTH_BITS not the request - the
  B-123 lesson); stencil cleared per frame. The B-124 16-bit FBO is
  RETIRED to a diagnostic arm (SL_Z_QUANT=1): it reproduces the lattice
  on demand, and the scene renders to the window's native 24-bit buffer
  again - precise sorting everywhere else comes back.
- Mark record: per-triangle "redraw=" on the depth line; [renderer]
  reports redraw-path status, depth/stencil bits, redraw loads and
  triangles for the frame; the 60-frame census line carries
  redraw=<loads>/<tris>.

What the detection flags on Surface at the mark (traced once, probe
removed): 41-54 loads / ~280-330 triangles a frame - the dome's white
skin, the sky's second layer (each sky submission reloads its 16 quad
vertices), room lists reloading positions under a SECOND combiner
(1ffc93fc after 1f1093ff - authored second material passes), and small
viewmodel reloads. All are later passes over positions already drawn;
where a redraw shares its first pass's triangulation the depths were
already exact ties and nothing changes visually. Flagged geometry gets
the hardware test and an exact write, so it can only be STRICTER than
the cartridge, never looser.

Cost: the render walk measured 40-47 ms/frame at the mark in BOTH arms
(temporary QPC bracket around sl_gfx_frame_dl, removed; the VI-delta
histogram is 2-3 per frame both ways, as the cartridge's own is) - the
redraw path's cost is inside the noise. The 40+ ms walk itself is a
pre-existing Surface cost, parked, not this round's subject.

Same-binary arms at the mark: default - one coherent white shell, no
dashes, no gores, the white pass's authored gradient only; SL_Z_REDRAW=0

Residual note: at the second exterior angle the slit region shows a

## 2026-09-13 - B-126: B-125's hardware-magnitude tolerance bled level-wide -
## the tolerance is now the re-triangulated quad's own tent difference

Owner replay of 327fa80b: "a big fail. A lot of textures are
bleeding/zplane fighting with others in front of them" (run
20260913-002517, marks 1-2). The marks' own records - which now carry a
per-triangle redraw flag - named the mechanism directly. At mark 1 (room
1, the snow road) the flagged draws were seq 56/57: the ROAD pass, a
second material (cc 1ffc93fc, texture 200a3ab0) over the SAME snow
triangles (1f1093ff, 200a34f8), same triangulation. At mark 2 the dome's
white skin (seq 157-182) and nothing else. Both are legitimate second
passes, but B-125 gave every redraw the RDP's far-range magnitude
(4.9e-4 window, tens of world units at range), and a later pass with that
much slack wins a band BEHIND nearer geometry drawn earlier wherever the
two converge in depth - every crest, every silhouette, level-wide.
Measured on the health line: 41-54 wholly-old loads and ~280-330
tolerant triangles a frame, only ~48 of them the dome.

The correction: the hardware magnitude is not imported at all.
- A redraw that reuses its first pass's triangulation (all three edges
  already drawn by this submission) is a PLAIN draw - its depths are
  bit-identical to the first pass's and GL_LEQUAL already gives the tie
  to the later pass. This is the road/sky/second-material case, and it
  is exactly the pre-B-125 rendering the owner had accepted for them.
- Only a RE-TRIANGULATED quad gets a tolerance, and precisely its own:
  for the redraw triangle (p, q, r) whose edge (p, r) was never drawn, s
  is the vertex both drawn edges (p, q) and (q, r) had opposite them in
  the first pass (a per-submission edge table, 16384 slots, keyed by
  position-set slot, two opposite vertices per edge), and the tents
  differ by at most D = |(z_p + z_r)/2 - (z_q + z_s)/2| in window depth
  (the pyramid's apex). D plus two 24-bit buckets is the tolerance -
  2e-5..5e-5 for the dome, four to five world units at that range - as
  a pure units offset, no slope term, no range floor.
- Anything unrecognised (two or more undrawn edges, no common fourth
  vertex, a vertex behind the eye) draws plainly.
- Redraw triangles' edges are NOT entered in the table, so a
  re-triangulated quad's second triangle still sees the new diagonal as
  undrawn.

Measured on the corrected build (health line redraw=<loads>/<tolerant>
/<plain>): mark 1 (road) 23/0/135 - nothing tolerant; mark 2 and the
dome mark 43-59/48/271-400 - the 48 white-skin triangles and nothing
else. Windowed: mark 1's crest is clean, the road stays on its own
surface; the dome at both marks a coherent white shell, no hash, no
gores, the slit wedge where the white skin is absent; the deck view's
railing in front of the dome, the treeline, the distant huts sane;
222555-002's bunker, stairs and snow sane (the 200311 run has been
pruned from disk since the previous round). Liveness surface/facility/
dam 400 PASS. Owner replay is final.

Lesson, recorded because it cost a replay: a tolerance that is right
for the hardware's compare is wrong for an emulation that applies it to
a SUBSET of draws in a different order - the cartridge's slack is
tolerable there only because every draw has it and rooms walk far to
near. The emulation must apply the geometric need, not the hardware
number.

## 2026-09-13 - B-127: the redraw tolerance must be taken at the diagonals'
## TRUE crossing - the midpoint form under-covered a band per quad

Owner replay of ad56b69a: "Dome is nearly good. However, there are a
couple areas ... that open rectangular patches in the dome depending on
where I am standing and looking. The areas are very narrow, but it seems
consistent" (run 20260913-054107 mark-001, room 7, eye -5914.693 443.976
-21773.842, theta 350.250 verta 7.250, centre 56 52 59 - a dark
horizontal rectangle across the dome under the crosshair).

Named from the mark's own record (the candidate table carries the redraw
flag and every vertex's clip row and screen position): the quad under the
crosshair is seq 404/405 (white, redraw=1) over its first pass. B-126's
tolerance was the MIDPOINT form |(z_p+z_r)/2 - (z_q+z_s)/2| = 1.05e-6.
But the two tents' difference peaks where the diagonals actually CROSS in
screen space, and that is their midpoints only for a parallelogram; under
perspective this quad's diagonals cross at t = 0.47 / u = 0.53, and the
difference there is 6.5e-6 with the redraw farther - six times the
tolerance. The white pass failed in the band where the true difference
exceeded 1.05e-6 + rounding, and the dark skin showed as the rectangle;
view-dependent because t and u are. (The other centre quads: 412/413 the
redraw nearer, passes regardless; 428/429 true 0.6x the midpoint form.)

Fix: the edge table keeps the opposite vertex's ndc x, y beside its
window z; rd_classify intersects p-r with q-s in ndc, clamps t, u to
[0, 1], evaluates each tent along its own diagonal at the crossing, and
the tolerance is the larger of that and the midpoint form, plus four
24-bit buckets. GL interpolates window depth linearly in screen space, so
this IS the tents' maximum difference over the quad (zero at the corners,
extremal at the overlay's one interior vertex).

Validated at the owner's exact held view (a temporary env-gated verta
hold on the teleport, removed before commit): the dome fully white where
the rectangle was; SL_Z_REDRAW=0 at the same view shows the gores (the
view is right, the path is what resolves it). Shipping binary: the
230216 dome mark coherent, the 002517 road mark clean; liveness
surface/facility/dam 400 PASS. Owner replay is final.

Owner also reconfirms: tracers still wrong (#16, untouched, next).

## 2026-09-13 - B-128: the bullet tracer's rainbow was a STALE tmem-map hit -
## a load is a range, a later load overwrites what it covers, and tile 1 of
## a mip chain is a level of its own block

Owner: "Dome looks good. We can close that issue. Still have the weird
bullet tracers ... shoot and it will happen every 2-3 shots on average"
(#10 closed at c142; #16 the tracer). Reproduced by bounded scripted
firing (a held F posted to the window queue, one F8) at the 20260912-
222555 mark-006 pose; no owner mark needed.

The beam (gunfire.c sub_GAME_7F061E18, item 5) is drawn with
flareimage3: RGBA32 16x32, level=6, an authored mip chain, which
texSelect's level != 0 branch (othermodemicrocode.c:602-686) loads as
ONE 700-texel block at tmem 0 under G_TL_LOD + G_CC_TRILERP, tiles 1..5
at words 128/160/168/172/174 inside it ("7F076D68 - generate DL for
ImgDecl.txt" :982-987, tmem += tilesize per level). SL_TEX_DUMP at the
shot: entry 181 src=2010f1c0 16x32 (level 0 decodes to the orange
glow), entry 182 "8x16" src=200a6880 fd-base=2010f1c0 - a DIFFERENT
address from the load that filled the tile. 200a6880 is the treeline's
RGBA16 64x23 strip (the TEXEL1 census tile), which B-118's two-image
material loads at word 128 earlier in the frame. The tmem map matched
by exact load START and replaced an entry only at the same start, so
tile 1 = word 128 answered with the strip, decoded as RGBA32 8x16 -
RGB noise - and mode 9 blended that in as TEXEL1 with the strip's alpha:
the wide rainbow streak. Every 2-3 shots = whenever a treeline segment
had drawn before the beam that frame.

B-119's discriminator was the same assumption from the other side:
"tiles 1..n point INTO the block at offsets no load named, so TEXEL1
can never resolve" held only while nothing stale sat at the word. The
Surface c=13 census carried the residue in plain sight: TEXEL1
unresolved 99..674 tris/frame were stale-start hits (dome shell, snow
ground) whose two-image decode then FAILED and fell to plain modulate
without mips - B-119's "655 remaining unresolved".

Fix (SL_TMEM_SPAN, default on): an entry carries its span in 64-bit
words and a sequence number; a lookup returns the most recent load
whose span CONTAINS the address, with the DRAM byte offset that address
stands for inside it. Word size per depth from the same note's line
rule - "width to nearest word" is (width+3)>>2 for 16-bit (:885-890)
and 32-bit (:870-875) alike, so 4 texels per word at both, 16 DRAM
bytes per word at 32bpp (gbi.h:431 LINE_BYTES=2 vs :430 _BYTES=4), 8
otherwise. The c=13 test becomes the one the layouts differ by: tile 1
at an address inside tile 0's own load = one image with mips (single
unit, GL pyramid); a different load = two images (mode 9); two tiles at
one address keep their old two-unit path. tile1_texture refuses an
interior address (a level, not a second image). The render-tile lookup
reads from src + offset (inert: inner-hits=0 measured on Surface, Dam,
Facility). Census line: "sl_cc: tmem map hits/misses/inner-hits/one-
image-mips".

Measured, same binary, same scripted witness: SL_TMEM_SPAN=0 (start-
match) - wide rainbow streak across the dome, rainbow score 1493/1373/
1200 on the top burst frames; default - short orange/white flare, top
frames 276/275/245 = the muzzle flash alone. Surface census: TEXEL1
unresolved 99..674 -> 0 (50 remain: same-address pairs, plain modulate
= TEXEL0, unchanged); one-image-mips 0..50 -> ~2500. Dam: unresolved 0
-> 0 (its chains were misses -> the same mip path either way). The
B-127 dome and road poses, Dam and Facility: no visible change (A/B
side by side; pixel diffs are idle-sway frame offsets). Liveness
facility x3 PASS. Owner replay is final acceptance of #16.

## 2026-09-13 - TOOLING: cheats and a starting weapon at direct boot
## (SL_CHEATS / SL_WEAPON, play.ps1 -Cheats / -Weapon), and a ROM oracle
## for whatever is in Bond's hand (tools/native/romweapon.py)

Owner acceptance of B-128 first (#16 closed): "All seems fixed". New
report in the same message: "The sniper rifle scope seems to be missing
textures" (run 20260913-175358-lvl36 marks 1-2), and the direction: "You
are going to need to use cheats to unlock weapons and load the sniper
rifle at the beginning of the level. And build a tool around that so we
can keep using it going forward."

The sniper rifle is minutes into Surface, so no direct boot could show
it; replaying the owner's run reached frame 5815 and stopped (window
closed by the stream), which sl_teleport.c already records as the wrong
instrument. src/native/sl_cheat.c, on the teleport's pattern (native,
polled from the shim, inert unless named, everything through the game's
own state and calls):

  SL_CHEATS=<names>  writes g_CheatActivated[id] and calls
      update_menu15_cheat() - the cheat menu's own leftovers (front.c:7959,
      :7842) - once the player exists; lv.c:1012-1025 applies them every
      ticking frame exactly as after the menu. Names are the menu's
      (allguns, maxammo, invincible, infammo, 2xhealth, dkmode, ...), the
      CHEAT_* stem, or the number.
  SL_WEAPON=<name>   once the camera is in FP (where bondview2.c:847-872
      equips the level's starting weapons; a request before that is
      overwritten by it) plus ten frames: bondinvAddInvItem if the level
      has not handed the item out, add_ammo_to_weapon to the weapon's own
      maximum if it holds none, then gunRequestHandWeaponChange - the
      next-weapon key's own path (gun.c:1104), so the draw animation, ammo
      display and hand state are the game's. Names: in-game (pp7, klobb,
      kf7, sniper, cougar, ...), ITEM_* stem, or number.

play.ps1 -Cheats <list> -Weapon <name> hands the strings over on the same
env table as -TeleportMark. Measured: -Level surface -Weapon sniper -Cheats
allguns,maxammo -TeleportMark <mark-001> boots standing at the owner's
mark with the sniper rifle up (8/392) in ~80 frames; without the teleport
the request fires when Surface's intro ends (~frame 1000) and equips.

THE ROM SIDE. tools/native/romweapon.py is the cartridge's answer to the
same question: the unmodified ROM under parallel_n64, direct-booted by
writing g_StageNum / g_SelectedDifficulty into RDRAM over the first
frames (boss.c:95's initialiser mechanism, without a rebuilt image - the
Windows tree builds no direct-boot ROMs, which is why every recorded
stream under tools/trace/inputs answers nothing here), the cheat menu's
state written the same way, A pressed until g_CurrentPlayer->hands[0]
reads the wanted item, frames saved outside the tree. Measured: Surface
36, weapon 17 up at tick 1459, four frames. It is the oracle B-129 was
judged against.


## 2026-09-13 - B-129: the sniper scope's eyepiece was alpha-tested - the
## B-121 treeline override took the whole c=13 family, and every first-person
## weapon is in it

Owner: "The sniper rifle scope seems to be missing textures" (marks
20260913-175358 1-2). Reproduced at mark-001 with the new tool. Texture
census at the pose: rejects 0, plain 0, every viewmodel texture decoded
(SL_TEX_DUMP: the wood stock, the ribbed section, the I4 lens images). So
nothing was MISSING; something drew wrong. The ROM oracle (romweapon.py)
gave the cartridge's rifle: same tube, chevrons, ribbing, stock - and an
eyepiece that is BLACK inside, where Sightline's was a bright grey mottle.
Pixels: cartridge interior 0..40, native 60..170.

The eyepiece is two I4 64x64 images (201b5460 mean 166, 201b3e98 mean 22)
drawn at shade 0x43 under G_CC_TRILERP (c=13, the viewmodel's 6-level
chains) and om c4112048 = AA_EN|IM_RD|ALPHA_CVG_SEL, no Z: G_RM_AA_OPA_SURF
(gbi.h:725-728). An I texture's alpha IS its intensity, and B-121 gave the
whole c=13 family GL_ALPHA_TEST > 0.06 (for the strip's transparent sky)
plus a forced z-write - so the lens's dark texels were cut and the snow
behind the gun shone through the scope. Found by the kill switch:
SL_CC_LODLERP=0 put the interior at mean 18 / p90 50 (the cartridge band);
SL_TEX_ENHANCE=0 and SL_TMEM_SPAN=0 changed nothing (62 / 107).

On the cartridge the lens is opaque because in the OPA_SURF modes
ALPHA_CVG_SEL selects the COVERAGE as the pixel alpha - the texel alpha
never reaches the blender, and the interior pixels are fully covered. The
corpus is silent on the coverage bits (grep -rni 'cvg|coverage' over the
notes: nothing; not_covered entry added); gbi.h names the modes and the
oracle frame is the measurement.

Fix: B-121's override is scoped to the shape it was written for - the
TWO-IMAGE detail blend (lodfam && !g_lodmip_draw, B-119's discriminator).
The one-image-plus-mips variant (dome shell, snow ground, every weapon)
keeps its authored render mode. Measured: eyepiece interior 62 -> 18
(cartridge 0..40); the rifle side by side with the oracle frame matches
part for part; the B-127 dome and road poses unchanged (treeline still
two-image, still z-written and alpha-tested); liveness facility x3 PASS.
Gitea #17 filed with the fix; owner replay is final.

## 2026-09-13 - OBSERVATION (Gitea #18, not a fix request): Surface 1 ground
## bullet decals appear only once the shot room has been visited

Owner acceptance of B-129 first (#17 closed: "That looks fixed"). Then:
"when i shoot the ground it seems like it only shows bullet decals when
i was near the spot i shot ... If i walk over to that area and shoot, i
get decals. If i return to the original spot and shoot the far spot
again, i get decals now." Filed at the owner's direction, no fix.

Lead from the source, UNMEASURED: a decal needs a BACKGROUND hit
(chrprop.c:1155-1231 - explosionCreateBulletImpact under gotbghit; the
stan-only branch gives sound and spark, no decal), and
bgTestBulletHitBackground (bg.c:3722) returns FALSE for a room whose
vtx_batch_bounds is NULL - which is every room whose model data is not
currently loaded (set by bgLoadRoomModelData, cleared by delete_room_data
at bg.c:2821). A room that is drawn but not yet resident for collision
therefore takes no decal until the player has come near enough to load
it, and keeps taking them while it stays resident. Whether the cartridge
loads rooms on the same trigger (Rare's behaviour, preserved) or native
loading is lazier (a divergence) is the open question; the oracle is
romweapon.py's direct-boot path with Z presses against the same shot
natively. Nothing in the tree was changed for this.

FIX (76e9404e): SL_WATCH_STICK = 70 (0x46), chosen once per poll on the
existing sl_game_menu_mode() seam (mode 1 = watch) and shared by keys and
wheel. 70 is the single value both unlatched bands exclude (`< 0x46`,
`>= 0x47`) that the latched one still accepts, so a press of ANY length
is one step and the game's own latch is the only repeat authority: a held
key steps once and stops until release. Horizontally 70 and 80 are
indistinguishable to every watch consumer (page changes latch at 0x2E,
the volume slider clamps to 0x46 itself, :2617-2621). The front end
keeps 80 (a cursor integrator, front.c:1189, not a stepped list). No
src/game change; the pad path untouched.

## reject on the eye-crossing population) FAILED witness (1) and was reverted;

THE RULE TRIED, from the cartridge's own instruction stream: gmain.s:512-524
builds each vertex's clip code (vch/vcl against its own unscaled w) and
:784-794 ANDs the three codes masked 0x7030 and rejects the triangle when the
result is non-zero. Implemented in emit_tri's eyec>0 branch, before the guard
clip, computing the five unscaled flags with VCH's own branch formulas so
behind-the-eye vertices get the flags the instruction gives at negative w
(signs differ: vs+vt<=0 / vt<0; signs agree: vt<0 / vs-vt>=0); kill switch
SL_NEARREJ=0; eyec==0 path untouched.

WITNESS (1), Silo swirl, same 55-shot window: 17 of 55 flat before, 17 of 55
after. FAIL -> reverted (git checkout of src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c), binary rebuilt
from HEAD, test.ps1 silo 400 PASS, facility 400 PASS.

WHY, from a temporary per-triangle dump (removed with the revert): 22,805
eye-crossing triangles reached the branch over the window; 22,322 rejected,
483 passed, and the fill is entirely in the 483. Their shape is ONE in-front
vertex off the right plus TWO behind the eye - v0=(149.5,-4.7,45.1,w 74.9)
{+x}, v1=(-18.9,-20.7,-35.6,w -5.6) {-x,-y,near}, v2=(-18.9,401.7,-63.6,w
-33.5) {+x,-x,+y,near}: AND = 0. A behind-the-eye vertex with c < -|w| carries
only the -side flag under either reading of vcc's bytes (the +side flag in
VCH's same-sign branch is c - w >= 0, false for it), so the reject cannot fire
on this population, and the kept sweep of that triangle (apex right of the
screen, crossing-edge directions down-left and up) covers the viewport.
Whatever the cartridge does with it is in the clipper overlay (gmain.s
lbl_1710), not in the reject. Witness (2), ad772496: v0 {+x,+y} and v2
{-x,-y,near} have an empty AND whatever v1 carries - would have stayed drawn;
not the failing witness. Witness (3) and the Dam/Surface controls were not
run: stopped at (1) as instructed.

area) is not on disk this session (reference/ holds two .cht files) and its

vch is a READING, not a citation, and the two readings disagree on whether
the fifth unscaled flag in 0x703 is NEAR (z <= -w) or FAR (z >= w) - one of
them also makes gmain.s:505-513's folded w-sign bit the only eye/near trigger

must be settled by the guide's VCH/VCL pages or by measurement before anyone

THE RULE (production default): in emit_tri's fan emission, a fan triangle of
the eyec>0 (guard, saturated) population is dropped when the cull bits in
force would drop it - the winding is well defined (all w>0 after the guard,
Sutherland-Hodgman preserves it) and equals the RSP's after its own near
retessellation. The eyec==0 near-clipped fan and every ordinary draw stay
under cull_apply exactly as before, so B-114's Dam-massif objection to sense
1 everywhere does not arise. Sense follows SL_CULL (0 none, 2 inverse, 3
left to emit_tri_slots' diagnostic); kill switch SL_NEARCULL=0; the sl_geom
census line reports `near-fan culled=`.

TEXEL was green: SL_TEX_DUMP showed the 32x32 "water" texture as green
noise (mean (6,122,38), maxima R<=16 G<=231 B<=90). SL_TEX_TRACE named the
cause: texSelect loads IMAGE_WATER_BLUE as the CI8 mip chain the texpool
holds (FD fmt=2 siz=2, F0 loadtlut n=24, F5 tiles 0-5 fmt=2 siz=1) with
G_TT_RGBA16 on, then unk_092E50.c:381-384 re-declares tiles 0/1 as
RGBA/16b line 4 without touching the LUT; gbi_to_sl_fmt returned RGBA16
and read index PAIRS as 5551 - exactly the maxima above. The RDP palettises
a LUT-enabled 16-bit fetch by the texel's high byte (notes silent: the LUT
field only, ucode05_old.txt:364; not_covered added). Fix 2e47da80:
SL_TEX_CI16_RGBA16/IA16 decoder formats, returned for an RGBA/16b tile
under LUT 2/3 only, SL_TLUT16=0 kill switch, tlut16= census counter,
self-test fixtures (695 checks). Witness at the same deterministic pose
(SL_VI_CATCHUP=0 f1305): on (8.2,26.2,56.6) - within 1 unit per channel of
the cartridge; the on/off diff is confined to rows >= 319 (sea + its strip

FIRST FINDING - A TOOLING DEFECT, fixed first (69850d27): reproducing the
mark by teleport gave a bright, barely fogged floor (near snow 150-180)
where the owner's frame was dark (~100). The owner run's events file shows
zfar 8000 -> 2000 and far-fog 40000 -> 10000 at the intro swirl; a
teleported run's never did. The game loads a level's fog row twice on the
way into FP - CAMERAMODE_INTRO loads the CINEMA row
(fogLoadLevelEnvironment(stage, 1), bondview2.c:780) and the SWIRL step
reloads the play row (arg 0, bondview2.c:812); FP with one player loads
nothing (bondview2.c:863). sl_teleport.c jumped INTRO -> FP directly, so on
the two levels with a cinema row (Dam and Surface 2, bgfog.c id+900:
Surface 2 cinema farfog 8000 / nearfog 6000 / maxvis 8000 vs the play row's
2000 / 2500 / 3055) every teleported capture drew under the intro fog. The
teleport now runs the SWIRL step's own fogLoadLevelEnvironment(stage, 0); a
teleported run's events now match the owner's. CAVEAT for the record: the
Surface 2 coverage sweeps above (2026-09-14) and every Dam -TeleportMark
measurement before this commit rendered under the cinema fog row; geometry,
textures and props stand, fog-dependent readings there do not. The Surface
2 palette pairing at the spawn (natural boot, not a teleport) stands.

MEASUREMENTS at the mark pose under the play row (posern: SL_TELEPORT_* to
the mark, a 28-record C-up hold reaches verta -21.4 repeatably):
- SL_CC_LODLERP=0, SL_TEX_ENHANCE=0: floor rows identical to baseline (the
  LOD lerp touches the treeline only); SL_FOG=0 brightens the far snow but
  a soft crease remains in the shade.
- The fog field alone (SL_FOG_VIZ=2, B channel): a smooth function of the
  screen row, identical profiles at x=150 and x=480 below the horizon. The
  crease is carried by the SHADE (vertex colour), the fog rides the same
  interpolation.
- SL_FOG_DUMP: per-vertex fog is z_ndc*fm+fo with fm 2976 / fo -2720
  (gSPFogPosition 957..1000 - fog 0 at ~45 eye units, ~56% at 100, full at
  ~1740), z_ndc = 1.002 - 4.004/z_eye under near 2 / far 2000.
- The rule: the RDP interpolates shade RGBA - and the fog value the RSP put
  in shade alpha - linearly in SCREEN space (Gouraud, ucode05.txt:400; the
  othermode "Texture Perspective" bit at ucode05.txt:853 is a control for
  texture only; docs otherwise silent - doc-routing not_covered entry
  added). GL's fixed pipeline interpolates every varying perspective-
  correct, exact only for world-affine quantities. Across a 40:1 depth
  range the two agree at the vertices only: each triangle bows, every
  shared edge creases, the pattern is anchored to the floor triangles and
  sweeps over the ground as Bond walks.
- Cartridge ground truth (tools/native/romintro.py variant with a C-up
  hold, output outside the repo): at the spawn pose and the same pitch the
  cartridge reads 47 -> 93 over rows 220..670 with a mid-band plateau at
  rows 430..580 (89..93); the pre-fix native read 54 -> 147 with the
  plateau at 121..132 and a diagonal crease; the fixed native reads 54 ->

THE FIX (9dd35b33, B-131): a GLSL 1.30 program bound around the DL
triangle batch only - the fixed pipeline's own transform (ftransform;
texture coordinates stay perspective-correct as the RDP corrects texture)
with the colour and the fog coordinate carried as noperspective USER
varyings, and a fragment stage reproducing texenv modes 0 (modulate), 3
(AEQ_ADD) and 4 (AEQ_LERP). Two dead ends measured on the way: a vertex
stage alone (22676 batches bound) changed nothing - the driver's own
fragment processing ignores the qualifier; and both stages with the
qualifier on REDECLARED BUILT-INS (noperspective out vec4 gl_FrontColor /
in vec4 gl_Color) compiled, linked and STILL rendered the fixed pipeline's
frame to a mean of 1.2 - NVIDIA 591.86 accepts and ignores it. User
varyings move the same pose by a mean of 13. The B-051 alpha program (mode
5) carries the same varyings. Modes 6-9 (register lerp, sky, water lerp,
two-image LOD blend) and any draw with the second unit live stay on the
fixed pipeline (vertical strips, small per-triangle depth range) -
RESIDUAL DEBT, recorded. Kill switch SL_SHADE_LINEAR=0; census line
`sl_shade: linear=.. program=.. batches=..`. Also: a clipper-generated
vertex's fog depth is its own z/w instead of a lerp of the endpoints' z/w
(the lerp puts a vertex 126 units out at fog 0 where the RSP gives 0.65);
measured on the walk witness it moves the frame by at most 1 LSB (the
generated vertices sit on the +-2 guard band off-screen), so it is kept as
a semantic with SL_CLIPDEPTH=0 as its A/B arm (3ce97580), not claimed as
the fix.

CARTRIDGE GROUND TRUTH (romintro.py variant with a scripted forward push,
every tick, frames outside the repo): the same walk's near band is
continuous (largest tick-to-tick step 2.3; 89 -> 129 -> 89 -> 123 -> 100).

for seven steps (109/107/106/104/102/100 vs 109/107/106/104/103/102; 117
vs 117). So the post-cut fan was RIGHT and the uncut triangle was the wrong

FIRST WRONG STAGE - geometry/clip: emit_tri took the guard-clip fan only
for a triangle with a vertex behind the eye or behind the near plane and
handed GL the whole triangle otherwise. The game sets the RSP clip ratio to
2 (gSPClipRatio(FRUSTRATIO_2), src/game/lv.c:711; the notes are silent on
the clip ratio - grep -rn -i 'clip ratio|guard band|FRUSTRATIO' over
notes/ returns nothing) and the RSP clips any triangle with a vertex
outside |x|,|y| <= 2w; a floor vertex a few units ahead and 167 below the
eye is far outside. With Gouraud shade the clipped polygon's vertices ARE
the visible shading, so B-100's "G only decides where offscreen the
generated edges land" holds for coverage and perspective-correct
attributes, not for shade.

FIX (1eb65fbd, B-132): any vertex outside the 2w box sends the triangle
through the four guard planes (on the near-cut polygon where there is a
crossing); the population without a violation is unchanged. Same walk:
near band continuous, largest step 2.0 (cartridge 2.3), peaks and troughs
in the cartridge's order. RESIDUAL, OPEN: the level sits 4-17 above the
cartridge on some steps (native 93-121 vs cartridge 89-129; shots 60-66
read a flat 118 where the cartridge declines 109 -> 101). Guard-clipping
only the population WITHOUT a near crossing was tried and re-creates the
jumps (the polygon changes as the vertex crosses the near plane), so the
shipped form is the one without jumps. SL_NEARSAT=0 still bisects the whole
fan path. Two measurement rounds spent (interpolation rule; clip
population) - the residual level is parked with the traces above rather
than narrowed.

:784-888, bounded to these two triangles): clip codes AND 0x7030 rejects,
OR 0x4343 goes to the clipper overlay (not in the reference); otherwise
the cross product of the three screen positions (DMEM +0x18, y down) in
command order, negated once per swap of the y-sort, masked with the
mode's 0x1000/0x2000 bits and the sign of the hi word. A constant-sense
screen-area sign - exactly tri_sign_of's, with the sense fixed by the
B-043 captures. The corpus is silent (not_covered entry corrected).

PROVENANCE FIRST (docs: gedocs.py topic models-animation, then a grep of
the corpus for LOD/mipmap - the model-part LOD is modelUpdateDistanceRelations
(model.c, MODELNODE_OPCODE_LOD, MinDistance/MaxDistance * model->scale); the
image LOD is the C0 type 0/1 level byte, "image declarations.txt" l.77-91;
neither is what switches here):
- The mark files' [submitted-lists] show the SAME prop lists at the far and
  near poses: 4x 05000930 (34 tris) + 4x 05000e28 for the door at marks 1
  and 2, 8x 05000488 (18 tris) for the crates at marks 3 and 4. No model
  part is selected by distance.
- What differs is the MATERIAL of the same triangles: far = cc fc26ea04
  1f10ffff / om_l c4104dd8 / blend on (the ENV-alpha combiner, alpha = ENV x
  SHADE, XLU_SURF2), near = cc fc26a004 1f1093fb / om_l c4112078 / blend
  off (G_CC_TRILERP + MODULATEIA2, OPA_SURF). Those are chrobjRenderProp's
  PropType 5 (objAlpha < 0xFF) and PropType 9 branches (propobj.c:7722).
- objAlpha comes from chrobjFogVisRangeRelated (propobj.c:13681, the
  formula D-003 derives) against the near-fog row. SL_TABLE_DBG at the
  marks: NearFog=1000 MaxVisRange=15000 MaxObfusc=750 lodscalez=1.0909; the
  door at 1445 -> alpha 250, the crates (size 72.7) at 973-1507 -> 252..237,
  the mainframe column at 1790 -> 247. A 2-7% fade, invisible as a fade.
- On the translucent path every authored vertex alpha is real: the crates'
  plank strips carry vertex alpha 0x7f (mark 3 seq 794: rgba 0000007f) and
  become 48% glass over the dark body; the door panels blend against the
  corridor; the mainframe column at 1790 all but disappears. On the opaque
  path (OPA_SURF) those alphas are ignored, which is why the near marks look
  right. The "LOD" is the path switch at the very start of a 14000-unit
  fade band.
- ONE bounded renderer A/B for orientation: SL_CC_LODLERP=0 at mark 3 drew
  the far crates opaque - because it also drops the c=13 family's mip
  pyramid, whose box-filtered texel alpha the single-image variant (B-119,
  sl_gfx_dl.c:5396 `want = lodmip ? 0 : 9`, plain GL modulate) multiplies
  into a word whose RDP alpha equation has no texel term. That is a real
  native inexactness on the fade path (the cartridge's crates are dark and
  faded, the native's were ghost boxes - romtele.py stage 27 at mark 3's
  pose, %TEMP%\sightline-oracle\b2-m3), but it is not what the owner ruled
  on and it is unreachable under the default below. PARKED on #26.

THE RULE (B-133, src/game/propobj.c chrobjFogVisRangeRelated, native only,
__sgi verbatim): a prop is either fully visible (alpha 1.0) or culled
(alpha 0 at MaxVisRange <= t, unchanged) - the translucent band is removed.
Derived, not tuned: the band contributes nothing the eye sees but the path
switch, and the only play-relevant value in the function is the cull. No
constant, no per-prop, per-level or resolution term. The "scale the switch
distance by output height / 240" rule the coordinator proposed was
considered and rejected: it moves the switch outward (1000 -> 3000 on this
level) but the artefact stays wherever the switch lands. Props now pop out
where they used to reach alpha 0 - the same distance as before (Bunker 2
crate: 10000+ units, beyond any room's portal range; outdoors the far-fog
cull in fogGetPropDistColor fires first). Covers props AND guards (chr.c
multiplies the same value into chrfadealpha; the death/spawn fade in
chr->fadealpha is untouched).

KILL SWITCH (project rule 5): SL_PROP_FADE=1 restores the cartridge's
translucent fade exactly. Default 0 is the owner's ruling. Recorded as
D-004 in docs/divergences.md (the documented exception to its rule 3).

STATE: render-only. The value feeds PropType / env alpha / draw-pass flags;
the two consumers' "not drawn" branches (objAlpha <= 0, chrfadealpha > 0)
see the same zeros, so time_other_players_on_screen and the prop bookkeeping
are unchanged. Nothing hashed moves. No trace-verify claim (no MIPS
toolchain); the preprocess proof stands in: `-E -P -x c -D__sgi`, includes
stripped, HEAD vs working tree, propobj.c __sgi arm 382610 b vs 382610 b
IDENTICAL; POSITIVE CONTROL (one token in the __sgi arm perturbed) DIFFERS,
so the comparison is not vacuous. cc1 must be on PATH for the driver
(C:\msys64\mingw32\bin) or gcc -E exits 1 with no message - the first run
did exactly that.

## 2026-09-15 - Bunker 2 owner report: "the throwing knife up close doesn't
## seem centred with the crosshair and goes to the right" - MEASURED: Rare's
## authored right-hand launch, parallel to the aim ray, no convergence; the
## cartridge lands right by the same amount; no native divergence; no
## production change (owner to decide on a toggle-able convergence)

OWNER REPORT (Bunker 2 replay, 2026-09-15): "When using the throwing knife
up close to an enemy, it doesn't seem centred with the crosshair and goes to
the right of the target. Not sure if there is a way to adjust the trajectory
to be better." Scope this round: measurement and provenance only.

DOCS FIRST: gedocs.py topic weapons-ammo (object/ammo tables only) and a
corpus grep for "throwing knife" / "projectile" - nothing on the launch
geometry (only GameShark and model notes); the decomp is the authority
here and it is unmodified game code.

MECHANISM (src/game/gun.c generate_player_thrown_knife, 0x7F05F09C):
- DIRECTION: bullet_path_from_screen_center (gunfire.c:5270) -> the
  crosshair's 2D position (g_CurrentPlayer->crosshair_angle, centre unless
  aiming) plus the weapon's Inaccuracy spread, turned into a unit vector
  and rotated by the view matrix. It is the SAME direction a bullet takes -
  i.e. the aim ray's direction, not a vector toward a point on the ray.
- ORIGIN: hands[hand].throw_item_pos_related.m[3] - the first-person hand's
  world position (gunfire.c:580, gunmtx_camspace through viewtoworldmtxf),
  which is the weapon's authored screen position: WeaponStats
  throwknife_stats PosX 14.0, PosY -24.8, PosZ -34.0 (assets/obseg/gun/
  gunWeaponStats.inc.c:71 - gunSetHorizontalOffset takes +PosX for the
  right hand, -PosX for the left) plus the throw animation's hand offset.
- VELOCITY: 25 units/tick along that direction, +5 units/tick upward, plus
  Bond's own velocity (gun.c:1935-1944); gunInitProjectileFromPlayer then
  runs the projectile under gravity.
So the knife leaves ~14 units to the RIGHT of the eye and travels PARALLEL
to the aim ray: it is offset right by the hand distance at every range and
never converges on the crosshair. At 100 units that is ~14/(100*tan(fovx/2))
of the half-width = ~85 px at 960 wide (~53 px at 150 units, ~26 at 300);
the +5 up bias lifts it ~5 units per tick before gravity takes over.
There is no close-range convergence anywhere in the throw path (grep
"convergence|converge" over src/game: none).

NATIVE MEASUREMENT (bunker2, invincible,invisible,maxammo, SL_WEAPON=
throwknife, teleport to room 31 (-1806,167,4472) theta 270 facing the
x=-1667 wall 139 units ahead, one Z press, SL_PROP_DBG=2, shots every 4
frames; scratch bunker2\kn1-sheet0.png, kn1-stuck-zoom.png): the knife
prop spawned at (-1767.4,147.3,4486.2) = eye + (38.6 forward, 14.2 right,
20.0 down) - the authored PosX/PosY/PosZ through the throw pose - and
flew +25.0 forward / +4.6 up per tick until it embedded at x=-1704.5
(101 units out). Rendered position relative to the screen centre
(480,360): in flight (+70,-3) then (+61,-14) px; the stuck-knife model
then draws up-right of the impact as it takes its embedded pose:
(+75,-67), (+84,-89), (+99,-95). Predicted from the spawn offset at 101
units: +85 px right, which is the in-flight number.

CARTRIDGE PAIRING (scratch bunker2\romknife.py: romweapon.py's boot,
romtele.py's per-tick pose poke, the inventory's all-guns flag and
AMMO_KNIFE written directly - the cheat write romweapon.py relies on does
not take on this stage, and romweapon.py's own cycle on Surface walks only
the level's items, so its "all guns" was never exercised - then A until
the throwing knife is up, one Z press, a frame per tick; frames under
%TEMP%\sightline-oracle\b2-knife5; sheet bunker2\rom-knife-sheet.png).
Same pose, same wall. Cartridge knife relative to centre, mapped to native
pixels (x*1.5, y*3 - the 320x220 view at y 10 is the native 960x660 at y
30): in flight (+56,-8) then (+58,-28); embedded (+82,-87), (+94,-102),
(+106,-114), (+116,-112). The native's (+61..+70 in flight, +99,-95
embedded) matches within the tick-sampling of the two clocks. THE
CARTRIDGE LANDS RIGHT OF THE CROSSHAIR BY THE SAME AMOUNT: this is Rare's
authored hand-offset launch, not a native divergence. The crosshair is a 2D
overlay drawn from the same crosshair_angle the throw reads; the owner's
marks show it at the projection centre (480,355-360). No Gitea issue.

PROPOSAL, for the owner to decide (NOT implemented): a toggle-able
convergence - in generate_player_thrown_knife (and generate_player_thrown_
object for grenades/mines, the same shape) replace the parallel direction
by normalize(aim_point - hand_origin) where aim_point = eye + aim_dir * D,
with D either a fixed convergence distance or the aim ray's first collision
(a hit-scan for the aim point); the knife then crosses the crosshair at D
and lands on it at close range, at the cost of a slight leftward skew
beyond D. STATE IT TOUCHES: throw_speed_vec -> the projectile's velocity ->
projectile physics (position, bounce, embed, who it hits), all of which
IS simulated and trace-hashed state (the character/prop pool); it would be
a D-005 divergence, toggle default = cartridge unless the owner rules
otherwise, and it must not touch the +5 up bias or Bond's velocity term
if the throw's feel is to stay recognisable. No trace-verify claim is made
for anything here (nothing changed).

THE TELEPORT'S TILE LOOKUP WAS WRONG FOR THIS LEVEL AND IS FIXED
(c6e3ad16, src/native only). Batch A registered a neighbouring room at
12 of 19 stops (r01 -> 50 from 426 units outside warehouse 50; r10 ->
62; r19 -> 30; the wrapper rooms 2-4/12-18 -> their warehouses).
Measured, not argued: sub_GAME_7F0AFB78 (stan.c:795, the spawn's own
lookup) ranks EVERY tile by the 3D distance from the request to three
near-corner points and the midpoint and never tests containment, so on
a yard built from very large tiles a point mid-tile is farther from its
own tile's candidates than from a small warehouse tile next door. The
game's containment lookup stanFindTileBelowPos (stan.c:342; the highest
floor tile under a point, restricted to a room list; its test is the
tile's reference triangle, stan.c:443, so it can miss a point inside a
large polygon) is now asked first for the requested room, then the
game's own tile walk walkTilesBetweenPoints_NoCallback (stan.c:1469)
from the nearest tile's candidate point to the requested XZ (crosses
linked edges only, so it ends on the containing tile or fails at a
wall), then the any-room containment, then the nearest-corner tile; the
applied line names which won (`tile=under-point-in-room /
walked-from-nearest / under-point-any-room / nearest`), so `nearest` now
MEANS no floor lies under the point. Witnesses: ctl07 (spawn) and ctl08
(yard 8 centre) in-room; r10 from (2000,-5618) in-room where its centre
had landed inside warehouse 62; the ten door slabs found their warehouse
by the walk. Regression control: four Archives points (r14, r10 on the
second floor at 250.6, r01, r05) all `under-point-in-room`, registration
unchanged from the accepted pass. The probe sits 120 above the requested
Y; the floorless margins were re-probed at Y=100 and room 19 at Y=600

WHY (source, US): propobj.c:11304-11308 refuses a 0x14 crate unless some
non-zero slot's ammo is below its maximum; lv.c:1012-1024 applies the
activated cheats when D_80048394 == 0 - the level's FIRST tick (lv.c:1213
accumulates the clock from then on; this corrects sl_cheat.c's "every
ticking frame", and it is why a cheat poked into the cartridge after that
tick never applied); cheat.c:1044 CHEAT_MAXAMMO ->
set_max_ammo_for_cur_player (gunfire.c:5820) fills every type, remote mines
to 10 ("ammo value tables and maximums.txt"). The WEAPON comes from the
ammo grant (add_ammo_to_inventory, propobj.c:10535 bondinvAddInvItem
(ITEM_REMOTEMINE) + ITEM_TRIGGER), so with the crate refused Bond never
gets remote mines. The JP/EU branch right below (propobj.c:11310-11319) is

FIRST WRONG STAGE: the renderer's texture-environment choice, measured
with the tri-watch (now printing fogcol, geom, texenv and the alpha-
equation uniforms): the pane draws reached tex_apply with texenv=0 and the
B-051 alpha shader's uniforms never uploaded (aeq-u=-1). sl_gfx_dl.c
tex_apply's B-119 LOD-family precedence - `if (lodfam) { want = lodmip ? 0
: 9; aeq_want = AEQ_OFF; }` - forced plain GL_MODULATE for every word
whose cycle 0 is the mip lerp, and the tinted-glass word is one, so the
cycle-1 PRIM alpha addend (Rare's calculatedopacity) was discarded and
every tinted pane drew at its texture's constant 102/255 = 40% alpha
whatever its opacity said - the rooms behind it (which the native still
traverses) showed through. Discriminators: SL_ALPHA_EQ=0 changed nothing
(the shader was not in force to begin with); SL_GLASS_MARK=1 painted the
pane translucent magenta, =2 (texture dropped) solid magenta - the
texture's alpha was the only alpha in force; SL_TEXGEN_LOD 0/1/2 moved
nothing (not a mip-level question). A regression from B-119 (2026-09-12);
Facility's panes were owner-validated before it (2026-08-28) and had
carried the same 40% since.

FIX 9b2d8c6a (B-138, src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c): the single-image mip variant
keeps the alpha-equation classification; only the two-image detail blend
(mode 9) still overrides. The shader's RGB is the same modulate sampled
through the same mip pyramid, so nothing about the mip lerp moves; a
trivial alpha word still classifies to OFF and draws mode 0. Blast radius:
draws of the tinted-glass word with PRIM alpha > 0 - the 0x2F panes and
windowed doors' calculatedopacity; ordinary props on the same word carry
prim alpha 0 and are unchanged (measured: the mainframe cabinet, lockers
and desks share the word under SL_GLASS_MARK).

## 2026-09-16 - Aztec crash (owner run 20260916-074840-lvl28): ACCESS
## VIOLATION reading 0x04000000 in the walker's vertex load - B-139, fixed
## 32083e8b (consumer semantic + witness + crash pose); producer of the unset
## segment NOT demonstrated; Gitea #32 OPEN pending owner replay; the Aztec
## pre-owner sweep NOT run (owner ruling: manual testing)

OWNER: "I got a crash playing through aztec." Then, once the fix shipped:
"If the crash is fixed, I'll continue testing. I think the automated might
not be worth it here." So this entry is the crash, not a coverage pass.

BINARY IDENTITY: the crashing exe was the HEAD build (build\win32\
sightline.exe of 2026-09-16 00:38, after the last source commit 9b2d8c6a
at 23:53 and before the crash at 07:50); no object newer than the exe. The
addresses below were resolved against that binary before anything was
rebuilt (mingw32 addr2line / nm / objdump; src/gfx has no line tables -
the native class compiles without -g - so the walker frames are named by
symbol span and disassembly).

WITNESS (crash.txt): ACCESS VIOLATION addr 0x04000000, READ, eip 0x0054470f,
esp 0x01f9f724, ebp 0x01f9f858, frame 0x3455 (13397). Return chain:
0x00542493 walk.part.0 -> 0x00546cfb sl_gfx_frame_dl -> 0x004fb477
rspGfxTaskStart (src/game/rsp.c:246) -> 0x0040301f bossMainloop (boss.c:653)
-> 0x00402649 bossEntry (boss.c:299) -> 0x00550d93 mainproc (init.c:284).
The pc is walk.part.0+0x4c3f: `movdqu (%esi,%eax,1),%xmm3` - the first of
four 16-byte loads of a variable-length copy from the operand into g_vbuf
(0x1671500), i.e. the OP_VTX handler's `memcpy(&g_vbuf[v0], src, n*16)`.
Stale stack words: dorottex (model.c:4441, the first-person star flash),
sub_GAME_7F061E18 (gunfire.c:1454), texSelect - the game's build of that
frame; the owner was firing. Session seams (env): SL_BOOT_LEVEL=28,
SL_BOOT_DIFFICULTY=1, SL_CHEATS=invincible,maxammo (no invisible), windowed
960x720, seed 6e9b909. `events` holds only the record-1 env/zfar lines and
`log` has no mission/room lines (SL_MISSION_DBG was off), so the artefacts
do not say where in the level it happened.

FIRST WRONG CONSUMED STATE: 0x04000000 is a G_VTX operand in SEGMENT form
(top nibble clear, segment 4 = SPSEGMENT_MODEL_VTX, offset 0 - a model's
first vertex batch) consumed on a submission where segment 4 was unset (or
set to something unmapped). dl_operand then tried it as a raw host pointer
and mem_readable's Windows probe (vq_region, the B-072 VirtualQuery memo)
ACCEPTED it, because its rule was "not MEM_FREE". MEASURED in-process (an
injected read of the same address in the same binary layout, scratch build
only, reverted): Windows reports at 0x04000000 a MEM_MAPPED allocation
based at 0x02f70000, size 0x371000, state RESERVE, protect 0 - reserved,
not committed. A read there faults and the VEH pager does not rescue it;
only the kseg2 window at 0xC0000000 pages in on touch. On the cartridge the
RSP would have DMA'd from 0x04000000 and drawn one batch of junk; natively
it was a fault. The consumer is the native seam (src/gfx), so the fix is
there and src/game is untouched (no __sgi proof needed).

FIX (32083e8b, B-139, native only):
- vq_region: readable = MEM_COMMIT and not PAGE_NOACCESS|PAGE_GUARD, OR
  inside the pager window (sl_pager_covers, src/platform/sl_ultra_shim.c).
  Same rule as the crash handler's own sl_win_readable. The per-frame memo
  is unchanged and still safe (an in-window answer is ok regardless of
  state; a committed region does not decommit under a walk).
- OP_VTX: an operand that resolves to nothing readable is dropped, counted
  into g_vtx_reject (the census `rej=`, which must be 0) and g_vtx_unres
  (`sl_vtx: loads-to-slot-nonzero=.. unresolved=..` under SL_DL_CENSUS),
  and REPORTED: `sl_vtx: fN UNRESOLVED load w0= w1= segment S base=
  depth= dl1= dlin= off=` plus the region state of the raw and K0
  candidates - first eight per run unconditionally, SL_SEG_DBG=1 every
  one. Before this a NULL src was dropped silently (no counter).
- crash.txt: `region at addr: base alloc size state protect type` for the
  fault address, and a [teleport] section (teleport-pos/theta/verta/room,
  crash-stage, crash-camera-mode, crash-tile-room - the F8 mark's keys)
  from sl_crash_pose (src/native/sl_game_query.c), read through the
  reporter's readability predicate, so `play.ps1 -Level <name>
  -TeleportMark <run>\crash.txt` lands where the crash was. Exercised with
  the injected fault: teleport-pos -332.000 277.794 0.000, room 23.

PRODUCER: NOT DEMONSTRATED. Which object had segment 4 unset is unknown.
Bounded rounds, every one clean (zero unresolved loads, no fault):
1. the owner's recording replayed through SL_INPUT (+.move/.vis/.spec):
   diverges at census frame 181 (tris 762 vs 760) and runs to its end -
   the owner's own ruling that replays do not reproduce a session, struck
   as a mechanism after this one run;
2. a teleport into every one of the 92 sl_map rooms with a 437-degree turn
   (the class-wide check of the consumer's table: every model class in
   every room resolved its vertex loads) plus 11 alternates;
3. PP7 fire and Moonraker-laser fire (SL_WEAPON=laser, that test only) in
   the monitor hall (room 23, 65 of the level's 84 single-monitor 0x0A
   displays - the one producer in the tree that emits a literal
   gSPVertex(0x04000000) is the monitor quad, propobj.c:7226, with segment
   4 set two words earlier), cheats invincible,invisible,maxammo;
4. a visible fight there under the owner's exact cheats (guards' lasers,
   a death).
Noted debt, not the cause: get_ptr_allocated_block_for_vertices (chr.c:1177,
the vtxallocator behind dorottex) is declared void and returns dynAllocate's
pointer only because EAX survives its `nop; leave; ret` epilogue at -O0
(disassembly checked) - the same accident as v0 on MIPS.

ACCEPTANCE: test.ps1 -Level aztec -Frames 400 PASS and -Level facility
-Frames 400 PASS (liveness only, after the revert of the injection).
Regression control: Facility (the reference; every level walks G_VTX
through the same dl_operand), 1500 windowed frames: rej 0, unresolved 0,

DEPOT (stage 30) yard floor, owner mark 20260916-130256-lvl30/mark-001
(3047.2,166.1,-9276.7 theta 108.5 verta -22.75 room 9): centre 95 00 00,
the floor red near and white far. Two causes, both FIXED; the audit's
findings carried forward, not redone.

CAUSE A (white) - B-141, src/gfx/sl_gfx_tex.c + sl_gfx_dl.c tex_acquire.
The floor is Rare's type-1 detail command (tex.c:731 texHandleType1):
TARDETAIL (images.def:23, CI8 16x16, 53-entry TLUT) at TMEM 0, the I4 base
at word 32, and texWriteTileFromDefinition sets tile 0 from the image
entry's flags 0x3/0x8/0xD/0x2: tmem = 3 + line(2)*8 = 19, mask s =
(4-13)&0xF = 7, mask t = 4-2 = 2 - a 128x4 window from byte 152 whose
indices run past the 53 loaded entries. Rare's authored data ("Detailflag1
used once with value 0x38D2", image.h), faithfully decoded. The decoder
returned SL_TEX_ERR_SHORT_PAL for the whole tile, tex_acquire gave name 0,
and the whole draw (the same fc26e404 1ffcfffc detail blend as the Dam
cliffs) went untextured. ONE CARTRIDGE COMPARISON (romtele.py stage 30 at
the mark pose, --keepxz; %TEMP%\sightline-oracle\dp-mark1k): the hardware
draws the yard as dark textured tarmac (near-floor region mean 36/32/24)
- neither white nor the base image alone. Docs: ucode05.txt F0 gives the
LOAD; nothing in the corpus says what the fetch reads for an index past
the loaded count (it is the TLUT half of TMEM: a stale entry; recorded in
doc-routing.json not_covered). The stale entry is not reproducible; the
production semantic is SL_TEX_FLAG_PAL_WRAP - an out-of-range index wraps
into the loaded entries (idx mod entries), so every texel stays in the
texture's own palette; a palette with NO readable entry still rejects.
Default on in tex_acquire (part of the cache key); SL_PAL_WRAP=0 is the
old reject. sl_tex_pal_wrapped counts wrapped texels; the census line
"B-141 pal-wrap images=N texels=M". Self-test fixtures (SL_TEX_SELFTEST):
strict still SHORT_PAL; wrap decodes, counts every texel, lands on
(idx mod 2) for CI4/CI8/CI16 x RGBA/IA; empty palette + wrap still
rejects. 725 checks pass. Stated approximation: the window's bytes past
the 256-byte block are RDRAM (the palette) natively and the I4 base data
on hardware (TMEM 256+); the texel pattern of that 72-byte tail is
therefore not the cartridge's byte-for-byte - the tone is.

CAUSE B (red) - B-142, src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c tex_apply. An untextured draw
(combiner names no texel, or the tile did not resolve) disabled unit 0 and
returned with the texture ENVIRONMENT as the previous draw left it. Every
fixed-function mode is inert with texturing off; mode 5 is the B-051 alpha
PROGRAM, kept bound across batches by design (shade_linear_bind defers to
it), and its fragment stage samples u_tex unconditionally - so the floor
was painted with the hazard-stripe pane's texture (GL name 4): red x
shade, 88 tris a frame. FIX: texenv_plain() on both untextured returns -
if mode 5 is current, end the batch and texenv_set(0), which is the same
"leave the program" every other mode change already performs; the next
textured draw re-establishes its mode through `g_texenv != want`. No
level, room or texture condition. INVARIANT COUNTER: sl_texenv census line
"plain-under-alpha-program=N (B-142 invariant, must be 0)" counts a batch
opening with unit 0 off under mode 5; "untextured-left-mode-5=N" counts the
resets.

### MARK 1 - FIXED. The four boundary answers, then the actual mechanism.

(1) G_VTX 04300040 0e000200 is n=4 at slot 0 (ucode05.txt "--RARE vtx--",

bits 20-23 / 16-19 reading, measured on dotube). No slot ambiguity.

ucode05.txt:297 says are not drawn - the interpreter's tri4() agrees nibble
for nibble; no terminator convention exists in the note.

screen box (ndc x -0.55..0.17, y -0.28..0.26, w 986..1242), so gmain.s:784-794
(AND 0x7030 rejects, OR 0x4343 clips) passes it straight to setup.

a room-table and visible-room-array dump, --poke16 per tick):
  - Zeroing all seven B1 words of room 1's list in cartridge RDRAM (read back

  - The cartridge's visible-room array (dword_CODE_bss_8007FFA0, 15 entries)
    gives rooms 23/35/26/27/28/29/1/2 the window [1.0,181.9]-[30.2,214.3] of

FIRST WRONG STAGE. SL_CC_LODLERP=0 - the render tile alone - matched the
cartridge (top bevel 112 vs 117, inner slope banded), so the two-unit
LOD_FRACTION lerp B-118 (ae77f478, 2026-09-12) put every c=13 draw on is
the difference, and accepted Dam (31e3ad44, 2026-09-07) predates it: a
regression by a global change, exactly the owner's hypothesis. The prop
list runs `ba001001 00000000` (G_MDSFT_TEXTLOD = G_TL_TILE) and `bb000001
ffffffff` before its CI image (list read from cartridge RDRAM, dam2\
paneldl2.txt); with LOD off the RDP computes no per-pixel LOD,
LOD_FRACTION is 0, and the lerp is TEXEL0. The native lerp used its own
per-triangle LOD estimate against a mip-pyramided unit 1, pulling the
faces toward a minified average - and unit 1 was ALSO the wrong image:
tile1_texture sized it from the load's texel count in the LOAD's texel
size (288 16-bit texels for a CI8 image loaded through a 16-bit block) so
tile 1 decoded as 24x12, the top half of the frame texture (dump pair
p-000 23x24 / p-001 24x12). Fixing the size alone did not change the
panel (the lerp toward a minified pyramid still flattened it); gating the
lerp on TEXTLOD did.

FIX (3b751551, src/gfx/sl_gfx_dl.c): OP_SETOTHH decodes sft 16
(G_MDSFT_TEXTLOD; the notes' own example "BA001001 00010000 ;images use
lod", Texture application (Rooms).txt); tex_apply routes a c=13 draw under
G_TL_TILE through the single-unit branch - plain modulate, alpha equation
kept exactly as B-138 keeps it for the mip variant, no pyramid - and never
arms mode 9 (the first attempt gated only tex1_apply and left mode 9 armed
over a dead unit: the frame went opaque white, the B-119 hazard,
withdrawn). tile1_texture converts the load's count through bytes to the
tile's texel size and bounds a clamped axis by the F2 window as the
render tile does (only shrinks; the explosion's 16-bit fire tile and every
wrapping masked axis are unchanged by construction). SL_TEXTLOD_GATE=0
reverts the routing. Census: "sl_cc: B-144 c=13 lerp under G_TL_TILE (LOD
off, drawn as TEXEL0) tris=N textlod-now=N gate=on". The F5 trace line
prints cms/masks/shifts/cmt/maskt/shiftt.

DATA/LAYOUT PATH. The INTROTYPE_CREDITS intro record (type 8, 0x8 bytes:
type, file offset - "Intro Block Commands.txt", 7F005D8C) names a table
of CreditsEntry records (bondtypes.h: u16 TextId1, TextId2, s16
Position1, u16 Alignment1, s16 Position2, u16 Alignment2 = 0xC bytes; the
cartridge's handler walks it LHU +0/+2 on a 0xC stride to a record whose
two ids are both 0). bondviewRenderCredits (bondview2.c:9095) carries
xpos/align state across rows (-1 = "as the row before"; defaults 0xdc /
CREDITS_ALIGN_RIGHT) and places row i at y = viewtop + i*16 - roll +
viewheight, x by alignment (RIGHT: from xpos; LEFT: ending at xpos;
CENTER: centred on xpos), textMeasure for the width, then textRender ->
textrelated.c texrects -> the 2D ortho (framebuffer 440x330 in this
stage's hi-res mode, stretched to the window).

(prop.c, native arm) swapped the boundpads span as 32-bit words to "the
next section" - propDefs - so every pair of 16-bit fields was exchanged.

## 2026-09-17 - #38 Controls: the native action/binding layer - E interact,
## R reload, Ctrl crouch, 1/2 + wheel weapon cycle, contextual scope zoom -
## implemented on sightline/qol-controls (cc4f900e, 24dad059)

Scope correction posted on #38 (comment id 298, read back): recorder/replay
support is NOT an acceptance condition; recorder coverage of the actions is
tooling/evidence debt (see the last section). #39-#43 not started.

### Architecture

Three files added, four touched, zero tokens for the IDO build:

- `src/platform/sl_action.h` / `sl_action.c` - `enum sl_action` (INTERACT,
  RELOAD, CROUCH, WEAPON_PREVIOUS, WEAPON_NEXT, ZOOM_IN, ZOOM_OUT; the enum
  order IS the bit order of the masks the game reads), `sl_binding` rows with
  a per-device source (`SL_SRC_KEY` scancode, `SL_SRC_MOUSE_BUTTON`,
  `SL_SRC_WHEEL` direction + context, `SL_SRC_PAD_BUTTON`, `SL_SRC_PAD_AXIS`
  half), `sl_action_eval(devices, out[])` -> per action HELD (level) and
  PRESSED (down edge from the previous poll's level, or counted wheel
  notches), `sl_action_reset`, `sl_action_name`, `sl_action_bindings`.
- `src/native/sl_action_channels.c` - the publish/read seam, same shape as
  `sl_move_channels`: `sl_action_channels_set(active, held_mask)` per poll,
  `sl_action_channels_pulse(action, n)` ACCUMULATES edges until the game's
  once-per-tick `sl_action_channels_get(held, pressed, zoom_in, zoom_out)`
  consumes them (polls and ticks are not 1:1 - measured in the #20 round -
  so a set-and-overwrite edge could vanish), `_peek` for a recorder later.
  Inactive (headless, replay, menu) drops everything. ZOOM: a notch becomes
  `SL_ACT_ZOOM_TICKS_PER_NOTCH = 2` game ticks of the cartridge's own
  `zoomIn/OutFovPersec = 1.0` rate, counted down in the getter, so the pulse
  is in ticks not polls: x1.21 per notch, ~11 notches sweep the sniper's
  60->7 range; 1 tick (x1.1, 23 notches) reads as no control, 3 (x1.33) too
  coarse to aim with. Owner's to judge; one constant.
- `src/native/sl_game_query.c` - `sl_game_scoped_zoom_active(player)`:
  insightaimmode AND the right-hand item's WEAPONSTATBITFLAG_DISABLE_CROUCH
  bit, the same two-term test as bondview2.c:5359-5361, never a weapon-id
  list (the bit is 0x8000 'can not crouch' per "Objects and Attributes/
  weapons/weapon statistics bitflags.txt", set on exactly the Sniper Rifle
  00178A70 and the Camera 0000A990 - routed in docs/doc-routing.json, new
  area `player-input`). Also `sl_game_action_witness` - the read-only string
  the SL_INPUT_DEBUG line prints (crouchpos, right-hand weaponnum,
  weapon_action_state / weapon_current_animation, sniper/camera zoom, the
  nearest door's openstate/openPosition) - the one diagnostic added.
- `src/platform/sl_input.c` - E and R leave `read_keyboard` (E was `action`
  -> N64 B, R was `next_weapon` -> N64 A); Space still raises B. Raw wheel
  notches are counted per direction beside the menu queue
  (`g_wheel_act_up/down`, cap 8, cleared per poll). Once per poll: build the
  device snapshot (keyboard state, mouse buttons only while captured, the
  notches only outside a menu, the active pad handle), decide the wheel
  context (menu -> the existing stick pulse; else scoped-zoom query == 1 ->
  SCOPED; else PLAY), `sl_action_eval`, publish with `active = live &&
  !menu`. Focus loss resets the edge history.
- `src/game/bondview2.c` - "NATIVE ACTIONS" block right after the movement
  seam, under its gates plus `g_CurrentPlayer == g_playerPointers[0]`; the
  get consumes on every pass (frozen path included) so intro-camera presses
  are dropped, not banked. INTERACT -> `moveData.btap = 1` +
  `g_sl_interact_only`; after Rare's btap block (tank exit / tank enter /
  `field_D0 = 1`) the native block takes `field_D0` into
  `g_sl_interact_pressed` and clears `field_D0`. RELOAD ->
  `g_sl_reload_pressed`. WEAPON_PREVIOUS/NEXT -> `weaponBackOffset` /
  `weaponForwardOffset`. CROUCH -> `crouchDown` while held, `crouchUp` after
  release while `g_sl_crouch_native` (only a crouch this key caused), both
  behind the same DISABLE_CROUCH test as :5375. ZOOM_IN/OUT ->
  `zoomIn/OutFovPersec = 1.0f` for the pulse tick, behind the same aiming +
  stat-bit test as :5359. Accessors `sl_bond_pressed_interact` /
  `sl_bond_pressed_reload` beside `bond_pressed_reload_activate`.
- `src/game/lv.c` - beside :756 (`lvlRender`): the interact-only press calls
  `bond_interact_object()` with the return ignored; the reload press calls
  `attempt_reload_item_in_hand` for GUNRIGHT and GUNLEFT.

CROUCH is HOLD-TO-CROUCH: down while Left Ctrl is down, up on release. That
is the cartridge's own shape (aim + C-down held = down, C-down released while
aiming = up) minus the aim requirement; the cartridge quirk of staying down
after leaving aim mode is left intact for the pad by raising `crouchUp` only
for a native crouch. Heights, SQUAT/HALF/STAND, the +/-2 step, the speed
penalty and the cannot-crouch weapons are untouched.

The pad is NOT in the default table (the kinds evaluate; no rows): B/A ->
B, X -> A, aim + C-down crouch, A+Z previous weapon - all through the
selected control style exactly as before. The remote-mine detonate chord
(:5389) is a pad chord and cannot arm from an action.

### Binding matrix

| action | keyboard | mouse | gamepad | edge/held | consumer seam |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INTERACT | E | - | - (B/A classic) | edge | btap -> Rare's tank branches; else lv.c `bond_interact_object()` only |
| RELOAD | R | - | - (B classic) | edge | lv.c `attempt_reload_item_in_hand` both hands |
| CROUCH | Left Ctrl | - | - (aim + C-down classic) | held | `crouchDown` held / `crouchUp` released -> `currentPlayerAdjustCrouchPos(-2/+2)` |
| WEAPON_PREVIOUS | 1 | wheel up (play) | - (A + Z classic) | edge | `weaponBackOffset` -> `backstep_through_inventory` |
| WEAPON_NEXT | 2 | wheel down (play) | - (X classic) | edge | `weaponForwardOffset` -> `advance_through_inventory` |
| ZOOM_IN | - | wheel up (scoped) | - (C-up classic) | edge -> 2-tick pulse | `zoomInFovPersec = 1.0` -> `camera_sniper_zoom_in` |
| ZOOM_OUT | - | wheel down (scoped) | - (C-down classic) | edge -> 2-tick pulse | `zoomOutFovPersec = 1.0` -> `camera_sniper_zoom_out` |
| (unchanged) fire / aim / B / confirm | F, LMB / Q, RMB / Space / Enter | | RB,RT / LB,LT / A,B / - | N64 buttons | the style tables |

Wheel context order: menu (stick pulse, unchanged) -> adjustable scoped
aiming -> weapon cycling.

### Recorder debt (#7 / B-104 class, NOT fixed here)

The `.input` stream carries the pad and the `.move` sidecar the four
channels + linear look; the action channels have no sidecar. A live session
that uses E / R / Ctrl / 1 / 2 / the wheel in play will therefore replay with
those inputs MISSING (Space, F, Q, WASD and the mouse still replay). The
`_peek` reader exists for the recorder to attach to; `_get` consumes and
must not be used by it.
